articles.title: OpenAI activa ChatGPT Ads en 14 países latinos: publicidad en español en la IA
articles.text:
OpenAI, la empresa liderada por Sam Altman, amplió la disponibilidad de ChatGPT Ads (su sistema de publicidad) a 44 mercados, incluidos 14 países de América Latina, mediante un acuerdo que permitirá a marcas y agencias contratar espacios publicitarios en la plataforma con facturación y asistencia en cada territorio.
El anuncio extiende la llegada de la publicidad a un servicio de inteligencia artificial (IA) que millones de personas usan para consultar información, resolver dudas y comparar opciones.
La lista regional abarca a Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, República Dominicana, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Panamá, Paraguay, Perú, Puerto Rico y Uruguay. En esos 14 mercados, las compañías y agencias podrán acceder a ChatGPT Ads con procesos comerciales y soporte disponible en español.
Cómo pautar dentro de ChatGPT en Latinoamérica
La comercialización estará a cargo de Aleph, que actuará como revendedor de OpenAI en los mercados contemplados. La empresa dispondrá de grupos locales para el proceso de incorporación, la atención de consultas y el soporte inicial a anunciantes y agencias.
Además, las contrataciones podrán gestionarse con facturación local, opciones de crédito y pagos en la moneda de cada país.
Qué significa esta novedad en ChatGPT para las marcas
Para empresas y agencias de los países latinos, la medida abre una vía para contratar presencia publicitaria en un espacio de inteligencia artificial sin depender de operadores de otras regiones. El acceso local puede simplificar aspectos administrativos, como la facturación, el cobro y el soporte en el idioma de cada mercado.
Gastón Taratuta, fundador y director ejecutivo de Aleph, afirmó que “los anunciantes de 44 mercados van a poder trabajar con OpenAI a través de un equipo local que habla su mismo idioma”.
Agregó que el esquema contempla facturación en moneda propia y crédito, dos factores que podrían facilitar la entrada de compañías de menor escala a este tipo de servicios.
Cómo cambia la experiencia de los usuarios de ChatGPT
Para el público, la principal novedad será la incorporación de una lógica publicitaria en una herramienta utilizada para hacer preguntas y recibir respuestas generadas por inteligencia artificial.
A diferencia de las redes sociales o los buscadores tradicionales, ChatGPT se organiza alrededor de conversaciones, lo que plantea dudas sobre la relación entre las respuestas, las sugerencias y los mensajes comerciales.
En qué otros países se habilita la contratación de anuncios en ChatGPT
El acuerdo incorpora 16 países de Europa y Asia Central: Azerbaiyán, Bulgaria, Croacia, Chipre, Chequia, Estonia, Hungría, Kazajistán, Letonia, Lituania, Rumania, Serbia, Eslovaquia, Eslovenia, Ucrania y Uzbekistán.
Asimismo, la cobertura se completa con 10 territorios de Medio Oriente y África —Egipto, Kenia, Kuwait, Marruecos, Nigeria, Qatar, Arabia Saudita, Sudáfrica, Turquía y Emiratos Árabes Unidos— y cuatro de Asia-Pacífico: Bangladés, Camboya, Hong Kong y Sri Lanka.
Por qué la publicidad llegó a las plataformas de IA
Los sistemas de inteligencia artificial se han convertido en una alternativa para buscar explicaciones, comparar productos, organizar tareas o encontrar sugerencias. Esa función puede acercar a los anunciantes a personas que ya expresan una necesidad concreta, aunque exige reglas claras sobre transparencia y protección de datos.
La expansión de ChatGPT Ads en América Latina y otros mercados traslada ese debate a una escala más amplia. A medida que la publicidad se incorpore a estos servicios, usuarios, empresas y reguladores deberán observar cómo se separan los contenidos promocionados de las respuestas generadas por la plataforma.
El despliegue de este modelo confirma que los asistentes virtuales de IA atraviesan una transformación similar a la que vivieron los buscadores hace décadas.
En los próximos meses, el foco estará puesto en la adaptación de cada mercado y en la capacidad de estas plataformas para mantener estándares claros de transparencia mientras integran nuevas dinámicas dentro de la conversación.

articles.title: Retadup Worm Resurfaces 7 Years After Takedown to Spread CoffeeLoader Malware
articles.text:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a new variant of CoffeeLoader, a malware designed to deliver additional payloads to infected machines.
"On launch, the NSIS-based installer executable dropped a file named '7z.dll' into a temporary directory and ran it through rundll32.exe," Kaspersky said in an analysis published today.
"The '7z.dll' file was a patched version of the original library of the popular 7-Zip archiver. Part of its code had been replaced with malicious self-decrypting shellcode that turned out to be a new version of the Armoury packer."
CoffeeLoader was first documented by Zscaler ThreatLabz in March 2025, detailing its use of the Armoury packer to resist analysis and ultimately run Rhadamanthys shellcode. The malware is assessed to share source code similarities with another loader family tracked as SmokeLoader.
Malware packed with Armory uses file names like "ArmouryAIOSDK.dll" and "ArmouryA.dll," with the packer hijacking some of the original Armoury Crate functionality with self-decrypting shellcode.
Notably, the shellcode extracts code that executes a decryption routine on a system's GPU by making use of the OpenCL library. The end goal is to install CoffeeLoader, establish persistence, and execute it by injecting it into a newly created "dllhost.exe" process.
The latest version of the packer continues to use the GPU, but replaces OpenCL with the OpenGL library. In addition, the new version of the packer delivers intermediate shellcode instead of a DLL. This shellcode serves as a downloader responsible for fetching the main CoffeeLoader malware.
"To establish persistence, the Trojan copies '7z.dll' to subfolders of %PROGRAMDATA% or %LOCALAPPDATA%," Kaspersky said. "The Run registry key is used for autorun. The subfolder, library, and registry value are named with eight hexadecimal digits generated from system volume information."
"To protect itself, the downloader creates a registry key that prevents the user from disabling autorun through Task Manager."
Once persistence is successful, the malware launches one of the legitimate processes (e.g., "dllhost.exe," "WerFault.exe," "svchost.exe," "OpenWith.exe," or "AtBroker.exe") and then injects itself into it, after which the malware shellcode is downloaded from a hard-coded command-and-control (C2) server.
The shellcode then decrypts and runs the CoffeeLoader payload. It supports the same three commands to run the next-stage malware from the C2 server -
- Injecting it into a process
- Saving it to disk as an executable and then running it
- Saving it as a DLL and then running it via "rundll32.exe"
As for how CoffeeLoader is distributed, it takes place via Retadup, a Windows computer worm that was disrupted by French law enforcement authorities in August 2019. The malware, which spreads via infected USB drives, has been used to drop additional payloads like cryptocurrency miners, the Stop ransomware, and the Arkei password stealer.
"Two years ago, someone began re-registering the domain names that Retadup had used as C2 servers and using them to issue commands to download third-party malware," Kaspersky said. "At first, this was the SmokeLoader downloader packed using the 32-bit version of Armoury, but in early 2025, the same servers started serving CoffeeLoader."
It remains unclear whether the worm's author or some other threat actor was instrumental in bringing the C2 servers back online. Kaspersky said it blocked around 15,000 systems from being infected with the resurrected version of the worm, most of them located in Peru, Angola, Russia, and Bolivia.

articles.title: Pour Scott Bessent, NVIDIA doit chercher un nouveau PDG au dehors de l'entreprise
articles.text:
La question de qui présidera au destin de NVIDIA à l'avenir excite les commentaires des plus grandes personnalités américaines. Dont celui du patron de l'économie américaine, le secrétaire au Trésor américain, Scott Bessent.
Passer à une ère post-Huang chez NVIDIA semble particulièrement compliqué, quand on sait que le fondateur est à cette heure le seul patron qu'ait connu l'entreprise, jusqu'à Colette Kress. Celle-ci n'est ainsi qu'un cheffe intérimaire, le temps que la société trouve une nouvelle figure pour mener la barque. Aujourd'hui, beaucoup hésitent à tout simplement redonner les rênes à Jensen Huang. D'autres proposent des solutions plus radicales.
Pour Scott Bessent, NVIDIA doit chercher un nouveau patron en dehors de l'entreprise
On le sait, à Washington, il y a de nombreux partisans de Jensen Huang, jusqu'à Donald Trump lui-même. Mais tout le monde ne pousse pas simplement pour que le fondateur du géant NVIDIA revienne à son poste. Même si un Elon Musk considère qu'il est irremplaçable, d'autres ont des conseils à donner à la société pour trouver un bon patron.
C'est le cas de Scott Bessent, le secrétaire au Trésor des États-Unis. Durant l'émission « Sunday Morning Futures », diffusée sur la chaîne conservatrice Fox News, il a ainsi estimé que NVIDIA devait « aller [chercher] en dehors de la firme » pour trouver un nouveau PDG. Car pour rappel, Colette Kress est à ce jour une solution interne, celle-ci étant l'ancienne directrice financière de NVIDIA.
Un choix qui permettra de créer un choc positif
Et si Scott Bessent propose ce conseil, c'est qu'il a une bonne raison. Pour lui, ce qui est arrivé à NVIDIA avec l'affaire Jensen Huang ressemble bien à un problème structurel, que personne dans la société ne pourra régler.
« Dans le cadre de la recherche d'un nouveau dirigeant menée par le conseil d'administration, celui-ci doit se tourner vers des candidats extérieurs à l'entreprise ; au vu de ce qui se passait au sein de celle-ci, un remaniement radical s'impose » a-t-il ainsi affirmé.
Il a par ailleurs profité de cette intervention pour rappeler que NVIDIA avait 10 jours pour répondre aux questions posées sur la culture de la conformité de la société sur le problème des restrictions à l'exportation.
Source : Reuters

articles.title: SANSAR Linux Cryptomining Malware Uses Modified NVIDIA Library to Hide GPU Activity
articles.text:
A financially motivated threat activity cluster tracked as REF3364 has been attributed to a Linux-focused cryptocurrency mining operation that tampers with the readings used to detect high GPU workloads.
Central to the intrusion is a toolkit called SANSAR, a Rust-based orchestrator that receives commands over the TOR anonymity network to manage CPU and GPU miners. The activity was observed in late October 2026.
"The threat actor also deployed a kernel rootkit to hide selected processes and files, an NVIDIA Management Library (NVML) wrapper to falsify GPU readings, and a separate backdoor named netns," Elastic Security Labs said in a report published last week.
"This backdoor retrieves its C2 [command-and-control] address from an Ethereum smart contract before connecting to the server directly."
In the attack chain documented by the company, initial access is said to have been achieved via an exposed Ray job agent, allowing the threat actor to execute commands. This includes jobs running the NVIDIA System Management Interface (nvidia-smi) to capture and exfiltrate the GPU inventory to an external server.
Subsequently, the attacker submitted a Python reverse shell job that connected to a remote listener, after which an SSH key was added to that account's authorized_keys file to establish persistent access.
"After obtaining root, the actor staged the toolkit under /opt/vadi_, built the acpi_thermal_mgr kernel module through Dynamic Kernel Module Support (DKMS) and added an initramfs loader," security researcher Salim Bitam said.
"An initramfs is a temporary root file system loaded into RAM during early boot, before Linux switches to its normal root filesystem. The module and loader are stored in the boot image on disk, so the rootkit can load again when the host boots with that image."
The installation also delivers a modified NVML wrapper that filters process information and changes GPU telemetry to evade detection. Specifically, the altered wrapper hooks NVML calls used by monitoring tools such as nvidia-smi to report GPU utilization as 0%. In addition, temperature and power readings are substituted with random values between 36 to 46 degree Celsius (96.8 to 114.8 degree Fahrenheit) and 100 to 200 watts.
Also delivered are the following payloads -
- sansar, used for TOR C2, launching or stopping the miner, miner configuration updates, connection management, spawning interactive shells, launching an IPv4 TCP SYN traffic task against a specified address and port, and NVML-hook maintenance
- kurt (XMRig version 6.25.0), the miner selected by sansar's CPU branch
- tilki (SRBMiner-MULTI version 3.6.9), the miner selected by sansar's GPU branch
- lyrebird, a legitimate pluggable transport proxy for TOR
- acpi_thermal_mgr.ko, a Linux rootkit used for process, directory, and socket-list concealment
- netns, an Ethereum-assisted backdoor
Once launched, SANSAR first performs an anti-debugging check by reading the value of TracerPid and exits if it's non-zero. TracerPid indicates the Process ID (PID) of the process currently tracing or debugging the target process.
It then reaches out to an onion service ("efxisnqldelyr5ra25oqfrsut54b34g26e7zrsiuupsoekjof2gho2id[.]onion") for C2 communication via Arti, receiving commands, collecting host and GPU information, and fetching the miner status. The main responsibility of SANSAR is to supervise the mining process and launch the appropriate miner executable based on the miner type (i.e., CPU or GPU) specified in the C2 response message.
The "acpi_thermal_mgr.ko" kernel rootkit, on the other hand, uses Function Tracer (ftrace) to conceal cryptomining activity on Linux systems by hiding processes, files, and socket entries.
It achieves this by intercepting system calls to directory listings, file access, and process termination signals, removing matching records or blocking requests for those hidden processes and files by returning the message "No such file or directory" or "No such process."
The other main component of the operation is the netns backdoor that's registered as a systemd service. It's used to retrieve a controller IPv4 address by sending requests to an embedded contract (0x43eb291f56688c63c93e8a93c4591fc997cf6349) and then sets up a plain TCP connection to that address on port 8080 to open a reverse-shell connection to the specified host and port in the C2 response.
It's not clear who is behind the operation, but Elastic said it found Turkish language comments in the rootkit's source code.
"Organizations expanding GPU infrastructure for AI and LLM workloads should check who can submit jobs and whether GPU monitoring libraries have been modified, as cryptojacking can divert compute capacity from legitimate workloads and increase operating costs," Elastic said.

articles.title: Chery, MG y Toyota anuncian más opciones de electrificación e hibridación: desde lujo hasta amplia autonomía
articles.text:
El Salón Internacional del Automóvil de Bogotá 2026 reúne en Corferias a más de 82 marcas con diferentes propuestas de electrificación e hibridación. Chery, MG y Toyota llegaron con vehículos para diferentes sectores y tipos de clientes, que cada vez más están interesados en estos avances.
Las tres compañías coincidieron en mostrar portafolios que cubren distintos niveles de hibridación, desde modelos a combustión hasta eléctricos puros, con el objetivo de que el comprador elija la tecnología según sus necesidades de movilidad y no al revés.
La propuesta de Chery durante las 24 horas
Para la feria, la marca cuenta con un salón virtual disponible las 24 horas entre el 12 y el 22 de noviembre, para que los consumidores de cualquier región consulten el portafolio y separen vehículos en línea.
“Queremos que la ubicación y el horario no sean una barrera para acceder a la experiencia del salón”, explicó Paola Vivas, directora de Marketing de Chery Colombia.
Entre los modelos destacados figura el iCAR 03T, híbrido de rango extendido enchufable con doble motor eléctrico y tracción iWheel Drive, un sistema de tracción que distribuye la potencia del motor a las cuatro ruedas de manera automática y permanente.
También sobresale el Chery E5, SUV 100% eléctrica con autonomía de 350 kilómetros, disponible en versiones Comfort y Luxury, de la cual ya se entregaron más de 1.100 unidades en dos meses.
A ellos se suma el Tiggo 4, primera híbrida completa de la marca en el país, con autonomía probada de 1.100 kilómetros, y la línea Tiggo 7, 8 y 9, híbridas enchufables con hasta 120 kilómetros de autonomía eléctrica y 1.200 kilómetros combinados.
Todo el portafolio cuenta con garantía de ocho años o 200.000 kilómetros sobre el vehículo completo. Entre enero y octubre de 2026, Chery registró 5.023 matrículas, un incremento del 287% frente a 2025, y en octubre alcanzó su mejor mes con 1.047 unidades matriculadas.
MG estrena la línea premium IM
MG llegó al salón con tres lanzamientos: el sedán MG5 Plus, la SUV MG HS Hybrid Plus y la nueva gama de lujo IM, representada por el modelo IM6.
Según explicó Manuel Correa, experto de marca, a Infobae la línea IM busca entrar al segmento de vehículos de gama alta con una única versión que integra todas las características, diferenciada por dos opciones de batería: una de 75 kilovatios hora con 450 kilómetros de autonomía WLTP, y otra de 100 kilovatios hora con 625 kilómetros en la versión Max.
El IM6 incorpora un procesador Snapdragon junto con Nvidia para agilizar las asistencias de conducción y el sistema de infoentretenimiento. También integra el modo cangrejo, con una inclinación de 18 grados en las ruedas traseras para facilitar giros en U y maniobras en espacios reducidos, además de carga inalámbrica de 50 vatios con refrigeración, modo masaje y modo mascota, que activa el aire acondicionado y muestra un aviso en pantalla mientras el dueño del animal regresa al vehículo.
Toyota también apuesta por la electrificación
Toyota mostró un portafolio que va desde vehículos a combustión hasta eléctricos puros, bajo garantías de cinco u ocho años según la tecnología y hasta diez años de cobertura comercial en algunos productos. Manuel Hernández, gerente nacional de ventas de vehículos nuevos y usados de Toyota, explicó a Infobae que la marca busca cubrir todas las necesidades sin dejar a ningún cliente atrás.
Entre los modelos que los asistentes podrán ver en el Salón están el Yaris Hatchback es el único híbrido completo de entrada del mercado, el Corolla Sedán y el Corolla Cross, además de otras sorpresas que se anunciarán en el transcurso de la feria.
Sin embargo, el bZ4X es la propuesta de innovación de la marca para el evento. Se trata de un auto 100% eléctrico con dos motores delanteros y traseros, sistema X-Mode y autonomía de 480 kilómetros con carga completa. Incorpora el sistema Toyota Safety Sense, que combina asistencias de seguridad activa y pasiva, y se exhibió también en versión Off Road para mostrar su comportamiento en terreno destapado.

articles.title: Uber data breach sees hackers steal license information on thousands of drivers
articles.text:
Uber data breach sees hackers steal license information on thousands of drivers
One of Uber's services was breached
- Uber discloses third-party breach that exposed driver data, including driver’s license information for thousands of individuals
- The incident stemmed from a compromise at AI infrastructure provider Fireworks, which was also targeted in broader LLMjacking attacks
- Uber is notifying affected users and offering identity theft and credit monitoring services while investigations continue
Popular ride-hailing service Uber has confirmed it lost sensitive data after one of its third-party service providers was hacked.
The company filed a new notice with multiple US Attorney General’s Offices and shared a copy of the letter it is now sending out to affected individuals.
In the letter, it says that a threat actor got ahold of login credentials belonging to an employee of the service and used them to pull Uber’s data.
Driver’s licenses and other data
The letter does not disclose key details, like the nature of the data that was stolen, or how many people were affected.
According to TechCrunch, however, “thousands” of drivers lost personal and driver’s license information, with the stolen data including driver’s licenses of 2,567 individuals in Massachusetts, 3,430 people across South Carolina, and 1,873 residents of Rhode Island.
More drivers in Illinois and California, and possibly elsewhere, may also be affected - but these figures are so far unconfirmed.
While Uber did not say which of its third-party service providers got hacked, the media uncovered it was a company called Fireworks AI which, itself, was also a victim of a third-party supply chain attack. Fireworks is a US-based AI infrastructure company that helps businesses deploy and run AI models at scale. Apparently, it provides access to hundreds of AI models, as well as the computing resources needed to run them, and its clients include heavy-hitters such as Shopify, DoorDash, and Notion.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Fireworks recently issued a notice saying it spotted a threat actor using internal company credentials to access “environment variables used in evaluation jobs” in a “limited number” of customer accounts.
At first, the company said it did not find evidence of unauthorized access to customer models, datasets, training data, personal information, or inference traffic, but a subsequent update changed the wording somewhat: “At the time of publishing the bulletin, only Fireworks stored secrets (e.g. used in evaluation jobs) were known to have been accessed. Since then, we discovered impacts to account and billing information. For a limited set of accounts, we also discovered impact to secrets, datasets, and incomplete models,” it said.
LLMjacking
The data stolen from Uber seems like added value, not the primary target, as Fireworks says all evidence indicates this was an LLMjacking attack.
LLMjacking is a relatively new term. Google’s Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) recently described it as “the monetization and resource-hijacking of foundation models, which actors achieve through token proxying, automated model streaming, and GPU hardware provisioning.” In other words, someone else is using your AI subscription while you get the bill.
The attacks are quite disruptive, too. Unlike cryptojacking, which takes a long time to rake up any meaningful bills, LLMjacking costs can go up in mere minutes. Google’s recent report showed how a Chinese actor tracked as UNC6993 cost its victims more than $100,000.
The company suffered a secondary attack, as well, less than a month later. On October 23, someone broke into a third-party cloud provider that hosted the company’s R&D machines and used it to reach Fireworks development machines.
There, they ran unauthorized workloads “that led to additional customer data impact.” The attack was spotted on the same day and stopped. “As of October 25, we have not detected further evidence of successful unauthorized access by the threat actor on the Fireworks platform customers use,” the company concluded.
Both Fireworks and Uber are now notifying affected individuals of the breach, and the latter is also offering free identity theft and credit monitoring through Cyberscout.

articles.title: Xbox : Microsoft ressuscite les écrans de démarrage mythiques des premières consoles
articles.text:
Pour célébrer les 25 ans de Xbox, Microsoft a décidé de faire un joli cadeau aux joueurs nostalgiques, avec les animations de démarrage des premières consoles de la marque. Et c’est franchement réussi !
En cette fin d’année 2026, Xbox fête ses 25 bougies. Un quart de siècle déjà depuis l’arrivée de la première console de Microsoft, un 15 novembre 2001. Pour marquer le coup, la firme américaine multiplie les clins d’œil à son histoire et aux joueurs qui l’accompagnent depuis ses débuts. Et parmi les petites attentions qui font plaisir, il y en a une toute récente (et gratuite) qui devrait réveiller quelques souvenirs.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Le plein de nostalgie chez Xbox
Comme l’a notamment relayé The Verge, Microsoft déploie actuellement une mise à jour permettant de retrouver plusieurs animations de démarrage historiques sur Xbox One et Xbox Series. Au programme : le boot emblématique de la toute première Xbox, mais aussi deux séquences tout aussi mémorables de la Xbox 360, celles de 2005, puis de 2010.
La mise à jour est en cours de déploiement et, bonne nouvelle, il y a de fortes chances qu’elle soit déjà disponible sur votre console. Nous avons d’ores et déjà pu essayer les différentes animations sur notre Xbox Series X, et quel plaisir de retrouver ces séquences pleines de nostalgie ! Notre préférence va évidemment au logo vert de la première Xbox, avec son ambiance sonore si particulière.
Pour en profiter, il suffit de se rendre dans les paramètres de la console, puis dans les options système et de démarrage, afin de sélectionner l’animation souhaitée. On peut ainsi passer d’une génération à l’autre en quelques secondes. C’est un détail, certes, mais qui permet d’ajuster son degré de nostalgie avant même de lancer son jeu (et c'est gratuit).
Cette initiative s’inscrit dans une célébration plus large des 25 ans de Xbox, avec notamment le lancement récent d’une manette dédiée et d'une console collector. Microsoft a aussi remis en lumière son catalogue historique, avec 21 nouveaux jeux de la première Xbox désormais compatibles avec les PC Windows, certains profitant même de succès à débloquer. Au total, 25 jeux Xbox sont compatibles PC.
De quoi prolonger les retrouvailles avec quelques classiques, sans forcément ressortir sa vieille console du placard.
PlayStation avait eu la même bonne idée… avant de faire marche arrière
Microsoft n’est pas le premier constructeur à jouer sur cette corde sensible. Pour les 30 ans de PlayStation, en décembre 2024, Sony avait lui aussi proposé aux possesseurs de PS5 de retrouver l’interface et les animations de démarrage des différentes générations de consoles, avec notamment le mythique lancement de la première PlayStation.
Une initiative qui avait été particulièrement bien accueillie par les joueurs. Mais cette parenthèse nostalgique n’avait malheureusement pas vocation à durer, puisque Sony avait rapidement retiré ces thèmes anniversaire, au grand regret d’une partie de la communauté.
Et c’est peut-être là que réside toute la bonne idée de Microsoft. Au-delà de la célébration ponctuelle, pourquoi ne pas laisser ces animations à disposition des joueurs ? Après tout, il ne s’agit que d’une option de personnalisation, qui ne gêne personne… Et qui fait manifestement plaisir à beaucoup de monde.
- La rétrocompatibilité au top
- Le Quick Resume, difficile de revenir en arrière
- Taillée pour l'avenir (HDMI 2.1, dolby vision/atmos, VRR)

Store passwords and passkeys across all your devices.
RoboForm Premium is a password manager designed to keep your logins secure and accessible across all your devices. It combines unlimited password and passkey storage with automatic form filling, secure sharing, and advanced two-factor authentication. With support for Windows, Mac, Linux, Android, and iOS, it's a handy option for anyone who wants to manage passwords without relying on browser-based storage.
Best For: Anyone managing numerous online accounts who wants secure password storage, automatic logins, breach monitoring, and access across unlimited devices.
The Deal: RoboForm Premium is reduced from $29.88 to $10.68 for the first year in the Black Friday sale, saving $19.20 (64%). The subscription renews annually, and there's a 30-day money-back guarantee.
Best Roboform Premium deal
RoboForm Premium offers unlimited password and passkey storage, unlimited devices, AES-256 encryption, advanced 2FA, breach monitoring, password generator, secure sharing, cloud backup, offline access, emergency access, and priority support.
Why we recommend it
RoboForm Premium provides a wide set of password management tools and stores unlimited passwords and passkeys, automatically fills login details and web forms, and generates strong passwords when you create new accounts.
It has AES-256 encryption and several two-factor authentication options, including authenticator apps, hardware security keys, and passkeys. An integrated TOTP authenticator also helps manage verification codes without your needing a separate app.
RoboForm monitors up to five email addresses for data breaches and it can also identify weak, reused, or exposed passwords. The Premium plan works across unlimited devices and browsers, with cloud backup and offline access included. If you're still relying on browser-saved passwords, reusing passwords across accounts, or juggling multiple devices. RoboForm Premium offers a number of security features and is it an inexpensive password manager.
❌ Skip RoboForm Premium if...
If you already use a password manager or only need basic password storage on one device. Free alternatives may be enough, and the subscription is a lot more expensive after the first year.

articles.title: Amazon Uncovers AI Agent Campaign Targeting LiteLLM, Dify, and Other Apps for API Keys
articles.text:
Attackers' AI agents have been hunting for weak spots in internet-exposed AI apps such as LiteLLM, One API, and Dify to steal the AI provider keys stored inside, according to the agents' own records.
The records, which Amazon's threat intelligence team captured with decoy servers, describe stolen keys being used to run the AI models that powered the search for more keys.
The team said this week that it cannot verify the outcomes reported by the agents. It has moderate confidence that the agents ran on ARTEX, an open-source AI tool for penetration testing.
The records include a playbook of known entry points for each targeted product. It lists default administrator credentials such as LiteLLM's default master key, unfinished installs that an outsider could take over, and known flaws in Langflow and RAGFlow.
In a separate case reported this week, Cloudflare's incident responders saw ARTEX gain access to a compromised API token that had been used for CI/CD. The token had no IP restrictions or rate limiting, and the activity that followed included 400 database dump requests in an hour. The company has not said whether those requests returned any data.
An operator gives ARTEX a target and a goal, and a planner agent splits the goal into tasks for worker agents that run security tools. To decide each next step, the agents send their work to a large language model (LLM).
The decoy servers, part of a network called MadPot, posed as popular LLM services. From October 3 to late last week, the agents sent it requests that often carried a campaign's full history, including the operators' instructions and the agents' reported findings.
Those captured agent records describe work done on systems MadPot does not watch. "Amazon Threat Intelligence did not observe that activity as it happened and cannot verify the outcomes the agents reported, but the records show what the actors were pursuing," the team said.
The team assessed, with moderate confidence, that the operators were separate China-linked groups, citing Simplified Chinese prompts and China time zone settings, among other evidence.
In the main campaign, the agents looked for internet-exposed AI apps, extracted the provider keys stored inside, verified that the keys worked, and added them to a shared pool. They focused on apps that hold keys for many providers, because one weak admin page there can expose many accounts.
Targets named in the records include LLM gateways and proxies such as One API, New API, Veloera, Sub2API and LiteLLM, and AI app builders such as Dify, FastGPT, Langflow, RAGFlow, Open WebUI, LobeChat and Ollama.
The playbook also covers management and provider settings endpoints that need no login, an authentication bypass through the isCliRequest header in One API family systems, and server-side request forgery (SSRF) through URL-fetch features to reach cloud metadata services. Other entries cover secrets left in client-side JavaScript, source maps, debug routes and environment files.
When the agents found cloud credentials, they targeted managed services that host AI models, secret stores, and application identities, prioritizing premium AI models over general cloud access.
To find leaked keys, the agents used internet scanning services and certificate transparency logs, and searched GitHub repositories and event archives, npm and PyPI packages, container image layers, notebooks, model-hosting spaces, paste sites, and Telegram channels.
The records cover hundreds of targets across AI app platforms and other systems. The team notified AWS customers who may have been affected.
Microsoft reported last week that attackers were using agentic AI tools such as ARTEX for GitHub secret hunting, looking for exposed credentials that included API keys for AI inference.
On August 26, the company described an earlier RAGFlow attack, in which a hidden hook captured AI provider keys as users entered them, and a compromise of a LiteLLM gateway that exposed provider keys.
In its RAGFlow case study, the company had only low confidence about which flaw, if any, let the attackers run code. It did not link those attacks to ARTEX.
The decoy records also describe a second campaign in which agents attempted to bypass identity checks at two cryptocurrency exchanges using deepfakes.
One verification vendor's server rejected the live deepfake video on every attempt the agents made to record it. The team did not say whether the forged photos of ID documents that the agents also fabricated passed document checks.
Over the past eight weeks, Cloudflare's incident responders were called into multiple investigations involving ARTEX and tools built from it.
In more than one incident, an attacker gained access to a customer's environment with a major cloud provider and moved directly into the customer's Cloudflare account. The common root cause was static CI/CD tokens that never expired, granting broad access across the customer's cloud setup, according to the company.
In the ARTEX case, the compromised token was an account-level API token. The compromise most likely came through a third-party cloud provider, according to the company's incident findings. How the token was first stolen has not been disclosed.
New Worker scripts with names such as artex-*, artex-pgrecon-*, artex-pgw-* and artex-do-* appeared in the account, each name matching a different task. The activity ran at more than 69 requests per minute across several parts of the account. It included attempts to establish persistence and validate session tokens for other third-party apps.
Much of this activity was lightly guided by a human operator, the company believes. Whether any attempt at persistence worked has not been disclosed.
Over three days this week, more than 50 families of AI penetration testing frameworks tried to scan the company's customers, and the IP addresses seen running such frameworks now number in the thousands.
The FBI said in a FLASH alert this week that a range of attackers have used ARTEX since at least August against organizations in many sectors around the world. The alert summarizes 11 earlier reports and describes no new incident.
ARTEX's developer made its GitHub repository unavailable on October 8 after reports of abuse, but community forks, archived copies, and a commercial version called ARTEX PRO keep it available.
The alert's examples include an earlier campaign against South Korean financial institutions that stole personal information on about 67,000 people, and the ConnectWise compromise.
What Defenders Can Check
"None of the techniques in these campaigns were new. What AI agents change is the speed and persistence of the attacker," Amazon's threat intelligence team said. The agents succeeded where basic security was missing, including default or hard-coded credentials, keys left in code and public files, interfaces and inference endpoints without authentication, and unpatched software.
The team recommends treating AI apps, model gateways, and inference endpoints like other production systems, assuming that exposed secrets will be found quickly, and watching for misuse through unexpected spending or unusual usage.
Here is the status of the flaws named in the playbook:
| Product | Flaw | Status | 
|---|---|---|
| Langflow | CVE-2025-3248, missing authentication that lets a remote attacker run code | Versions before 1.3.0 are affected, and 1.3.0 is the fixed version ( release notes ). CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog on May 5, 2025, after earlier Langflow exploitation , and the KEV entry marks it as known to be used in ransomware campaigns. | 
| RAGFlow | CVE-2026-28797, server-side template injection (SSTI) that lets any logged-in user run operating system commands on the server. The attack needs a registered account, and self-registration is on by default, the security advisory says. | NVD lists 0.24.0 and earlier as affected. The advisory lists no patched version. Version 0.25.0, released on April 21, renders templates in the sandbox the advisory recommends, according to its SSTI fix notes . | 
| One API family | Authentication bypass through the isCliRequest header | The team's report names no affected versions or fix. | 
Other checks that apply to these attacks:
- Change default administrator credentials, such as LiteLLM's default master key, and do not leave a new install unfinished where an outsider could take it over.
- Search configuration files, environment variables, deployment scripts, CI/CD pipelines and databases for embedded secrets, keep scanning repositories and container images for exposed ones, and rotate exposed credentials quickly, as the FBI advises.
- Give Cloudflare API tokens an expiry date and limit the client IP addresses that can use them. Both are optional token restriction settings, and new tokens carry a cfut_ prefix that secret scanners can detect.
- Look for Cloudflare Worker scripts named artex-*, artex-pgrecon-*, artex-pgw-* or artex-do-*.
- Check logs for the 11 IP addresses published with the decoy findings, and for the more than 2,500 addresses that researchers at Cisco Talos link to ARTEX in their indicator files.
- The researchers' detection rules for ARTEX are Snort 3 rules 7:76, 7:77 and 7:78, and Snort 2 rules 1:67494, 1:67495 and 1:67496. Rules 7:78 and 1:67496 are off by default and detect traces of norma, the agent harness ARTEX uses.

articles.title: Qué celulares Android se quedan sin WhatsApp a partir del 20 de noviembre de 2026
articles.text:
WhatsApp dejará de funcionar en una serie de celulares Android antiguos desde el 20 de noviembre de 2026. Los dispositivos que no puedan operar con Android 6.0 o una versión posterior perderán la posibilidad de instalar actualizaciones y de utilizar el servicio.
La medida alcanza a modelos de Samsung, Motorola, LG y Sony que ya no admiten la actualización necesaria. La antigüedad del teléfono no determina por sí sola la exclusión: el punto decisivo es la versión del sistema operativo que el fabricante permite instalar en cada modelo.
Qué celulares Android se quedan sin WhatsApp en noviembre de 2026
La lista incluye varios modelos de Samsung: Galaxy S3, Galaxy S4 Mini, Galaxy Note 2, Galaxy Core, Galaxy Trend y Galaxy Trend Lite. Todos quedaron por debajo del mínimo de Android 6.0, así que no cumplirán las condiciones requeridas por WhatsApp desde el 20 de noviembre.
En el caso de Motorola, los dispositivos afectados son el Moto G de primera generación, el Moto E de primera generación y el Droid Razr HD. Perderán compatibilidad el Optimus G, Optimus L5, Optimus L7, Optimus F7, Lucid 2, Nexus 4 y G2 Mini de LG, junto con los Xperia Z y Xperia SP de Sony.
Cómo revisar la versión del sistema operativo del celular
Los usuarios pueden verificar la situación de su teléfono desde el menú de configuración. En los dispositivos con Android, hay que abrir Ajustes, ingresar en Acerca del teléfono y buscar la opción Información de software o Versión de Android. Allí aparece el número de versión instalado.
Si el celular tiene Android 6.0 o una edición posterior, conservará la compatibilidad con la aplicación, siempre que se pueda actualizar WhatsApp desde la tienda correspondiente.
Si muestra una versión inferior y el fabricante no ofrece una actualización disponible, será necesario trasladar la cuenta a otro dispositivo para seguir utilizando el servicio.
De qué forma respaldar la información guardada en la cuenta de WhatsApp
Antes de reemplazar un teléfono que perderá el acceso, conviene guardar las conversaciones, imágenes, videos, notas de voz y documentos. El respaldo se inicia desde WhatsApp al ingresar en Ajustes, luego en Chats y, por último, en Copia de seguridad.
En los celulares Android, la copia se almacena en Google Drive. Al configurar un nuevo teléfono compatible, el usuario debe instalar la aplicación, validar el mismo número telefónico y aceptar la restauración del contenido disponible en la cuenta. Este paso permite recuperar el historial guardado sin perder los chats previos.
Qué pasará con los teléfonos iPhone desde el 30 de noviembre
El cambio para los teléfonos de Apple tendrá otro calendario. Hasta el 30 de noviembre de 2026, WhatsApp seguirá disponible para dispositivos con iOS 15.1 o versiones posteriores. Desde esa fecha, el requisito aumentará y será necesario contar al menos con iOS 15.5.
Los modelos que quedarán fuera de soporte son el iPhone 5, iPhone 5c, iPhone 5s, iPhone 6 y iPhone 6 Plus, porque no admiten iOS 15.5. En cambio, el iPhone 6s y el iPhone SE de primera generación pueden ejecutar esa versión o una posterior. Para comprobarlo, hay que abrir Configuración, entrar en General y seleccionar Información.
La falta de compatibilidad no elimina la cuenta ni el número asociado a WhatsApp. La restricción afecta al dispositivo, que deja de poder ejecutar la app por no cumplir con el sistema operativo mínimo exigido. Los datos permanecen disponibles si existe una copia de seguridad reciente.
En los iPhone, el respaldo se guarda en iCloud y se recupera durante la configuración de WhatsApp en el nuevo dispositivo. Quienes tengan alguno de los modelos afectados deberán revisar cuanto antes la versión de su sistema operativo, realizar una copia de seguridad y migrar a un teléfono compatible antes de perder el acceso al servicio.

articles.title: No contracts, no hidden fees, and up to 67% off — 3 of our top-rated subscription-free video doorbells just hit bargain Black Friday prices
articles.text:
Looking for a subscription-free video doorbell? 3 of our top-rated Ring alternatives just hit bargain Black Friday prices, with up to 67% off
Video doorbells always get deep discounts in the Black Friday sales, but the deals aren't always what they seem. Although the doorbells themselves might be cheap, they often come with subscription fees that are unavoidable if you actually want to store footage and check it later — and you can bet your bottom dollar those subscription plans won't be any cheaper during the sales.
That's why I've put together this list of video doorbells that our reviewers have given the TechRadar seal of approval, that don't carry additional fees for storage. Best of all, they are all going cheap right now at Amazon. With up to 67% off, why wait for Black Friday itself?
All of these devices have earned a place in our roundup of the best video doorbells, so you can be confident you're getting a device that will be easy to use, with crisp video footage and intuitive features to protect your home — and your Black Friday package deliveries.
Best for packages
1. Eufy Video Doorbell Dual
We awarded this dual-camera video doorbell a near-perfect four and a half stars, and it's a great budget pick. Its forward-facing lens captures visitors' faces, while its bottom camera monitors any packages they leave on your doorstep (ideal for keeping track of those Black Friday packages).
The standard doorbell comes with 8GB local storage built in, and if you want to store more videos, you can pick up a bundle including a chime/base station that accepts microSD cards (and comes with a 32GB card already fitted).
There are AI tools included in the base price too, including smart package detection and a 'familiar faces' feature that identifies specific people and sends you a notification when they are detected, including their name — ideal for letting you know when the kids have arrived home from school, for example.
Read our full Eufy Video Doorbell Dual review
Amazon has knocked a hefty $70 off this bundle, which gives you far more storage than the doorbell alone. You can also grab it without an SD card for $109.99 if you already have a card that you're not using.
This top-notch video doorbell is an even better deal in the UK, where you can snap it up for less than half price. It's only been cheaper than this once before, so this is a Black Friday deal not to be missed.
Best for security

Swann generously provides a 32GB card in the box, but if that's not enough, you can expand the storage to 128GB.

articles.title: Black Friday : malgré la hausse des prix d’Apple, la Fnac affiche ce MacBook Air M5 à 1 199€
articles.text:
À onze jours du Black Friday, fixé au 27 novembre, la Fnac affiche le MacBook Air 13 pouces M5 à 1 199 € au lieu de 1 399 €, alors qu’Apple a relevé ses prix. Notre test, noté 8/10, porte sur une version plus chère que celle de l’offre.
Le MacBook Air 13 pouces associe la puce M5, avec 10 cœurs de processeur et 8 cœurs graphiques, à 16 Go de mémoire et 512 Go de stockage, ici dans le coloris Minuit. La Fnac l’affiche à 1 199 € au lieu de 1 399 €, soit -14 % sur son prix barré, Apple ayant relevé ses prix. Cdiscount la proposait au même tarif lors de notre relevé du 16 novembre. Cette configuration à 16 Go de mémoire vise surtout la bureautique, les études et la création légère.
Le MacBook Air 13 pouces M5 (16 Go, 512 Go, Minuit) est affiché à 1 199 € chez la Fnac, contre 1 399 € barrés, soit -14 % selon le marchand.
Pourquoi choisir le MacBook Air 13 pouces M5 ?
- Un ultraportable sans ventilateur : la puce M5 travaille sans bruit, ce qui compte en bibliothèque, en réunion ou dans le train.
- Un SSD enfin rapide : ses vitesses de lecture et d’écriture doublent par rapport aux anciens modèles, ce qui profite aux gros fichiers et aux exports, avec plus de stockage à tarif inchangé.
- Un écran et un clavier solides : la dalle IPS de 13,6 pouces monte à 500 cd/m² et reste bien calibrée en DCI-P3, tandis que le duo clavier et trackpad reste l’un des points forts de la machine.
Bureautique, cours et montage léger : ce que fait cette machine
Au quotidien, le MacBook Air M5 vise la bureautique, la navigation, la visio et les études. L’autonomie mesurée tourne autour de 10 heures en usage mixte et de 12 heures en lecture vidéo, soit une heure de moins que sur le M4 dans ce test. Son processeur domine la concurrence en mono-cœur, mais il se montre moins à l’aise en multicœur face aux puces à 16 cœurs de certains PC Windows. Ces mesures viennent de la version 1 To et GPU 10 cœurs de notre test du MacBook Air M5, et non de la version 512 Go de l’offre.
Ce Mac convient à l’étudiant, au télétravailleur ou à quiconque veut un portable fin, d’à peine plus de 1,2 kg pour 11,3 mm d’épaisseur. La retouche photo et le montage vidéo occasionnel restent à sa portée. Il convient moins à ceux qui enchaînent les calculs lourds, car nous avons relevé une légère baisse de performance sous charge prolongée, ni à ceux qui tiennent au 120 Hz, absent ici.
Face aux ultraportables Windows et aux autres marchands
Le MacBook Air M5 n’est pas seul sur ce segment. Dans notre comparatif des meilleurs PC portables, le Dell XPS 14 prend la tête avec une autonomie de 12 à 17 heures et un écran OLED en option, tandis que l’Acer Aspire 14 AI joue la carte de l’accessibilité. Le Mac se distingue par son silence, sa finition et sa puissance mono-cœur, pas par l’autonomie. Chez Cdiscount, le prix relevé le 16 novembre est le même : le marchand se choisit donc sur le service plutôt que sur le tarif.
✅ Les points forts
- Puce M5 sans ventilateur, donc silencieuse
- SSD deux fois plus rapide que sur les anciens modèles
- Écran IPS de 500 cd/m², bien calibré en DCI-P3
- Clavier et trackpad excellents
- Léger : à peine plus de 1,2 kg
❌ Les limites
- Autonomie en baisse : 10 à 12 heures mesurées
- Chauffe plus marquée que sur le M4, jusqu’à 51 °C au point le plus chaud
- Écran limité à 60 Hz
- Très peu de nouveautés de design depuis 2022
Le MacBook Air 13 pouces M5 (16 Go, 512 Go, Minuit) est affiché à 1 199 € chez la Fnac, contre 1 399 € barrés, soit -14 % selon le marchand.
À 1 199 €, le MacBook Air 13 pouces M5 16/512 Go reste un excellent ultraportable : notre test lui attribue 8/10 et le range parmi les meilleurs du marché. Apple ayant relevé ses prix, les 200 € de remise affichés par la Fnac ramènent la machine sous son tarif actuel, et Cdiscount affiche le même prix. Seule réserve : notre test porte sur la version 1 To, pas sur celle de l’offre.
L’achat se justifie si vous cherchez un portable fin, silencieux et fiable pour travailler ou étudier, et si le coloris Minuit vous convient. Si vous pouvez attendre, les offres du Black Friday peuvent encore évoluer, sans aucune garantie. Une baisse sous 1 199 € serait le signal à guetter, et les amateurs de calcul lourd ou de jeu soutenu regarderont plutôt du côté des PC Windows.

articles.title: BO Team Exploits Log4Shell in VMware vCenter, Compromises Russian Firm's Code-Signing Server
articles.text:
An investigation into suspicious activity within a Russian software developer's network has uncovered a months-long compromise of its development infrastructure and a software code-signing server.
The activity, documented by Kaspersky's ICS CERT team after it was contacted by the affected developer in June 2025, has been attributed to a threat actor named BO Team (aka Black Owl, Hoody Hyena, and Lifting Zmiy). The name of the targeted company was not disclosed, but it operates from within Russia and develops software that has a "customer base in the Russian Federation," according to Kaspersky.
Over the course of several months, the intrusion resulted in the theft of confidential information and the compromise of all components of the organization's IT infrastructure, including Windows and Linux servers, workstations, hypervisors, backup servers, security solution management servers, and network equipment.
Active since at least 2023, BO Team focuses on cyber espionage and hacktivism, and has a history of targeting Russian entities to steal valuable data and break into compromised infrastructure using tools like Mythic and Cobalt Strike, along with its own malware such as BrockenDoor and ZeronetKit. The group is assessed to be of Ukrainian origin.
"Their primary motivation is to degrade the Russian military-industrial complex to weaken Moscow's operational capabilities on the battlefield," Orange Cyberdefense said in an analysis of the group. "They also engage in cognitive warfare aimed at humiliating Russian institutions and demonstrating their vulnerability to Ukrainian digital resistance."
While BO Team is known to deploy ransomware and publicize its activities on a dedicated Telegram channel, the attack targeting the unspecified software developer did not involve any data destruction or public posts claiming responsibility for it.
"Instead, the attackers worked to entrench themselves in the victim's network by setting up convenient command channels and planting backdoors to restore access in case it was lost," Kaspersky said. "The compromise of the software development (CI/CD) infrastructure and the software code-signing server indicated that the attack would likely develop into a supply chain scenario."
The attack, per the Russian cybersecurity company, involved the threat actors compromising the organization's Linux terminal server by taking advantage of an exposed SSH service, and using it to conduct reconnaissance of the internal network to flag systems with accessible SMB, Kerberos, SSH, Telnet, FTP, HTTP, HTTPS, WinRM, and LDAP services.
The adversary has also been found unsuccessfully attempting to access internal portals, along with websites like proxy-sale[.]com, start.duckduckgo[.]com, vcsa.vmware[.]com, and vulners[.]com, among others.
Event logs show that the attackers further attempted to connect from the compromised terminal server to the virtualization system servers, including logging in to the VMware vCenter web interface. These sign-in efforts ended in failure.
However, the threat actor managed to successfully target a VMware vCenter server (version 7.0.3) vulnerable to CVE-2021-44228 (aka Log4Shell and LogJam), obtain a remote command line with root privileges, connect to the hypervisor over SSH, and identify accessible hosts.
This phase also involved the deployment of a backdoor on the hypervisor that was run every hour by planting a shell script in the "/etc/cron.hourly/" directory. The script carried the name "pgcache" in a likely attempt to disguise it as a legitimate PostgreSQL component.
The primary responsibility of the backdoor is to download and run a secondary shell script from "lo1yaizaeghaevarooD1ahtaichootae.nofrillsdns[.]com." The shell script is designed to download and run the Global Socket (GSocket) utility, enabling the attacker to gain remote control of the compromised host.
Select variants of the script have been found to point to a hostname-specific payload staged on "lo1yaizaeghaevarood1ahtaichootaz.nofrillsdns[.]com" to deliver an as-yet-undetermined next-stage payload.
"The attackers used the nofrillsdns[.]com service, which allows domain names to be created for free by calling the curl utility," Kaspersky said. "By default, when the malware's command-and-control server is not operating, the attackers set the corresponding DNS record to 127.0.0.1, which is what the script checks. Activating the backdoor requires only a change to the DNS record -- the script will then download and run the malware."
Some of the other post-exploitation actions undertaken by the BO Team following the backdoor deployment are listed below -
- Gaining access to the corporate proxy server.
- Abusing the certificate of the compromised hypervisor to connect to servers associated with a second virtualization cluster and place a similar backdoor.
- Collecting information about virtual machines and firewall rules, accessing some of them via a command-line interpreter in the guest OS from the hypervisor.
- Running an obfuscated bash script to decrypt and run an ELF binary designed to provide remote control over SSH.
- Searching for secrets on the compromised virtual machines, allowing the attackers to breach the virtual machine of the GitLab software development platform, as well as gain access to some of the repositories containing source code and seize the server's private key.
- Using the private key of the GitLab virtual machine to connect to the organization's Ansible orchestration system.
- Using access to the Linux terminal server to locate credentials of several domain accounts and connect to the domain controller using the account of one of the system administrators after likely accessing the memory of virtual machines running on the compromised hypervisors.
- Changing the security attributes of the user's Windows Downloads directory.
- Using legitimate binaries like tasklist.exe, findstr.exe, taskmgr.exe, and ipconfig.exe to identify which security solutions were running on the system and to gather details about network interfaces.
- Attempting to take a dump of the lsass.exe process using the Nanodump utility and obtain the credentials of domain administrators and other privileged users with access to the domain controller. The attackers deleted the event logs after the activity was detected and blocked by a security solution.
- Using system utilities such as comsvcs.dll rather than established utilities like Mimikatz and Nanodump to create a memory dump of the lsass.exe process.
- Dumping the system registry using the regedit.exe utility, and using it to decrypt the Active Directory domain database ("ntds.dit") to extract the credentials of all domain users.
- Launching the OpenSSH scp.exe utility to transfer the collected information to the terminal server.
- Logging in to the domain controller using the Kerberos ticket of one of the domain administrators and ultimately compromising the organization's entire Windows infrastructure by taking advantage of the fact that the same password was used for system administrator accounts in different domains.
- Connecting to the terminal server over SSH using root account credentials after possibly stealing them from a system administrator's computer post obtaining domain administrator privileges.
- Modifying "/usr/bin/nxnode-login" to intercept and write user credentials to a shared-memory file at "/dev/shm/pulse-shm-3088612174."
- Successfully brute-forcing the password of the administrator's terminal server after about 2,500 failed attempts to place the private key of the Ansible system.
- Complicating detection efforts by timestomping, obfuscation of malware code, usage of living-off-the-land (LotL) techniques, systematic deletion of event logs, and dressing up malware files as legitimate software.
"We found numerous traces of BO Team connecting to various Windows servers, though the attackers only used malware in one case," Kaspersky explained. "The server which apparently held particular interest for hackers, was used to sign compiled builds of the commercial software developed by the attacked organization."
"Attackers may be interested in such a server for two reasons. First, they may try to carry out a supply chain attack by injecting malicious code into a product build right before it is signed. Second, the attackers may try to steal the organization's digital signature to use later to sign malware."
It's suspected that the attackers likely attempted to execute a malicious WMI script and install a backdoor similar to the Linux variant in the temporary files directory.
But after the incident was detected and countermeasures were enacted, the attackers, after having lost access to the compromised infrastructure, orchestrated a phishing campaign towards the end of July in an attempt to collect employee credentials. The phishing email contained the "Account disconnected from the mail server" subject line and sought to trick the recipient into clicking on a link to change their password.
What's more, the email managed to bypass SPF and DKIM checks, indicating the attackers had in their possession a private key that was obtained after gaining control of the organization's mail server. The phishing attack was detected and prevented.
"The attackers used a service that automatically generates phishing pages," Kaspersky said. "The service loads the content of a targeted organization's official website and displays a password entry form on top of the official site's layout. After entering the password, the user sees an error message. However, the information is actually sent to the attacker."
"We repeatedly noted that the attackers tried not to use malware and hacking utilities in order to evade detection," Kaspersky said. "Instead, they actively used system tools such as RDP, SSH, and SCP, as well as system utilities to steal user credentials. This enabled them to develop the attack using legitimate accounts, which also matches the BO Team profile."
The activity has been found to originate from IP addresses 193.3.23[.]236 and 80.76.42[.]139, both of which belong to a provider in Ukraine. Further analysis into the malicious activity has revealed that the attackers followed a standard work schedule and operated in a time zone that differed "only slightly" from that of the victim Russian entity.
"Based on the totality of the circumstantial evidence, such as the attackers' interest in the source code repository and software build signing server, as well as their use of a software composition analysis (dependency analysis) platform, we believe that BO Team may have set out to inject malicious code into a solution released by the attacked organization in order to subsequently compromise its customers, i.e., carry out a so-called supply chain attack," Kaspersky concluded.
"Thanks to the rapid response measures applied after the incident was discovered, the attackers lost access to the compromised infrastructure and were apparently unable to bring the attack to its intended conclusion."

articles.title: Apple busca a 200.000 personas en Estados Unidos para estudiar cómo usan la IA en consultas de salud
articles.text:
Apple lanzó el 15 de noviembre una aplicación para estudiar cómo usan las personas la inteligencia artificial cuando buscan respuestas sobre su salud. La compañía busca reclutar hasta 200.000 participantes en Estados Unidos, que podrán hacer preguntas médicas a un asistente y calificar sus respuestas durante un máximo de 12 meses.
El Apple Health AI Usage Study se realiza junto con OpenEvidence, una empresa de IA clínica que los médicos usan para consultar literatura científica. Según el sitio Fierce Healthcare, que cubrió el anuncio en la conferencia HLTH26, la herramienta de OpenEvidence genera las respuestas a partir de publicaciones con revisión de pares y guías clínicas.
Esas fuentes incluyen The New England Journal of Medicine, JAMA, Nature, Cochrane y la red estadounidense de guías contra el cáncer NCCN. Las respuestas llegan en lenguaje sencillo y con enlaces a los estudios en que se apoyan.
Pueden participar mayores de 21 años que vivan en Estados Unidos y tengan un iPhone 15 Pro o posterior con iOS 26 o una versión más reciente. La aplicación es independiente de Salud y de Investigación, las apps que Apple ya ofrece.
Qué hacen los participantes
Los voluntarios pueden preguntar por síntomas, recuperación tras un procedimiento, ejercicio u otras dudas cotidianas. Después califican cada respuesta e indican qué les resultó útil o qué faltó. Cada mes completan encuestas que permiten a los investigadores medir cómo usan la información recibida y qué hacen a continuación.
Al inscribirse, los participantes dan su consentimiento informado y entregan datos demográficos como edad y nivel educativo. Apple explicó que así podrá analizar si esas variables influyen en las preferencias y en la forma de comunicar las respuestas. El estudio está supervisado por un comité de revisión independiente.
También pueden compartir datos del programa Salud de Apple, como frecuencia cardíaca en reposo, actividad y sueño, para recibir respuestas más personalizadas. Quienes hayan importado sus historiales clínicos y lo autoricen pueden aportar además resultados de laboratorio.
La aplicación incluye herramientas para preparar una consulta médica y encuestas posteriores a la visita. Con ellas, los investigadores quieren saber si el chatbot hace que los pacientes lleguen mejor preparados y si mejora el diálogo con su médico.
Cómo protege Apple los datos médicos
Apple afirmó que las preguntas se procesan primero en el iPhone para quitarles los datos que identifican a la persona. Luego pasan por un entorno de estudio gestionado por un contratista externo, que las desvincula del número de cada participante y las revisa otra vez antes de enviarlas a OpenEvidence.
La compañía aseguró que los datos del estudio no se usarán para entrenar modelos de IA. El sitio TechCrunch añadió que OpenEvidence elimina las preguntas y respuestas a las 24 horas.
La aplicación también tiene medidas de seguridad para detectar preguntas que suenan preocupantes. En esos casos sugiere consultar a un profesional de la salud u otros recursos.
Sumbul Desai, vicepresidenta de Salud y Actividad Física de Apple, afirmó en una declaración que una investigación formal es la forma más adecuada de entender cómo las personas usan, comprenden y evalúan la IA de salud en su vida diaria. Según Desai, los resultados aportarán a la discusión científica sobre el tema.
Apple no informó si llevará respuestas con IA a la aplicación Salud o a Siri, según TechCrunch, y la aplicación del estudio no está integrada con el asistente de voz, de acuerdo con el medio The Verge. La app está disponible para descargar desde el 15 de noviembre solo para usuarios en Estados Unidos.

articles.title: 'Massive moments like this are prime hunting season for scammers': Surfshark joins the GTA VI excitement with an in-app easter egg — but warns of the risks the launch brings
articles.text:
'Massive moments like this are prime hunting season for scammers': Surfshark joins the GTA VI excitement with an in-app easter egg — but warns of the risks the launch brings
A Miami-themed visual skin arrives on iOS and Android alongside warnings that more than 750 scam sites could target eager gamers by launch day.
Anticipation for the latest Grand Theft Auto game is at fever pitch. But with cybercriminals looking to profit from the excitement, Virtual Private Network (VPN) provider Surfshark is marking the occasion with an in-app easter egg and a stern warning to those looking to grab the new game before release day.
The provider revealed that its researchers tracked more than 200 GTA-themed domains registered immediately after recent beta announcements. At least one in four of those sites was created to defraud eager players.
The company projects that the number of malicious or opportunistic domains will exceed 750 by the time the game finally hits store shelves.
The finding fits into a wider pattern of gaming fraud, echoing Surfshark's prior scam research showing how threat actors exploit major cultural moments to trick unsuspecting consumers.
A neon Easter egg on mobile
Firstly, to celebrate the release, Surfshark has rolled out a hidden visual theme across its iOS and Android apps.
Inspired by Google Doodles, the cosmetic skin is based on the neon-soaked Miami aesthetics closely associated with the franchise's fictional Vice City setting.
The feature is rolling out gradually to mobile users in the lead-up to launch day. It serves as a lighthearted touch for gaming enthusiasts who use the app on phones and tablets.
“As a huge gamer myself, I’m just as hyped as everyone else for this release, and sneaking a little game-inspired Easter egg into the app is a great testament to our teams’ creativity and drive for giving something fun back to the gaming community,” said Dovydas Godelis, CEO of Surfshark, in a press release.
“At the same time, massive moments like this are prime hunting season for scammers, and as a cybersecurity company, we must remind our users of that.”
Fake PC builds and bogus beta keys
Behind the colorful promotion lies a genuine security problem. Threat actors know that millions of players want early access or alternative ways to play. That demand makes gamers easy targets for credential harvesting and payment fraud.
According to Surfshark, existing fraudulent sites are baiting visitors with fake pre-orders, non-existent mobile installations, bogus beta keys, and cryptocurrency schemes. Others advertise cracked PC versions of the game, taking advantage of desktop gamers who do not want to wait for a delayed computer release.
"Cybercriminals thrive on cultural hype, and this release is the biggest opportunity in gaming history," added Godelis. "Gamers are being baited into downloading cracked builds or entering payment details on fake storefronts. We wanted to remind everyone to stay level-headed, double-check URLs, avoid suspicious third-party links, and keep their guard up. Scammers are counting on the moment when excitement outgrows caution."
Can a security app actually protect you from these scams? Only up to a point. While Surfshark's DNS-filtering and ad-blocking tools can block known malicious domains, software cannot stop you from handing over credit card numbers or account passwords on a convincing fake storefront if you ignore browser warnings.
Staying safe requires skepticism. Stick exclusively to official publisher announcements, verify website addresses carefully, and treat any download promising early PC builds or beta access as an immediate red flag.
Rene Millman is a seasoned technology journalist whose work has appeared in The Guardian, the Financial Times, Computer Weekly, and IT Pro. With over two decades of experience as a reporter and editor, he specializes in making complex topics like cybersecurity, VPNs, and enterprise software accessible and engaging.

articles.title: Crypto : un homme interpellé pour un home jacking à 900 000 euros
articles.text:
C'est une autre affaire d'attaque à domicile en lien avec les cryptomonnaies sur laquelle la police avance. Un homme vient d'être interpellée pour un rapt dont la rançon a été particulièrement élevée.
Les fortunes rapides faites en cryptomonnaies attirent malheureusement la convoitise des malfaiteurs - et ce, particulièrement chez nous en France. On a ainsi vu un certain nombre d'affaires de kidnapping, allant jusqu'au cofondateur de Ledger, se multiplier en France, avec l'objectif d'obtenir une rançon. Et certaines fois, les kidnappeurs vont directement au domicile de leurs victimes, pour les y menacer et obtenir une somme conséquente. Comme dans cette affaire.
Un couple séquestré à son domicile, pour une rançon en crypto d'une valeur de 900 000 euros
Au mois de mars dernier, un homme et une femme dans la cinquantaine et vivant au Chesnay étaient la cible d'une attaque à leur domicile de la part d'un groupe de trois hommes. L'un d'eux a alors utilisé un couteau pour menacer la femme du couple, afin d'obliger l'homme à payer une rançon en cryptomonnaies.
Il a alors cédé à la menace, et a payé la somme exigée en bitcoins, d'un valeur estimée à environ 900 000 euros. D'après les informations de la police, les deux personnes du couple ont ensuite été installées sur leur canapé, puis ligotées, après quoi les malfaiteurs ont fui le domicile. Et depuis, une enquête pour séquestration et vol en bande organisée a été ouverte.
Un homme interpellé à la suite du rapt
Aujourd'hui, cette enquête connaît une avancée notable avec l’interpellation d'un homme dans son domicile à Blois (Loir-et-Cher), dans le cadre de ce dossier. Il a été ensuite mis en examen puis en détention préventive, sans que le parquet de Versailles n'ait pour le moment produit les détails de ses chefs de mis en examen.
Reste maintenant à savoir à quel point ces actions seront efficaces sur le long terme. Car malgré l'alarme sonné depuis déjà un certain temps, le nombre d'enlèvements liés aux cryptomonnaies a continué à augmenter entre 2025 et 2026. Ils étaient ainsi entre 45 et 67 l'an dernier, selon les bilans, alors qu'ils étaient déjà plus de 70 sur les huit premiers mois de l'année 2026, d'après le Parquet national anticriminalité organisée.
Source : Le Figaro

articles.title: Laboratorio de Ghana hizo que su IA diseñara más de 6.000 posibles toxinas tras quitarle las barreras de seguridad
articles.text:
Investigadores de MinoHealth AI Labs, un laboratorio de inteligencia artificial de Accra, Ghana, quitaron las barreras de seguridad de su modelo para descubrir medicamentos y le pidieron diseñar toxinas. El programa generó diseños de 1.020 proteínas y 5.000 moléculas pequeñas que un software de predicción calificó como probablemente tóxicas.
Los investigadores no fabricaron ninguna de esas sustancias en un laboratorio. Algunos diseños se parecían a la ricina, un veneno mortal. El estudio se subió en mayo de 2025 al servidor de preprints arXiv, según informó Rest of World.
“Todos quedamos impactados”, dijo a ese medio Darlington Akogo, fundador de MinoHealth. El experimento se hizo en 2024 y, según Akogo, bastaron unos pocos días para que el modelo, llamado Moremi Bio, ignorara sus salvaguardas.
Akogo sostiene que su trabajo fue el primero en mostrar que un modelo de lenguaje puede diseñar armas biológicas. Antes, en 2022, científicos de una farmacéutica de Estados Unidos habían usado un programa de aprendizaje automático para generar diseños de posibles armas químicas.
El eslabón pendiente: la fabricación de ADN
La preocupación de Akogo va más allá del diseño. Alguien podría enviar esas secuencias a una empresa que fabrica ADN por encargo. Algunas de estas compañías revisan los pedidos para detectar secuencias tóxicas, pero un actor malicioso podría burlar ese filtro con ayuda de la IA, advirtió.
En junio, los directores de OpenAI, Anthropic y Google DeepMind se sumaron a un pedido a legisladores de Estados Unidos para que esos controles sean obligatorios. El Consorcio Internacional de Síntesis de Genes, un grupo voluntario de proveedores, también apoya una ley que exija revisar los pedidos en toda la cadena.
Sandra Roy, gerente de programa del consorcio, dijo que trabajan con desarrolladores de modelos para detectar secuencias diseñadas por IA con el fin de evadir los filtros. En Kenia, Brenda Obuya, funcionaria del Ministerio de Información, Comunicaciones y Economía Digital, afirmó que la necesidad de regular este sector llegó a los niveles más altos de gobierno en África.
Los chatbots comerciales también se pueden engañar
Peter Garraghan, fundador de la empresa de seguridad Mindgard, dijo que investigadores lograron que varios modelos soltaran sus límites mediante jailbreaking, es decir, redactar los pedidos de forma que el modelo ignore sus reglas. Mencionó a Kimi, Grok, Claude y ChatGPT. A su equipo le tomó un día vulnerar Kimi.
Los modelos más recientes tienen mejores salvaguardas frente a pedidos biológicos, pero no son infalibles, según el Instituto de Seguridad de la IA, organismo de investigación del gobierno británico. Ayantola Alayande, investigadora del Centro Global sobre Gobernanza de la IA, opinó que ya no sorprendería que usuarios sin formación obtengan ese tipo de resultados con chatbots.
En septiembre, Anthropic informó de cinco casos en que personas intentaron usar sus modelos para apoyar el desarrollo de armas biológicas. Ken McCallum, director general del servicio de inteligencia británico MI5, afirmó que ese es hoy el mayor riesgo de mal uso de la IA. Bill Gates dijo ese mes, en el podcast The Ezra Klein Show, que la IA ya permite a un bioterrorista causar muertes masivas.
MinoHealth nació en 2016 con otro objetivo: paliar la falta de personal sanitario en Ghana. En 2023 recibió USD 149.533 de la Fundación Gates para construir un modelo capaz de analizar imágenes médicas. Hoy tiene un equipo de 20 personas y se financia sobre todo con la venta de su sistema.
Moremi Bio propuso cientos de candidatos a fármacos contra cáncer, tuberculosis y dengue. Akogo pide que las Naciones Unidas formen un grupo de trabajo sobre estos riesgos y que se endurezcan los controles a la síntesis de ADN.
La empresa participa ahora en un consorcio financiado por la Unión Europea para desarrollar anticuerpos y diagnósticos contra la viruela símica y la malaria.
