articles.title: Goodbye, manual work: AI-native CRM platform Dreamteam raises $53M to automate enterprise sales - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Goodbye, manual work: AI-native CRM platform Dreamteam raises $53M to automate enterprise sales
Intelligent sales software startup Dreamteam AI Inc. said today it has raised $53 million in early-stage funding to try to flip the narrative around customer relationship management platforms, which often seem like more of a hindrance than a help, by actually getting work done for sales teams.
The funds come by way of a seed and Series A round led by Accel Partners with participation from Together Fund and Premji Invest.
CRM platforms such as Salesforce and Hubspot have served as vital cogs in the wheel sales-focused enterprises for more than a quarter of a century. But these days they often create just as much work as they save, says Dreamteam co-founder and Chief Executive Anand Venkatraman (pictured, center, alongside co-founders Ramesh Parthasarathy and Senthil Kanthaswamy). While organizations are striving to use artificial intelligence to automate more of their business processes, CRMs are holding them back, he believes.
The problem with legacy CRM platforms is that they’re totally reliant on manual data entry, Venkatraman explained. Because their architectures are built around structured data fields and rigid, hand-coded workflows, they create a tight bottleneck that makes it almost impossible for autonomous AI agents that feed primarily on semantic data to get anything done.
“When a sales prospect expresses price hesitation or mentions a competitor, a salesperson registers it immediately,” he said. “But a legacy CRM, starving for unstructured nuance, misses it entirely, leaving AI agents without the vital context needed to reason effectively.”
To provide this context, Dreamteam has rebuilt the CRM from the ground up around the idea of a “company brain,” or a living memory of the business that constantly updates itself by ingesting new information from meetings with clients, prospects and team members, emails and other connected tools. As with all AI-native platforms, there’s also a generous dose of automation in the shape of four AI agents, or teammates, which specialize in different tasks.
The agents include Rachel, which handles account research; Sally for meeting preparations and follow-ups; Raj, which monitors for pipeline risks; and Alex, which serves as the CRM administrator, keeping the platform ticking over without any human intervention.
Venkatraman said he and his co-founders designed Dreamteam’s architecture specifically to address the historic shortcomings of legacy CRM platforms, which struggle to dig up the most vital business intelligence, leaving teams flying blind. “When a CEO asks why the quarter’s three biggest deals were lost, RevOps spends two weeks building a partial answer from whatever the reps happened to type,” he said. “The richest signals from meetings, emails, and calls were never captured, so the answer is always incomplete and always late.”
Legacy CRMs also fail to capture institutional knowledge, which means that everything a senior sales representative knows about the clients they work with leaves when they depart the company. There’s also a heavy administrative tax, with users forced to waste valuable time entering data to keep the platform up to date.
“CRMs don’t have a shortage of features,” Venkatraman said. “But they have a shortage of context and trust, and they lack the ability to get actual work done.”
Dreamteam does things differently. By capturing the unspoken context around each deal an organization does, it says, its platform can help to prevent new leads from going stale. Monitoring everything that’s said and agreed to in meetings, via chats and emails and other tools, the platform can pick out the most important signals, such as pricing sensitivities, objections and stakeholder dynamics.
It remembers all of the fine details of each specific deal. That way, even if the main sales rep involved suddenly leaves, it will retain all of the context so whoever takes over the account knows what needs to be done next.
The platform also employs humanlike reasoning. “When a prospect says, ‘The board is pushing hard on costs,’ it knows the proposal should lead with ROI, not features,” Venkatraman explained. “The CRM was supposed to give companies a complete picture of their customers, yet the richest parts of that picture have always lived outside the CRM.”
The startup has already witnessed significant traction with its agentic, contextual approach: It’s used by hundreds of organizations across the AI, healthcare, manufacturing, consulting and online media sectors. Dreamteam has enabled those early adopters to transform the way they handle sales.
Because the CRM continuously self-updates its records following daily customer interactions, it means sales people have much more time to focus on actually selling rather than data entry. Senior leaders have more visibility into deal pipelines, and can immediately find out why deals are stalling or how their customer’s sentiments are shifting.
Scott Olechowski, chief product officer at the video streaming service Plex Inc., said he was especially taken with the tight level of integration with Dreamteam and the company’s existing information technology stack. “The combination of simplicity and power hits the sweet spot for us,” he said. “The ability to integrate with the AI tools we are using across our organization is a game-changer.”
Venkatraman believes Dreamteam can have an even greater impact in future by expanding its shared intelligence layer beyond sales operations. His ambition is to build a platform that spans the entire customer lifecycle, from onboarding to customer success, renewals and upselling, to ensure that organizations can squeeze the most value out of the deal context it captures.
“Much of what’s learned during sales is lost or fragmented when a customer moves into implementation or customer success,” he pointed out. “But the same company brain that knows why a customer bought should also help teams onboard them, spot risks and find ways to grow the relationship.”
One way Dreamteam intends to pursue this vision is through what it calls “Magic Apps,” which is a capability that lets users build custom dashboards and tailored CRM workflows using natural language prompts. “The apps live inside Dreamteam, inherit its data permissions and action-level authorizations, and stay connected to customer records, workflows and the Company Brain, so you can customize without rebuilding the foundation,” Venkatraman said.
Premji Invest’s Saravanan Nattanmai has already bought into this vision, stressing the need for CRM systems to become more than just a system of record. He characterizes what Dreamteam is building as a “system of intelligence.”
“Dreamteam sets out to intuitively understand user intent, build deep contextual intelligence and execute workflows seamlessly through autonomous AI teammates,” he said. “We believe the future of enterprise software lies in AI-native systems that don’t just augment existing workflows but fundamentally reimagine how work gets done.”

articles.title: Cómo evitar los spoilers de GTA 6 en redes sociales si aún no lo puedes jugar
articles.text:
Grand Theft Auto VI se estrena el 19 de noviembre y trae consigo un problema para millones de jugadores: el riesgo de spoilers antes de poder disfrutarlo en algún momento. El juego llega primero a Nueva Zelanda, lo que generará horas, incluso casi un día completo, en las que circularán videos y comentarios sobre la trama antes de que la mayoría del público hispanohablante pueda jugar.
A esto se suma una gran cantidad de usuarios que no podrán tenerlo desde el día de su lanzamiento, ya sea porque no lo pueden comprar aún o porque no tienen PS5 o Xbox Series X|S, las consolas en las que estará disponible. Por lo que es importante saber cómo evitar este tipo de spoilers.
Las palabras que conviene silenciar antes del estreno
Silenciar siempre que entras a jugar a GTA 6 implica anticiparse y filtrar ciertos términos en redes sociales. Entre las expresiones recomendadas figuran:
- GTA 6
- GTA VI
- Grand Theft Auto 6
- Grand Theft Auto VI
- Jason
- Lucia
- Vice City
- Leonida
- Spoiler
- Leak
- Gameplay
- Filtraciones
- Final
- Misión Secreta
- Historia Completa
- Mapa Completo
- Ending
Bloquear estos términos no garantiza eliminar todos los contenidos, pero reduce las probabilidades de toparse con ellos en el feed o en las notificaciones durante los días más críticos tras el lanzamiento.
Cómo configurar los filtros en cada red social
En X, la opción se encuentra en los ajustes de privacidad, dentro del apartado de palabras silenciadas. Allí se pueden añadir las frases del listado y elegir si el filtro aplica a cuentas que no se siguen o a cualquier cuenta, además de definir cuánto tiempo estará activo: una semana suele ser un margen razonable.
En TikTok, el camino pasa por Perfil, el menú de Ajustes y privacidad, luego Preferencias de contenido y finalmente Filtrar palabras clave, donde se pueden cargar los términos en los distintos feeds disponibles.
En Instagram, el control aparece entre las opciones de contenido sugerido, que permite ocultar recomendaciones que incluyan determinadas palabras o hashtags en el texto, aunque los nombres de los ajustes pueden variar según la versión de la aplicación.
En Facebook, no existe un filtro de palabras como tal, pero se puede pausar durante 30 días a los perfiles, páginas o grupos que suelen compartir spoilers, usando los tres puntos disponibles junto a sus publicaciones.
En YouTube, el riesgo aparece incluso sin reproducir ningún video, ya que una miniatura puede mostrar un personaje o una escena, y un título puede explicar directamente qué ocurre en una parte del juego. Ante canales que repiten esta práctica, conviene usar el menú de tres puntos junto a sus videos y seleccionar la opción de no recomendar ese canal, o marcar “no me interesa” en cualquier contenido relacionado con el título.
Los comentarios y los grupos de amigos, otro foco de riesgo
Incluso cuando una publicación, un video o una noticia logran evitar los destripes, los comentarios siguen siendo un punto débil. Alguien puede filtrar un detalle de la trama por desconocimiento, por error o directamente con la intención de arruinar la sorpresa a otros usuarios, algo que también puede ocurrir en los chats de las transmisiones en vivo.
Por esa razón, conviene mantener cierta prudencia al leer la sección de comentarios en publicaciones relacionadas con el juego, sobre todo durante los primeros días tras el estreno.
En el caso de los grupos de WhatsApp o Discord con amigos, la recomendación pasa por acordar reglas antes del lanzamiento. Crear un grupo o canal específico para hablar de la historia, separado de las conversaciones habituales, permite a quienes ya avanzaron en el juego comentar la trama sin exponer a quienes todavía no llegaron a esas partes.

articles.title: Melhor TV Box e Sticks: 6 modelos 4K para comprar em 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Melhor TV Box e Sticks: 6 modelos 4K para comprar em 2026
Precisa transformar sua TV em smart? Encontre os melhores modelos de TV Boxes e Sticks compatíveis com conteúdo em resolução Ultra HD
TV Boxes e TV Sticks são ótimas opções para quem quer transformar o televisor em um modelo smart, sem precisar comprar uma nova TV. Esses dispositivos também servem para smart TVs mais antigas, com poder de melhorar a fluidez de navegação.
Dongles avançados como o Fire TV Stick 4K Max são ideais para TVs 4K compatíveis com formatos HDR. Também há TV Boxes mais simples, a exemplo da Smart Tv Box 4K Intelbras, que focam no suporte aos principais apps de streaming.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog lista seis opções de TV Boxes ou Stick com resoluções de até 4K UHD. Confira modelos da Amazon, Xiaomi, Roku, Vivensis e Intelbras.
O Fire TV Stick 4K Max é o dispositivo de streaming mais potente da Amazon. O dongle oferece saída de imagem de até 4K UHD (3840 x 2160 pixels), chega com 2 GB de RAM e 16 GB de armazenamento para alocar seus aplicativos de streaming e jogos favoritos.
Além disso, o Fire TV Stick também suporta as tecnologias Dolby Vision e HDR10+ para aproveitar os realces de brilho, cor e contraste de conteúdos HDR em TVs elegíveis. E ainda é compatível com Dolby Atmos para uma experiência sonora mais imersiva.
O padrão Wi-Fi 6E é um dos diferenciais, já que é compatível com a banda de 6 GHz para alcançar velocidades de conexões mais rápidas e com menos latência. O dispositivo roda sob o sistema Fire OS da Amazon e tem saída HDMI 2.1 para conexão com televisores.
Dimensões: 108 mm (C) x 30 mm (L) x 14 mm (E)
A Xiaomi TV Box S 4K é um dispositivo de streaming ideal para quem deseja instalar vários aplicativos, já que possui 32 GB de armazenamento. Além disso, a TV Box com resolução máxima 4K UHD possui 2 GB de RAM para entregar desempenho fluido de navegação.
Há suporte para formatos de vídeo avançados como Dolby Vision e HDR10+, além de experiência sonora com Dolby Atmos e DTS:X. Vale lembrar, no entanto, que o televisor também precisa ser compatível com essas tecnologias para aplicar as melhorias de imagem e áudio.
O dispositivo opera sob o sistema Google TV, com Google Assistente e espelhamento de smartphones facilitados com o Google Cast. E também conta com Wi-Fi 6 para conexões mais rápidas, Bluetooth 5.2 e uma porta USB-A 2.0 para dispositivos de armazenamento externos.
Dimensões: 97 mm (C) x 97 mm (L) x 17 mm (A)
O Roku Streaming Stick Plus é um dongle custo-benefício focado em streaming com resoluções de até 4K. Ele tem apenas 1 GB de RAM, mas o sistema RokuOS é leve e otimizado, o que ajuda a reduzir o consumo de memória.
O dispositivo suporta HDR10 e HDR10+ e consegue reproduzir esses conteúdos se sua TV também for compatível com esses formatos. No entanto, o Roku Streaming Stick Plus não pode reproduzir imagens em Dolby Vision, ainda que seu televisor conte com a tecnologia.
Já falando sobre conectividade, o Roku Streaming Stick Plus chega com Wi-Fi 5 e conectividade Bluetooth, apesar de a empresa não especificar a versão.
Dimensões: 97 mm (C) x 20 mm (L) x 13 mm (E)
O Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K é uma versão mais modesta do modelo Max. Ele também oferece resolução máxima de 4K UHD e 2 GB de RAM, mas tem um processador menos potente e 8 GB de memória interna — a metade da capacidade da variante Max.
Outra diferença está no padrão Wi-Fi adotado, que é o Wi-Fi 6. Ele também utiliza o padrão de rede wireless 802.11ax e suporta as mesmas velocidades de acesso do Wi-Fi 6E, embora não funcione na frequência de 6 GHz que está sujeita a menos congestionamento de rede.
Ainda assim, o dongle roda sob o sistema Fire OS e é compatível com as tecnologias Dolby Vision e HDR10+ para reproduzir imagens de alta qualidade no padrão HDR.
Dimensões: 108 mm (L) x 30 mm (A) x 14 mm (E)
A Vivensis Stick VX Smart 4K é uma TV Box para quem quer assistir a séries, filmes, novelas e programas televisivos. Ele é o único dispositivo da lista que recebe sinal de TV aberta via satélite (banda KU), oferecendo mais de 80 canais gratuitos.
Fora isso, o aparelho também roda os principais apps de streaming sob o sistema operacional Android TV com resoluções de até 4K. E também é compatível com conteúdos HDR10 e HDR10+, caso seu televisor também tenha suporte.
O dispositivo ainda traz duas portas USB, conectividade Wi-Fi 5 e porta RJ45 para conexões cabeadas mais rápidas e estáveis. Há Bluetooth integrado, mas a versão 5.0 não dispõe de melhorias de estabilidade e eficiência das versões mais recentes.
Dimensões: 120 mm (C) x 120 mm (L) x 26 mm (A)
A Smart Tv Box 4K Intelbras é um dispositivo básico para transformar qualquer televisor em uma smart TV. Para isso, a TV Box roda o sistema Android TV, compatível com os principais apps de streaming como Netflix, Prime Video e HBO Max.
O aparelho é mais indicado para TVs simples que não suportam conteúdos em HDR, já que não possui suporte a HDR10 ou Dolby Vision.
Em compensação, ele traz uma porta RJ45 para conexões cabeadas à internet, duas entradas USB 2.0 e Bluetooth integrado na versão 5.0.
Dimensões: 162 mm (C) x 162 mm (L) x 75 mm (A)
A escolha pela melhor TV Box deve considerar desde o aspecto físico do dispositivo até as especificações de hardware, levando em conta também as limitações da TV. Fique de olho em:
TV Box e TV Stick são dispositivos que conseguem transformar TVs comuns em smart TVs. Mas os aparelhos têm formatos e conexões diferentes.
TV Boxes têm formato de caixa e precisam de um espaço para fixação no rack ou bancada. Eles também precisam estar conectados à tomada para funcionar e costumam oferecer portas USB e RJ45. Alguns modelos ainda podem receber sinal de antena parabólica, como o Vivensis Stick VX Smart 4K.
Já TV Sticks são extremamente compactos, em formatos similares ao de um pen drive. Eles não precisam ocupar uma entrada de tomada, já que a alimentação simples pode ser feita via USB do próprio televisor. Em compensação, eles não oferecem as portas de conexão que TV Boxes costumam entregar.
Não necessariamente. Uma TV Box precisa de internet para acessar apps de streaming e ferramentas que só funcionam online. Contudo, alguns modelos recebem sinal digital de TV aberta ou podem reproduzir conteúdos gravados em cartões microSDs e dispositivos de armazenamento, sem depender de internet.
TV Boxes falsificadas costumam ter falhas de impressão na embalagem, incluindo acabamentos de baixa qualidade e fontes diferentes. Enquanto isso, embalagens de produtos originais têm detalhes de fabricação completas e informações claras de fabricação.
Encontrar a certificação Play Protect nas informações da Google Play Store também é um bom indicador de produto original. E vale abrir o Mi Home pela Xiaomi TV Box e emparelhar o controle remoto: apenas produtos originais vão se conectar corretamente e aparecer no ecossistema Xiaomi.
Depende muito do modelo de sua TV e do quanto você está disposto a gastar. Comprar uma TV Box é a forma mais acessível de transformar seu televisor em um modelo smart. Mas se a TV for muito antiga, ela talvez não consiga aproveitar de tecnologias como HDR, processadores recentes e construções de tela mais modernas.
Por outro lado, adquirir uma smart TV elimina a necessidade de adquirir TV Boxes ou sticks à parte e ainda garante compatibilidade com tecnologias atuais. E ainda que o custo seja maior do que uma TV Box ou Stick, você pode encontrar smart TVs boas e baratas.

articles.title: Prise en main du Magic9 Pro Max : HONOR en fait tout un film !
articles.text:
Mini chamboulement chez HONOR : cette année, le flagship du constructeur chinois sera le Magic 9 Pro Max. Le nom, d’une folle originalité, laisse présager celui qui est identifié comme son concurrent direct. Nous l’avons pris en main lors d’une rencontre avec le constructeur.
On savait qu’HONOR était épaté par les trouvailles d’Apple en matière de design. Manifestement, le constructeur ne s’est toujours pas remis du changement de look de l’iPhone. Après l’Honor 600, qui rendait un vibrant « hommage » à son modèle californien, c’est au tour du Magic 9 Pro Max de céder aux sirènes de l’esthétique selon Apple.
Un design vraiment très inspiré…
Exit donc la caméra dorsale regroupée dans une plateforme circulaire : le Magic 9 Pro Max fait siennes les deux platines arrière : l’une héberge la caméra dorsale tandis que l’autre, un poil matifiée, reprend la couleur dominante de l’appareil. Celle-ci est au choix noire, blanche ou verte : pas d’orange (so 2025…) ni de bordeaux à l’horizon.
Côté dimensions, on reste sur un produit de grande taille : 161,64 x 76,98 x 8,59 mm pour 233 grammes. Cela permet d’y loger une dalle OLED de 6,8 pouces dont la luminosité maxi en pic HDR est annoncée à 10 000 nits (2000 nits hors HDR). Si c’est le cas, il conviendra de parler d’écran éblouissant au sens littéral du terme.
Autre changement notable, la caméra dorsale est désormais composée de trois modules circulaires au lieu d’un, le téléobjectif ayant une taille disproportionnée par rapport aux deux autres. Pourquoi pas, après tout ? L’ensemble reste plaisant à regarder et surtout à prendre en main.
Après la photo, focus sur la vidéo
La caméra dorsale, justement, affiche des propriétés physiques impressionnantes : module principal équipé d’un capteur 200 Mpx (capteur 1/1,28") et d’un objectif ouvrant à f/1,57 et d’une stabilisation certifiée CIPA 8.0 (cherchez pas : y’a pas mieux pour un smartphone pour l’instant).
Le téléobjectif a lui aussi son capteur 200 Mpx (capteur plus petit 1/1,4") ainsi qu’un objectif ouvrant à f/2,6 et d’une stabilisation toujours certifiée CIPA 8.0. Enfin, l’ultra-grand-angle doit se contenter d’un capteur 50 Mpx et d’un objectif ouvrant à f/2.
Enfin, la caméra frontale est construite autour d’un capteur de 55 Mpx et d’un objectif ouvrant à f/2. Il est accompagné d’un module 3D servant au déverrouillage de l’appareil ainsi qu’à la réalisation de bokeh sur les selfies.
Si tout cela semble très correct, ce n’est pas vraiment complètement nouveau… Ou à un (gros) détail près. Après s’être associé au Studio Harcourt Paris pour le peaufinage du mode portrait, Honor s’adjoint les compétences d’ARRI pour la vidéo. Vous ne connaissez pas ARRI ? C’est que vous n’êtes pas un cinéaste professionnel (voir encadré).
OK mais concrètement, ça donne quoi ? Si, par exemple, on filme une rue à la tombée de la nuit, on souhaite généralement garder la chaleur des vitrines, l’ambiance des éclairages publics tout en captant l’action.
C’est ce que propose le mode ARRI Cinema : on choisit un traitement des couleurs et des contrastes (on parle de Look) afin de l’appliquer directement à l’enregistrement. Le rendu est visible en temps réel lors du cadrage et présente fidèlement ce qui sera enregistré. Le Magic 9 Pro Max propose 14 Looks prédéfinis auxquels peuvent s’ajouter une cinquantaine d’autres par téléchargement gratuit.
Pour les vidéastes plus exigeants, il est possible de filmer directement au format LogC3 : une fois les rushes importés dans le logiciel de montage, ils disposent d’une grande latitude de réglage colorimétrique et d’ajustement des contrastes.
Lors d’une captation réalisée en LogC3, il est possible d’appliquer temporairement un des looks pour se faire une idée du rendu, sans altérer le fichier d’origine.
Le son n’est pas oublié avec l’intégration d’un micro directionnel de « qualité cinéma » dont la démonstration qui nous a été montrée est impressionnante (forcément). Il va sans dire que nous sommes impatients et curieux d’évaluer tout cela lors d’un test !
HONOR propose en supplément trois accessoires vidéo : une coque faisant office de grip, deux téléconvertisseurs (200 et 500 mm) ainsi qu’un rig conçu avec l’accessoiriste Smallrig.
Qui est ARRI ?
Fondé à Munich en 1917 par August Arnold et Robert Richter, ARRI est un fabricant allemand de caméras et d’éclairages professionnels pour le cinéma. Son patronyme provient des premières lettres des noms de ses deux fondateurs.
De l’ARRIFLEX argentique aux caméras numériques ALEXA (oui !), ARRI a accompagné plus d’un siècle de tournage. Ses produits ont gagné en notoriété parmi les professionnels de la profession jusqu’à décrocher pléthore de récompenses techniques : vingt Oscars et six Emmy Awards, notamment pour la conception d’une caméra reflex 35 mm et pour l’enregistreur sur pellicule ARRILASER.
Pour l’HONOR Magic 9 Pro Max, la collaboration des deux sociétés porte essentiellement sur l’intégration du format LogC3 et non pas sur l’aspect matériel.
De la puissance à la pelle
Pour motoriser son bolide, HONOR a fait le choix du SoC Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, soit le plus puissant proposé par Qualcomm en cette fin d’année. Il est accompagné de 12 Go de RAM et de 256 ou 512 Go de stockage
Là aussi, on est curieux de voir comment l’appareil gérera la chauffe générée par la puce. Peut-il, comme l’iPhone, accepter un SSD externe afin d’y stocker les séquences filmées en direct ? Cela éviterait de saturer la mémoire interne dont la 4K est particulièrement gourmande…
Côté autonomie, on devrait être comblé, HONOR optant pour une batterie de Si-Ca de 7030 mAh. Reste à savoir si l’on pourra dépasser les deux jours d’utilisation, comme nous l’avons constaté sur l’OPPO Find X10 Pro Max. La charge filaire rapide monte à 100 Watts si l’on utilise le-chargeur-qui-va-bien (et qui n’est pas fourni, comme d’habitude) tandis que l’induction pousse le curseur jusqu’à 80 W.
La magie de l’IA et de la compatibilité Apple
Le Magic 9 Pro Max fonctionne sous MagicOS 11, basé sur Android 17. L’intelligence artificielle prend davantage de place dans l’interface et gagne même un bouton dédié sur la tranche. Gemini, Google Lens et les suggestions liées au contenu affiché à l’écran font partie des outils proposés
Honor annonce aussi une fonction capable de repérer les moments forts d’une vidéo et d’en tirer un montage sous-titré. Elle devrait arriver un peu plus tard grâce à une mise à jour.
Non content de « rendre hommage » au design et au logiciel de l’iPhone, HONOR a l’ambition de le remplacer en lui piquant ses accessoires. La compatibilité avec les AirPods est assurée, tandis que celle avec l’Apple Watch devrait arriver par une prochaine mise à jour. D’après ce que nous avons compris, elle serait dans un premier temps limitée à la réception de notifications provenant d’un Magic 9 Pro Max.
HONOR Connect assure le transfert de fichiers par Airdrop avec n’importe quel appareil d’Apple. Là aussi, on est curieux de voir jusqu’où s’immisce le constructeur dans le monde d’Apple… Et la réaction de celle-ci, généralement assez chatouilleuse dès qu’il s’agit de marcher sur son pré carré (souvenez-vous de FaceTime…)
Prix et disponibilité
HONOR a été à peu près aussi loquace que la Grande Muraille de Chine un jour de fermeture sur la disponibilité et les prix du Magic 9 Pro Max. Nous en déduisons qu’il sera disponible prochainement en France, pour un certain prix. Avec un peu d’audace, on pourrait même s’aventurer à supposer qu’il devrait être accompagné d’offres de lancement irrésistibles. À suivre, donc

articles.title: El Bluetooth va a ser casi cuatro veces más rápido en 2027. Y los auriculares serán los primeros en notarlo
articles.text:
La tecnología Bluetooth promete un gran salto a partir de 2027, y en el sector del audio van a ser los primeros en notar la diferencia. Y es que el Bluetooth Special Interest Group (SIG), la organización que mantiene el estándar, ha adoptado una nueva función llamada High Data Throughput (HDT) como parte de Bluetooth Core 7.0. Esto eleva la velocidad máxima de Bluetooth Low Energy (LE) a 7,5 Mbps, casi cuatro veces el límite actual. Se espera que los productos compatibles comiencen a llegara partir del año que viene. Bajo estas líneas te contamos todos los detalles.
Audio sin pérdidas. Hoy en día, conseguir audio sin compresión o de alta resolución a través de Bluetooth suele implicar depender de tecnologías propietarias como LDAC de Sony o aptX Lossless de Qualcomm, que solo funcionan cuando tanto tu teléfono como tus auriculares son compatibles con la misma. HDT pretende integrar esa capacidad en el propio estándar. Esto podría hacer que el audio inalámbrico premium esté mucho más presente en futuros auriculares, sin depender del códec de ninguna empresa en particular.
Si los fabricantes lo adoptan, que es muy probable, la compatibilidad debería extenderse a una amplia gama de auriculares, altavoces y todo tipo de hardware específico de sonido.
En detalle: El aumento de velocidad proviene de una nueva capa física, la parte del chip de Bluetooth que envía y recibe señales de radio. Tal y como comparte el medio CNET, los nuevos esquemas de modulación permiten que esta capa empaquete más datos en cada transmisión. La tasa actual de 2 Mbps se remonta a Bluetooth 5.0 en 2016. La base de HDT abarca 2, 3 y 4 Mbps, mientras que los 6 y 7,5 Mbps son opcionales, y cualquier dispositivo que sea compatible con 7,5 Mbps también debe admitir los 6 Mbps. Tendremos qué ver a qué tasas podrán alcanzar nuestros dispositivos cuando la función vaya aterrizando.
Entre líneas. Como el sistema en teoría podría mover los mismos datos en menos tiempo, puede pasar más tiempo en modos de bajo consumo, lo que debería traducirse en una mejor eficiencia. El SIG también afirma que HDT está diseñado para mantener las conexiones estables en entornos más exigentes, especialmente importante en lugares abarrotados donde las señales inalámbricas compiten. Además, muchas transmisiones de audio de alta resolución viajan actualmente a través de Wi-Fi, y enviarlas a través de Bluetooth LE podría quitar esa carga en nuestra red doméstica.
Más allá de los auriculares. El SIG espera que los wearables, las gafas de realidad virtual o aumentada, los aparatos para el hogar inteligente y los dispositivos con IA integrada también se beneficien. Damon Barnes, director de marketing técnico del SIG, declaraba a CNET que un reloj inteligente podría sincronizar horas de datos de entrenamiento captados por sus sensores con un teléfono en segundos, y un producto para el hogar inteligente podría finalizar una actualización de firmware con un tiempo de inactividad apenas visible. Oyvind Strom, de Nordic Semiconductor, contaba además a Heise Online que las gafas inteligentes podrían descargar datos para su procesamiento y así ofrecer mejores experiencias de IA.
Qué esperar. No esperes que tus dispositivos actuales mejoren, pues HDT es una parte opcional de Core 7.0, por lo que cada fabricante decide si lo incluye, y los dispositivos existentes no lo obtendrán. Ambos extremos de la conexión deben admitirlo también, pues tanto los teléfonos, como tablets y ordenadores portátiles que se conecten necesitan HDT, no solo los auriculares. De momento, los móviles que incluyan el modem FastConnect 8800 de Qualcomm tendrán soporte para Bluetooth 7 y HDT.

articles.title: Uber permite pedir robotaxis de Amazon en Las Vegas sin costo extra, pero no se pueden elegir
articles.text:
Los usuarios de Uber en Las Vegas pueden recibir desde este lunes un robotaxi de Zoox, la empresa de vehículos autónomos de Amazon. Es la primera vez que Zoox ofrece sus autos a una plataforma de terceros, y la primera vez que Uber suma un vehículo sin volante.
No hay un botón para pedir un Zoox. Quien solicite un UberX, Uber Comfort, Uber Electric, Uber Comfort Electric o Wait & Save puede ser asignado a uno de los vehículos si hay disponibles, según TechCrunch. El viaje no cuesta más que uno con conductor.
Para aumentar la probabilidad, el usuario puede activar los viajes autónomos en las preferencias de viaje dentro de la aplicación. Zoox mantendrá además su propia app en la ciudad.
Los vehículos funcionan solo en zonas turísticas: los hoteles y locales de la avenida principal, el centro y el distrito de las artes, según Zoox. La empresa dijo que sumará más destinos pronto.
Zoox cobra por sus viajes en Las Vegas desde agosto, después de casi un año de viajes gratuitos, señaló el Las Vegas Review-Journal. Desde entonces amplió el servicio al aeropuerto internacional Harry Reid y al centro de la ciudad.
Los robotaxis de Zoox son cabinas de cuatro plazas, con dos asientos de cada lado enfrentados, y avanzan en ambos sentidos. Los pasajeros pueden cargar el teléfono y controlar la temperatura y la música desde pantallas táctiles.
Un acuerdo con MGM para ordenar las recogidas
Las dos compañías anunciaron un acuerdo de varios años con MGM Resorts International, que las convierte en socias oficiales de transporte y robotaxis en sus propiedades de Las Vegas. Trabajarán en mejores puntos de recogida y bajada, señalización y guías dentro de la aplicación.
Zoox también será el socio oficial de transporte del Gran Premio de Las Vegas a partir del año próximo, según el Review-Journal.
Samarth Kejriwal, director global de movilidad autónoma de Uber, dijo que el lanzamiento acerca el transporte autónomo a ser “parte de la vida cotidiana”, según el diario.
Uber diversifica sus socios en robotaxis
Uber tiene alianzas con más de 30 empresas de tecnología autónoma, aunque no todas llegaron a operar comercialmente, según TechCrunch. Zoox va detrás de Waymo y Tesla, líderes del sector. Uber no dará mantenimiento a los vehículos de Zoox en Las Vegas, a diferencia de otros socios.
Este año, la Autoridad de Transporte de Nevada aprobó por unanimidad un permiso para que Uber ponga hasta 1.000 robotaxis en el condado de Clark, donde está Las Vegas, con Zoox y Motional, filial de Hyundai, como socios, según TechCrunch.
El director ejecutivo de Uber, Dara Khosrowshahi, dijo en la llamada de resultados del tercer trimestre que Las Vegas será la primera ciudad de Estados Unidos donde se podrá acceder a dos socios totalmente sin conductor: “Empezaremos con flotas limitadas y ampliaremos la oferta en los próximos meses”. Planea además una opción autónoma dedicada en la aplicación.
La alianza exclusiva con Waymo, que asigna sus robotaxis a usuarios de Uber en Austin y Atlanta, terminará en enero de 2028, según TechCrunch. Waymo planea ofrecer sus viajes por su propia app, como en otras ciudades.
Zoox prevé abrir un servicio comercial en Los Angeles antes de que termine este año con su propia aplicación. Los viajes en esa ciudad por medio de Uber llegarán en 2027.
El desembarco de Zoox en Uber ocurre mientras Las Vegas se consolida como un laboratorio para el transporte autónomo comercial. La coexistencia de aplicaciones propias y servicios integrados permitirá medir cómo responden los pasajeros a distintas modalidades de reserva, tarifas y puntos de ascenso.
Asimismo, la expansión dependerá de la disponibilidad de vehículos, la regulación local y la capacidad de las empresas para operar con seguridad en áreas de alta demanda.

articles.title: Palo Alto Networks report finds organizations struggle to track and secure AI agents in the cloud - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Palo Alto Networks report finds organizations struggle to track and secure AI agents in the cloud
A new report out today from cybersecurity company Palo Alto Networks Inc. finds that artificial intelligence agents have quickly become a fixture in software development, but many organizations can’t properly track or secure what those agents are doing in the cloud.
Now in its sixth year, the State of Cloud Security Report 2026 is based on a survey of 2,800 security executives and practitioners in 10 countries. Along with how AI is being used to build and deploy software, the report looks at how quickly organizations are able to respond when something goes wrong.
The use of AI agents was found to be close to universal, with 99% of respondents saying they use agents for autonomous or semiautonomous actions in their development pipelines. Some 73% said the agents are allowed to modify code, pipeline configurations or production environments, and agents are even doing security testing at 44% of organizations.
The amount of change is going up as a result. Some 82% said AI-driven development has increased the volume of infrastructure updates reaching their cloud, yet organizations on average enforce fewer than three of the eight predeployment security checks measured in the survey. AI is also being used to generate infrastructure-as-code templates at 42% of organizations, but only 34% scan that code before production.
Not surprisingly, problems are getting through. Respondents said that on average, 19% of high and critical application security issues reached production over a 90-day period. It takes an average of 18.4 days to get a fix for a security issue found in code into production.
When respondents were asked what was stopping them from fixing issues before deployment, the most common answer was business pressure to release quickly at 39%. Unclear risk acceptance policies came second at 30%.
Accountability is also an issue when it comes to agents. Two in five organizations said they are unable to reconstruct what an AI agent did, a share that rises to 46% in financial services, while 53% said agent activity is logged under a developer’s identity or personal access token. That means when something goes wrong, investigators first have to figure out which actions were taken by a person and which were taken by an agent before they can work out what was affected.
Removing access once something does go wrong is also slow. Some 60% of organizations still need manual intervention to revoke access for nonhuman identities, and it takes an average of 2.5 days to revoke or rotate compromised developer credentials, API keys or pipeline secrets.
Data governance has its own issues. Nearly all organizations, 99%, said they had found ungoverned AI in their environment in the past year, yet only 9% are able to automatically discover and classify it. Some 40% said governed data had been copied into ungoverned AI tools, and 39% had seen sensitive or regulated data used to train or fine-tune models without authorization.
Despite the gaps, confidence is high. Almost every respondent, 97%, said they are at least somewhat confident they can secure their AI supply chain and applications, though only 36% can monitor AI behavior in production and just 30% can detect prompt injection.
The final section of the report looks at the threat from frontier AI models that can find and exploit software vulnerabilities on their own. Nearly all respondents, 98%, said they are concerned about it, and 65% said it poses a significant or severe threat to global critical infrastructure and financial systems over the next 12 to 18 months. Utilities were the most likely of any sector to rate the threat as significant or severe at 79%, compared with 48% in telecommunications.
Interestingly, though the report refers to “frontier AI-powered capabilities,” the survey questions at the back of it call them “Mythos-grade” threats, a reference to Anthropic PBC’s Claude Mythos models. Palo Alto Networks was one of the launch partners in Anthropic’s Project Glasswing, which gave defenders early access to Claude Mythos Preview in April.
The report argues that against attackers working at machine speed, an 18.4-day fix cycle leaves organizations exposed for more than 17 days after a vulnerability can be discovered. Part of the problem, according to the report, is fragmented tooling, with only 19% of organizations saying they operate with unified telemetry and workflows across code, cloud, identity and runtime. Nearly half of organizations, 47%, still do the work of correlating application vulnerabilities with runtime threats by hand, a number that’s even higher in the U.S. at 55%.
The report ends with a series of recommendations for organizations to secure their cloud environments as AI agents take on more work. Agents should be given their own identities with a clear owner and only the permissions they need to do their job. Security teams are also advised to automate the fixing of recurring issues, though only after rollback procedures have been put in place.

Modelos com taxas de atualização de 100 Hz a 200 Hz e tecnologias de sincronização adaptativa oferecem alternativas para diferentes perfis, desde jogadores casuais até quem prioriza jogos competitivos.
Para ajudar na escolha, o Tecnoblog selecionou 5 monitores por menos de R$ 800, de marcas como AOC, Samsung e LG. Confira as características, vantagens e limitações de cada modelo.
O AOC Agon G50 é uma opção para quem procura um monitor de entrada voltado a jogos competitivos. Ele traz tela IPS de 23,8 polegadas, resolução Full HD (1920 × 1080 pixels) e taxa de atualização nativa de 144 Hz, permitindo exibir movimentos com maior fluidez que monitores de 60 Hz.
O tempo de resposta é de 0,5 ms (MPRT), que pode ser útil em jogos competitivos. O monitor também oferece compatibilidade com Nvidia G-Sync, recurso de sincronização adaptativa que ajuda a reduzir cortes na imagem, além de suporte a HDR10 para contraste mais definido.
Nas conexões, o AOC Agon G50 oferece HDMI e DisplayPort e também conta com saída de áudio, recursos de assistência para jogos e compatibilidade com suportes VESA de 100 × 100 mm.
O que significa o tempo de resposta do monitor? 🎯
O MPRT (Tempo de Resposta da Imagem em Movimento) indica por quanto tempo a imagem permanece visível enquanto está em movimento, o que influencia o desfoque percebido.
O GtG (Cinza para Cinza) mede quanto tempo um pixel leva para mudar de um tom de cinza para outro.
Como medem coisas diferentes, 0,5 ms MPRT e 5 ms GtG não dizem, por si só, qual monitor deixa menos rastros nos jogos.
A taxa de atualização de 200 Hz é o principal diferencial do AOC Agon G42, tornando-o uma alternativa para jogadores que priorizam fluidez em jogos competitivos, como FPS e de corrida. O modelo traz painel IPS de 23,8 polegadas, resolução Full HD e tempo de resposta de 0,3 ms (MPRT).
O monitor também oferece compatibilidade com Nvidia G-Sync e outros recursos como Shadow Control, para ajustar a visibilidade em áreas escuras, modo de baixa latência e suporte a HDR10. O conjunto de conexões inclui uma entrada HDMI 2.0, uma DisplayPort 1.4 e saída de áudio.
O produto também possui suporte VESA de 100 × 100 mm e acompanha cabo DisplayPort. A base, porém, permite apenas ajuste de inclinação, sem regulagem de altura ou rotação.
O Samsung Essential S3 pode atender quem procura um monitor para jogar e realizar atividades cotidianas no mesmo computador. A tela plana de 24 polegadas utiliza painel IPS, resolução Full HD e 120 Hz de taxa de atualização, combinação adequada para jogos, navegação e produtividade.
O painel possui brilho típico de 250 nits e tempo de resposta de 5 ms (GtG). Entre os recursos estão o Game Picture Mode, que disponibiliza configurações de imagem voltadas a jogos, o Eye Saver Mode e a tecnologia Flicker Free.
Em contrapartida, a Samsung informa que o modelo não possui suporte a AMD FreeSync ou Nvidia G-Sync, uma ausência relevante para jogadores que procuram pelo recurso.
A conectividade é composta por duas entradas HDMI 1.4, permitindo conectar dois dispositivos sem trocar fisicamente os cabos. O monitor também possui ajuste de inclinação e compatibilidade com suportes VESA de 100 × 100 mm, mas não oferece regulagem de altura, saída para fones ou alto-falantes integrados.
O LG MS500 também tem uma proposta de uso misto, combinando recursos para jogos casuais com características voltadas a trabalho e estudos. Seu painel IPS de 24 polegadas possui resolução Full HD (1920 × 1080 pixels) e taxa de atualização de 100 Hz.
Essa frequência oferece maior fluidez do que monitores tradicionais de 60 Hz, embora fique abaixo dos 144 e 200 Hz disponíveis nos modelos da linha Agon deste guia. A tecnologia IPS também favorece a visualização em diferentes ângulos.
Entre as especificações estão o tempo de resposta de 5 ms (GtG) e recursos para jogos, como Dynamic Action Sync, voltado à redução do atraso de processamento, Black Stabilizer, que ajusta a visibilidade em cenas escuras, e Crosshair, que adiciona uma mira virtual à tela.
O monitor da LG possui duas entradas HDMI e saída para fones de ouvido, permitindo conectar diferentes equipamentos ao monitor. Também conta com ajuste de inclinação de -5° a 15° e compatibilidade VESA de 75 × 75 mm.
O AOC B35 pode ser interessante para quem busca um monitor gamer compacto. Ele traz painel VA de 21,5 polegadas com resolução Full HD (1920 × 1080 pixels).
A combinação resulta em uma densidade de pixels superior à dos modelos Full HD de 23,8 polegadas deste guia, favorecendo a definição de textos e elementos pequenos em distâncias semelhantes.
Apesar de ser anunciado com taxa de atualização de 120 Hz, o B35 possui frequência nativa de 100 Hz, sendo necessário utilizar overclock para alcançar o máximo pela entrada HDMI. O tempo de resposta é de 1 ms (MPRT), útil em jogos competitivos.
O modelo também oferece Adaptive-Sync, recurso que ajusta a frequência de atualização de acordo com a saída de dispositivos compatíveis. Nas conexões, o produto oferece uma entrada HDMI 1.4 e uma VGA. O monitor também possui tratamento antirreflexo, além de ajuste de inclinação e suporte VESA de 100 × 100 mm.
A escolha do melhor monitor gamer barato depende dos jogos que você costuma jogar, do espaço na mesa e do equipamento que pretende conectar. Verifique o seguinte:
Um monitor Full HD pode funcionar melhor no Xbox Series S, pois os jogos rodam em resolução menor nesse console. É ideal ter uma TV 4K para jogar no PlayStation 5 e Xbox Series X para aproveitar mais detalhes nos jogos que oferecem essa resolução.
Depende do modelo. Alguns monitores atingem a frequência máxima tanto por HDMI quanto por DisplayPort. Em outros, a taxa máxima de Hz só é possível pela HDMI com overclock, enquanto a VGA fica limitada a uma frequência mais baixa em Full HD.
Sim, alguns monitores gamer de entrada têm alto-falantes embutidos, mas o recurso varia de um modelo para outro. O som integrado costuma ser suficiente para ouvir diálogos e sons do jogo.
Mas, se você valoriza graves mais presentes ou quer perceber melhor a direção dos sons, vale considerar um headset avançado ou caixas de som externas.
Monitores gamer QHD são mais caros, por isso ficaram de fora desta seleção. A resolução 2560 × 1440 pixels ajuda a preservar a nitidez da imagem em telas maiores, como as de 27 polegadas. Assim, o preço tende a subir quando o monitor combina essa resolução com uma taxa de atualização alta.
No PC, jogar em QHD também exige mais da placa de vídeo para manter a mesma taxa de quadros. Se a prioridade é economizar e jogar com fluidez em uma tela de 24 polegadas, o Full HD costuma oferecer um bom equilíbrio.

articles.title: Cyber giant Infoblox confirms security incident after hackers access 'company information' | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Cybersecurity and automation giant Infoblox has confirmed a cybersecurity incident, during which hackers accessed company information through one of its technology vendors.
Infoblox is a privately held cyber giant that provides companies cybersecurity and networking services, such as domain name resolution, and identity and user access management.
In a statement, a spokesperson for Infoblox told TechCrunch that the company is “investigating a security event involving unauthorized access to certain company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor.”
“We immediately activated our incident response procedures, took steps to contain the incident and are working with leading outside cybersecurity experts to investigate the facts, understand the scope and address any confirmed risks.”
TechCrunch has learned that the data breach involves a vendor that provides SharePoint data migration services, according to a notification sent by Infoblox about the breach, two people with knowledge of the incident told TechCrunch.
One of the people said sensitive customer data was taken in the breach.
According to public internet records seen by TechCrunch, Infoblox hosts much of its files, emails and infrastructure with Microsoft, including a SharePoint server, which TechCrunch confirmed is accessible through Infoblox’s single sign-on provider. SharePoint is web-based software that companies use to share and host internal files and documents.
Infoblox has not named the third-party migration vendor that was hacked, but one person with knowledge of the incident said that Infoblox has terminated its work with the vendor.
The company’s spokesperson did not comment on this, but added that the company has “no indication that any Infoblox products, cloud services, software updates or build-and-release processes were involved” in the breach.
Infoblox would not say how many customers were affected by the incident, or if the company is aware at this time. The company also did not say, when asked, if it had been contacted by the hackers and if they had made any demands.

articles.title: Intel bets on Classiq acquisition to turn Quantum efforts into commercially viable business — deal positions company as leading vendor of qubit chips, acquisition to close by the first half of 2027
articles.text:
Intel bets on Classiq acquisition to turn Quantum efforts into commercially viable business — deal positions company as leading vendor of qubit chips, acquisition to close by the first half of 2027
Intel becomes a top-to-bottom quantum computing company.
After having spent more than a decade pursuing quantum computing research, Intel is making its first real push at commercializing its efforts. First, with the pending acquisition of quantum computing company Classiq, which has an existing list of enterprise customers. Intel says it'll be the only company that can produce qubit chips and cryogenic control electronics at scale; the deal would give it a complete top-to-bottom hardware-to-software stack, and Intel will also gain the chance to become a leading vendor of quantum computing products. Intel's acquisition of Classiq is expected to complete in the first half of 2027.
The key ingredient of that strategy is the pending acquisition of Classiq, which offers a hardware-agnostic quantum software development platform that enables engineers to design, synthesize, optimize, simulate, and execute quantum algorithms using high-level programming tools and AI-assisted automation, essentially untying software design from the complexity of quantum hardware. Meanwhile, Intel also plans to manufacture quantum processors using specialized versions of its 18A process technology, offer foundry services, and eventually sell complete quantum computers. Although the company expects its quantum business to become profitable, it acknowledges that commercial success will take time.
Intel has spent more than a decade developing quantum computing technologies, including silicon spin-qubit processors, cryogenic control electronics, and software for hybrid quantum-classical computing. However, the company has largely treated these activities as research and development projects rather than an actual business. The acquisition of Classiq, which Intel expects to complete in the first half of 2027, marks a shift toward commercialization as Classiq already has many clients and established revenue streams.
"Up until now […] our quantum computing group for the last ten years was […] purely a research and development project," said Pushkar Ranade, chief technology officer at Intel, during a media briefing. "It was not really viewed as a commercial activity."
Intel's quantum hardware: The journey so far
Intel's quantum computing journey kicked off in 2015 with a research collaboration with QuTech — the quantum research institute of TU Delft and TNO — to develop quantum computing technologies, including silicon spin qubits. The idea was to leverage Intel's extensive expertise in silicon transistor development and its high-volume semiconductor manufacturing infrastructure to produce quantum processors in the same fabs that make conventional CPUs, overcoming the manufacturing scalability challenges alternative quantum computing architectures faced at the time. Intel subsequently developed Horse Ridge, a cryogenic control SoC manufactured using a 22nm process technology in 2020. Three years later, the company introduced Tunnel Falls, a 12-qubit silicon spin processor manufactured on a 300mm wafer.
Intel's quantum computing effort focuses on silicon spin qubits, which use spin states of individual electrons to store and manipulate quantum information. The company chose this approach partly because silicon spin qubits can be manufactured using equipment and processes similar to those employed for conventional semiconductor devices. This compatibility enables Intel to re-use most of its existing manufacturing infrastructure and expertise rather than build dedicated semiconductor fabrication facilities for quantum processors that yet have to become commercial products.
Despite the recent cuts at Intel, the company sustained its quantum computing project. Intel has developed two specialized versions of its 18A manufacturing technology for quantum computing: 18A-Q for silicon spin-qubit processors and 18A-CC for cryogenic control and readout electronics. To define/build 18A-Q, Intel has collaborated with Hitachi, AIST, and NEDO (three major supporters of quantum computing from Japan), and there appears to be a design kit intended to support large quantum computing systems. Without a doubt, 18A-Q and 18A-CC put Intel on the map of quantum computing chips in a big way. A couple of things should be kept in mind, though.
"The underlying device that we use, underlying process that we use to make the actual qubit device is a unique process, but it fits into those design rules," Ranade explained. "We can make these chips […] in the same fab that we use to make our CPUs."
Although Intel 18AQ uses BEOL interconnect geometry and design rules derived from Intel 18A, its underlying qubit devices require a different manufacturing process. According to Ranade, the technology requires a specialized thin-film stack and several additional manufacturing tools. Nevertheless, more than 90% of the manufacturing equipment is identical to that used for conventional semiconductor production, according to Intel.
"Intel 18A-CC, meanwhile, uses 18A-based geometry but requires additional characterization for operation at cryogenic temperatures," Ranade said. "Crucially, Intel can manufacture quantum processors alongside conventional CPUs in existing semiconductor fabs, which could reduce the capital expenditure required to scale production. […] More than 90% of the process equipment is exactly the same."
A major piece in the quantum computing puzzle: Classiq
For conventional x86 architectures and IA-64 (while it was active), Intel has historically offered compilers that made software run better on its hardware (and sometimes on AMD hardware too). By contrast, with its quantum computing efforts, Intel has generally focused on hardware and while it has its own Quantum SDK that includes a compiler, this is not enough in the quantum computing realm as Classiq's offering operates at a higher abstraction level. With the acquisition of Classiq, the company intends to fill that gap.
Classiq develops a hardware-agnostic quantum software platform that applies electronic design automation (EDA) principles to quantum programming, which lets developers design, synthesize, and optimize quantum algorithms without manually constructing circuits from individual quantum gates. The company's software provides high-level modeling, automated algorithm synthesis, optimization, debugging, and execution capabilities across different quantum computing architectures, which somewhat resembles Intel's approach to its x86 compilers, albeit working at a different level.
Intel already has its Quantum SDK, which includes a C++-based compiler, runtime environment, and simulator for hybrid quantum-classical applications. Classiq's platform will sit above these tools and provide an application-development environment for programmers who lack extensive expertise in quantum computing.
Intel compares the potential significance of Classiq's software layer to Microsoft's MS-DOS, which helped establish the personal computer software ecosystem; Nvidia's CUDA, which enabled developers to exploit GPUs for general-purpose accelerated computing; and EDA tools, which abstracted high-level design descriptions from the complexities of transistor-level integrated circuit implementation and essentially set the stage for the multi-billion foundry industry today.
Furthermore, unlike Intel's quantum hardware business, Classiq already has commercial customers and generates revenue. The company employs approximately 130 people and serves more than 50 enterprise customers, including BMW, Comcast, Lufthansa, Rolls-Royce, and Toshiba. It also participates in more than 10 national quantum computing programs and supports over 50 quantum processors and simulators.
As existing quantum processors remain insufficient for many practical applications, companies can develop and optimize software ahead of hardware availability. As a result, these customers primarily use Classiq products to develop quantum algorithms, train engineers, and create intellectual property in preparation for commercially useful quantum computers.
Intel's CTO described Classiq's revenue and anticipated growth as healthy, but did not disclose actual financial figures.
"They have a very healthy revenue this year and a very healthy revenue CAGR over the coming years," Ranade said. "We hope that… we want that to continue."
It is necessary to note that Intel intends to preserve Classiq's hardware-agnostic approach, which means allowing the company to continue supporting quantum processors and simulators from competing vendors. This is essential to maintain Classiq's existing customer relationships and expand its revenue opportunities, as its clients can/will be able to develop quantum applications without committing to a particular hardware architecture. Obviously, Intel can generate software revenue regardless of which quantum computing technologies ultimately become commercially successful.
"We very much want to maintain that hardware-agnostic platform that they have developed to attract more and more customers," Ranade said.
From quantum chips to complete systems
When it comes to quantum computing, Intel's ambitions extend beyond manufacturing silicon spin-qubit processors. The company intends to become a supplier of complete quantum computing systems, which would combine quantum processors, cryogenic control electronics, classical computing resources, and software. For now, Intel has most of the building blocks required to develop complete quantum computing systems, but it still has to demonstrate that it can integrate them into commercially viable quantum computing at scale.
"We want to be in the business of building quantum foundry components, but also complete quantum systems," said Pushkar Ranade, chief technology officer at Intel.
Intel is also considering opportunities to provide quantum foundry services to other hardware developers. While its internal processor development will remain focused on silicon spin qubits, the company is open to manufacturing components for alternative quantum computing technologies, which somewhat resembles its approach to its x86 CPU and foundry businesses.
"We are committed to spin qubits," Ranade said. "But we are also open to providing foundry services to other modalities."
Intel believes that its capabilities in photonics, advanced packaging, and semiconductor manufacturing could become commercially relevant even to companies developing quantum processors based on different physical principles than silicon qubits.
Can quantum computing become profitable?
Intel's decision to expand its quantum computing activities with the takeover of Classiq comes as chief executive Lip-Bu Tan emphasized profitability, financial discipline, and high-margin products across the company’s established businesses. Given that Intel's quantum computing initiative barely generates any revenue, let alone profits, the CEO stance raises questions about the viability of quantum computing for Intel, especially in a situation where the industry has yet to demonstrate widespread practical applications that justify the cost of large-scale quantum hardware.
When asked how Intel’s quantum computing strategy fits Tan's profitability requirements, Ranade explained that the company's immediate financial priorities primarily concern its established client and server processor businesses. Nevertheless, Intel must continue investing in emerging technologies that could shape future computing markets.
"This is really a bet on the future," Ranade said. "This is something we also have to do in addition to our mainstream businesses today."
The Intel CTO acknowledged that quantum computing is not set to become a high-margin business in the near future. Meanwhile, the acquisition of Classiq gives Intel an established commercial software operation and revenue stream here and now, as well as an opportunity to expand customer relationships well before its own quantum processors reach commercial maturity. Intel also hopes that combining its hardware and software capabilities (probably including Classiq) will attract customers interested in complete quantum computing solutions.
When asked whether vertical integration would make Intel's quantum computing operations profitable, Ranade acknowledged that he could not predict gross margins of the quantum computing business because the industry is still in its infancy. Nevertheless, he expressed confidence in the commercial prospects of Intel's quantum hardware and software.
"I expect it to become a profitable business very quickly on the hardware side, but too early to tell," Ranade said.
Quantum computing will remain hybrid
Even though quantum processors evolve at a rapid pace, the technology is unlikely to replace existing CPUs and GPUs for conventional computing any time soon. Instead, Intel expects quantum computing systems to operate alongside the usual processors in data centers and supercomputing environments.
Classiq's software platform will provide high-level quantum algorithm development capabilities, while Intel Quantum SDK will handle compilation, simulation, and hybrid quantum-classical execution. This approach differs from Nvidia's CUDA-Q, which is designed to integrate quantum computing workflows with existing accelerated computing infrastructure. According to Classiq chief executive Nir Minerbi, Classiq operates at a higher level of abstraction and can complement CUDA-Q rather than compete with it.
"CUDA Q is very much low-level; it is gate-level. It is a good platform, by the way, but it is very low-level," said Minerbi. "The reason companies like Rolls-Royce and BMW and others use the Classiq platform on top of CUDA Q is due to the level of abstraction. It is much, much easier to develop quantum programs with Classiq and then to simulate it with CUDA Q rather than only with CUDA Q."
Meanwhile, commercial success of quantum computing still depends on substantial advances in quantum hardware, including qubit scalability, error correction, control electronics, and system integration. For now, many Classiq customers are developing applications for quantum computers that have yet to reach the scale required for commercially valuable workloads.
Summary
Intel expects to complete its acquisition of Classiq in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions. The company has not disclosed the purchase price or other financial terms.
The transaction will bring Classiq's software development capabilities and established customer relationships into Intel's quantum computing organization, but will preserve the platform's compatibility with competing hardware technologies. For Intel, the acquisition represents an opportunity to turn more than a decade of quantum computing research into a commercial business unit as it will have all the building blocks required to create quantum systems. Furthermore, Intel's quantum computing business will be open to third parties in the sense that Intel will be able to build quantum processors for partners using its 18AQ and 18ACC process technologies.
Whether Intel's quantum computing business eventually delivers the high margins Intel seeks will depend not only on Intel's ability to build systems, produce quantum chips for others, or Classiq's software revenue, but also on the industry's ability to develop quantum processors and systems capable of solving real-world problems that people are willing to pay for.
Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Una jueza dejó avanzar la demanda contra Samsung, SK Hynix y Micron por el precio de la memoria RAM
articles.text:
La jueza federal Noël Wise rechazó el 14 de noviembre el pedido de Samsung, SK Hynix y Micron para frenar una demanda colectiva que los acusa de restringir de manera coordinada la oferta de memoria DRAM, la que usan las computadoras y los teléfonos. La decisión no establece que hubo un acuerdo ilegal: solo permite que el caso siga.
Los demandantes son 17 consumidores y pequeñas empresas de cinco estados, según la orden judicial. Medios surcoreanos como Seoul Economic Daily precisan que son 14 consumidores y tres ensambladoras y distribuidoras de computadoras, y que presentaron la demanda en junio.
Sostienen que los tres fabricantes recortaron la producción al mismo tiempo, coordinaron el giro hacia la memoria de alto ancho de banda (HBM, el tipo que necesitan los chips de inteligencia artificial) y abandonaron los formatos DDR3 y DDR4. Según la demanda, la oferta de memoria convencional quedó bloqueada mientras los precios subían casi 700%.
La orden recoge otro dato de la demanda: al tercer trimestre de 2025, las tres empresas concentraban más del 91% de los ingresos mundiales de DRAM. SK Hynix tenía el 33,2%, Samsung el 32,6% y Micron el 25,7%. En su pedido de rechazo, las propias compañías admitieron que el sector es un oligopolio, dominado por pocos actores.
Por qué la jueza no vio una repetición de 2018
Las empresas argumentaron que el caso repetía otro, presentado en 2018, sobre el alza de precios de 2016 a 2018, cuyo rechazo confirmó en 2022 un tribunal de apelaciones. Wise respondió que no es así. Los demandantes, escribió, no buscan volver a discutir aquel episodio y describen conductas distintas.
Entre ellas figuran recortes de producción simultáneos, una reasignación coordinada de la capacidad, la salida paralela de productos, el retiro de equipos usados por parte de Samsung y SK Hynix y controles casi idénticos que cada empresa aplicó a sus clientes. Cada compañía sostuvo que sus decisiones fueron racionales y respondieron a su interés propio.
Para la jueza, el cuadro cambia por los detalles: SK Hynix y Micron iniciaron los recortes más arriesgados, no un único líder del mercado, y las decisiones eran difíciles de revertir si los demás no las seguían. Las empresas tampoco aprovecharon, al menos hasta la demanda, un alza cercana al 700%. Eso distingue este caso del anterior, concluyó.
Los demandados habían citado una frase del juez Posner: en los mercados concentrados, los competidores se vigilan “como halcones”. Wise respondió que lo alegado va más allá de que se vigilen entre sí. Se parece más a halcones que vuelan en formación, escribió, “una actividad que los halcones normalmente no hacen”.
También pesó el historial. Según la demanda que cita la orden, una investigación del Departamento de Justicia llevó a que cuatro empresas se declararan culpables de fijar precios de DRAM, entre ellas Hynix (multa de USD 185 millones) y Samsung (USD 300 millones). Micron participó, pero obtuvo inmunidad por colaborar. Para Wise, esos antecedentes respaldan a los demandantes.
Un fallo preliminar que no declara culpables
La resolución corresponde a la etapa inicial del proceso. Wise precisó que, para avanzar, los demandantes no necesitan demostrar que se descarta toda conducta independiente y lícita: les basta con exponer hechos más compatibles con una acción coordinada que con decisiones separadas. Las empresas pueden seguir defendiéndose y la jueza no resolvió si hubo colusión.
El telón de fondo, según la propia orden, es la caída de la demanda de memoria a fines de 2022 y el auge posterior de la inteligencia artificial, que llevó a los compradores a adquirir memoria en volúmenes que la industria no había visto. La demanda alega que los fabricantes respondieron a ese salto con restricciones de oferta.
Las tres compañías deben presentar su respuesta formal a la demanda antes del 7 de diciembre de 2026. La primera audiencia de gestión del caso quedó fijada para el 12 de enero de 2027, según la orden de la jueza.

articles.title: Après les tirs dans les lycées, le gouvernement interdit la vente de feux d'artifice, on a décortiqué le décret
articles.text:
Après des semaines de tirs de mortiers d'artifice jusque dans les salles de classe, le gouvernement a interdit par décret la vente et l'utilisation de nombreux feux d'artifice. Treize jours de diète pyrotechnique, à l'échelle du pays.
L'interdiction de vente et d'utilisation des mortiers d'artifice et d'une large gamme d'engins pyrotechniques est parue au Journal officiel le dimanche 15 novembre, avec effet immédiat. Signé la veille par le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu, le décret entend désamorcer les violences qui accompagnent la mobilisation lycéenne depuis septembre, et qui ont parfois atteint les salles de cours. Avec les fusées, batteries et pétards, la liste est longue, les exceptions peu nombreuses, et le décret que nous pu consulter mérite quelques explications.
Des mortiers d'artifice jusque dans les salles de classe
Tout est parti du lycée Saint-Exupéry de Créteil, mi-septembre. Puis le manque de professeurs, Parcoursup, et les suppressions d'options sont très vite venus s'ajouter aux revendications qui ont gagné le pays, et les étudiants ont fini par rejoindre le mouvement. Le 30 septembre, 356 lycées subissaient déjà des blocages ou des tentatives de blocage. Sauf qu'en marge des cortèges, une autre bande-son s'est installée, à base de détonations, poubelles en feu, tirs contre les forces de l'ordre. Une proviseure a même été blessée par un tir de mortier, entre autres incidents.
Le pas le plus inquiétant a été franchi à l'intérieur des établissements. À Villeurbanne, des individus encagoulés sont entrés dans le lycée Frédéric-Faÿs et ont tiré des mortiers depuis un étage. À Villefranche-sur-Saône, le lycée Claude-Bernard a fermé ses portes après l'explosion d'un engin pyrotechnique en pleine classe, devant les élèves et leur professeur. La diffusion sur les réseaux sociaux de vidéos d'affrontements est évoquée par le gouvernement pour expliquer la montée des tensions et justifier la prise de certaines décisions.
Matignon s'est d'ailleurs appuyé sur l'article 37 de la Constitution, qui lui donne la main sur tout ce qui ne relève pas de la loi, et a invoqué l'urgence. Le décret n° 2026-1047 veut prévenir les troubles graves à l'ordre public lors des blocages devant les lycées et les universités, mais aussi pendant les manifestations. Il s'applique partout en France jusqu'au 27 novembre inclus, ce qui couvre la journée de mobilisation nationale de ce mardi 17 novembre.
Feux d'artifice interdits : ce que dit (et ne dit pas) le décret
Pour comprendre ce que vise le décret, un détour par la réglementation s'impose. En France, comme partout dans l'Union européenne, les feux d'artifice sont rangés en catégories selon leur niveau de risque. La F1 regroupe les articles les plus inoffensifs. Les F2 et F3 désignent des produits plus puissants, réservés à un usage en extérieur avec des distances de sécurité qui augmentent d'une catégorie à l'autre.
C'est dans ces deux catégories, F2 et F3, que le gouvernement a établi sa liste noire de quatorze types d'articles. On y trouve les fusées, les batteries, les chandelles romaines, plusieurs familles de pétards et, surtout, les « pots à feu en mortier ». Ces tubes, conçus pour projeter une charge vers le ciel, sont au cœur des incidents de ces dernières semaines. Enfin, le texte interdit leur vente, sans distinguer la boutique du commerce en ligne.
Tout ce qui ne figure pas dans cette liste reste autorisé, à commencer par les articles F1, à très faible risque, comme les cierges magiques. La catégorie F4, qui nécessite de détenir un certificat de qualification artificier, était déjà réservée aux professionnels, donc elle n'est pas concernée par le décret pris par le gouvernement. Ces derniers peuvent d'ailleurs continuer à travailler s'ils disposent des agréments requis, tout comme les collectivités publiques. Les spectacles pyrotechniques encadrés restent possibles.
Mais il reste quelques zones grises. Le décret interdit la vente et l'usage, mais pas la détention. Donc les stocks achetés avant le 15 novembre restent hors du champ du texte. Ce dernier ne prévoit pas non plus de sanction propre. Tirer sur quelqu'un ou dans un lycée relève toutefois déjà du droit pénal, bien plus sévère. Nous verrons désormais si ces treize jours de sevrage suffiront à faire retomber la fièvre.

articles.title: Making a typo when trying to access AI could land you on a malware site
articles.text:
Making a typo when trying to access AI could land you on a malware site
Popular AI brands abused in a new typosquatting campaign
- Attackers registered hundreds of typo-squatted domains impersonating popular AI brands such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Perplexity
- Victims who mistyped URLs were redirected to malware, malicious browser extensions, or ClickFix-style attacks
- Researchers warn the campaign remains active, making bookmarks and careful URL verification essential defenses
Be careful when typing your favorite AI tool’s website into the address bar - one mistake and you might end up with malware on your computer.
This is the warning given out by security researchers Island, who recently uncovered a large-scale domain squatting campaign spoofing popular AI brands.
Users who want to open ChatGPT or Claude might misspell the name and end up on sites like chtgpt.com or cluade.ai. In a perfect world, these websites would return a 404 error (page not found) or would at least automatically redirect the visitor to the legitimate website. But we don’t live in a perfect world, but rather in one filled with malicious actors looking to benefit from even the tiniest of mistakes.
Benefitting from mistakes
In its report, Island said it found 186 typo-squatted domains impersonating 27 popular AI brands, among which are your usual household names - ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Midjourney, and Cursor.
What threat actors did, Island claims, is purchase 186 of these slightly erroneous domains and create websites which, depending on the visitor’s location, operating system and browser, would redirect them to different destinations. On these destinations, one of three things could happen: the victims would be shown a fake Cloudflare verification page, a fake security-check page, or instructions to download various browser extensions.
All three scenarios are malicious. The first one is a typical click-fix attack that instructs Windows users to copy and execute malicious PowerShell commands. These downloaded and executed additional scripts from attacker-controlled infrastructure but unfortunately, Island does not say what the final payload is or what it does.
The fake security-check pages offered a seemingly legitimate, Microsoft Store-signed application called Net Guard, which is actually able to hijack the victim’s browser. This one is particularly worrisome, since it was signed and distributed through a package matching the legitimate Microsoft Store listing, and could change default search engines, modify browser profiles, install extensions and execute JavaScript remotely.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The third attack instructed victims to download malicious extensions that hijacked their default search engine, which allows the attackers to generate profits through monetized searches, or by selling harvested search engine queries.
Are the domains still active?
Island says ChatGPT was the most popular company to spoof, with 25 identified lookalikes. It is followed by Claude (18 typosquatted domains), DeepSeek (16), and Runway (12). Perplexity, Lovable and Character.ai all have 11 each, it added.
It is worth mentioning that this was likely not done by a single actor, but rather numerous ones all using the same technique to target their victims. Also, Island stressed that the campaign likely extended beyond AI services - after examining shared infrastructure, the researchers connected the operation to 211 entry domains, including lookalikes of banks, insurers, telecom companies and enterprise software providers.
Security researchers usually publish these reports after helping minimize the risk which, in this case, would be seeing the domains seized and the malicious websites brought offline.
However, Island’s report does not discuss any takedowns, so it is safe to assume at least some of these domains are still active today. As a rule of thumb, make sure to carefully review the domain typed into the address bar before navigating anywhere. Alternatively, bookmarking your favorite tools is a good option, as well.
Malicious browser extensions did not get the same treatment, though. Of the 30 identified ones, 13 have already been removed from the Chrome Web Store, while 17 remained listed as of November 3, 2026. If not already, we can expect them to be removed in the coming days and weeks.
