articles.title: 80 dueños de Tesla se enfrentan a dos años de cárcel por activar ilegalmente el FSD
articles.text:
80 personas han sido detenidas en Corea del Sur. El motivo: llegar donde Tesla no ha llegado. Ilegalmente, claro. Porque 80 dueños de coches de la marca estadounidense habrían activado ilegalmente el sistema Full Self Driving (FSD, por sus siglas en inglés) en sus coches. Un sistema que, al menos de momento, no está permitido utilizar en el país.
¿Qué ha pasado? Cuentan nuestros compañeros de Motorpasión que 80 conductores de Tesla han sido detenidos por utilizar el FSD, el sistema más avanzado de ayuda a la conducción de la marca, en sus coches. El problema es que este sistema es ilegal en el país y no ha obtenido el visto bueno de los reguladores para ser utilizado. O no, al menos, para todos los coches.
El FSD. El FSD es el sistema de ayuda a la conducción más avanzado de Tesla. Éste permite seleccionar un destino y que el coche nos lleve de forma autónoma, sin tener que poner las manos en el volante o pisar los pedales. El sistema también está activo en zonas urbanas pero obliga siempre a prestar atención a lo que ocurre alrededor y estar en alerta para poder tomar el mando en cualquier momento.
Desde hace meses, la Unión Europea está estudiando su aceptación en los países miembros pero algunos de ellos están reflejando dudas sobre su seguridad o quieren obligar a Tesla a que quite la opción para que el coche se salte los límites de seguridad automáticamente. De momento y por muchos rumores que se han publicado, el FSD sigue sin estar activo en la Unión Europea.
Made in... La clave de todo este lío está en dónde se produjeron estos coches. Realmente, Corea del Sur sí permite utilizar el sistema FSD de Tesla pero de sólo en aquellos coches que han sido fabricados en Estados Unidos y, por tanto, se han importado desde el país. Según cálculos de la empresa de investigación de mercado automotriz Carisyou Data Lab recogidos por los medios locales, estaríamos hablando de alrededor del 20% de los Tesla vendidos en el país.
Y es que en Corea del Sur hay contabilizados alrededor de 229.000 Tesla, sin embargo, sólo algo más de 47.000 unidades pueden utilizar este sistema. Estos son los Tesla Model S y X importados desde Estados Unidos, los Tesla Model 3 y Model Y salidos de las fábricas chinas y europeas quedan fuera de esta aprobación.
¿Qué han hecho? Para poder utilizar este sistema, a los detenidos se les acusa de haber hackeado el coche con dispositivos que permitían desbloquear estas funciones avanzadas de ayuda a la conducción. Con ellas podían circular con todas las ventajas del sistema y, por tanto, ceder el control al vehículo por completo incluso en áreas residenciales.
Señalan en InsideEVs que la mayoría de los conductores habrían comprado los dispositivos para romper el sistema de seguridad de Tesla pero que algunos de ellos, siguiendo tutoriales en GitHub, habrían conseguido crear sus propios dispositivos y desbloquear estas funciones.
¿Es un riesgo? Por su puesto. Y es que romper el sistema de seguridad de Tesla y utilizarlo como si se hubiera pagado por él legalmente puede provocar errores en el reconocimiento que el vehículo hace del entorno. Esto es clave porque dependiendo del tráfico y de elementos como los peatones o la luz de los semáforos, el coche actúa de una u otra manera.
¿A qué se enfrentan? Ahora, según el medio local Korea JoongAng Daily, los conductores ahora se enfrentan a una pena de cárcel de dos años y una multa de unos 14.000 euros (20 millones de wones). Además, las autoridades ya han señalado que se mantienen activas para encontrar más infractores por lo que las detenciones no podrían haber quedado aquí.

articles.title: Exaforce's ExaU lets security staff spin up a personal team of AI agents - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exaforce’s ExaU lets security staff spin up a personal team of AI agents
Agentic security operations startup Exaforce Inc. today announced the launch of ExaU, a service that lets any security staff member spin up a personal team of artificial intelligence agents.
The new service seeks to move past the first wave of AI agents in security, which Exaforce says were built to offload a single task such as alert triage, risk assessment or penetration testing.
Exaforce argues that as AI absorbs more of the routine work, security staff are now responsible for outcomes that cannot be handed off one task at a time. Added to the mix is that staff are also facing a backlog of tasks, such as checks they mean to run, questions they plan to chase down and briefings owed to senior management.
Leading the list of ExaU features is the ability to create an agent by describing the job in plain language, down to the way a practitioner wants it done. Templates are also available. Each agent is designed to retain decisions, exceptions and past instructions.
To use, a security staff member begins by telling an agent what they are responsible for. The agent then works out what needs doing next and when. The response includes discoveries, questions and recommendations.
The new service also supports sharing agents across a security organization. A chief information security officer’s briefing agent can gather status from the agents used by every team. Exaforce’s own example has a finding setting off a threat hunt, an activity audit and outreach to an employee at the same time. A single assessment then pulls the results of all three together.
Everything runs inside Exaforce on the customer’s own data. With connections to identity providers, cloud services and security telemetry already part of the platform, there are no tokens to mint for ExaU agents. The company’s real-time security knowledge graph is claimed to give each agent an understanding of how systems relate from its first task.
Investigations are carried out by the agents on their own. Under the controls built into ExaU, any action affecting employees, systems or communications requires approval first. Recorded in the Exaforce audit log, every step an agent takes can be reviewed later.
Exabots, the agents Exaforce manages itself, already handle threat detection, alert triage and investigation for every customer on the platform. ExaU is pitched as a complement to that standing workforce. Available now as part of the Exaforce platform, the release follows the September launch of Exaforce AI Security, a kill switch for AI agents that go rogue.
HarbourVest Partners, Peak XV Partners, Mayfield Fund, Khosla Ventures and Seligman Ventures were among the investors in Exaforce’s $125 million Series B round in May. Including that round, total funding since the company’s 2023 founding comes to $200 million.

articles.title: Faire tourner le vrai Windows 11 sur un iPhone Duo : Google réussit l’exploit grâce à son IA Gemini 4 Carbon
articles.text:
Windows 11 sur iPhone Duo : un cadre de Google l’a fait sans jailbreak avec l’aide de Gemini 4
Un responsable de Google a réussi à faire tourner Windows 11 localement sur l’iPhone Duo. Une prouesse rendue possible grâce à un allié de taille, l’intelligence artificielle la plus puissante de la firme américaine : Gemini 4 Carbon.
Sorti en octobre dernier, l’iPhone Duo attire déjà les expérimentations les plus audacieuses. Ammaar Reshi, responsable produit et design chez Google AI Studio, vient ainsi de démontrer qu’il est possible d’exécuter la véritable version ARM64 de Windows 11 sur le smartphone pliable d’Apple. Pour relever ce défi technique sans recourir au jailbreak, il s’est appuyé sur Gemini 4 Carbon, donnant au passage naissance au projet open source “WindowsiOS”.
L’iPhone Duo devient un véritable mini-ordinateur portable sous Windows 11
Pour arriver à faire tourner Windows 11 sur l’iPhone Duo, Ammaar Reshi a dû faire face à deux contraintes : les restrictions d’Apple liées à la virtualisation sous iOS et la lenteur de l’émulation logicielle classique. Afin de contourner tout cela, il a conçu une application iOS dédiée reposant sur un moteur de traduction binaire en temps réel pour adapter directement les instructions ARM64 de Windows à la puce de l’iPhone. Le développeur a également créé des composants matériels virtuels pour que Windows reconnaisse les haut-parleurs, le microphone ou encore le réseau mobile.
Une fois l’iPhone Duo plié à la manière d’un ordinateur portable, l’illusion est saisissante : l’interface de Windows 11 24H2 s’affiche sur la moitié supérieure de l’écran interne, tandis que la partie inférieure se transforme en clavier tactile et en trackpad. Une fois l’appareil refermé, l’écran externe offre quant à lui une utilisation 100 % tactile, à l’instar d’une Surface.
I used Gemini 4 Carbon to get Windows 11 running on my iPhone Duo! 💻
Unfold the screen and it's a pocket PC, including Antigravity running coding agents on my phone.
This is the actual desktop ARM OS running locally with touch controls. 
Demo + repo below! pic.twitter.com/LVdeqvvOU1
— Ammaar Reshi (@ammaar) November 11, 2026
Selon le responsable de Google, l’ensemble tourne à des vitesses “quasi natives”. Dans sa démonstration publiée sur X, il fait fonctionner l’OS sans problème, naviguant sur Microsoft Edge et exécutant des agents de code via Google Antigravity. Le système prend même en charge Prism, la couche d’émulation de Microsoft permettant d’utiliser des applications x86 et x64 sur une architecture ARM.
Pensé comme une vitrine des capacités de Gemini 4 Carbon, le code du projet est accessible sur GitHub. L’installation demeure toutefois réservée aux utilisateurs avertis. Faire fonctionner Windows 11 sur l’iPhone Duo nécessite en effet de disposer d’un Mac Apple Silicon, d’outils de développement ainsi que d’une image Windows 11 ARM64, le tout au prix d’une configuration complexe et sans garantie de stabilité.

articles.title: Critics raise competition, affordability concerns over Quebcor-Telus merger
articles.text:
Comments are coming out from key figures across the country following reports of a proposed merger between Quebecor and Telus.
For context, Montreal-based Quebecor, which owns the telecom brands Videotron, Fizz, and Freedom Mobile, sent Telus a proposal to purchase the company in a cash-and-stock deal valued at $19.45 per share, or $31 billion.
Quebecor initially proposed the merger in June 2026, and sent a revised proposal to the company on Nov. 9.
In a statement issued by the Canadian Government on Monday, Industry Minister Melanie Joly said that the government has “taken note” of Quebecor’s proposal to Telus, and that “the transaction will be independently and rigorously reviewed by the Competition Bureau and the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission and will follow regulatory processes under the Telecommunications Act.”
“We will not predetermine the outcomes of the reviews related to this or any other specific transaction,” Joly added in the statement.
There is also considerable doubt about the proposal. Scotiabank analyst Maher Yagi spoke to BNN Bloomberg and noted that a potential deal would face significant obstacles, including the previously mentioned CRTC, Competition Bureau, and Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED), as well as additional reviews or approvals that might be required “given the strategic nature of Canadian telecommunications infrastructure.”
Alongside this, Michael Phillips, the President of United Steelworkers Local 1944 (UNW1944), the largest representative for Telus employees, said that it “seems doubtful whether it would get approved by [the federal government] at this point,” pointing to the federal government’s priority of “keeping the industry competitive and affordable.”
Yagi also made a similar point to BNN Bloomberg, adding that this merger would “undo the competitive structure regulators set up when they required Freedom to be divested as part of the Rogers-Shaw approval.”
Phillips also noted that his biggest worry with the deal was instability, adding that “our members at this point are tending to want stability and security at Telus after many years of industry downsizing, and this is another thing for them to wonder about.”
UNW 1944 represented workers affected by Rogers’ lockout of Shaw employees and added that “we had never had a dispute in the many years that Shaw was running the operation, but we have to attribute some of the instability to the new management post-merger.” For context, UNW 1494 also represented Rogers workers who went on strike in Abbotsford, BC.
Canada already has some of the most expensive phone plans in the world. We should be breaking up the telecom monopolies, not adding another.
The Competition Bureau must block this sale.
www.cbc.ca/news/busines…
— Avi Lewis (@avilewis.ca) November 16, 2026 at 1:49 PM
Federal NDP leader Avi Lewis said in a post to Bluesky that Canada already has “some of the most expensive phone plans in the world,” while adding that “we should be breaking up the telecom monopolies, not adding another.”
Phillips also noted something similar, adding that “consumers have made it clear that they are looking for choice, and they’re looking for affordability.”

articles.title: All the questions Nvidia should answer on Tuesday — but probably won’t | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Nvidia interim CEO and long-time CFO Colette Kress is about to have one of the biggest days of her career on Tuesday when the company reports its third-quarter results.
For the first time, Kress will be running through the numbers and sharing guidance without Nvidia’s charismatic but now-disgraced founder Jensen Huang.
Huang was forced to resign last week after he admitted to having an affair with an exec of a customer, Alice Huang, a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy, and he was accused of having two more affairs with Nvidia employees.
Now, the company is facing questions about its restricted chips allegedly being smuggled into China, especially by Huang’s mistress’s company. Nvidia promised to conduct an internal investigation. Meanwhile, Huang was commanded to answer questions to Congress in a closed-door joint session with three Republican-led committees. Plus, top Democrats have also vowed to investigate the company.
Given the turmoil Nvidia is in, there are a number of questions that Kress should answer.
Huang’s role now and going forward. Huang ran Nvidia with an iron fist, having some 60 direct reports and his fingers in everything. No one knows the company better than him.
An internet petition signed by 180,000 and growing is calling for the board to reinstate him. Huang may also have been mounting an attempt to return, the Financial Times reported. However, CNBC is reporting, citing unnamed sources, that the company is not in talks to reinstate Huang.
So, we’ll be looking for language from the interim CEO about Huang’s ongoing involvement with the company, its search for a new CEO and any talks to bring him back.
China and Singapore. As Huang vehemently argued in favor of easing export restrictions for Nvidia chips to China, Huang said that he’s seen no evidence that its powerful semiconductors were being diverted from legit buyers to China.
But in October 2025, The New York Times reported that the U.S. was investigating Huang’s mistress’s company, Megaspeed, over allegations it was doing just that. Nvidia at the time vouched to CNBC that Megaspeed was legally using the chips for its cloud. However, Nvidia recently told The Wall Street Journal that it had voluntarily blocked Megaspeed from receiving more chips way back in June 2025.
Last year, Nvidia said that Singapore, the region where Megaspeed was located, was one of its fastest-growing, accounting for 22% of its total revenue for its second quarter of that year. After the investigation into Megaspeed came to light, Nvidia changed how it reported revenue. It now reports based on a company’s headquarters, instead of its shipping address. That completely hid sales to Singapore and Megaspeed’s impact.
So we’re listening to what Kress says about the future of sales to the China region and the cloud business in Singapore that was once 20% of sales. We’re especially listening for what she says about Nvidia keeping track of where its restricted chips wind up.
China sales policy. Huang’s argument was, essentially, that the U.S. can’t stop China from developing advanced AI models, so the West is better off selling them less powerful Nvidia chips and keeping them dependent, he said on the Dwarkesh Podcast last summer. Notably, that’s a position that would make Nvidia a lot of money.
The China hawks counter that selling an adversary any powerful chips at all will help them, and U.S. companies shouldn’t do that. So we’re listening for any indications that Kress is reversing Nvidia’s goals with China.
Bankrolling the AI build-out. The expectation is that Kress, the CFO who reportedly had unsuccessfully tried to push back against Huang’s extreme AI dealmaking, will be conservative on such deals going forward. We’ll be listening for what she says about the impacts of existing deals on the books. (Will she subtly try to throw Huang under the bus for those controversial deals?) We’ll also be listening for her future plans.
Governance. With the ousting of Huang and more fallout sure still to come, has the board learned its lesson about too much power in the hands of one person? We’ll be listening for information about how Nvidia might restructure itself.

articles.title: UAE's Vision Makers secures $4 million in a dual round
articles.text:
UAE's Vision Makers secures $4 million in a dual round
- Dubai-based Web3 startup Vision Makers has secured $4 million in cumulative funding across pre-seed and seed rounds, with its latest financing completed at a $20 million valuation. Investors include MH Ventures, Castrum Capital, Titans Ventures, Archer Capital, M2M Capital and Mira Capital.
- Founded in 2023 by Paul Farhi, Vision Makers develops a platform combining cryptocurrency research, blockchain data analysis, token discovery, market intelligence and decentralised trading tools.
- The funding will support platform development, product integration, technology infrastructure and improvements to its market intelligence and trading capabilities. Vision Makers has also secured a listing for its AI Hub in the Telegram Apps Center.
Press release:
Dubai-based Web3 startup Vision Makers has raised a cumulative $4 million across its pre-seed and seed funding rounds, with its latest financing completed at a valuation of $20 million.
The company named 11 investors across the rounds, including MH Ventures, Castrum Capital, Titans Ventures, Archer Capital, M2M Capital, Gemhead Capital, MYR Venture, AITECH Cloud Network, Block Rise, Zerone Ventures and Mira Capital.
Founded in 2023 by Paul Farhi, Vision Makers develops a platform that brings together cryptocurrency research, market intelligence, token discovery, blockchain analytics and decentralised trading tools. The company aims to reduce the need for users to navigate multiple services when researching and trading digital assets.
Its platform includes conversational AI-powered research tools that help users analyse market information, identify digital assets and access trading functions. Vision Makers has also launched an AI Hub, listed in the Telegram Apps Center, featuring AI agents, simulations, digital items and marketplace functionality.
The company said it has surpassed 600,000 registered users across its ecosystem, with more than 110,000 marketplace transactions completed and over 14,000 listings created. It also reported more than 30,000 active users during a 30-day period, although it did not specify the dates covered.
The funding will support further platform development, improvements to user experience and deeper integration across its existing products. Vision Makers also plans to strengthen its technology infrastructure, market intelligence capabilities and trading tools.
The company did not disclose how the $4 million was divided between its pre-seed and seed rounds or the amount raised in its most recent financing.

articles.title: Meta dijo que no obedecerá una orden de Canadá que debilite el cifrado de WhatsApp
articles.text:
Meta afirmó que se negará a cumplir cualquier orden del gobierno de Canadá que la obligue a debilitar el cifrado de sus servicios, entre ellos WhatsApp. La empresa lo dijo antes de declarar ante el Senado canadiense, que examina el proyecto de ley C-22 sobre el acceso de la policía a datos de usuarios.
Rachel Curran, jefa de política pública de Meta Canadá, dijo al diario The Globe and Mail que, si recibe una orden así, la compañía evaluará todas sus opciones. “No vamos a debilitar ni a romper nuestros sistemas. Es una línea roja para nosotros”, afirmó. El cifrado de extremo a extremo impide que alguien, salvo quien envía y quien recibe, lea un mensaje.
Curran recordó que Apple retiró de Reino Unido su servicio de cifrado avanzado para copias en la nube cuando recibió una orden parecida del gobierno británico. Meta, añadió, ya bloqueó las noticias en Facebook e Instagram en Canadá en 2023 para quedar fuera de otra ley del país.
La ley permite órdenes secretas y guardar datos medio año
El proyecto C-22 obligaría a los proveedores de servicios electrónicos, incluidas las aplicaciones de mensajes, a modificar sus sistemas cuando el gobierno lo pida, para dar capacidad de vigilancia a la policía y al Servicio Canadiense de Inteligencia de Seguridad. El ministro de Seguridad Pública podría emitir órdenes que las empresas deberían mantener en secreto.
La ley también exigiría conservar metadatos de los clientes durante un máximo de seis meses. Una enmienda redujo ese plazo desde 12 meses. Los metadatos no incluyen correos, historial de navegación, redes sociales ni mensajes de texto, pero sí pueden mostrar qué números telefónicos se comunicaron entre sí y la ubicación de una persona.
Curran dijo que Meta no recopila hoy esa información y que obligarla a hacerlo crearía “una base de datos de vigilancia prospectiva que trata a todos los canadienses como posibles delincuentes”. También sostuvo que es “el peor momento” para pedir que se debiliten sistemas seguros, por el aumento de intentos de hackeo, muchos con ayuda de IA.
El gobierno niega que exija puertas traseras
Simon Lafortune, vocero del ministro de Seguridad Pública, Gary Anandasangree, respondió que el proyecto no autoriza una vigilancia indiscriminada ni obliga a crear vulnerabilidades en los sistemas, las llamadas puertas traseras. Según Lafortune, una enmienda establece que ninguna obligación de la ley exige descifrar información protegida de extremo a extremo. Su oficina dijo estar abierta a más cambios.
Google considera insuficiente esa enmienda. En una nota enviada a los senadores en octubre, advirtió que el texto permitiría crear una “nueva infraestructura de vigilancia” y exigir la retención masiva de datos. En junio ya había dicho que los cambios aprobados en comisión no resolvían muchos de los problemas centrales.
Apple tampoco los acepta. En mayo, Erik Neuenchwander, su director sénior de privacidad de usuarios, dijo ante un comité de la Cámara de los Comunes que no conoce una forma de aplicar cifrado que dé acceso solo a los buenos sin abrir un camino a los malos. “Cuando se construye una puerta trasera, cualquiera puede cruzarla”, afirmó.
Signal, la aplicación de mensajes cifrados, dijo en mayo que se retiraría de Canadá si le pidieran comprometer la privacidad de sus usuarios. En octubre de 2026, su vicepresidente de estrategia, Udbhav Tiwari, señaló que las enmiendas de junio no bastaban para que cambiara esa decisión.
Meta, Signal y Tailscale declaran ante el Senado
Según Bloomberg Law, ejecutivos de Meta, Apple y Alphabet, matriz de Google, hacen una ofensiva de último momento en Ottawa para reescribir el proyecto antes de que se apruebe. La audiencia del Senado, de la que participan Meta, Signal y Tailscale, es clave para definir la forma final de la ley.
Curran y Tiwari declaran ante el comité de Seguridad Nacional del Senado el 16 de noviembre. Curran dijo que el gobierno de Estados Unidos también está preocupado, porque una orden de Canadá podría debilitar la seguridad de usuarios estadounidenses.

articles.text:

Obviando los robots aspiradores (que lo hacen casi todo solos), un buen aspirador en seco y húmedo nos puede venir genial, especialmente en hogares con mascotas y niños. Y precisamente ahora que estamos en Black Friday prácticamente, ha llegado la mejor oferta del Dreame T16 Pro Steam: es uno de los mejores que hay y su precio ha caído hasta los 529 euros.

Un aspirador eficaz hasta con las manchas más rebeldes
Este dispositivo de Dreame llegó a las tiendas en España en septiembre y, aunque ya ha tenido una pequeña rebaja en alguna ocasión, no tan grande como los 120 euros de descuento que tiene ahora mismo. Otro punto interesante de este aspirador Dreame es que tiene un diseño reclinable de 180 grados, por lo que se puede pasar bajo muebles y camas sin dificultad. Para terminar, su batería ofrece una autonomía de hasta 70 minutos por carga y cuenta con un sistema que combina también vapor y agua para limpiar tanto el cepillo como la base, evitando así posibles malos olores.

articles.title: Avec l'Ultimate Multi-drink, SodaStream réinvente sa machine à soda avec un distributeur sans bouteille
articles.text:
Avec sa nouvelle machine à gazéifier l'eau Ultimate Multi-Drink, SodaStream opère un changement de taille et supprime les bouteilles en faveur d'un format distributeur à servir directement dans le verre, à l'image de ceux que l'on peut voir dans les fast-foods. À la maison comme au resto ? C'est en tout cas la promesse de l’appareil.
On connaissait SodaStream pour ses appareils permettant de gazéifier l'eau directement en bouteille, mais la dernière machine de la marque, l'Ultimate Multi-Drink, mise en vente à 190 €, met fin au débat entre plastique et verre.
Alors que les machines SodaStream fonctionnent habituellement avec des bouteilles à fixer au goulot de la machine, cet appareil privilégie un service de type distributeur au verre, ou dans l'autre contenant de votre choix. Changement de style, donc, pour un tarif revu à la hausse, les (nombreuses) références de la marque coûtant habituellement entre 90 et 140 €.
SodaStream nous avait habitués à des appareils faciles à caser sur un plan de travail. Ici, nous voici face à un bloc noir de 4,5 kg et 43 cm de hauteur, 37 cm de profondeur et 19 cm de largeur ; des dimensions qui font davantage penser à celles d'une machine à café avec broyeur. À titre de comparaison, s'il est aussi haut que l'Ultimate, le modèle Terra, par exemple, fait 19,5 cm de profondeur et 13 cm de largeur.
L'ensemble jouit d’un design sobre et élégant pouvant s'intégrer aussi bien dans une cuisine ouverte qu'un bureau, avec un poids relativement contenu. Il faut dire que SodaStream a opté pour une finition entièrement en plastique, même au niveau du distributeur qui imite seulement le métal argenté. Le support dédié au verre est simplement posé et non fixé, tandis que la réserve d'eau est simplement calée sur son socle. L'ensemble peut certes être déplacé aisément, mais on peut craindre que ses éléments ne se cassent au fil du temps (ou pire, se perdent dans le cas du support pour verres).
Au déballage, on trouve aussi un cylindre de CO2 et deux bouchons flavor connect équipés d'une paille, permettant de raccorder des bouteilles d'arôme à la machine.
L'Ultimate Multi-Drink est donc un véritable distributeur avec, sur sa face avant, un bac d'égouttage à plusieurs niveaux permettant de poser son verre (ou autre contenant) à trois hauteurs différentes. On identifie également un distributeur au centre, comprenant le bouton d'activation sur le dessus, et un curseur à déplacer pour régler l'arôme des boissons.
Enfin, deux boutons en haut à gauche permettent de déterminer le volume des boissons (S : 236 ml, M : 473 ml, L : 710 ml) et le niveau des bulles (léger, moyen ou fort). Attention, ils sont accompagnés de témoins lumineux signalant le choix opéré : les leds émettent une faible luminosité, et sont peu lisibles dans un environnement bien éclairé.
Toujours sur l'avant, à droite de l'appareil se trouve le compartiment prévu pour les bouteilles d'arôme. Pour parfumer les boissons, ces dernières (vendues séparément) sont à équiper du bouchon avec paille, puis à fixer au compartiment par le haut. Il faut ensuite tourner l'ensemble afin que l'embout se bloque au niveau du distributeur. Le voyant d'arôme, symbolisé par un quartier d'agrume, s'allume lorsque la bouteille est enclenchée.
Attention, le bouchon distributeur est lui-même doté d'un petit capuchon qu'il ne faut pas retirer, sous peine d'empêcher le raccordement à la bouteille d'arôme.
À l'arrière de l'appareil, du côté gauche, se trouve la trappe abritant le cylindre de CO2, à placer par le bas après avoir relevé la poignée de verrouillage. Le bouton de réglage du niveau de gazéification s'allume en blanc lorsque le cylindre est installé et prêt à l'emploi. Il s'allume en orange lorsqu'il est absent ou vide.
À droite trône une autre nouveauté : le réservoir à eau amovible, à remplir avec de l'eau fraîche. D'une contenance de 1,4 l (soit plus que les bouteilles de 1 l des précédents modèles), il autorise le service de deux boissons de taille L ou six de taille S. Grâce à ses dimensions assez compactes (28,5 cm de hauteur, 14 cm de profondeur et 7,3 cm de largeur), on peut le glisser dans la porte du réfrigérateur. Lorsqu'il est en place et plein, le bouton de réglage du volume de boisson s'allume en blanc ; s'il n'est pas installé ou vide, il s'allume en orange.
Enfin, l'appareil est livré avec des fiches à broches à fixer à l'adaptateur secteur, correspondant aux diverses prises existantes dans le monde, nous donnant au passage l'avantage de pouvoir voyager avec sa machine.
Après quelques manipulations détaillées dans le mode d'emploi pour lancer un premier cycle de rinçage et amorcer la bouteille d'arôme lors de sa première utilisation, la SodaStream Ultimate Multi-Drink est prête à remplir sa mission… et votre godet.
Pour se servir un verre, il faut choisir sa contenance et son niveau de gaz à l'aide des boutons en haut à gauche de l'appareil.
Si l'on veut uniquement de l'eau pétillante, il suffit de laisser le bouton du niveau d'intensité de saveur sur 0 et appuyer sur le dessus pour lancer la distribution. La boisson coule selon la taille sélectionnée, mais si l'on souhaite arrêter la machine avant la fin du cycle (par exemple, lorsque nous nous sommes rendu compte que nous avions choisi un verre trop petit), il faut presser de nouveau le bouton central. Attention, une fois un cycle arrêté, celui-ci s'allume en orange et il faut purger l’appareil en appuyant une nouvelle fois pour que l'eau restante soit évacuée.
Pour un soda aromatisé, il convient de tourner le bouton de niveau de 1 à 4. Le fabricant indique que le niveau “classique”, à savoir celui qui se rapproche le plus de ce que l'on trouve dans le commerce, correspond au niveau 4.
Lors de la distribution d'eau, la machine ajoute plus ou moins de sirop à la boisson en fonction du réglage et le mélange se fait directement lors de l'écoulement.
Le mode “boost” permet d'ajouter “une touche de saveur” supplémentaire à la boisson, selon SodaStream. Il permet aussi de varier les plaisirs et d'ajouter une dose d'un autre arôme dans un soda qui vient d'être versé, pour les amateurs de mélanges.
Nous avons testé un Pepsi classique avec une puissance de 4. Le résultat s'avère assez proche de ce que l'on pourrait trouver dans un fast-food, avec un goût moins intense que celui de la même boisson achetée en bouteille. On recommandera alors davantage l’Ultimate Multi-Drink aux amateurs d'eau pétillante qu'aux vrais fans de sodas. À moins, bien sûr, d'aimer les boissons servies dans la restauration rapide, dont les saveurs sont naturellement plus diluées que leurs homologues du commerce.
Faute de pouvoir prendre une mesure stable avec notre sonomètre, nous avons relevé que le service d'une boisson taille S dure une trentaine de secondes pendant lesquelles la machine se met en marche et prend l'eau du réservoir avec un bruit similaire à celui d'une machine à café (5 s). On entend ensuite l'action du cylindre de CO2 avant que le service de la boisson débute.
L'appareil se nettoie avec un chiffon humide et doux. Les pièces démontables, telles que le bac collecteur, le réservoir d'eau et les bouchons pour bouteilles d'arôme, peuvent être placées au lave-vaisselle à une température inférieure à 70 °C, selon SodaStream.
Les bouchons pour bouteille d'arôme nécessitent un soin particulier en raison de l'encrassement possible des différents éléments dû au sirop. Il est conseillé de démonter les éléments du bouchon (tige, buse, pompe et bouchon) et de les laver à l'eau chaude savonneuse.
Avec l'Ultimate Multi-Drink, SodaStream révolutionne la machine à gazéifier l'eau pour la transformer en distributeur, à la manière de ceux que l'on voit dans les établissements professionnels. Si la saveur des sodas ainsi obtenus peut ne pas être au goût de tous, difficile d'ignorer la praticité de l'appareil que l'on conseillera plutôt aux amateurs de pétillant souhaitant une eau gazéifiée minute, sans risque de perte des bulles dans le fond d'une bouteille.
Difficile de comparer la SodaStream Ultimate Multi-Drink, tant cet appareil constitue une innovation sur le marché de la gazéification maison, la machine proposant un service au verre plutôt qu'en bouteille. La comparaison se joue avec tous les autres appareils existants, ceux de la marque compris, et peut se faire au niveau de l'encombrement, logiquement plus important ici, bien que le service proposé par l'Ultimate soit unique en son genre.

articles.title: Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304 review: A quiet and compact Wildcat
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
Minisforum’s smallest and cheapest mini PC packing Intel's Wildcat Lake silicon is here. It is small, quiet, and easy to stow away, but this machine's performance is really only for light workloads.
Reasons to buy
- + Compact and light
- + Quiet
- + Low power use
- + Capable enough for home office and media consumption
- + Expandable RAM and SSD
Reasons to avoid
- - Weak performance in creator tasks
- - Only old or lightweight games and emulators are playable
- - Plastic top shell
- - Not a cheap option unless you have spare parts and go barebones
- - Single SODIMM and single M.2 slot
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
Minisforum’s Intel-based M2 line includes mini PCs with powerful processors such as the Core Ultra X7 Processor 358H (with 16C/16T CPU and B390 graphics), and the Core Ultra 7 356H (16C/16T). But there are more modest systems, too. The M2 Air-304 here is the most affordable option, based around the Intel Core 3 processor 304 with its 5C/5T CPU (1x Cougar Cove P-core and 4x Darkmont LP E-cores) and an iGPU with just a single Xe3 core.
No surprise, the little brother in the pack, both in terms of physical size and computing resources, is the most affordable. It currently starts at $263 for a barebones version. However, our test sample with 16GB DDR5-5600, a 500GB SSD, and Windows 11 Pro is listed at $559 - direct. That’s an introductory price, and Minisforum’s small text threatens that our configuration will bump up to $699 at some point in the future. Such a rise would put this product offering on very shaky ground, and we see B&H Photo has already raised the price at $729.
Overall, this Mini PC was pleasant to use, though. It ran quietly and only strained in gaming and productivity benchmarks which put it under loads that casual users aren’t going to be running on such a machine.
Design of the Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304 Mini PC
The Mini M2 Air looks stylish enough, and feels solid. Looks can be deceiving, though, and the top shell is a silver colored plastic, not a metallic alloy. Sometimes a metal shell can be used to help conduct away heat, but that seems less important with this actively cooled machine with a 15W processor. We note that there are thermal pads connecting the installed RAM and SSD to the bottom of this mini PC, which is metal.
A VESA mounting bracket is provided in the box if you prefer to hide the tiny device out of sight. It doesn’t have a remote power switch like the MSI Cubi NUC AI+ 3MG we reviewed earlier in the year, though, so you’ll have to consider reachability. A simple LED-lit power button is on the front of the device, alongside a couple of handy ports (more on the ports later). It also has a reset / clear CMOS hole on the front, and a Kensington lock slot on the rear.
Minisforum’s component choices mean this is a particularly small and light mini PC. The official M2 Mini specs state it is 112 x 112 x 37.15mm, which is roughly 4.4 x 4.4 x 1.5-inches. That’s a volume of 0.47 liters. It weighs in at just 440 grams, which is 0.97 pounds.
The power supply isn’t built-in. There’s a surprisingly bulky 65W power brick in the box, which connects to using a detachable figure-eight cable. However, this mini PC can be powered by USB-C, too, so you could pack a far more compact multipurpose power brick if portability is important.

Specifications of the Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304 Mini PC

| Graphics | Intel integrated graphics, 1x Xe3 core runs at up to 2.3 GHz, supports up to 3x displays |

| Storage | 1x M.2 2280 PCIe 4.0 x4 NVMe SSD slot (up to 2TB), microSD card expansion |

Ports and Upgradeability

On the front of the Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304 there are 2x USB-A 3.2 Gen 2 ports and a 3.5mm audio jack. Turn it to the side and you’ll see the microSD card slot. Then, around the back you have access to 1x USB4 (40Gbps, DP Alt Mode, PD), 1x USB-C 10Gbps, 1x USB 2.0, 2x HDMI 2.0, 2x RJ-45 2.5GbE LAN, and a DC-IN barrel jack.
Some might like to have at least one of the Type-C ports on the front, instead of two Type-As. But for its size the Mini M2 Air packs quite a few ports, including the very capable USB4, two HDMI ports, and two Ethernet ports. Realistically, a machine like this won’t be connected to oodles of wired peripherals, but if you found the port count lacking, USB4 allows for a capable and fast dock.
Wireless connectivity seems adequate, with an M.2 2230 card inside providing Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.4. I had no problems with either during the test period. The wireless card is socketed. It's located under the SSD, making it easy to repair or upgrade down the line.

Accessing the components inside the Minisforum Mini M2 Air is straightforward, but you need to peel off all the four rubber feet to get to four long fastening screws. When they’re removed, just flip off the metal bottom to access the M.2 slots and SODIMM. Be aware there’s some adhesive force holding this metal plate in place, due to the sticky thermal pads on the RAM and storage.
There’s just a single M.2 2280 storage slot and one SODIMM slot, both populated. That means, there’s no way to upgrade the RAM than swapping the module you already have in place. Our sample came with a 16GB DDR5-5600 SODIMM, but the system supports up to DDR5-6400. This only non-barebones configuration also came with a 500GB SSD in the M.2 slot.

Productivity Performance on the Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304
We have Intel’s latest 18A silicon inside this tiny PC, but not that much of it. Our review unit came with an Intel Core 3 304 "Wildcat Lake" chip that runs up to 4.3 GHz. Previous mini PCs based on Intel 300 series mobile silicon like the previously MSI and the GMKtec Evo-T2 came with a 16C/16T CPU. However, here we have just 5C/5T, and that’s just one performance core supported by four low power efficiency (LPE) cores.
Still, single core performance continues to be important for system and app responsiveness. The proof of the pudding is in the testing, though. And while this system felt perfectly usable in Windows 11, internet browsers, and word processing — preparing and writing this review, for example — the benchmarks are somewhat tougher.

As we expected, the single core tests show Wildcat Lake has some bite. It easily beats its AMD-based rivals in the POV Ray single core rendering tests, for example. Moreover, in tests like Cinebench 2024 single core, the Mini M2 Air might trail the pack, but not by very much. It's roughly 107 points is actually within touching distance of the 120 points scored by ‘high performance’ mini PCs like the Beelink SER10 MAX (Gorgon Point) and MSI Cubi NUC AI+ 3MG (Panther Lake).
Multicore tests exposed obvious weaknesses of the 5C/5T CPU configuration with single-channel RAM. All the other mini PCs we’ve tested this year come with 12C/24T (AMD) or 16C/16T (Intel), so the productivity benchmarks we run which can take advantage of multithreading for demanding rendering or encoding tasks make the Minisforum here seem weak. However, it might still be acceptable for transcoding a short video or two, occasionally, as long as you aren’t in a rush. If you are coming from an older, less efficient desktop sporting something like an i7-7700K or i5-10400, this 15W Wildcat Lake chip is an improvement in both single and multicore performance.
During our demanding tests, the Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304 stayed cool and quiet thanks to its 15W processor and capable cooling.
Gaming and Graphics on the Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304
For anything other than the most casual gaming or emulation of older consoles you should look at other devices. We’ve looked at Intel 300 silicon powered devices with iGPUs packing 12 Xe3 cores, and four Xe3 cores, but this just has one, and it is further hampered by sharing the single-channel system RAM.
Prepare to see some low frame rates / scores in our standard tests. I felt that some of these tests probably shouldn’t be run on this mini PC, but did it anyway, for completeness. However, some 3DMark benchmarks simply wouldn’t run, as Intel has pruned the features that work on this iGPU due to limited resources. For example, 3DMark Solar Bay doesn’t run on this system, and neither does Speed Way. Error messages about unsupported hardware pop up when you try these tests.
Steel Nomad ran, though, and the Minisforum and its solo Xe3 core achieved a score of 135. The aforementioned Evo-T2 with Intel Core Ultra X7 358H and (B390) iGPU with 12x Xe3 cores scored 1,624. That’s incredibly close to 12x faster than the Core 3 304’s ‘Intel Graphics.’ A score of 135 means Steel Nomad ran at just a little more than 1 FPS, which actually doesn’t hurt your eyes to watch as much as 10 FPS.
Using the multi-scene benchmarks built into Shadow of the Tomb Raider and Cyberpunk 2077 using our standard settings selections resulted in some unpleasant experiences. Performance of no better than 10 or 12 FPS was observed in these tests. To achieve 25 or even 30 FPS in these titles I found that reducing the game resolution to 720p and low/lowest settings would just about get there.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
So, for some actual fun on the Mini M2 Air I decided to try the latest version of the Sony PSP emulator PPSSPP and play some Wipeout Pure. I managed to run this game on my 1440p monitor with a 6x render resolution, and it achieved a nice steady 60 FPS, delivering an enjoyable futuristic racing experience. It would also therefore likely be good for retro emulation of similar era and older consoles as well as home computers.
Power, Heat, and Noise when using the Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304
During my day-to-day use, the Minisforum system consumed around 9W when idling on the desktop. When under the heaviest loads I threw at it, the highest system power consumption I saw was around 31W.
I didn't find it surprising that this low-power system ran cool and quiet. System tools showed that during light activities like browsing the web the CPU temperature remained in the low 30s Celsius. Playing games or benchmarking for length periods, I never saw the reported CPU temperature rise beyond the low 70s Celsius.
Minisforum’s tiny mini PC was a quiet operator at idle and under load. My measurements from about half a foot in front of the device show noise levels under 30 dBA at idle, which is very quiet and actually said to be beneath the measurement threshold of my meter. Stressing the system with simultaneous CPU and GPU loads I managed to observe just a reading of a little over 37 dBA from the system.
Software and Warranty on the Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304
The Mini M2 Air ships with Windows 11 Pro installed in the configuration we received. I found no pre-installed bloatware. The official specs don’t mention compatibility with other OSes like Linux.
Minisforum sells this mini PC with a two-year warranty and a 30-day money-back guarantee.
Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air-304 configurations
Minisforum sells only two Elite Mini M2 Air-304 configurations in the U.S. There’s a barebones model, or the configuration we tested with pre-installed RAM, SSD, and OS.
At the time of writing our 16GB / 500GB / Windows 11 Pro configuration is listed by the mini PC maker at $559 but the product page says the price is normally $699. The barebone model is currently $263, discounted from $329. We don’t know when the prices might get adjusted. However, we’ve noted U.S. retailers like B&H Photo are now selling the 16GB / 500GB model at $729.
Bottom Line
Though the Mini M2 Air’s performance may lack in performance, it also probably the smallest cheapest, and least power-hungry mini PC we’ve tested all year. If these kinds of qualities are important to you, the Minisforum might be appealing.
It is admirable that this mini PC is so small but leaves RAM and storage upgrades on the table for later. Other positives are the sturdy build, despite the use of plastic for the top shell, and a good port selection considering its size. In addition to being easy to hide due to its small stature, and supplied VESA mount, you probably won’t hear it very much, either.
Of course, the performance is a weakness that can’t be ignored, especially in the context of our ever-growing tested mini PCs chart from 2026. It is great to see this latest-gen processor barebones at just over $260 direct from Minisforum. If you have a spare DDR5 SODIMM and SSD, perhaps from a laptop upgrade or wherever, this might help you get a new mini PC system up and running cheaply. However, the 16GB RAM and 500GB SSD (and Windows 11 Pro license) currently more than doubles the list price (it adds $296). That’s a bit painful.
Furthermore, if the Minisforum Elite Mini M2 Air ever rises to its apparent MSRP of $699, we’d definitely look elsewhere. Around this price, especially during sale periods, you can shop for mini PCs employing far more powerful previous-gen processors. One good alternative candidate might be the Geekom IT13 Max 2026 we reviewed in August at $799. Price trackers show this Core Ultra 185H machine with 24GB RAM has been available for under $600 with discount / coupon over the last few months. There are also a lot of capable older gen AMD mini PCs to ponder over at attractive prices.
Mark Tyson is a news editor at Tom's Hardware. He enjoys covering the full breadth of PC tech; from business and semiconductor design to products approaching the edge of reason.

articles.title: Detectify's Agentic Tooling lets AI agents test suspected flaws in running applications - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Detectify’s Agentic Tooling lets AI agents test suspected flaws in running applications
Swedish application security company Detectify AB today launched Agentic Tooling, a set of tools aimed at letting an organization’s own artificial intelligence agents test whether suspected vulnerabilities can be exploited in running applications.
A new Security Ledger, also part of the launch, is designed to record the evidence behind each test. Detectify is pitching the release at DevSecOps teams that are unsure whether they can trust what their AI agents report.
Detectify customers report that roughly 80% of the findings from their AI-driven static application security testing tools are noise. Under pressure to deliver an answer, an agent can also produce a convincing report about a test it never ran, the company warned.
Even before AI agents enter the picture, many security teams are falling behind. Nine in 10 open critical and high-severity vulnerabilities had stayed exposed for more than 90 days, according to Detectify’s H2 2026 Cyber Hygiene Index. In a study by researchers at Fudan University and Tencent Holdings Ltd., 76% of the static-analysis alerts examined were found to be false positives. Each one took developers 10 to 20 minutes to review.
Through Agentic Tooling, agents can tap the testing engines Detectify has built over more than a decade. Included are payload assessments sourced from its ethical hacker community, attack surface data from its Surface Monitoring product and Alfred, an AI system the company launched in March 2025 to automate tests for known vulnerabilities.
Running in a customer’s own environment, the tools connect to agents through either the Model Context Protocol or a command-line interface. They operate only on the data a customer provides and are said to work with whichever agent the customer already uses.
At the center of the design is loop engineering, an emerging practice of running AI agents in automated, repeating workflows rather than prompting them by hand. Kicking off each loop is a trigger such as a continuous integration run. Whether it comes from a code scan, a bug bounty report, a red team or Detectify’s own attack surface data, each finding is turned into a ticket.
Once an agent picks up a ticket, it reads the relevant code before testing the live application from the outside, as an attacker would. Run continuously, the loop becomes what Detectify calls a verification factory.
The requests sent, the payloads used and the results returned are all logged in the Security Ledger each time an agent uses Detectify’s tools. Written by Detectify rather than the agent, the append-only ledger lets teams separate findings backed by actual tests from unsupported AI conclusions. Any ticket that could cause harm, such as a denial-of-service test, is marked unsafe for a person to decide on.
“Ask an agent to write your code, then ask the same agent whether it’s secure. If it says yes, you don’t actually know,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Rickard Carlsson. There are plenty of examples of agents fabricating proof to please the person asking, according to Carlsson, who described Detectify’s aim as “building proof that an agent can’t fabricate.”
Available on request starting today, Agentic Tooling builds on the Detectify MCP Server that the company announced in May to give AI agents access to its security findings. Investors include Insight Partners, which took a majority stake in October 2024, along with Balderton Capital (UK) LLP, Inventure, First Fellow Partners Oy and SquareOne App Ltd.

articles.title: Windows 11 sur un iPhone Duo ? Il l'a fait avec Gemini 4 Carbon, et sans jailbreak
articles.text:
Un responsable de Google a réussi à faire tourner Windows 11 sur le tout premier iPhone pliable d’Apple, avec l’aide de Gemini. Une expérience insolite qui transforme le smartphone en (presque) vrai PC miniature, au prix de quelques acrobaties techniques.
Voilà quelques années, déjà, que Microsoft a jeté l’éponge concernant Windows sur smartphone, mais il semblerait que tout le monde n’ait pas encore renoncé à l’idée. Ammaar Reshi, responsable du produit et du design chez Google AI Studio, vient de publier une vidéo sur X dans laquelle il fait fonctionner Windows 11 sur un iPhone Duo, le tout premier smartphone pliable d’Apple. Pas de jailbreak ni de PC distant pour faire tourner le système, mais un projet développé avec l’aide de Gemini 4 Carbon en seulement deux heures, à en croire son auteur.
Windows 11 et iOS, une cohabitation assez improbable
Baptisé WindowsiOS, le projet ne remplace pas iOS, mais exécute Windows 11 24H2 dans sa version ARM64 au sein d’un environnement virtuel. Pour contourner les restrictions d’Apple sur la virtualisation matérielle, il exploite un moteur de traduction binaire capable d’adapter à la volée les instructions de Windows à l’environnement d’exécution de l’iPhone Duo. Une opération facilitée par l’architecture ARM64 commune au système de Microsoft et à la puce A20 Pro du smartphone.
Ce moteur, Ammaar Reshi l’a repris de Henge, un projet open source qui avait déjà permis de faire fonctionner macOS sur iPhone, puis l’a adapté aux exigences de Windows grâce aux agents de Gemini 4 Carbon, en retravaillant la gestion de la mémoire, le démarrage du système et la prise en charge des périphériques virtuels.
L’interface a également été adaptée au format pliable de l’iPhone Duo. Entièrement ouvert, le smartphone fait office de tablette Windows sur son écran de 7,6 pouces. Replié à moitié, il se transforme en petit ordinateur portable, avec clavier et pavé tactile virtuels, sur lequel il est même possible de naviguer sur Internet grâce à Microsoft Edge.
Une prouesse, mais pas tout à fait un PC de poche
Avant d’espérer transformer son propre iPhone en PC Windows, il faudra tout de même s’armer d’un peu de patience et de solides connaissances techniques. L’installation nécessite un Mac équipé d’une puce Apple Silicon, les outils de développement d’Apple et une image de Windows 11 ARM64, tandis que chaque lancement impose de passer par un débogueur pour autoriser l’exécution du code traduit.
Ammaar Reshi revendique des performances proches d’une exécution native sur l’iPhone Duo, seul appareil sur lequel WindowsiOS a été testé jusqu’ici. Pour parvenir à ce résultat, il a dû alléger Windows 11 afin de le faire tenir dans les 4,5 Go de mémoire qui lui sont alloués, en désactivant ou supprimant plus de 35 services et composants, parmi lesquels les protections de Microsoft Defender.
Bref, il faut quand même avoir un sacré goût pour la bidouille, et les moyens de se l’offrir, pour installer sur un iPhone à 2 339 euros une version de Windows 11 dont le support vient de prendre fin, vous en conviendrez.
- Fabrication et charnière remarquables
- Format passeport très agréable
- Écran mat nano-texturé, pliure discrète

articles.title: AI is reshaping the creator economy: trust will decide who wins it
articles.text:
AI is reshaping the creator economy: trust will decide who wins it
Building creator trust in the age of AI
There’s always been a balancing act between creators and creator platforms over profit, value, and ownership. Now, AI tools are upsetting that balance and reshaping commercial dynamics, while raising new concerns about transparency and control.
As creators compete for engagement against low-effort AI “slop,” they must also navigate opaque monetization policies and inconsistent enforcement. These pressures are rapidly increasing the friction between creators and the platforms they rely on.
At the same time, as more platforms and revenue streams emerge, creators have greater choice about where to build an audience.
President of Tipalti.
As the terms creators operate under keep changing, creators are pushing for more control. They want their voices to be heard, their work protected, and the value they generate recognized.
For platforms, this raises the stakes for attracting and retaining top creators. Trust is becoming a competitive differentiator, and the platforms that recognize this are protecting their creators and paying them reliably in the age of AI.
The creator economy’s ongoing transparency issue
Today, high-volume, low-effort AI-generated content has become an inescapable part of the online experience. But for creators, lax moderation of that content can directly impact earnings by creating an uneven playing field and increasing competition for engagement and views.
Not only must creators compete with AI-generated content, but concerns are also mounting that their work is being used to train the models producing it, without their consent or compensation. Trust is eroding as a result, and inaction risks alienating the very people whose work underpins the success of digital platforms.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
These challenges are becoming increasingly evident. Recently, a US court approved a $1.5 billion settlement relating to Anthropic’s use of pirated books to train its AI models. While the case represents a clarification for rights holders, smaller creators and artists often lack the resources required to pursue litigation in the first place.
Concerns have also been raised about YouTube reportedly using AI to alter creators’ videos without their consent. Even where there is no evidence of financial loss, the incident highlights a potential broader imbalance in the relationship if platforms can make unilateral changes to creators’ work without meaningful consultation.
Creators rely on platforms to distribute, monetize, and govern their work fairly. But platforms need creators too. Their business models depend on compelling content that attracts and retains audiences. It’s a mutual dependency that makes listening to and responding to creators’ concerns a strategic imperative.
Creator trust is intrinsically linked with income reliability
Questions about trust extend beyond how content is used to how creators earn a living. In just a few decades, the creator economy has evolved from a relatively informal ecosystem into a multibillion-dollar global industry. The decisions made by the platforms shaping this industry now directly affect how millions of creators build their careers and earn income.
Even before AI, changes to recommendation algorithms, monetization models, and advertising guidelines meant creators had to become accustomed to their earnings changing overnight. These realities have encouraged them to move away from relying on individual platforms for predictable income and monetizing their content and brands across multiple platforms and revenue streams instead.
Whether they earn through commission-based selling on ecommerce platforms, livestreaming, brand sponsorships, or content views, creators’ incomes are becoming increasingly fragmented. While this diversification reduces their dependence on any single platform, it also creates greater complexity for the businesses responsible for managing and paying them.
Across the industry, poor payout experiences are already damaging creator relationships. Tipalti’s recent global payments research revealed that 26% of businesses lost contributors because of payment-related issues in the past 12 months, with creators accounting for 36% of those losses. Payment friction can directly affect a platform’s ability to retain the people generating its content.
Failing to address these pain points creates a commercial risk, particularly when creators have more options than ever to build and monetize their audiences. If a platform is frustrating to work with or fails to provide reliable payouts and transparent breakdowns of earnings, creators can move to a competitor that offers a better customer experience.
The foundations of creator trust
To keep creators engaged and earn their trust, platforms must address two priorities: protecting creators' work and paying them reliably and transparently.
First, creators need confidence that their interests are protected and that they remain in control of their work. Platforms must acknowledge the issues posed by AI, introduce safeguards for creators’ content, and ensure that any resulting benefits are shared fairly.
Second, platforms must offer a transparent and reliable payout experience. At the end of each payment cycle, creators should receive a clear breakdown of how their payout was calculated, including the factors responsible for any monthly variations. They should feel confident that the economic value they create is recognized and that they will be paid accurately and on time.
Both priorities carry more weight as creator economies grow worldwide, presenting new opportunities for global partnerships. New markets often bring inconsistent standards for content protection and payments, and incompatible financial infrastructure can bottleneck growth.
To compete for creators in these regions, platforms need protections that hold up regardless of where a creator is based, and payout infrastructure capable of supporting an expanding range of currencies, payment methods, and regional requirements.
The next stage of the creator economy
AI is changing what creators make, how platforms distribute it, and how value gets created. But the fundamental relationship hasn’t changed: creators need platforms to reach audiences, and platforms need creators to keep those audiences coming back.
As that relationship becomes more complex, trust will matter more, not less. Creators need to know their work is protected, their earnings are transparent, and they’ll be paid accurately and on time, no matter where they are. These aren't minor priorities. They show whether a platform actually values its creators, or just profits from them.
In the age of AI, trust won’t just shape the creator economy. It will shape who succeeds in it.

articles.title: AMD Completes Acquisition of World Labs
articles.text:
Monday, November 16th 2026
AMD Completes Acquisition of World Labs
AMD today announced the completion of its acquisition of World Labs, expanding its capabilities across the AI stack with a world-class model team. The acquisition brings together leading AI model researchers and AMD engineers to shape the next generation of AMD hardware, software and systems for the open AI ecosystem.
"Delivering the infrastructure that will power the next era of superintelligence requires us to optimize compute platforms and models together," said Dr. Lisa Su, chair and CEO of AMD. "We are thrilled to welcome Fei-Fei Li and the exceptional World Labs team to AMD. Their pioneering model research will help shape our future hardware, software and systems. Together, we will enable researchers and developers across the ecosystem to push the boundaries of what AI can do."World Labs develops AI models that create and simulate interactive 3D environments, as well as technology for robotic learning and simulation. Dr. Fei-Fei Li joins AMD as executive vice president and chief scientist, reporting directly to Su.
The World Labs team will continue advancing foundational model research while collaborating with AMD engineers to apply insights from emerging model capabilities to the development of future AI infrastructure for customers and developers across the open AI ecosystem.

articles.title: Monitor gamer IPS: 8 modelos para comprar em 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Monitor gamer IPS: 8 modelos para comprar em 2026
Guia reúne telas IPS de 120 Hz a 300 Hz com baixo tempo de resposta e fidelidade de cor para jogos competitivos, campanhas imersivas e uso diário em 2026
Escolher um monitor gamer IPS em 2026 exige equilibrar taxa de atualização, tempo de resposta e precisão cromática de acordo com o perfil de jogo.
Os painéis IPS (In-Plane Switching) consolidaram-se como o padrão preferido para setups versáteis porque oferecem amplos ângulos de visão de 178° e cobertura de cores superior aos painéis TN e VA tradicionais, sem sacrificar a agilidade exigida em títulos competitivos.
Nesta lista, selecionamos 8 modelos disponíveis no mercado brasileiro que cobrem diferentes faixas de desempenho e orçamento, partindo de opções de entrada de 120 Hz até telas avançadas de 300 Hz com retroiluminação MiniLED e resolução Quad HD.
O TCL 25G64 eleva o patamar dos monitores competitivos ao combinar um painel IPS Full HD (1920 x 1080) de 25 polegadas com retroiluminação QD-MiniLED, taxa de atualização de 300 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms (GtG).
Essa combinação elimina rastros em movimentos bruscos de câmera em jogos de tiro em primeira pessoa (FPS), enquanto o controle local de iluminação proporciona pretos mais profundos e brilho máximo de 600 nits com certificação HDR600.
Para quem busca fidelidade visual além da velocidade, o modelo entrega profundidade de cor de 10 bits, cobertura de 96% do espectro DCI-P3 e calibração de fábrica com precisão Delta E menor que 2.
A conectividade inclui duas portas HDMI 2.1 e uma DisplayPort, acompanhadas de base ergonômica com ajuste de altura e compatibilidade com AMD FreeSync Premium.
Voltado para jogadores que priorizam definição de imagem sem abrir mão da fluidez, o AOC Agon Q27G4F traz tela Fast IPS de 27 polegadas com resolução Quad HD (2560 x 1440 pixels), taxa de atualização de 180 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms GtG (0,5 ms MPRT).
A maior densidade de pixels garante nitidez superior para identificar alvos a longa distância e amplia a área útil de trabalho no dia a dia. O painel cobre 120% do espaço de cores sRGB, conta com brilho típico de 300 cd/m² e suporte a HDR10, entregando tonalidades vibrantes em jogos de mundo aberto.
Compatível com NVIDIA G-SYNC e Adaptive Sync para evitar cortes na imagem (screen tearing), o modelo ainda se destaca pela base completa com ajustes de altura, inclinação, giro e rotação (pivô), além de entradas DisplayPort 1.4 e HDMI 2.0.
O Samsung Odyssey G40 de 25 polegadas é projetado especificamente para o cenário de eSports, operando com painel IPS Full HD, taxa de atualização nativa de 240 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms (GtG).
O formato compacto de 25 polegadas mantém toda a ação dentro do campo de visão periférico do jogador, permitindo reações imediatas em partidas ranqueadas de alto nível.
Com brilho típico de 400 cd/m² e suporte a FreeSync Premium e G-SYNC Compatible, o monitor mantém boa visibilidade mesmo em ambientes bastante iluminados e sincroniza os quadros da GPU sem engasgos.
O conjunto oferece duas entradas HDMI, uma DisplayPort e suporte ergonomicamente ajustável em altura, inclinação e modo retrato.
O Dell SE2426HG entrega especificações de nível competitivo em um chassi sóbrio de 24 polegadas, equipado com painel IPS Full HD de 240 Hz e tempo de resposta de 0,5 ms. Essa configuração garante transições de pixels limpas e baixa latência de entrada, atendendo jogadores de títulos competitivos que buscam alto desempenho com investimento controlado.
O modelo integra suporte a AMD FreeSync, compatibilidade com HDR10 e tecnologias de conforto visual, como tela antirreflexo, redução de luz azul e operação livre de cintilação (Flicker-Free). Conta ainda com conectividade DisplayPort 1.4, HDMI e furação padrão VESA 100 x 100 mm para instalação em braços articulados.
Posicionando-se acima do padrão tradicional de 144 Hz e 180 Hz, o AOC Agon 24G42HE apresenta tela IPS de 23,8 polegadas com resolução Full HD, taxa de atualização de 200 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms GtG (0,3 ms MPRT). O ganho extra de frequência proporciona rastreamento de alvos mais suave e resposta rápida aos comandos do mouse.
Com brilho de 300 cd/m², contraste estático de 1000:1 e cobertura de 116% do padrão sRGB, o painel reproduz cores vivas em jogos e conteúdos multimídia.
O monitor possui certificação NVIDIA G-SYNC Compatible, design sem bordas em três lados, entradas HDMI 2.0 e DisplayPort 1.4, além de ajuste de inclinação e suporte VESA.
O LG UltraGear 24GS60F-B equilibra velocidade e precisão cromática em um painel IPS de 24 polegadas (23,8 polegadas visíveis) com resolução Full HD, taxa de atualização de 180 Hz e tempo de resposta real de 1 ms (GtG). A combinação reduz o efeito fantasma (ghosting) em cenas rápidas sem comprometer a estabilidade das cores.
O display cobre 99% da gama sRGB, suporta HDR10 e oferece ampla compatibilidade com NVIDIA G-SYNC e AMD FreeSync. Entre os recursos voltados para jogos estão o Dynamic Action Sync (redução de atraso de entrada), o Black Stabilizer (clareamento de áreas escuras) e mira integrada na tela, conectados via HDMI 2.0 e DisplayPort 1.4.
Para quem prefere uma área de visualização maior mantendo a resolução Full HD, o LG UltraGear 27G411B traz tela IPS de 27 polegadas com taxa de atualização nativa de 144 Hz e tempo de resposta de 1 ms com Motion Blur Reduction (5 ms GtG nativo).
O tamanho ampliado favorece a imersão em jogos de corrida, RPGs e consumo de vídeos, sem exigir uma placa de vídeo topo de linha para empurrar os quadros.
O painel apresenta contraste estático de 1500:1 — superior à média da categoria IPS —, cobertura de 99% sRGB, suporte a HDR10 e sincronização adaptativa via NVIDIA G-SYNC Compatible e AMD FreeSync.
A construção inclui bordas finas em três lados, entradas HDMI e DisplayPort, saída para fones de ouvido e padrão VESA 100 x 100 mm.
O Samsung Essential S3 LS24F320GALMZD é o modelo mais básico da lista, mas ainda usa painel IPS e resolução Full HD, se saindo melhor para jogos casuais, trabalho remoto e uso multimídia.
A taxa de atualização menor que a de modelos gamer avançados limita o apelo competitivo. Mesmo assim, recursos como FreeSync, baixo input lag e boa reprodução de cores ajudam em consoles, notebooks e PCs simples.
A indicação é para quem quer gastar pouco e evitar painéis de qualidade inferior. O Essential S3 funciona como monitor IPS de entrada para jogar ocasionalmente, estudar e montar um setup econômico em 2026.
A escolha do monitor gamer IPS ideal depende da potência da sua placa de vídeo (GPU), dos gêneros de jogos praticados e do espaço disponível na mesa. Antes de fechar a compra, avalie quatro critérios técnicos fundamentais:
Na faixa de entrada intermediária, modelos de 24 polegadas Full HD entre 180 Hz e 200 Hz, como o LG UltraGear 24GS60F-B e o AOC Agon 24G42HE, oferecem o equilíbrio mais eficiente entre preço e desempenho.
Ambos entregam painéis IPS rápidos de 1 ms GtG, boa cobertura de cores sRGB e sincronização adaptativa sem exigir placas de vídeo avançadas.
Para quem busca salto de resolução e ergonomia completa pagando menos que em modelos OLED, o AOC Agon Q27G4F (27″ QHD 180 Hz) destaca-se como a opção mais equilibrada da categoria intermediária.
A taxa de atualização ideal começa em 144 Hz para jogos competitivos. Esse patamar já oferece movimentos mais suaves que 60 Hz ou 75 Hz e melhora a resposta visual em partidas rápidas.
Monitores de 180 Hz são o ponto de equilíbrio em 2026, pois entregam fluidez alta sem exigir tanto quanto 240 Hz. Eles combinam bem com placas de vídeo intermediárias em Full HD.
Modelos de 240 Hz, como o Samsung Odyssey G40, fazem mais sentido para jogadores de e-sports. Para aproveitar a tela, o PC precisa manter taxas próximas em jogos como CS2, Valorant e Overwatch 2.
Os painéis IPS dominam o mercado de monitores gamer por equilibrarem velocidade e qualidade de imagem, mas apresentam limitações físicas inerentes à tecnologia LCD:
O monitor OLED entrega contraste praticamente infinito, pretos reais e tempo de resposta extremamente rápido. Em jogos HDR, terror e single-player cinematográfico, a imagem costuma ser superior à de um IPS tradicional.
O monitor IPS vence em preço, disponibilidade e menor risco de burn-in. Para uso prolongado com HUD fixo, planilhas, navegador e barra de tarefas, ele tende a ser uma escolha mais tranquila.
Em 2026, OLED é a opção premium para quem busca qualidade máxima. IPS continua sendo a melhor compra racional para a maioria, especialmente em monitores Full HD e QHD com 144 Hz a 240 Hz.
O monitor IPS é melhor para quem prioriza cores, ângulo de visão e resposta mais previsível em jogos rápidos. Nossa equipe prefere IPS para FPS competitivo, uso misto e setups com duas telas.
Já o monitor VA oferece contraste maior, com pretos mais profundos e imagem forte em filmes ou jogos escuros. Porém, alguns modelos podem apresentar ghosting em transições rápidas, especialmente em cenas com tons escuros.
A escolha depende do perfil do jogador. Para e-sports e versatilidade, IPS é mais seguro; para imersão, contraste e consumo de mídia, VA pode agradar mais se o modelo tiver boa resposta.
