articles.title: Diese Haken erwarten die ersten Cybercab-Käufer
articles.text:
300-Dollar-Zwangsabo und mehr: Diese Haken erwarten die ersten Cybercab-Käufer
Anfang September 2026 ist das erste Cybercab-Robotaxi in Austin (Texas) vollautonom und ohne Kontrollperson an den Start gegangen. In den Wochen zuvor waren noch interne Personen an Bord gewesen, um für mehr Sicherheit zu sorgen. Mittlerweile soll Tesla bei seinem autonomen Taxidienst 278 Cybercabs im Einsatz haben.
Tesla startet Cybercab-Verkauf
Bisher können Privatpersonen zwar mit den Cybercab-Robotaxis mitfahren. In den Verkauf sind die Fahrzeuge aber bisher noch nicht offiziell gegangen. Das dürfte sich aber bald ändern. Seit Mitte November 2026 ermöglicht Tesla offiziell Bestellungen des lenkrad- und pedallosen E-Autos.
Wie das Unternehmen per X einschränkt, sollen aber nur „ausgewählte Kund:innen“ zu einem entsprechenden Kauf eingeladen werden. Nicht die einzige Einschränkung. So sollen die Cybercabs nur in Gebieten fahren können, in denen Tesla schon seinen Robotaxidienst anbietet, wie The Verge berichtet.
Verfügbarkeit und Einsatzfähigkeit begrenzt
Vollständig autonome Fahrten gibt es aktuell lediglich in Austin, Dallas, Houston, Fort Worth und San Antonio (Texas) sowie Miami, Tampa und Orlando (Florida). Zudem warnt Tesla in entsprechenden E-Mails, dass die anfängliche Verfügbarkeit begrenzt sei.
Ebenfalls auf die potenzielle Kauflust dürfte drücken, dass der Preis für ein Cybercab zwar auf den ersten Blick bei unter 30.000 Dollar liegt, wie Tesla-Chef Elon Musk es versprochen hatte. Allerdings kommen monatlich weitere 299 Dollar für das sogenannte Autonomie-Abo dazu.
Eigentlich wenig überraschend, wenn man das mit den 99 Dollar pro Monat vergleicht, die die FSD-Funktion Model-3- und Model-Y-Fahrer:innen kostet. Allerdings kann dieses Paket jederzeit abbestellt werden. Wer das Autonomie-Abo kündigt, dessen Cybercab bleibt anschließend einfach stehen.
Autonomie-Abo erhöht Cybercab-Kosten
Und das Abo macht das Cybercab auf Dauer teuer. Wer die Gebühr etwa fünf Jahre lang zahlt, dessen Cybercab schlägt dann mit insgesamt 47.600 Dollar zu Buche – ohne Steuern, Kosten für das Laden sowie die Versicherung.
Zudem müssen Cybercab-Besteller:innen eine Gebühr von 1.000 Dollar zahlen, um – bestenfalls – schon im Dezember 2026 eines der Fahrzeuge geliefert zu bekommen. Das Geld wird aber nicht auf den Kaufpreis angerechnet, obwohl Tesla keine Garantie für eine Dezember-Lieferung gibt.
Ein weiterer einer ganzen Reihe von Haken dreht sich um das Versprechen Musks, das Cybercab in Teslas Robotaxi-Netzwerk einbinden zu können, wenn man es selbst gerade nicht nutzt. Doch das scheint derzeit unmöglich zu sein. Denn Tesla untersagt jegliche kommerzielle Verwendung der an Privatpersonen verkauften Cybercabs.
Monetarisierung vielleicht ab Frühjahr 2027
Teslas KI-Chef Ashok Elluswamy hat in Aussicht gestellt, dass eine solche Monetarisierung für Cybercab-Besitzer:innen ab dem zweiten Quartal 2027 möglich sein könnte. Derweil hängt Teslas Cybercab-Offensive ohnehin an einem seidenen Faden.
Musk zufolge hänge eine umfassendere Einführung der Robotaxis von der „behördlichen Genehmigung“ ab. Und die lässt auf sich warten. Die US-Verkehrsbehörde NHTSA hat Anfang September 2026 entsprechende Untersuchungen eingeleitet. Denn eigentlich ist das „Fahren“ eines Autos ohne Lenkrad und Pedale in den USA nicht erlaubt.

articles.title: Sabika secures new investment to expand gold and silver trading platform
articles.text:
Sabika secures new investment to expand gold and silver trading platform
- Egypt-based digital precious metals investment platform Sabika has announced the completion of multiple funding rounds for an undisclosed amount. The company did not reveal the investors, funding stages or the number of rounds completed.
- Founded in 2022 by Mohammed Darwish and Ibrahim Anwar, Sabika enables users to buy and sell gold and silver, monitor market prices, set price alerts, manage their holdings and request physical delivery of purchased metals.
- Sabika said its user base has surpassed 120,000, as it seeks to expand its presence in Egypt's digital precious metals investment market.
- The funding will support further development of Sabika's platform, strengthen its technology infrastructure and enable the launch of new gold and silver savings and investment products.
- Last year, Sabika secured a six-figure USD investment, led by M-Empire Angels.
Press release:
Sabika, a digital platform for investing in gold and silver, announced the successful completion of its funding rounds. The funding will support Sabika’s plans to develop its digital platform, strengthen its technological capabilities and expand its range of services. The company’s user base has also surpassed 120,000.
The Sabika platform lets users buy and sell gold and silver, track prices and set price alerts at target levels. Users can also manage their holdings, review their transaction history and request physical delivery of their purchases.
Commenting on the move, Ahmed Khaled, CEO of Sabika, said, "Our successful funding rounds reflect investor confidence in Sabika’s business model and growth potential. They also underscore our ability to continue improving the digital gold and silver investment experience. We see promising opportunities to use technology to make precious metals more accessible to individuals and to offer services that meet their expectations.”
Khaled added: “We believe technology proves its real value when it delivers an integrated experience for users, one that combines digital convenience with the option of physical delivery. We make sure innovation shows in every detail of that experience. That includes easy-to-follow steps, clear information and the ability for customers to track their transactions and manage their holdings.”
Khaled continued: “Surpassing 120,000 users marks an important milestone for Sabika and reflects growing demand for our services. Our user base also gives us deeper insight into our customers’ needs, which we will use to develop our services in the next phase.”
As part of its expansion plans, Sabika continues to develop new products and services that give customers more options for saving and investing in gold and silver. It focuses on offering solutions that address real market needs and deliver clear value to users. The company will announce details of these products and services as they become ready for launch.
The plans come in a market where Egyptians bought around 22 tonnes of gold in the first half of 2026, according to World Gold Council data. Purchases were split between 11.9 tonnes of gold bars and coins and 10.1 tonnes of jewellery. The figures reflect gold’s standing as a savings and investment tool for individuals. They also point to opportunities for digital solutions that give people easier access to investment gold and more flexibility when buying and selling it, as digital financial services expand.

articles.title: Alerta con Microsoft Word: archivos antiguos serán alterados por falta de compatibilidad
articles.text:
Abres un contrato que redactaste hace más de diez años y el texto ya no aparece donde debía: una tabla saltó a otra página y el total de hojas cambió. Es el riesgo que advierte Microsoft para quienes conservan archivos antiguos de Word.
La compañía retirará un conjunto de opciones de compatibilidad del programa, lo que podría alterar documentos creados o guardados por última vez en Word 2010 o versiones anteriores.
Según The Register, la propia empresa reconoce que los archivos afectados “pueden mostrar diferencias de diseño”, como texto que se reacomoda, cambios en el espaciado o en la cantidad de páginas, e imágenes y formas que se desplazan a otra hoja.
Qué es el modo de compatibilidad y qué cambia
El modo de compatibilidad es la función que permite que una versión nueva de Word abra un archivo hecho en una más antigua sin modificar su diseño original. Mientras el documento permanece en ese estado, las funciones más recientes del programa quedan desactivadas.
El usuario tiene la opción de convertir el documento para desbloquear esas funciones nuevas. Sin embargo, precisó The Register, quienes trabajen con versiones más viejas de Word podrían después tener dificultades para editar ciertas partes del archivo convertido.
Microsoft no detalló cuáles son las opciones específicas que eliminará. La empresa se limitó a señalar: “Estamos retirando un conjunto de opciones de compatibilidad en Microsoft Word (aplicación de escritorio) para documentos en modo de compatibilidad”. El motivo declarado es simplificar cómo el programa maneja el diseño de las páginas y ofrecer una experiencia más uniforme entre plataformas.
La recomendación de la compañía, recogida por el medio, es exportar a PDF cualquier documento cuyo diseño sea importante antes de que se aplique el cambio, dado que ese formato mantiene fija la apariencia de cada página sin importar el programa o el dispositivo donde se abra.
Cuándo llegará el cambio a Word
El despliegue comenzará en la versión de Word para Windows en diciembre de 2026 y debería completarse en enero de 2027. La versión para Mac recibirá el mismo cambio a comienzos de 2027, según el cronograma difundido por la empresa.
The Register recordó que Word tiene más de 40 años de historia y que su primera versión para Windows salió hacia el final de los años 80. El procesador de textos se transformó a lo largo de las décadas y sigue siendo uno de los programas centrales del paquete de productividad de Microsoft.
El modo de compatibilidad funcionó hasta ahora como una salvaguarda para que los documentos antiguos no sufrieran cambios abruptos de diseño al abrirse en versiones nuevas. Con la eliminación de ese conjunto de opciones, parte de esa protección desaparece.
Quiénes se verán afectados y qué hacer
El golpe, anticipó The Register, lo sentirán sobre todo los administradores de sistemas, es decir, quienes se encargan de los computadores de una organización. El medio prevé que podrían recibir una oleada de consultas de usuarios desconcertados por lo que le pasó a su documento.
A esos administradores les conviene revisar plantillas antiguas, formularios y otros archivos cuya paginación deba mantenerse exacta, antes de que el cambio llegue a los equipos de la empresa.
El cambio en Word afecta a cualquier archivo creado o guardado por última vez en Word 2010 o versiones anteriores. Al perder parte del modo de compatibilidad, esos documentos pueden mostrar texto reacomodado, páginas de más o de menos, e imágenes desplazadas al abrirse en la versión actualizada del programa.
Esto toca a cualquiera que guarde archivos viejos de uso recurrente, como informes, cartas o formularios que se reutilizan año tras año. En los casos de documentos que se imprimen o se presentan con un formato preciso, el desplazamiento de unas pocas líneas puede desordenar el contenido completo.
Una medida práctica antes de que llegue la actualización es revisar qué archivos antiguos se tienen guardados y conservar una copia en PDF de los más importantes. De esa manera, aunque Word reorganice el documento original al abrirlo tras el cambio, existirá una versión disponible que conserve la apariencia inicial.

articles.title: Apple reveals new Mac security controls as AI agents raise privacy risks | TechCrunch
articles.text:
As promised last month, Apple on Monday announced changes to Mac security controls designed to protect users’ data from the growing popularity of AI agents and their apps’ demand for “full disk access.”
“Before granting an app such extraordinary access, users should understand that it puts all of the data on their Mac at risk,” Apple wanred in a new blog post aimed at app developers.
Unlike AI chatbots that simply answer questions, agents run on a user’s device where they can take actions across the operating system, files, and apps on the user’s behalf.
While the tools can be useful, Apple has grown concerned about the increased risks to users’ data and privacy that these AI agents introduce. At the same time, the company has been benefiting from sales of Mac minis and Mac Studio computers that AI early adopters have been purchasing specifically to run their local AI models.
To balance these competing interests, Apple said in October that it would revise some of its security settings around Mac apps. The announcement followed two notable incidents involving AI agents. In one, a journalist claimed that Meta’s Muse app read their private messages without consent; a separate report from Wired cited a flaw in ChatGPT’s Mac app that could have allowed hackers to access sensitive data.
Now, Apple is sharing the changes it’s making.
For starters, it’s splitting up Device Control and Data Access into two settings: System & App Protection Override and Accessibility. The changes is designed to help users better understand that selecting the first option means overriding built-in security protections.
To streamline configurations, Apple says there will now also be a single method for granting permissions that involves selecting the requested app from a list. The company will also introduce new guidance encouraging users to grant access only to the specific apps that need it when they enable the System & App Protection Override setting. Similar guidance will appear when users enable Full Disk Access to allow an app to access their folders.
The company will also provide users with “increased visibility into the wide range of data apps will receive access to or control over if full permissions are granted,” the blog post notes.
Another change will give users more granular control over when an AI agent or app can gain access by allowing users to configure their apps to ask for permission every time access is needed. While arguably tedious and a potential obstacle to true automation, the feature could allow users to experiment with local AI without giving the agent carte blanche.
There will also be a new transparency indicator that appears when an app is controlling another app through the System & App Protection Override option.
The changes, which are arriving with macOS 27.3, don’t appear to prevent Mac users from installing and running AI agents or other apps that ask for higher levels of access. Instead, they give users more nuanced options, control, and information about the choices they’re making.
Apple advises app developers to adjust their onboarding processes to account for the new changes and suggests that their apps learn to “gracefully handle having access to only a limited set of folders or apps.”
Developers of apps that request Full Disk Access for disk backup or to provide assistive technologies can request exceptions to the new rules (which Apple calls “entitlements”) to preserve the same functionality they offered before the macOS 27.3 update.

articles.title: Anthropic says Claude Mythos Preview cut AMD MI355X onboarding from up to 12 months to around three days
articles.text:
Anthropic says Claude Mythos slashed software work to onboard AMD GPUs from up to 12 months to around three days —writing almost 100% of kernels autonomously chips away at Nvidia's CUDA moat
If AI can write the low-level code that ties models to Nvidia, CUDA matters less.
Anthropic told IPO investors that its Claude Mythos Preview model did the software work required to get its AI running on AMD’s GPUs in about three days, with “basically no human intervention,” a job it says used to take six to 12 months. The three days cover prompt processing for one Anthropic model on AMD MI355X GPUs “at a useful level of performance,” with Mythos porting or writing “almost 100% of the kernels.” That kind of low-level code, which ties an AI model to one company’s chips, has long been part of Nvidia’s CUDA moat, and an AI that can write it in days would suggest that moat is eroding.
Tom Brown, Anthropic’s co-founder and chief compute officer, made the time comparison, noting to investors that the original meant using a team of “dozens of engineers.” The company already runs its models on multiple kinds of chips — on GPUs from Nvidia and AMD, Google’s TPUs, and AWS Trainium — and its fleet is managed as “one fungible pool of compute.” Brown called the early multi-chip decision “an unconventional bet.” It may have been a wise one, given that Google’s TPUs can now natively run AI models built in PyTorch, and Meta uses them in production.
Anthropic's claim that the job used to take six to 12 months comes from past work, from its “historical experience bringing up new accelerators using traditional engineering approaches,” where tailoring the code to each hardware platform was a challenge. Removing that onboarding barrier could reduce things to a purchase decision, and Anthropic started working with AMD GPUs for the first time this year, with an agreement for up to 2 gigawatts now in place.
CUDA, Nvidia’s programming platform, is very mature at nearly two decades old. AMD has an equivalent, ROCm, with HIP as its programming layer. Code written for CUDA has to be transformed to work there, and AMD even built a tool called HIPify for the process. There is still a conversion cost to switching, and AMD’s vice president of AI software, Anush Elangovan, told EE Times in April that “Claude is better than HIPify because it has web search built in.”
AMD has been making the argument that AI can write this type of code since August of last year, presenting a research agent that fell short of human experts at the time. In September of that year, AMD CEO Lisa Su said on the Possible podcast that much of AI software is written in CUDA, which needs to be “translated to AMD,” and “a ton of that can now be done in software.”
Moving forward to July earlier this year, AMD’s senior vice president of AI, Vamsi Boppana, said its engineers were using AI models to generate GPU kernels, and Su said that when she asked whether her team was helping the Anthropic engineer working on the MI355X, she was told they didn’t need any help. Boppana said that in some cases, the resulting kernels were even “better than the most manually tuned versions.” Under its July agreement with Anthropic, AMD is also using Claude to optimize workloads for its Instinct GPUs and to speed up ROCm development.
At AMD’s Advancing AI event in July, OpenAI’s Philippe Tillet said that once OpenAI got its Helios racks, a single engineer confirmed everything worked within a few days, and that “agents are taking over our jobs, in a sense, as kernel engineers.” Before the event, AMD’s Andrew Dieckman, corporate vice president and general manager of the company’s data center GPU business, told reporters that he has had practically zero conversations with AMD’s customers about CUDA.
| Date | Who | What they said or showed | Where | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Aug. 1, 2025 | AMD researchers | Published GEAK, an AI agent that writes GPU kernels; against 30 expert-written kernels it got 19 right, at 0.92 times the experts’ speed on average | AMD’s ROCm blog | 
| Sept. 24, 2025 | Lisa Su, AMD chair and CEO | Asked about AI coding tools, said much of the code written for CUDA can now be translated to AMD in software: “We’re using software to significantly optimize our customers’ code so that they can run on AMD” | Possible podcast | 
| April 1, 2026 | Anush Elangovan, AMD vice president of AI software | Compared Claude with HIPify, AMD’s tool for converting CUDA code: “Claude is better than HIPify because it has web search built in” | EE Times interview | 
| April 15, 2026 | Jensen Huang, Nvidia CEO | “We use a ton of AI to create the kernels that we have”; “nobody knows our architecture better than we do” | Dwarkesh Patel interview | 
| July 23, 2026 | Andrew Dieckman, AMD corporate vice president and general manager, data center GPU business | “I have almost zero conversations with our customers about CUDA at this point in time” | PC Gamer, from a pre-event AMD briefing | 
| July 23, 2026 | Vamsi Boppana, AMD senior vice president of AI | AI-assisted GPU programming will “remove any remaining barriers to broad adoption” | AMD Advancing AI keynote | 
| July 23, 2026 | Philippe Tillet, OpenAI | “agents are taking over our jobs, in a sense, as kernel engineers” | AMD Advancing AI keynote | 
| July 23, 2026 | Tom Brown, Anthropic co-founder and chief compute officer | One engineer asked Claude to bring up an MI355X rack and left it running “over the weekend” | AMD Advancing AI keynote | 
| Nov. 10, 2026 | Tom Brown, Anthropic co-founder and chief compute officer | Mythos “got Claude running on AMD in just three days with basically no human intervention”; the slide footnote limits the three days to prompt processing for one model | Anthropic’s IPO roadshow video | 
Until this week, though, all of this came from AMD or its stage, not from Anthropic to its own investors. Anthropic buys the chips rather than selling them, and it’s heading into its IPO next week, so its multi-chip approach — now with at least some numbers to back it up — carries more weight than a chipmaker’s claims. Its prospectus says it in writing, too, though without a number: “We can onboard new chip platforms in a fraction of the time it once took.”
| Where Anthropic said it | Who did the work | How long | What it covered | What it replaced | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AMD’s Advancing AI keynote, July 23 | One engineer and Claude | Not stated; left running “over the weekend” | Its “leading model” on an MI355X rack, with performance climbing | What it called “a big effort” | 
| IPO roadshow video, narration, Nov. 10 | Mythos, with “basically no human intervention” | Three days (“in just three days”) | Getting “Claude running on AMD”; Claude “ported or wrote almost 100% of the kernels” | Work that “took dozens of engineers months” | 
| IPO roadshow video, slide footnote, Nov. 10 | Claude Mythos Preview | About three days (“~3 day timeline”) | Bringing up “prompt processing for one Anthropic model on AMD MI355X GPUs at a useful level of performance” | Six to 12 months (“~6-12-month estimate”), from “historical experience bringing up new accelerators” | 
| Prospectus (S-1/A No. 2), Nov. 10 | Its engineering teams, “leveraging Claude” | No figure; “more quickly” | Bringing “new chip platforms into production”; no chip named | What it calls “intense engineering effort over many months” | 
The prompt processing (prefill) part of the workload is the step where a model reads and processes what it’s been given before it starts replying, and Anthropic hasn’t said whether the replying step (decode) was included as well. Anthropic’s chart, with its axis labeled “Time to onboard new silicon,” shows both lines reaching the same “~100%” mark without saying 100% of what. The company also hasn’t said how fast the model ran on AMD’s GPUs versus Nvidia’s, and that’s the comparison we want to see to show whether AMD’s chips, running AI-written code, can match Nvidia silicon.
On the other hand, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in an April interview with Dwarkesh Patel that Nvidia already uses AI on its own kernels and knows its chips best — “nobody knows our architecture better than we do” — and can get the most out of them. Asked why labs like Anthropic use other accelerators, he called Anthropic “a unique instance, not a trend.” Nvidia and AMD, among seven companies, are buying $26.0 billion of Anthropic’s stock at the IPO price, so Nvidia is investing in the very company Huang called the exception.
In late July, SemiAnalysis published an article, “Can AMD break the CUDA Moat?,” which essentially said that software creation is not the same moat it was even a year ago. That said, the catch for AMD is that with agentic coding, “each agent requires GPUs to test their code against,” which means that the AI writing the code still needs the hardware. It has found a constant lack of GPUs inside AMD for this type of development, which has held AMD back and may be a new bottleneck.
That leaves CUDA’s moat somewhere in between. Getting a model running on a new chip, once the expensive part, appears to be getting cheaper, and better AI may wear down Nvidia’s claim that it knows its hardware best. As for Anthropic’s fungible pool, the chips in it aren’t fully interchangeable — Google’s TPUs are increasingly specialized, for example — and getting the most out of any of them still takes the hardware to test on. The moat is narrowing, but is not gone.
Anthropic’s first AMD MI450 chips, in Helios racks, are expected in the first half of 2027. That’s a new generation and an opportunity to see if the three-day bring-up can be repeated. Anthropic’s IPO comes sooner, after which it will report as a public company.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.

articles.title: « Ce n'est pas un PC » : Microsoft précise la nature de sa prochaine Xbox Helix
articles.text:
Microsoft tranche : la prochaine Xbox, nom de code Helix, est une console capable de lancer des jeux PC, pas un PC qui accepte aussi les jeux console. Le message est clair, le mode d’emploi, lui, reste flou.
Dans un entretien publié dans le magazine du 25ème anniversaire de la marque, Jason Ronald, vice-président Next Generation chez Xbox, dit vouloir lever l’ambiguïté qui entoure Project Helix depuis des mois. Cette clarification de positionnement ne répond toutefois pas à la question que se posent les joueurs : comment, concrètement, ces jeux PC tourneront-ils sur la machine ?
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Une console d’abord, avec des réglages de PC en option
C’est Windows Central qui a relevé la formule la plus nette de Jason Ronald : « Helix est conçue comme une console capable aussi de faire tourner des jeux PC. Ce n’est pas un PC capable également de faire tourner des jeux console. » Beaucoup avaient compris l’inverse, à force d’entendre que la machine accueillerait les jeux PC.
L’objectif affiché : un accès simple, intuitif et instantané aux jeux. Ronald précise que les joueurs exigeants pourront malgré tout accéder à un niveau de personnalisation plus poussé, sur les réglages comme sur les options de performance. Autrement dit, la console promet la simplicité par défaut et laisse la porte ouverte aux bidouilleurs.
Reste le flou : Windows Central note que la formule « Des jeux provenant de votre PC » ne dit rien du fonctionnement réel. Ronald n’a pas non plus précisé si des plateformes comme Steam seraient prises en charge. Et la nuance de vocabulaire ne dit pas si l’on parlera d’un système fermé ou d’un système ouvert à la Windows.
La ROG Xbox Ally sert de brouillon, mais Helix aura sa propre interface
Ronald présente la ROG Xbox Ally et son Xbox Mode comme un « précurseur » de Helix, nourri par les retours des joueurs. L’intégration de plusieurs bibliothèques de jeux et de plusieurs types de commandes a, dit-il, « fondamentalement informé et modifié » les plans de Microsoft pour la future console.
Pour autant, l’interface de Helix aura sa propre identité, tout en reprenant les leçons déjà testées. Windows Central en déduit que la console n’héritera pas telle quelle du Xbox Mode livré sur les PC actuels. L’ambition, elle, est de proposer une expérience « très Xbox » quel que soit l’écran : télévision, portable ou PC.
Côté héritage, Ronald évoque quatre générations de bibliothèque Xbox et de progression, disponibles instantanément. Un engagement dans la lignée de la rétrocompatibilité visée par Helix, dont le périmètre se précise au fil des déclarations.
Le rendu neuronal doit compenser une facture de composants qui grimpe
Ronald assure que la prochaine génération ne se définira ni par la 8K ni par les 240 Hz, mais par l’innovation de gameplay et l’immersion. Pour y arriver sans gonfler la puissance brute, Microsoft mise sur le rendu neuronal, « une manière entièrement nouvelle de générer une image » sans davantage de puissance de calcul ni de mémoire. On suppose qu’il s’agit d’upscaling, de génération d’images et de reconstruction du ray tracing par IA, sans que l’entretien le précise.
Le contexte pèse : la crise des composants renchérit le matériel, et Ronald reconnaît devoir arbitrer entre progrès technique et accessibilité tarifaire. Aucun prix ni date de sortie n’est annoncé. Les kits de développement alpha sont attendus en 2027.
Un discours rassurant, donc, sur le papier. Mais tant que Microsoft n’aura pas dit comment ces jeux PC arrivent sur la machine, « ce n’est pas un PC » restera surtout un slogan.
- La rétrocompatibilité au top
- Le Quick Resume, difficile de revenir en arrière
- Taillée pour l'avenir (HDMI 2.1, dolby vision/atmos, VRR)

articles.title: Former Freshworks executives founded AI native CRM startup Dreamteam raises $53M in funding
articles.text:
Former Freshworks executives-founded AI startup Dreamteam raises $53M
Dreamteam raised this funding from Together Fund, Accel and Premji Invest and this capital will be primarily used to enhance its tech platform
Dreamteam, an AI native customer relationship management (CRM) startup founded by former executives of Freshworks, has raised $53 million in funding from Together Fund, Accel and Premji Invest.
Founded in 2025 by Anand Venkatraman, Ramesh Parthasarathy and Senthil Kanthaswamy with headquarters in California and core engineering team in Chennai, is building a technology platform that can understand customer context and have the right AI coworkers to execute.
“The CRM was supposed to give companies a complete picture of their customers, yet the richest parts of that picture have always lived outside the CRM,” said Anand Venkatraman, Co-founder and CEO of Dreamteam.
“AI finally gives us a way to change that foundation. Dreamteam learns from the work your team is already doing, keeps the context alive and gives every salesperson skilled AI teammates that can reason over it and move deals forward. Your sellers and leaders can spend their time on relationships, judgement and closing deals, while Dreamteam takes care of everything required around them,” he said.
According to a statement from Dreamteam, companies across diverse industries, including AI, online media, healthcare, manufacturing, and consulting are using their technology platform.
Girish Mathrubootham, Founding partner at Together Fund, the first institutional investor in Dreamteam added: “CRM is among the biggest software categories ripe for disruption. I've worked alongside Dreamteam's founders since day one as their vision for an AI-native CRM took shape. Their deep CRM expertise and proven record of scaling enterprise software make them uniquely positioned to lead this reinvention.”
Looking ahead, Dreamteam aims to extend its intelligence layer beyond sales to the entire customer lifecycle, including prospecting, onboarding, customer success and upselling. The company also offers Magic Apps, which allows business users to create custom applications and dashboards using natural language without writing code.
Shekhar Kirani, Partner at Accel said, “In the AI era, the companies that understand their customers deeply have an enormous advantage. Today, everyone on a team sees a different version of the customer, because no central system holds all the information. Dreamteam is building that system with AI agents.”

articles.title: La justicia italiana interviene a Revolut por fallos en sus sistemas de prevención del blanqueo de capitales en sus cuentas
articles.text:
Revolut basó su modelo de crecimiento en la facilidad para operar online, de forma automática y con la posibilidad de operar con criptodivisas ha encontrado en esa agilidad operativa su mayor problema con la justicia europea.
Tal y como ha adelantado Reuters en exclusiva, un tribunal de Milán ha decidido poner bajo supervisión a su filial italiana durante un año. La justicia italiana no acusa a la entidad de colaborar con el blanqueo de capitales para la mafia, pero le reprocha que sus controles no frenaron los movimientos de dinero sospechoso de ciertos clientes.
Un año bajo administración judicial. El Tribunal de Milán ha puesto a la sucursal italiana de Revolut Bank UAB bajo administración judicial durante un año. La Fiscalía sostiene que fallos en los sistemas antiblanqueo de la entidad bancaria ayudaron a mover, ocultar o desviar capitales por valor de 76,5 millones de euros. Con controles bien aplicados, esas operaciones se habrían podido frenar a tiempo e iniciar el rastreo de su origen.
La medida se ejecutará bajo la supervisión de la la Guardia di Finanza y se ampara en el artículo 34 del Código Antimafia. Según recoge el italiano Il Giorno, dos administradores judiciales, abordarán las deficiencias en los controles contra el blanqueo de capitales. El Tribunal les ha encomendado llevar a cabo una lista de 15 acciones, entre las que se incluyen asistir a las reuniones de dirección, acceder a las actas y resultados de las auditorías internas, presentar informes periódicos, verificar a los beneficiarios finales de las cuentas y actualizar los procedimientos antiblanqueo.
Lo que dice la Fiscalía. De acuerdo a lo publicado por MilanoToday, la fiscalía italiana asegura que la medida de control a la filiar italiana de Revolut se debe a "la reiteración y la heterogeneidad de los casos comprobados han mostrado la inidoneidad de las medidas adoptadas en concreto para prevenir el uso de la infraestructura bancaria por parte de sujetos insertados en circuitos ilícitos".
Antes, una inspección antiblanqueo ya había detectado más de un millón de infracciones en la verificación de clientes y la conservación de datos. También hubo fallos sistemáticos al comunicar operaciones sospechosas de blanqueo de capitales.
Cientos de avisos y ninguno de Revolut. Entre 2023 y 2024, 24 clientes residentes en el área de Milán estaban implicados en procesos por delitos relevantes. Según recoge El Mundo, en ese periodo otros bancos enviaron 112 comunicaciones de operaciones sospechosas sobre esas personas investigadas. Revolut no mandó ninguna sobre sus movimientos.
Tal y como subraya el Corriere della Sera, Revolut Italia no está investigada por ningún delito de carácter económico o fiscal, sino que la justicia italiana pone en duda la eficiencia de sus sistemas de detección del fraude. La entidad dijo en un comunicado al que ha tenido acceso El Mundo, que " "Nos tomamos muy en serio nuestras obligaciones normativas y los controles contra el blanqueo de capitales. Invertimos constantemente en reforzar nuestros sistemas de prevención de delitos financieros, nuestros modelos de supervisión de transacciones y los equipos especializados en cumplimiento normativo en todos los mercados en los que operamos".

articles.title: Ils savent où vous habitez : les noms et adresses de 22 millions de Français volés chez La Poste
articles.text:
Fuite de données La Poste : les noms et adresses de 22 millions de Français volés, des courriers ont pu être lus
“Maileva, plateforme de confiance numérique”
Pendant deux mois, la cyberattaque contre Maileva, la filiale qui imprime et poste le courrier de milliers d'entreprises, est restée dans l'ombre. La Poste admet maintenant que les noms et adresses de 22 millions de personnes ont été volés. Et dans certaines enveloppes, les pirates ont pu lire bien davantage : un loyer, une facture, une dette d'hôpital.
Le groupe La Poste a reconnu le 15 novembre que Maileva, filiale de sa branche numérique Docaposte, avait subi mi-septembre une cyberattaque d'ampleur. Les pirates sont repartis avec le nom, le prénom et l'adresse postale de 22 millions de personnes, soit près d'un Français sur trois. Les victimes sont les destinataires des lettres que Maileva imprime et expédie pour ses clients : bulletins de paie, quittances de loyer, factures, recommandés. Beaucoup n'avaient jamais entendu parler de l'entreprise. Le parquet de Paris a confié l'enquête à la brigade de lutte contre la cybercriminalité (BL2C).
Ce que les pirates ont trouvé dans les enveloppes
Officiellement, seules les données d'identification ont fuité. Le groupe postal glisse pourtant une précision lourde de sens : le contenu des courriers relève de ses clients, à qui il revient de prévenir leurs propres destinataires.
	
Le contenu des informations présentes dans les documents n'appartient pas à Maileva mais relève de la relation entre les clients de Maileva et leurs propres clients destinataires de ces documents.
Les premiers expéditeurs à sortir du bois donnent la mesure du problème. Le bailleur social Flandre Opale Habitat évoque des courriers envoyés sur dix ans, avec des informations sur le logement et des montants de factures. L'hôpital Foch, à Suresnes, a averti ses patients que des relances d'impayés expédiées entre le 9 et le 23 septembre mentionnaient le numéro de facture, la date des soins et la somme due.
Rien ne dit que tous les clients de Maileva soient touchés, mais la liste donne le vertige. L'entreprise revendique plus de 20 000 clients, parmi lesquels de grandes banques, des assureurs, des opérateurs télécoms, la SNCF et des laboratoires médicaux, selon Next. Le scénario rappelle celui d'Engie, dont les clients ont été exposés fin octobre par la fuite d'un prestataire : le maillon faible se trouve souvent chez un sous-traitant dont personne ne connaît le nom.
Deux mois de silence, et maintenant le risque d'arnaques
Le calendrier interroge. Les sites spécialisés Cyberattaque.org et FrenchBreaches ont signalé l'incident dès le 24 septembre, et Maileva a coupé ses services pendant six jours. La reconnaissance publique n'est venue qu'à la mi-novembre, une fois la presse lancée sur l'affaire. La CNIL a été notifiée et une plainte déposée. Le groupe avait déjà essuyé en décembre 2025 une attaque par déni de service qui avait paralysé ses services en ligne, sans vol de données cette fois.
Aucune coordonnée bancaire n'a fuité. Mais un nom, une adresse et l'identité de votre créancier suffisent à fabriquer une fausse relance très convaincante. Les escrocs savent exploiter une adresse postale : en 2021, après une fuite chez Ledger, ils avaient envoyé par la poste de faux portefeuilles piégés à leurs victimes.
Dans les semaines qui viennent, méfiez-vous de toute lettre, de tout SMS ou de tout appel qui réclame le règlement urgent d'un loyer ou d'une facture. Vérifiez directement auprès de l'organisme, par un numéro ou un espace client que vous connaissez déjà. Les faux conseillers et les messages personnalisés sont devenus la forme la plus redoutable du phishing après une fuite. La Poste ne propose pour l'instant aucun moyen de savoir si son nom figure dans le fichier.

articles.title: New WinPOPBit tool bypasses Windows 11 CPU restrictions to support truly ancient PCs
articles.text:
In brief: Unlike previous releases, Windows 11 significantly limits the number of systems on which users can attempt to install the new operating system. Needless to say, some developers have recognized Microsoft's challenge and raised the stakes considerably.
A new open-source utility is bringing the latest Windows editions to places where Microsoft developers dared not go. Initially released a few weeks ago, WinPOPBit is designed to "pop" some of the most restrictive hardware requirements in newer Windows 11 versions. The project is progressing rapidly, which means even more ancient CPUs could soon become "compatible" with the latest PC operating systems.
WinPOPBit primarily targets Windows 11's requirement for CPUs with POPCNT and SSE4.2 instruction support, as well as Windows 10's NX bit requirement. Microsoft introduced the new CPU requirements with the Windows 11 24H2 update, preventing OS enthusiasts from installing the latest release on PCs still running decades-old processors.
Despite acknowledging these new "hard" CPU requirements, WinPOPBit's developers have found a way to restore compatibility. The Python tool is essentially an "experimental patcher" capable of modifying a few relevant bytes in Windows system files, allowing newer OS releases to boot and run on CPUs that date back to before Windows 7 was even a thing.
 – Bob Pony (@TheBobPony) November 7, 2026
WinPOPBit is designed to directly patch binary files that host the Windows NT kernel (ntoskrnl.exe), the system boot loaders (winload.efi and winload.exe), and several additional DLL files. The developers explain that Windows 11 24H2 and newer versions check for POPCNT and SSE4.2 CPU support but do not actually require these newer instructions for 99% of their files. Meanwhile, Windows 10 primarily requires the NX bit for its innermost, ring 0-level kernel code.
WinPOPBit has already restored Windows 11 and Windows 10 compatibility on some truly ancient x86 processors, including AMD's Athlon II and Intel's Pentium 4 "Northwood" CPU from 2002. Now, the developers are working to expand the tool's capabilities even further, bringing support to increasingly old hardware.
The latest code commits could allow Windows 10 and Windows 11 23H2 to run on AMD systems based on Socket 754, 940, and 939, as well as AM2-based CPUs from the AMD K8 family. The upcoming WinPOPBit release should also force Windows 11 to boot on the Athlon 64. You heard that right: thanks to a third-party Python script, hardware enthusiasts may soon be able to install a modern 64-bit Windows release on AMD's first 64-bit processor, released in 2003.
Additionally, WinPOPBit is expected to support patched versions of Windows 10 and Windows 11 23H2 on Intel LGA 775 systems, including those powered by Pentium 4 "Prescott" and Pentium D "Smithfield" processors. Using the tool isn't for the faint of heart, and the WinPOPBit developers clearly state that Microsoft will not provide official support for this kind of tinkering.

articles.title: Onde roda GTA 6? Confira os requisitos para console • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Onde roda GTA 6? Confira os requisitos para console
O GTA 6 está chegando aos consoles de nova geração, como PS5 e Xbox Series X/S, mas sua versão para PC deve estrear apenas em algum momento de 2027
O aguardado GTA 6 chega oficialmente aos consoles PS5 e Xbox Series X/S após 13 anos desde o último título da franquia. O novo título da Rockstar Games promete revolucionar o mundo dos games com um mapa imersivo e gráficos ultrarrealistas.
Entre os hardwares compatíveis, o PS5 Pro se destaca como a melhor opção para quem busca máxima fidelidade gráfica, fluidez e outros recursos. Já a chegada do GTA 6 no PC ainda exigirá paciência, pois a versão deve demorar mais alguns meses para sair.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog te mostra a lista de requisitos e detalhes de desempenho do GTA 6 nas plataformas disponíveis.
O GTA 6 está disponível nativamente para consoles da atual geração, como PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X/S, e em certos dispositivos via streaming. Conforme a Rockstar, o jogo terá desempenho travado em 30 quadros por segundo (fps), garantindo fluidez visual estável em todas essas plataformas.
| Plataforma | Qualidade | 
|---|---|
| PlayStation 5 | Versão nativa | 
| PlayStation 5 Pro | Versão nativa aprimorada | 
| PS Portal | Via PS Remote Play | 
| Xbox Series X | Versão nativa | 
| Xbox Series S | Versão nativa com recursos limitados | 
| Xbox One | Via Cloud Gaming | 
| PC | Versão nativa (ainda não anunciada) | 
Até o momento, a versão para PC segue sem data oficial de lançamento divulgada pela Rockstar Games. Além disso, a desenvolvedora não confirmou planos de levar o título ao console híbrido Nintendo Switch 2.
O PS5 Pro entrega a melhor qualidade visual para GTA 6 com reflexos realistas (ray tracing) e imagens mais nítidas via inteligência artificial (PSSR), embora ainda rode com 30 fps. Segundo a Rockstar Games, a família PlayStation oferece imersão superior pelos carregamentos rápidos, áudio espacial e às respostas táteis do controle DualSense.
O PS5 padrão e o Xbox Series X mantêm um nível gráfico equivalente entre as plataformas. Já o Xbox Series S vai rodar GTA 6 com cortes na resolução e nos detalhes visuais para preservar a estabilidade por conta do hardware mais limitado.
O Xbox One roda GTA 6 exclusivamente via Xbox Cloud Gaming com qualidade visual equivalente ao Xbox Series S, enquanto o antigo Xbox 360 fica de fora. Sem a necessidade da instalação local devido ao processamento nos servidores da Microsoft, é indispensável ter uma internet rápida e estável para evitar atrasos ou falhas na imagem.
Para jogar GTA 6 dessa forma, é obrigatório comprá-lo separadamente, já que ele não faz parte do catálogo padrão do Xbox Game Pass. Além da cópia do jogo, o usuário precisa de uma assinatura com tempo de nuvem incluso ou adquirir horas avulsas do serviço.
Não, o GTA 6 não roda no PlayStation 4 ou PlayStation 3, pois ele foi desenvolvido exclusivamente para a nova geração de consoles. Ou seja, não há possibilidade de comprar e instalar o jogo localmente nestes aparelhos mais antigos.
Não há especificações oficiais para GTA 6 no PC, pois o título está previsto para chegar ao computador em algum momento de 2027. O game deve estrear em lojas digitais como Steam, Epic Games e no próprio aplicativo da Rockstar.
Com base no poder dos consoles atuais, estima-se que os requisitos mínimos de GTA 6 exijam um processador (CPU) de 6 núcleos, 16 GB de memória RAM, armazenamento SSD e uma placa de vídeo (GPU) com 8 GB de memória dedicada (VRAM).
Para quem deseja aproveitar o GTA 6 com resoluções mais altas e gráficos no máximo, a máquina “perfeita” deve ter uma CPU de 8 núcleos, 32 GB de RAM, SSD NVMe ultrarrápido e GPU com 12 GB de VRAM.
O GTA 6 exige até 212 GB de armazenamento livre, embora o tamanho exato dos arquivos de instalação possa variar ligeiramente conforme o console escolhido. Confira no quadro abaixo a estimativa de espaço que você precisa reservar no SSD de cada plataforma antes do download.
| Plataforma | Quantidade de armazenamento | 
|---|---|
| PlayStation 5/PS5 Pro | Mínimo de 212 GB. | 
| Xbox Series X / Series S | Acima de 212 GB, dependendo do console. | 
Além desse volume inicial para baixar o jogo base, vale manter uma folga extra na memória interna do videogame ou computador para futuras atualizações e patches de correções.

articles.title: Microsoft outage explained: a three-month-old bug's global impact
articles.text:
Microsoft has finally explained what caused last week’s massive outage, which disrupted businesses and governments worldwide.
The Microsoft 365 outage, which started on Nov. 12 and continued until the morning of Nov. 14, was caused by a combination of issues, including a defect introduced in a July 2026 patch.
Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents, and Platform, took to Twitter/X to share the details behind the outage. First, Lamanna noted that “a latent defect caused servers to become overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions.” Notably, Lamanna said the defect was the “result of a fix that was prepared specifically for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers” and didn’t impact broader Windows deployments.
The defect was introduced in July, but did not cause any issues until now. Moreover, Lamanna said the defect wasn’t detected by Microsoft’s internal tests, which focused on “weaker hardware SKUs with fewer cores.” The defect, however, was “worsened on machines with more cores and newer hardware.”
The second issue Lamanna highlighted was a surge in load caused by a Teams issue that happened roughly 15 hours before the Microsoft 365 outage. Lamanna explained that Microsoft maintains multiple network gateway systems for its services so that if there’s an issue with one, there’s a fallback. The Teams issue caused it to move to the same gateway used for Exchange Online (which powers email services like Outlook), significantly increasing the load on that gateway.
Finally, Lamanna said that “nearly 14% of server capacity for the networking gateway was out of service due to an unrelated issue from the previous day.”
Combined, these issues triggered the July defect, leading requests to build up until servers ultimately stopped responding in the midst of North America’s peak traffic window. Worse, Microsoft’s traffic management systems respond to outages like this by automatically routing traffic to healthy servers. But that caused the July bug to trigger again, resulting in multiple servers failing — at the worst point, over 80 per cent of the company’s servers were unresponsive.
Lamanna explained that recovery took longer than usual because as servers came back online, waiting traffic immediately overwhelmed them again, causing the July defect to trigger and make the servers unresponsive. And since the bug was several months old, Microsoft wasn’t able to quickly revert the change. Instead, the company had to patch the bug, restart the servers in batches, and slowly bring things back online.
Microsoft is expected to publish a final post-incident report on Nov. 20, which will likely include more details about the cause of this outage. Still, the fact that this outage happened is cause for concern, and yet another valid reason for getting off U.S. tech. At the very least, Microsoft should be held accountable for the mess this caused — perhaps a Canadian law firm will do just that.

articles.title: 370 Bücher in 20 Monaten: Wie eine Autorin ihre Werke mit ChatGPT, Claude und Grok schreibt
articles.text:
370 Bücher in 20 Monaten: Wie eine Autorin ihre Werke mit KI schreibt – und wie sie dafür kritisiert wird
Schon seit einigen Monaten ist die Autorin Coral Hart Gesprächsthema in der Welt der Literatur. Denn sie ist eines der öffentlichen Gesichter der KI-Ära des kreativen Schreibens. Im Gegensatz zu vielen anderen Autor:innen, die ihre Werke mit KI schreiben, aber ihre Nutzung verheimlichen, geht Hart offen damit um. Sie stellt sich trotz eines Pseudonyms der Öffentlichkeit und damit auch der Kritik.
Wie 370 Bücher in 20 Monaten entstehen
Wie sie bei ihrer Arbeit vorgeht, hat sie jetzt in einem Interview mit AFP (via Yahoo News) verraten. Bevor sie mit der KI-Nutzung begann, hatte Hart schon 14 Jahre Erfahrung als Autorin und hat 96 eigene Werke ganz ohne Tool-Hilfe geschrieben. Da sie sich mit KI nicht auskannte, probierte sie im Verlauf von mehreren Monaten zahlreiche Modelle aus, um sich ein Framework zu errichten, das in der Lage ist, Bücher zu schreiben.
Mittlerweile wechselt sie zwischen mehreren Modellen hin und her. Die einzelnen Tools haben ihrer Meinung nach ihre eigenen Vor- und Nachteile. So soll ChatGPT etwa besonders gut bei Dialogen sein, aber bei Prosa versagen. Claude nutzt sie hingegen für Story-Strukturen. Grok kommt ins Spiel, um ihren Romance-Büchern „scharfe Szenen“ hinzuzufügen, da der Chatbot von xAI „komplett enthemmt“ ist.
Hart sagt dazu: „Wenn du sagst: ‚ChatGPT, schreib mir ein Buch‘ oder ‚Claude, schreib mir ein Buch‘, bekommst du eine brennende Müllhalde, weil die KI nichts hat, um damit arbeiten zu können.“ Als sie mit ihrer KI-Arbeit begann, hat sie sich Absatz für Absatz mit den Tools an der Story-Idee des Buches entlanggehangelt. Das hätte etwa zwei bis drei Prompts in Anspruch genommen. Mittlerweile kann sie ganze Entwürfe für Bücher mit den Prompts und Mitteln erstellen, die sie im Laufe der Monate erlernt hat.
Die Entwürfe sind aber weit entfernt von finalen Büchern. Sie müssen einen mehrstufigen Bearbeitungsprozess durchlaufen, der ebenfalls durch KI realisiert wird. Dabei werden etwa Kontinuitätsfehler in der Geschichte, unvollständige Charakterentwicklungen und Plot-Holes behoben. Zu guter Letzt muss noch ein Mensch über die KI-Bücher schauen und sicherstellen, dass keine „KI-Anzeichen durchgerutscht sind.“
Wie KI-Bücher zum Geschäft werden
Hart hat allein 2026 mehr als eine Million Bücher verkauft und damit etwas mehr als eine Million US-Dollar verdient. Das ist aber nur ein Teil des Geschäfts, das sie betreibt. Sie hat mittlerweile die „Coral Hart Group“ gegründet, die Menschen beim Prozess des Buchschreibens mit KI begleiten soll. Seit Launch sollen mehr als 2.400 Autor:innen betreut worden sein.
Die KI-Autorin bietet über die Plattform an, Bücher von einer ersten Idee in fertige Werke zu verwandeln. Kund:innen erhalten hochladbare Bücher mit einer Länge von bis zu 50.000 Wörtern. Ein einziges Buch kostet dabei 260 Dollar. Kund:innen, die mit ihrer Idee in Serie gehen wollen, bekommen einen Rabatt. So kostet etwa eine Buchreihe mit neun Teilen knapp 1.900 Dollar.
Ihr Geschäft wird dabei nicht von allen Literaturenthusiasten geschätzt. Im Interview verriet die Autorin, dass sie im Laufe der Zeit mehrere Tausend Hassnachrichten und sogar Todesdrohungen erhalten hat. Dazu sagt sie: „Ich habe mich dazu entschieden, diejenige zu sein, die vortritt und sagt, dass wir diese Konversation jetzt haben müssen.“ Sie ist überzeugt, dass die KI-Ära in der Literatur gekommen ist, um zu bleiben: „Das Ganze wird nicht einfach wieder ausgeschaltet oder abgestöpselt, weil ein paar Autoren es so wollen.“

articles.title: El primer monitor 5K2K de 39 pulgadas del mundo también se suma al Black Friday con un descuentazo de 500 euros
articles.text:
En el pasado mes de mayo, os contábamos cómo LG lanzaba su nuevo UltraGear OLED 39GX950B-B, el primer monitor de 39 pulgadas con doble resolución 5K2K. Lo hizo con un precio por encima de los 1.700 euros, pero ahora que estamos en Black Friday, lo tenemos disponible con una rebaja considerable en Amazon: cuesta 1.299 euros (también en PcComponentes).
Monitor gaming LG UltraGear OLED 39GX950B-B - 39'', 5K2K (5120 x 2160) | 165 Hz, 0,03 ms, DP 2,2, Inclinación (eje horizontal) / Altura / Giro (eje vertical), NVIDIA G-Sync, Dual Mode 165Hz/330Hz
Un monitor con doble resolución y panel OLED
Es evidente que sigue siendo un precio elevado para un monitor, pero son casi 500 euros de descuento con respecto a lo que costaba hace tan solo unos meses. Estamos ante un monitor ultrawide que destaca por varias cosas, aunque lo mejor sin duda es su doble resolución. ¿Y eso qué significa? Que, pulsando un botón, podemos elegir tener un monitor con resolución 5K o resolución 2K.
Esto es muy útil porque nos da mucha versatilidad. Con resolución 5K podemos tener una imagen más nítida a la hora de jugar, así como a la hora de trabajar (esta resolución es ideal para leer o escribir). Así, la tasa de refresco del monitor es de 165 Hz. Si preferimos una mayor fluidez (por ejemplo, para juegos competitivos), podemos cambiar a 2K con una tasa de refresco de 330 Hz. En ambos casos, el tiempo de respuesta es de 0,03 ms.
A todo esto, debemos sumarle que estamos ante un monitor con panel OLED. Eso se traduce en que tendremos un negro puro y un contraste sobresaliente, algo que agradeceremos especialmente en títulos single player o de terror. Para terminar, cabe destacar que este LG cuenta con un puerto USB-C de carga de 90 W y compatibilidad tanto con G-Sync como con FreeSync Premium Pro.

articles.title: Plusieurs armées européennes s'équipent en drones français Parrot, avec des contrats jamais annoncés jusqu'ici
articles.text:
Les drones militaires français de Parrot continuent de séduire en Europe. L'entreprise annonce ce lundi plus de 10 millions d'euros de commandes de micro-drones ANAFI UKR, en cours de livraison auprès de plusieurs armées du Vieux continent.
Le fabricant français Parrot a annoncé, ce lundi 16 novembre 2026, que plus de 10 millions d'euros de commandes de son micro-drone militaire ANAFI UKR sont en cours de livraison au quatrième trimestre. Elles proviennent de plusieurs programmes d'équipement de forces de défense européennes remportés cette année, et pour partie de l'OTAN. Elles s'ajoutent à une série de contrats qui, depuis février, ont fait de ce petit drone de reconnaissance le principal moteur de la croissance du groupe tricolore.
L'ANAFI UKR, un micro-drone français qui sait voler sans GPS et sans faire de bruit
Pour situer l’engin, l'ANAFI UKR est un micro-drone de moins d'un kilo, pensé à partir de ce que la guerre en Ukraine a appris aux armées. Avec sa batterie longue durée XLR, il peut rester en l'air jusqu'à 50 minutes, selon Parrot. Surtout, il ne perd pas le nord quand l'ennemi brouille le GPS, une pratique devenue courante sur le front. Sa caméra et une intelligence artificielle embarquée prennent alors le relais pour le guider à partir de ce qu'il voit. Son rôle est de servir d'yeux aux soldats, ce que les militaires appellent l'ISR, pour renseignement, surveillance et reconnaissance.
Ce sont justement ces missions que les nouvelles livraisons doivent renforcer, dans plusieurs pays européens que Parrot ne nomme pas. Les commandes s'inscrivent dans des programmes d'équipement d'une durée d'un à trois ans. Certaines découlent de contrats signés avec des clients européens de la défense, qui n'avaient jamais été rendus publics.
Le reste passe par la NSPA, la fameuse centrale d'achat de l'OTAN, qui si vous avez bonne mémoire avait fait entrer l'ANAFI UKR dans son catalogue en mars. Il s'agit cette fois de commandes complémentaires, venues alimenter des programmes déjà lancés. Et autant dire que les besoins ne faiblissent pas. Chris Roberts, Chief Revenue Officer de Parrot, confirme aujourd'hui une « adoption croissante d'ANAFI UKR par les forces de défense ».
Finlande, OTAN, blindés : les drones Parrot enchaînent les galons
L'annonce arrive presque pour boucler une année déjà copieuse et évidemment réussie pour Parrot. En février, la Finlande, fidèle aux drones français depuis plusieurs années, signait pour environ 15 millions d'euros d'ANAFI UKR. L'OTAN suivait en mars, puis un programme européen de véhicules blindés étalé sur dix ans en mai. Pas plus tard qu'en octobre, Parrot annonçait aussi près de 2 millions de dollars de commandes sur l'UAS Marketplace, la plateforme d'achat lancée par l'US Army.
Au troisième trimestre, le chiffre d'affaires du groupe a d'ailleurs grimpé de 40 %, à 23,7 millions d'euros, et les 81 millions cumulés sur neuf mois dépassent déjà tout l'exercice 2025. Parrot vise plus de 20 millions d'euros de ventes de micro-drones d'ici fin décembre, ce qui porterait cette activité autour de 80 millions d'euros sur l'année. Elle en prend le chemin.
Avec le recul, on se dit qu'en 2019, après plusieurs années difficiles, Parrot a peut-être bien fait de renoncer, vampirisé par le géant chinois DJI, à ses mini-drones grand public, lui qui avait lancé l'AR.Drone. Le groupe fondé en 1994 par Henri Seydoux s'est alors recentré sur les professionnels. Sept ans plus tard, ses drones ont quitté les rayons des magasins pour les casernes et les forces armées, avec succès qui plus est.

articles.title: Three small failures combined to take down Microsoft 365
articles.text:
A hidden defect in Microsoft’s cloud gateway, dormant since July, was to blame for one of the largest outages in the company’s history last week. A preliminary Post-Incident Report (PIR) released by the company outlines how the latent bug, changes in traffic, and reduced server capacity combined to knock much of Microsoft 365 and Exchange infrastructure offline at the end of last week. Microsoft’s report lists the incident’s final status as “a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents.”
Microsoft’s preliminary report places the outage between November 12 at 16:20 UTC and November 13 at 16:10 UTC, just under 24 hours total, and additional monitoring remained in place for any affected systems through November 14.
The outage started on November 12 and quickly rippled through businesses and public offices that depend on Microsoft’s cloud and email exchange infrastructure. The outage is covered in Microsoft’s incident IDs EX1550543 and MO1550821. You need Microsoft 365 admin credentials to see the full report on the company’s status pages, but Office Watch has reproduced the preliminary report, and the University of Pennsylvania maintains an archive of Microsoft’s service-health updates.
A perfect storm
Microsoft attributes the outage to three factors. A change deployed to Microsoft’s cloud gateway starting in July created a bug where, under certain conditions, CPU and memory resources could become exhausted and unresponsive. Microsoft contends that the defect was never discovered in pre-release testing because the hardware used was less powerful than some systems already deployed in production, where higher CPU core counts on newer machines apparently contributed to the lockout.
The second factor was server load. Microsoft said that “Traffic shifts during standard network maintenance and upgrades exposed a latent bug.” The company keeps two independent gateway systems in place to access Microsoft 365 for resilience. If one system encounters trouble and users can’t get through the front door, the other is opened to keep traffic flowing. According to the report, about 15 hours prior to the outage, traffic from Teams was shifted from the alternate gateway to the primary, where Exchange Online access is maintained. The switchover was a standard fail-safe, but it left the gateway handling more traffic, with a different mix of requests than before. As requests continued to pile up, affected servers exhausted their capacity and refused new connection requests.

articles.title: California state AG sues OpenAI over rogue agent incidents | TechCrunch
articles.text:
OpenAI is facing a new lawsuit from the California Attorney General’s office, alleging that the company’s training practices and lax security pose an ongoing danger to the public.
At the center of the case is the July 2026 Hugging Face compromise, in which a pre-release model within OpenAI compromised both companies’ security systems to complete a training benchmark. In its official report on the incident, OpenAI called it “an outlier scenario involving a rare and unexpected confluence of events.”
The California lawsuit represents one of the first attempts by a government regulator to hold an AI lab legally accountable for a rogue agent incident, with significant implications for both OpenAI’s competitors and its clients.
The complaint centers on the Hugging Face incident, but also cites similar incidents involving RubyGems, DseWiki, the Wikimedia Foundation, and Australian government websites as evidence that the underlying behavior is ongoing.
The complaint also alleges that dozens of similar incidents have occurred without public disclosure.
“OpenAI has recently sent notices to dozens of additional third parties whose websites or internal systems have been infiltrated by OpenAI agents,” the complaint reads. “In some cases, OpenAI agents were able to access sensitive personally identifiable information, such as employee records containing names, birth dates, addresses, and more. The vast majority of these incidents have not been disclosed or discussed publicly by either OpenAI or by the affected third parties.”
The central allegation is that OpenAI’s ongoing testing practices constitute a public nuisance because the lack of safety controls present an ongoing risk to the public. A secondary claim alleges unfair competition stemming from the marketing of an unsafe product. If the lawsuit succeeds, OpenAI could face an injunction “to abate the ongoing public nuisance,” leaving broad discretion in the hands of the court.
It’s the first regulatory case targeting OpenAI specifically over rogue agent incidents, although public endangerment claims have been considered by other states. In June, the Florida attorney general sued the company over allegedly harmful effects on users, particularly children and teenagers. In August, the Alabama attorney general launched a probe into deceptive practices related to the breach, but no case has been filed.
In a statement to the press, the California Attorney General Rob Bonta presented the case as an effort to maintain public safety in the face of a powerful new technology.
“OpenAI’s actions escalated real-word cybersecurity risks, threatening the safety, health, and well-being of society. The company knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it,” Bonta said in the statement. “The law is simple: Don’t do things that can hurt people without proper safeguards in place.”
In a statement, OpenAI emphasized the company’s extensive effort to investigate the Hugging Face incident and improve its systems in the aftermath.
“This lawsuit appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that’s been identified by every major AI lab,” OpenAI said. “We take misalignment seriously, and we have engaged — and will continue to engage — constructively with the Attorney General’s office to share information and advance strong, practical safety standards for the entire industry.”
Updated 12:23pm PT: Added OpenAI statement.

articles.title: Overlocker uses vibecoded BIOS modification to target Intel's non-K overclocking restrictions — attempts to revive ASRock's discontinued SkyOC technology
articles.text:
Overlocker uses vibecoded BIOS modification to target Intel's non-K overclocking restrictions — attempts to revive ASRock's discontinued SkyOC technology
An old ASRock trick gets a second shot.
In an attempt to resurrect ASRock's discontinued SkyOC overclocking feature, an enthusiast has vibe-coded a motherboard BIOS using AI, potentially bringing non-K CPU overclocking to modern Intel CPUs. According to a post on X, Hardware 360º used Chat-GPT Astra to decompile and compare two versions of an ASRock BIOS, one released with SkyOC and another with the feature disabled. The AI reportedly identified the code responsible for enabling the overclocking workaround and modified it to create a BIOS ready for implementation on a compatible motherboard. Unfortunately, it remains to be seen whether the modified firmware can restore SkyOC on modern Intel platforms, as the workaround is yet to be fully tested.
For context, Intel offers multiplier-based overclocking only on its unlocked K-series processors like the Core i9-14900K and the newer Core Ultra 270K Plus. Non-K models have locked multipliers, which restrict users from pushing CPU frequencies. However, there’s another way to raise the speed of a processor by pushing the base clock itself. The base clock, or BCLK, typically runs at 100 MHz and works alongside the CPU multiplier to determine its operating frequency. For example, raising the base clock speed of a CPU to 105 MHz increases the clock speed by 5%. The only downside is that BCLK adjustments can also affect the entire motherboard, including memory and PCIe-based components, thereby potentially causing system instability.
ASRock's SkyOC technology, which was introduced for Intel's Skylake processors in 2016, allowed users to overclock locked non-K CPUs through BCLK adjustments. Certain motherboards also featured independent clock generators, allowing CPU clock adjustments without affecting the rest of the system. Intel was not particularly pleased with the workaround, and ASRock eventually had to remove SkyOC from its motherboards via BIOS updates. Additionally, Intel introduced microcode changes to prevent non-K overclocking.
The current experiment revisits that workaround by identifying the original BIOS code and adapting it for modern motherboards. Hardware 360º claims Intel's restrictions include a mechanism that triggers a shutdown when BCLK exceeds 103 MHz, and that SkyOC originally worked around this by tricking the processor with a false report of the actual BCLK value.
Finding the original code for SkyOC does not necessarily mean it can be successfully ported to a modern motherboard BIOS. Newer Intel processors use different firmware, microcode, and clock-management mechanisms, which would make adapting the workaround considerably more complicated. Flashing modified motherboard firmware also comes with its own set of risks, including the possibility of rendering the board completely unusable. Nevertheless, it is interesting to see how AI-assisted reverse engineering can help gain access to BIOS modifications that would otherwise require a considerable amount of effort.

articles.title: Anthropic sale a bolsa: fecha, precio y claves del debut en Wall Street
articles.text:
El dato central. Anthropic fija el precio de su salida a bolsa el miércoles 18 de noviembre, después del cierre de Wall Street, y empieza a cotizar el jueves 19 en el Nasdaq con el símbolo ANT, según informó CNBC. Vende 825 millones de acciones a un precio de entre USD 70 y USD 78.
En el techo de ese rango, la empresa recauda USD 64.400 millones y queda valuada en torno a 1,4 billones de dólares, si se cuentan las acciones que todavía no se emitieron por opciones de empleados y deuda convertible. Sobre las acciones que ya existen, la cifra ronda 1,02 billones.
Por qué importa. Es la segunda salida a bolsa más grande de la historia, detrás de SpaceX, que en junio levantó USD 75.000 millones. Si se suman los 26.000 millones que siete socios, entre ellos Google, Nvidia y Microsoft, comprarán en una colocación privada al mismo precio, la operación supera ese récord.
También es la primera vez que el inversor común puede comprar en forma directa acciones de uno de los grandes laboratorios de inteligencia artificial.
Los números de la operación
Qué se vende. De los 825 millones de acciones, 801,4 millones son nuevas y 23,6 millones pertenecen a accionistas actuales. Los bancos tienen también una opción para colocar otros 123,75 millones de papeles, que sumarían unos 9.700 millones adicionales.
Quién la conduce. Goldman Sachs y Morgan Stanley encabezan un grupo de 22 bancos. JPMorgan tiene a su cargo la venta a inversores minoristas en Estados Unidos, según Bloomberg.
El salto de valuación. En mayo, en su última ronda privada, la empresa fue valuada en 965.000 millones. Menos de seis meses después, sale al mercado hasta un 45% más cara. En 2021, en su primera ronda, valía 461 millones, según datos de PitchBook.
La demanda desborda la oferta
Lo que se sabe. Bloomberg informó que los pedidos superan unas seis veces las acciones disponibles. The Financial Times publicó que los bancos esperan fijar el precio por encima de los USD 78, lo que llevaría la valuación a 1,5 billones o más.
La letra chica. Los bancos avisaron a los interesados que los accionistas actuales tendrán prioridad en el reparto, según Bloomberg. Quien llega de afuera recibirá menos de lo que pidió, o nada.
La consecuencia. La demanda que quede afuera del reparto se traslada al jueves, a la apertura. Esa es la receta clásica de un primer día con salto.
Qué negocio se está comprando
Los ingresos. Anthropic facturó USD 33.240 millones en los primeros nueve meses de 2026, contra 2.545 millones en el mismo período de 2025: la cifra se multiplicó por 13. Solo en el tercer trimestre vendió 17.000 millones, un 1.127% más que un año antes.
La empresa informó que su proyección de ingresos anualizados rondaba los 81.000 millones a fines de octubre. Es una cifra que lleva a un año el ritmo de las últimas semanas, no ventas ya registradas.
La pérdida que asusta. El prospecto muestra una pérdida neta de 104.000 millones en nueve meses. Cerca del 91% es un ajuste contable sin salida de caja: 94.300 millones por deuda que se convierte en acciones y cuyo valor en los libros sube cuando sube la valuación de la propia empresa.
Cuanto más vale Anthropic, más pierde en el balance.
El número que sí importa. La pérdida operativa, la que mide el negocio, fue de 1.260 millones en nueve meses. En el segundo trimestre, la compañía ganó 974 millones a nivel operativo; en el tercero volvió a perder 567 millones.
El precio. A 1,4 billones, el mercado paga unas 17 veces los ingresos anualizados. Es caro para casi cualquier empresa y razonable solo si el crecimiento se sostiene.
Los riesgos que el prospecto no esconde
El cómputo. Anthropic asumió compromisos por unos USD 900.900 millones, casi todos en capacidad de cómputo e infraestructura, con proveedores como Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Broadcom y SpaceX. Los contratos con Microsoft, Google y Amazon se pagan aunque la capacidad no se use. Es una apuesta a que la demanda de IA seguirá creciendo durante años.
El control. Anthropic es una corporación de beneficio público, una figura legal que la obliga a atender su misión y no solo la ganancia. Sus siete cofundadores conservan el 50,1% de los votos y un fideicomiso independiente elige a la mayoría del directorio. Se compra participación económica, no poder.
El momento. Nvidia perdió cerca del 30% de su valor en seis semanas y su fundador, Jensen Huang, renunció el jueves pasado. El Nasdaq acumula una caída cercana al 10% desde su máximo de octubre. El mercado da por descontado que la Reserva Federal subirá las tasas el 9 de diciembre.
Anthropic sale a un mercado que duda de la IA y, al mismo tiempo, hace fila para comprarla.
El antecedente. SpaceX debutó en junio, valuada en 1,77 billones. A fines de julio, sus acciones habían caído casi 50% desde el pico de la primera semana y cotizaban por debajo del precio de salida.
Quiénes ganan
Los primeros. Unos 300 inversores institucionales pusieron dinero en la compañía, según PitchBook. Entre los que lideraron rondas figuran Jaan Tallinn, Spark Capital, Menlo Ventures, Lightspeed, Iconiq, GIC, Coatue, Altimeter, Dragoneer, Greenoaks y Sequoia.
Los gigantes. Amazon y Alphabet son accionistas y, a la vez, proveedores de cómputo. Sus participaciones valdrían en conjunto USD 411.000 millones en el techo del rango, según cálculos de Reuters sobre el prospecto. Quien tiene acciones de Amazon o de Alphabet ya es dueño indirecto de una parte de Anthropic.
Qué lugar tienen los inversores minoristas
La novedad. Hasta el 20% de la oferta está previsto para inversores minoristas, contra el 5% a 10% que suele reservarse, según recogió Business Insider.
La realidad. Con pedidos seis veces por encima de la oferta, la mayoría recibirá poco o nada al precio de salida. El resto de esa demanda queda para el mercado abierto, al precio que marque la apertura.
La cifra. Vanda Research proyecta compras minoristas netas por USD 250 millones el primer día, más del doble de los 118 millones que tuvo SpaceX.
Qué mirar esta semana
Miércoles 18. El precio final. Si queda por encima de USD 78, la demanda era real. Morningstar calcula que la acción vale USD 92. Esta semana también presenta resultados Nvidia.
Jueves 19. El precio de apertura y la distancia con el precio de salida. Ese salto es lo que paga el que llega tarde.
Los meses siguientes. El vencimiento de las restricciones de venta, que suele traer oferta nueva al mercado. Los empleados pueden vender hasta el 10% de sus acciones desde el primer día; la restricción general dura 180 días y llega a un año para los fundadores. Después, el primer balance como empresa pública.
La conclusión. Anthropic es un negocio extraordinario a un precio que no admite errores. Sus ingresos se multiplicaron por 13 en un año, pero el jueves no se compra ese crecimiento: se compra la expectativa de que continúe, con el Nasdaq en baja y las tasas en suba.
El primer día de una salida a bolsa es una fiesta para quienes ya estaban adentro. Para los demás, la paciencia suele ser el mejor precio de entrada.

articles.title: Black Friday – Le très endurant Xiaomi 17T Pro perd 250 € sur Amazon
articles.text:
Black Friday – Le très endurant Xiaomi 17T Pro perd 250 € sur Amazon
Pour le Black Friday, Amazon fait fondre le prix du Xiaomi 17T Pro : le smartphone du géant chinois tombe à 653 € en version 256 Go, contre 903 € comme tarif de référence. Une remise de 28 % qui donne un sérieux coup de pouce à ce modèle bien équipé, passé par notre labo récemment.
Le Xiaomi 17T Pro avait un défaut au lancement : son prix, moins doux que celui de ses prédécesseurs. À 653 €, le discours change un peu. Ce grand smartphone de 6,83 pouces embarque 12 Go de RAM, 256 Go de stockage et une puce Dimensity 9500 qui ne manque pas de répondant au quotidien. Et sous son allure assez sage se cache une fiche technique qui a de quoi faire de l'œil aux amateurs de photo comme aux power users.
Xiaomi 17T Pro
Un écran qui en met plein la vue
Lors de notre test, sa dalle Amoled nous a particulièrement convaincus. Bien calibrée, elle grimpe jusqu'à 3584 cd/m², de quoi conserver une bonne lisibilité en extérieur. Le rafraîchissement peut atteindre 144 Hz, même si le gain face à 120 Hz reste discret. Côté photo, le partenariat avec Leica porte ses fruits, notamment grâce à un téléobjectif x5 efficace pour aller chercher les sujets éloignés. L'ultra grand-angle se montre en revanche moins inspiré, surtout à la nuit tombée.
Une batterie qui voit (très) grand
L'autre gros argument du Xiaomi 17T Pro, c'est son accumulateur de 7000 mAh. Notre protocole viSer a mesuré 24 h 48 min d'autonomie, un résultat confortable qui évite de vivre les yeux rivés sur la jauge. La charge filaire grimpe à 100 W sur le papier, mais il nous a tout de même fallu 1 h 12 min pour refaire le plein. Le mobile chauffe aussi assez vite lorsqu'on le pousse, ce qui bride ses performances en jeu.
À 653 €, ce Xiaomi 17T Pro retrouve donc une partie de l'agressivité tarifaire qui faisait le charme de la gamme. Il reste imposant et son logiciel un peu encombré, mais entre son écran, son zoom et son endurance, l'offre Amazon mérite le détour.
