articles.title: MSI Powers the Next Era of AI Infrastructure at SC26
articles.text:
Monday, November 16th 2026
MSI Powers the Next Era of AI Infrastructure at SC26
MSI, a leading global provider of high-performance server solutions, showcases its latest AI innovations at SuperComputing 2026 (SC26), booth #5429. From liquid-cooled platforms based on NVIDIA MGX and desktop AI supercomputing based on NVIDIA DGX Station architecture to next-generation multi-node compute and enterprise servers, MSI delivers a comprehensive portfolio designed to power agentic AI and AI factory deployments. Spanning the latest AMD and Intel processor architectures, MSI's solutions combine rack-scale compute density with flexible, balanced performance to support enterprise AI workloads, from large-scale infrastructure to local AI development.
Danny Hsu, General Manager of Enterprise Platform Solutions at MSI"Building a modern data center takes more than computing power. It requires strong technology partnerships and a trusted infrastructure foundation that can turn innovation into real-world value," "Through our collaborations with AMD, Intel, and NVIDIA, we combine leading-edge technologies with MSI's system integration expertise to deliver reliable, flexible, and efficient infrastructure that helps customers maximize their investments, scale with confidence, and prepare for the next era of AI."
Build AI-Ready Infrastructure with Liquid-Cooled Architecture Solutions
Built on the NVIDIA MGX architecture, MSI showcases its 6U liquid-cooled CG681-S6093 systems alongside a 48RU rack configuration featuring four CG681-S6093 systems. Leveraging an open, modular reference architecture, MSI delivers liquid-cooled building blocks that scale from single-node servers to rack-scale AI Factory deployments, helping system builders design future-compatible systems faster, reducing costs, accelerating time to market, and improving ROI.
NVIDIA MGX Rack: A 48RU rack configuration featuring four MSI CG681-S6093 liquid-cooled NVIDIA MGX systems, NVIDIA Spectrum-4 SN5600 data switches, and SN2201 out-of-band networking switches. This integrated solution provides a foundation for rack-scale accelerated computing deployments.
CG681-S6093: A 6U liquid-cooled NVIDIA MGX platform supporting up to eight liquid cooled NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs, dual AMD EPYC 9006 Series Server processors, eight NVIDIA ConnectX-8 SuperNICs with 400 Gbps Ethernet connectivity per port, PCIe 6.0 expansion, and up to 32 DDR5 DIMM slots. It is designed for high-density AI and accelerated computing workloads.
Accelerate Enterprise AI at Scale with NVIDIA MGX Servers and NVIDIA DGX Station
To address diverse enterprise AI deployment needs, from cloud computing and edge inference to desktop AI development, MSI offers 4U and 2U NVIDIA MGX servers supporting NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 and RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs. These platforms are designed for demanding workloads, including large language models (LLMs), deep learning training, and NVIDIA Omniverse applications.
- CG480-S6053: A 4U dual-socket AMD EPYC 9005 platform supporting up to eight double-wide GPUs, 24 DDR5 DIMM slots, eight U.2 NVMe drives, and five additional PCIe 5.0 expansion slots for scalable AI infrastructure.
- CG290-S3063: A 2U single-socket Intel Xeon 6 platform supporting up to four double-wide GPUs, 16 DDR5 DIMM slots, and four rear U.2 NVMe drives. It is ideal for edge computing and small-scale AI inference deployments.
For enterprise AI teams seeking powerful local computing for AI development, the MSI XpertStation WS300, built on the NVIDIA DGX Station platform, brings desktop AI supercomputing to the workplace. Designed for AI development, fine-tuning, inference, and data-intensive workflows, it will support Windows for local AI application and agent development.
Powered by the NVIDIA GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip, the WS300 delivers up to 748 GB of coherent memory with ECC and 7.1 TB/s of HBM3e GPU memory bandwidth to accelerate CPU-GPU communication and large-model processing. Dual 400GbE networking via NVIDIA ConnectX-8 SuperNICs, combined with a liquid-cooled thermal design, brings data-center-class AI computing to a compact deskside form factor.
DC-MHS Open Compute and Core Compute Servers—Maximum Rack Density for AI and Cloud Infrastructure
Designed for hyperscale data centers and cloud service providers, MSI's Open Compute and Core Compute platforms deliver high-density, multi-node server architectures optimized for rack-scale deployments. MSI's 21-inch Open Compute platforms support ORv3 infrastructure in air-cooled 2OU 2-node and direct-to-chip (DLC) liquid-cooled 1OU 2-node configurations, with CPU TDPs of up to 600 W. Complementing these solutions, MSI's 19-inch DC-MHS Core Compute platforms offer 2U 2-node and 2U 4-node configurations to maximize compute density and infrastructure efficiency. Powered by AMD EPYC 9006 Series SP7 Server processors or Intel Xeon 6 processors, these platforms provide a scalable foundation for large-scale AI, cloud, and HPC deployments.
AMD EPYC 9006 Series SP7-Based Servers
- CD281-S4091-X2: An ORv3 2OU 2-node, single-socket server featuring 16 DDR5-8000 RDIMM slots and eight front E3.S 1T PCIe 6.0 x4 NVMe drive bays per node.
- CD182-S6091-X2: An ORv3 1OU 2-node, direct liquid-cooled, dual-socket server featuring 32 DDR5-8000 RDIMM slots and four front E1.S PCIe 6.0 x4 NVMe drive bays per node.
- CD270-S4091-X2: A 2U 2-node, single-socket server featuring 16 DDR5-8000 RDIMM slots and eight front E1.S PCIe 6.0 x4 NVMe drive bays per node.
Intel Xeon 6 Servers
- CD270-S3061-X4: A 2U 4-node, single-socket server featuring 16 DDR5 DIMM slots and three PCIe 5.0 x4 U.2 NVMe drive bays per node.
DC-MHS Enterprise Servers—Optimized Enterprise IT Performance, Storage, and Flexibility
Designed for mainstream enterprise IT environments, MSI's DC-MHS Enterprise Servers deliver a balanced combination of compute performance, memory capacity, and storage flexibility for virtualization, databases, business-critical applications, and AI-assisted workloads. Available in 1U and 2U configurations powered by AMD EPYC 9006 Series SP8 Server processors or Intel Xeon 6 processors, these platforms offer flexible memory configurations, high-density NVMe storage, and scalable expansion options. With configurations supporting up to 32 DIMM slots and 32 E3.S 1T PCIe 6.0 NVMe drives, MSI's Enterprise Servers help businesses optimize infrastructure utilization, maximize return on investment, and adapt to evolving IT demands.
AMD EPYC 9006 Series SP8-Based Servers
- CX272-S6082: A 2U dual-socket server featuring 32 DDR5-8000 RDIMM slots, 32 front E3.S 1T PCIe 6.0 x4 NVMe, and two front PCIe 4.0 x4 E1.S NVMe drive bays.

In addition, MSI offers AMD Instinct MI350P-based solutions, enabling enterprises to extend their existing infrastructure with advanced AI computing capabilities and scale generative and agentic AI workloads.
Intel Xeon 6 Servers

articles.title: Nubank libera período de teste grátis do NuCel • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Nubank libera período de teste grátis do NuCel
Clientes podem testar a operadora do Nubank com número provisório e sem custo. Oferta inclui até 5 GB de internet e WhatsApp ilimitado.
O Nubank começou a oferecer um período de testes gratuito do NuCel, sua operadora móvel virtual. Clientes interessados podem experimentar o serviço por até 10 dias, sem precisar transferir imediatamente o número de outra operadora.
Em resposta ao Tecnoblog, o banco informou que os clientes terão direito a até 5 GB de dados móveis e WhatsApp ilimitado durante o teste. A ativação é feita pelo app do Nubank por meio de um eSIM, sem necessidade de comprar ou receber um chip físico.
Ao fim do período, o cliente pode optar por fazer a portabilidade do número atual e continuar com a NuCel ou cancelar o serviço diretamente pelo aplicativo. Segundo o Nubank, um aviso será enviado antes do encerramento do teste e não há cobrança de multa ou taxa adicional para quem decidir não permanecer na operadora.
Quem decidir continuar com a NuCel pode contratar um dos planos da operadora, com preços a partir de R$ 45 por mês e franquia de 35 GB. Nos três primeiros meses, há um bônus de 10 GB mensais, elevando o pacote para 45 GB nesse período.
O teste termina quando o usuário completar 10 dias ou consumir os 5 GB disponíveis, o que acontecer primeiro. A proposta é permitir que potenciais clientes avaliem a conexão e os recursos do serviço antes de transferir seu número principal.
Lançada em outubro de 2024, a NuCel já ultrapassou 1 milhão de linhas em serviço. A operadora virtual (MVNO) utiliza a rede da Claro.

articles.title: Comcast's "fiber-powered Wi-Fi" is just cable, AT&T says in false advertising case
articles.text:
AT&T on Friday accused Comcast of false advertising in a lawsuit challenging the marketing claim that Comcast’s cable broadband service and Wi-Fi is “fiber-powered.”
“This case challenges Comcast’s false advertising campaign for its residential Internet service, marketed under the Xfinity brand to consumers nationwide,” AT&T’s lawsuit said. “At the center of that campaign is Comcast’s claim that Xfinity Internet and its associated Wi-Fi service are ‘Fiber-Powered.’”
While Comcast has deployed plenty of fiber throughout the US, its cable Internet service makes the final connection to homes with coaxial cable. This results in upload speeds being far slower than download speeds.
In contrast, fiber-to-the-home service can provide symmetrical upload and download speeds. Comcast has deployed fiber-to-the-home in only small portions of its cable territory while advertising its service as fiber-powered in the majority of areas where cable makes the final connection.
AT&T’s lawsuit said that in describing its cable broadband as fiber-powered, Comcast “conveys to reasonable consumers the misleading impression that Xfinity Internet is a fiber-to-the-home service comparable to AT&T Fiber. In fact, the vast majority of Xfinity Internet runs over a hybrid fiber-coaxial (‘HFC’) network, where the critical ‘last mile’ connection to the customer’s home uses copper coaxial cable, not fiber.”
AT&T has its own history of ads that mislead customers about the nature of its network. It used to advertise 4G LTE service as “5GE” or “5G Evolution,” and displayed a 5GE network icon on 4G phones. AT&T claimed that its 5G Evolution ads “served to educate customers about the billions of dollars AT&T has invested to give customers an outstanding experience,” but the BBB National Programs’ National Advertising Division found the term was likely to mislead consumers into thinking they had 5G connections.
AT&T: Fiber-powered is “literally false”
AT&T’s lawsuit said that Comcast’s fiber-powered claim “is literally false” because the cable firm’s HFC “architecture is fundamentally different from true fiber-to-the-home services like AT&T Fiber, which deliver fiber optic cables directly to the customer’s premises.”

articles.title: Alemania excluyó a Palantir, empresa estadounidense de software, de la lista de opciones de IA para su ejército
articles.text:
Alemania dejó a Palantir fuera de la lista de soluciones que evalúa para la plataforma de inteligencia artificial que quiere desplegar en su ejército desde el próximo año, según informó la agencia Reuters. Francia y Países Bajos también buscan proveedores europeos para reducir la dependencia de la tecnología de Estados Unidos.
La agencia citó a una persona al tanto del asunto, que explicó que el Gobierno alemán redujo las opciones a un puñado de soluciones. Ninguna igualaría las capacidades de Palantir, pero serían suficientes, garantizarían la soberanía sobre los datos nacionales y podrían cubrir cerca del 80% de lo necesario en un año.
Palantir es una empresa estadounidense de software que analiza grandes volúmenes de datos. Su sistema Maven Smart System es el programa central del Pentágono y fue muy usado por Ucrania en la guerra contra Rusia. El cuartel general militar de la OTAN lo adoptó el año pasado y en junio lo declaró listo para uso operativo en toda la alianza.
Según Reuters, algunos funcionarios y militares reconocen que Europa no tiene hoy un equivalente exacto en tamaño, despliegue y experiencia. Los ejércitos enfrentan así un dilema: apostar por sistemas propios, con más autonomía pero menos maduros, o usar una plataforma probada pese al riesgo de dependencia estratégica.
Francia desarrolla una plataforma militar soberana con IA llamada Arcadia. Alexandre Lahousse, subdirector de la agencia francesa de compras de defensa, dijo a Reuters que incluirá a varios proveedores. La agencia prevé adjudicar al menos algunos contratos antes de que termine el año y tener una versión operativa para el campo de batalla a mediados de 2027.
Países Bajos usa hoy parte del software de Palantir, pero quiere una alternativa europea en dos años. El ministro neerlandés de Compras de Armamento, Derk Boswijk, explicó a la agencia que su ejército se reúne con posibles proveedores y probablemente combinará empresas neerlandesas y de otros países europeos. “Tenemos mucho conocimiento en Europa sobre IA y toma de decisiones. Pero está muy fragmentado, y ese es el problema”, afirmó Boswijk.
Una empresa alemana presentó una alternativa europea
El 11 de noviembre, la empresa alemana Helsing presentó Clarity, un programa de inteligencia militar que, según la compañía, usa cientos de agentes de IA (asistentes que ejecutan tareas por su cuenta) para analizar imágenes de satélite, video de drones y partes escritas. Identifica posibles objetivos y prepara datos para los sistemas de armas, con aprobación humana de cada uno, según Helsing.
“Una capacidad tan crítica debe ser soberana”, dijo el cofundador y codirector ejecutivo de Helsing, Gundbert Scherf, en el comunicado de la compañía, citado por Kyiv Independent. Helsing aseguró a Reuters que podría entregar una versión inicial en pocos meses a la brigada alemana desplegada en Lituania.
Reuters mencionó otros fabricantes europeos de software militar: la danesa Systematic, cuyo producto SitaWare usan el ejército alemán y partes de la OTAN, las francesas Thales y Safran, y la startup parisina Comand AI.
Palantir intenta tranquilizar a los europeos. Su director internacional, Louis Mosley, dijo a la agencia de noticias que el sistema usado por la OTAN no tiene un “interruptor de apagado”, que sigue habiendo demanda en Europa, incluido el Reino Unido, donde el Ministerio de Defensa firmó el año pasado un acuerdo de tres años, y que espera convencer a Alemania.
El jefe del ejército alemán, el teniente general Christian Freuding, señaló en una conferencia en Berlín que persisten dudas sobre seguridad de los datos, entrenamiento de los sistemas y compatibilidad entre plataformas. Francia prevé adjudicar los primeros contratos de Arcadia antes de que termine 2026.

articles.title: Trump says ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy did not threaten national security | TechCrunch
articles.text:
U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters on Monday that he does not believe the country’s national security was put at risk as a result of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
“It was not put at risk,” Trump said when asked by reporters in light of his own friendship with Huang. “Our country is now stronger than ever before. And you know, China plays games with us, and we play games with China.”
Trump went on to contradict previous findings from U.S. officials by doubting that Huang’s paramour, former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy.
“He probably shouldn’t have been doing on a personal basis what he did … That’s a different story,” Trump added. “But nobody’s proven that she’s a spy. She may not be a spy.”
Last year, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly oversaw the production of an internal memo, circulated among top policymakers, which warned that Alice Huang was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. Trump was reportedly briefed about these intelligence findings at least twice, including once in May aboard Air Force One, shortly before the former Nvidia CEO joined him on a trip to China. But Trump has maintained that he was not aware of these claims.
The U.S. regulates the exports of Nvidia’s top chips to China as a way of maintaining a competitive advantage. But prior to news of Huang’s affair publicly emerging, both the U.S. and Singaporean governments had been investigating Megaspeed for illegally smuggling Nvidia chips into China. Huang has since stepped down from the role he has had for 33 years at Nvidia after more reporting revealed that he also had affairs with two Nvidia employees, at least one of whom was a direct report.
Given Huang’s importance to Nvidia, some prominent figures in the industry — including Elon Musk, Y Combinator president and CEO Garry Tan, and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney — have signed a public letter calling for Nvidia to reinstate Huang.
“A lot of people are asking Jensen — they think Jensen should go back. That certainly isn’t a bad idea,” Trump said. Referring to the former Apple chief executive, Trump added: “I recommended Tim Cook.”

articles.title: 25 Milliarden Kilometer entfernt: Wie die Nasa mit Voyager 1 kommuniziert
articles.text:
Voyager 1 ist bald einen Lichttag von der Erde entfernt: So läuft die Kommunikation mit der Nasa-Sonde
Seit 49 Jahren schwebt die Raumsonde Voyager 1 durchs Weltall. Trotz ihrer alten Tage ist die Sonde noch teilweise funktionsfähig. Und schon bald wird sie einen Meilenstein erreichen, den zuvor noch kein anderes menschengemachtes Objekt im Weltall erreichen konnte.
Voyager 1 erreicht historische Lichttag-Distanz
Die Raumsonde wird als erstes einen Lichttag von der Erde entfernt sein. Dies entspricht etwa 25,9 Milliarden Kilometern. Wie das Wort „Lichttag“ schon sagt: Das Licht, das von einem Objekt in dieser Distanz ausgestrahlt wird, benötigt 24 Stunden, um die Erde zu erreichen. Die Nasa hat den Moment, an dem Voyager 1 einen Lichttag von der Erde entfernt sein wird, schon exakt berechnet. Demnach ist es am 18. November um 5:16 Uhr US-Ostküstenzeit so weit. Zu diesem Zeitpunkt wird die Distanz der Sonde zur Erde exakt 25.902.068.356 Kilometer betragen.
Ein Radiosignal, das die Kontrollstation auf der Erde in Richtung Voyager abschickt, ist dann ebenfalls einen ganzen Tag unterwegs. Das sorgt für massive Delays in der Kommunikation. „Wenn man ‚Voyager ‚Hallo‘ sagen will, schickt man seine Nachricht ab, geht nach Hause und wartet zwei Tage, bis man endlich eine Antwort bekommt“, sagte Suzanne Dodd vom Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) der Nasa in der Mitteilung.
Voyager 1 reagierte zweimal nicht auf Kontaktversuche
Erst kürzlich kam es zu einem Zwischenfall, der den Meilenstein fast verhindert hätte. Das Funk- und Kommunikationsnetzwerk der Nasa hatte am 18. und 19. Oktober Voyager 1 kontaktiert. Doch die Raumsonde blieb bei beiden Kontaktversuchen stumm. Wie die US-Raumfahrtbehörde kürzlich bekannt gab, löste sich das Problem aber von selbst. Am 20. Oktober meldete sich Voyager zurück. Seitdem ist die Kommunikation stabil.
Mittlerweile haben Nasa-Ingenieur:innen auch die Ursache herausgefunden. Eine Gruppe von Triebwerken der Voyager 1 ging unerwartet offline. Das System schaltete dann automatisch eine Backup-Gruppe hinzu. Um diesen Wechsel fehlerfrei durchzuführen, begibt sich das System in eine Art abgesicherten Modus und pausiert bis zur Umsetzung alle anderen Funktionen.
Fast 50 Jahre im All: Voyager 1 trotzt dem Zahn der Zeit
Voyager 1 startete am 5. September 1977 von Cape Canaveral aus. Seitdem bewegt sie sich mit einer Geschwindigkeit von über 60.000 Kilometern pro Stunde durchs All. Die Nasa-Sonde erforschte zunächst Jupiter und Saturn. Im Sommer 2012 trat sie als erstes von Menschen geschaffenes Objekt in den interstellaren Raum ein.
Doch ein Jahr vor ihrem 50. Geburtstag nagt der Zahn der Zeit an der Sonde. Deswegen musste die Nasa im Frühjahr 2026 ein weiteres Instrument abschalten, den Teilchenmesser LECP. (Low-energy Charged Particles). Die Abschaltung spart Energie, die der Sonde ein Jahr weiterer Lebensdauer verschaffen soll. Von ursprünglich elf Instrumenten an Bord der Voyager 1 sind damit nur noch zwei aktiv.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 05.11.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.
Interessant! Aber… die NASA Kontaktiert am 18.10. und die Sonde blieb still…
2 Tage auf eine Antwort warten, dann am 20.10. eine Antwort.
also, nicht still geblieben, oder? Aber genug für einen spannenden Artikel… denke ich!

articles.title: Amazon’s Starlink rival sees major setback after 40 satellites destroyed in rocket failure — ‘anomaly’ occurred 10 minutes after the Vulcan launch on Sunday
articles.text:
Amazon’s Starlink rival sees major setback after 40 satellites destroyed in rocket failure — ‘anomaly’ occurred 10 minutes after the Vulcan launch on Sunday
Currently Amazon has 392 broadband satellites in orbit and hoped to move the service out of beta by the end of this year.
Amazon has suffered a major setback in its plans to offer a viable Starlink rival, after 40 satellites destined for low Earth orbit (LEO) were destroyed. Just ten minutes after the Vulcan vehicle launched from Space Launch Complex 41 in Cape Canaveral, Florida, on Sunday, there was an “anomaly,” meaning that the rocket “failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit.” The language seems quite vague, but the United Launch Alliance (ULA) says that data needs to be analyzed “to understand what occurred today.”
Shortly after the triumphant takeoff clip was shared by the ULA, above, the space tech firm updated its X feed with a confirmation that its mission on behalf of Amazon failed.
Sadly for Amazon, the ULA, and folks who want a viable substitute for Starlink in the satellite internet business, this failure will surely delay the full commercialization of this service. ISPReview notes that Amazon has successfully launched 392 Kuiper communications satellites, but needs at least 500 for basic global coverage. Moreover, Amazon Leo service’s transition from the current commercial beta phase to launching properly at the end of 2026 now looks uncertain.
Reports indicate Amazon has already manufactured 1,000 satellites, but ULA, which is a joint venture of Boeing and Lockheed Martin, will need to analyze and assure customers that Sunday’s failure won’t be repeated. ULA's Vulcan vehicle had already been out of action for nine months after technical investigations into issues with its solid rocket side boosters and core BE-4 engines (made by Amazon Blue Origin).
For some context, the ULA has (or had) a great track record. Sunday's incident was its first total mission failure in its 20-year history. Early telemetry from the organization is already pointing towards some suspected causes of the destruction of the 40 satellites. Likely fault candidates include the first-stage BE-4 engines burning longer than planned, and there may have been some altitude issues near staging.
The headline failure and essential careful analysis of the anomaly won’t hold up Amazon’s other launch partners, though. A week from today, the Amazon Leo constellation is set to grow by 36 more satellites. They will be sent into orbit aboard a European Ariane 64 Block 2 (LE-04) rocket.
Amazon has approval for an initial constellation of 3,236 LEO broadband satellites, with 392 now in orbit, plus 5,105 for 5G service. Satellite tracking sites suggest Starlink already has 11,200+ satellites in orbit.

articles.title: 5 lessons from Here, There and Everywhere by Sudha Murty
articles.text:
5 lessons from Here, There and Everywhere by Sudha Murty
Discover five meaningful lessons from Here, There and Everywhere by Sudha Murty on kindness, humility, relationships, gratitude, and simple living.
Life's most meaningful lessons often come from ordinary experiences, unexpected encounters, and the people we meet along the way. Sometimes, a simple conversation or a small act of kindness can change the way we understand the world.
In Here, There and Everywhere, Sudha Murty brings together a collection of stories inspired by her experiences and observations of people from different walks of life. Through everyday situations, she explores human relationships, generosity, humility, and the values that make life meaningful.
The book reminds readers that wisdom is not always found in grand achievements. Often, it is hidden in the simplest moments of everyday life.
5 lessons to learn from Here, There and Everywhere by Sudha Murty
1. Kindness can change someone's life
Small acts of kindness can have a lasting impact on people. Sometimes, helping someone does not require wealth or influence; it simply requires empathy and a willingness to understand their situation.
The stories remind us that even a small gesture, such as helping a stranger or supporting someone during a difficult time, can create a meaningful difference.
2. Never judge people by their appearance
We often form opinions about people based on their clothes, financial status, education, or social background. However, appearances rarely reveal someone's true character or circumstances.
The book encourages readers to look beyond outward appearances and treat everyone with dignity and respect.
3. Education builds confidence and independence
Education is not limited to academic qualifications. It also gives people the confidence to express themselves, make informed decisions, and challenge social expectations.
Through stories drawn from different experiences, Murty highlights how learning can open doors, particularly for those who face social and economic barriers.
4. Humility is more valuable than wealth
Success and financial achievements do not automatically make someone a better person. What truly matters is how we treat others, especially those who cannot offer us anything in return.
The book encourages readers to remain humble, regardless of their achievements, and remember that kindness and character are more meaningful than material possessions.
5. Every person has a story worth understanding
We often meet people without knowing what they have experienced or the challenges they have overcome. A stranger's behaviour or circumstances may have a story behind them that we have never considered.
The book reminds us to listen, observe, and approach people with empathy rather than making quick assumptions. Every encounter can teach us something about human nature and life.
Final thoughts
Here, There and Everywhere by Sudha Murty is a collection of stories that finds extraordinary lessons in ordinary experiences. Through encounters with people from different backgrounds, the author explores kindness, courage, education, humility, and human relationships.
The biggest takeaway is that we do not always need extraordinary experiences to learn something valuable. Sometimes, the people we meet and the simplest moments we experience have the most important lessons to offer.

articles.title: Un encapuchado sube a un panel de tráfico sobre la A-92, en uno de los accesos a Sevilla, prende fuego a un radar y huye
articles.text:
Hay un aparato en España que tiene más enemigos que Batman, si bien solo cumplen una función informativa: el radar de tramo. Y es que ayer mismo alguien encapuchado se subió a la estructura de un panel informativo sobre los carriles de la A-92 (es decir, a la entrada de Sevilla) y le prendió fuego. Corre por la pasarela, se baja por una escalera lateral y se marcha. Y parece que el vídeo viral ha dado pie a otros, así que conviene separar los veraces de toda la imaginería que ha venido después, porque algunos contenidos incluso puede que estén hechos con IA.
El primer vídeo. Lo publicó el perfil de Instagram @lasevillaenfurecida. Según la prensa local, el radar está en la entrada a Sevilla desde Alcalá de Guadaíra, a la altura del Centro Zoosanitario municipal. Las versiones difieren en un punto. Unas dicen que el material ardiendo cae sobre el firme de la autovía. Otras, que las llamas alcanzan la zona bajo el dispositivo, junto a la calzada. No hubo avisos ni consta ningún accidente.
Un ataque más. El vídeo es parte de una serie de tres. En la SE-30, frente al mural del grupo SFDK, varios individuos cortan el poste de un radar con una herramienta de grandes dimensiones, lo cargan en un coche y lo queman. En Alcalá de Guadaíra, otro radar se ata a un vehículo, que lo arranca de cuajo, tirándo de él al estilo Mad Max, recurriendo quizá a una soga o cinchas.
El de la Ronda Urbana Norte. Aunque el vídeo se ha difundido ahora, ese ataque ocurrió a principios de mayo de 2026. Era uno de los cinco radares fijos que el Ayuntamiento instaló el otoño pasado en vías de 50 km/h. Los autores se llevaron la caja y el cableado, y el equipo apareció quemado en un descampado junto al aeropuerto de San Pablo. Según fuentes del caso, las pinzas hidráulicas se habrían sustraído antes de un parque de bomberos de la provincia. El Ayuntamiento sabía de la desaparición desde el 4 de mayo y a finales de junio solo quedaba el poste cortado.
Qué se sabe de la investigación. La unidad de investigación del Sector de Tráfico de Andalucía de la Guardia Civil (UNIS) ha abierto diligencias. No se ha comunicado oficialmente cuántos radares han resultado dañados ni quiénes son los implicados. Tampoco se conocen las fechas exactas de los ataques de la A-92 y de Alcalá. Una plataforma de verificación recoge el caso como abierto y aún sin investigar. Y aunque los vandalizados son los más visibles, la miniaturización de radares ha llevado a que cada vez estén mejor ocultos (el de Velolaser apenas mide 50 cm y mide 3kg).
Quién está detrás. La cuenta que difunde los vídeos atribuye las acciones a un "justiciero". Curiosamente, similar al grupo de jóvenes que se presentaba hace seis años como 'Payasos Justicieros', en referencia a los revolucionarios del bloque en la serie de comedia 'La Que Se Avecina'. Dice que actúan contra radares que consideran recaudatorios. La cuenta también los relaciona con otros vídeos ajenos a los radares, si bien no hay confirmación policial de ese vínculo.
Qué dice la ley. La DGT ya se pronunció en 2025, tras la vandalización de siete radares en otras comunidades. Lo considera un delito de daños, recogido en los artículos 263 a 267 del Código Penal. El tipo agravado, que se aplica cuando el daño busca impedir el ejercicio de la autoridad, prevé cárcel de 1 a 3 años y multa de 12 a 24 meses. La investigación dirá si procede aquí. Además, los autores deben responder por el coste del aparato, unos 67.000 euros por radar fijo según la DGT. Desde entonces, Tráfico ha instalado cámaras de vigilancia en esos puntos, conectadas a sus centros de gestión.
Por qué el radar. Los radares de la DGT recaudaron 246,8 millones de euros en 2025, un 14% más respecto al curso anterior, según Automovilistas Europeos Asociados. La velocidad ya supone el 41,5% de la recaudación por multas, sin contar País Vasco ni Cataluña. Solo 50 dispositivos concentraron 1,3 millones de denuncias. Sevilla fue la sexta provincia por recaudación total de multas de tráfico, con 26,3 millones.
La asociación sostiene que muchos son “meros instrumentos de recaudación”. La DGT replica con otro dato: según el Observatorio Europeo de Seguridad Vial, la velocidad excesiva está detrás del 10-15% de los accidentes y del 30% de los mortales. Su director, Pere Navarro, defiende los radares como la única vía eficaz para bajar la velocidad.
El precedente. En Francia, durante las protestas de los chalecos amarillos de 2018 quedaron inutilizados cientos de radares. En una radio se llegó a hablar de hasta el 60% de todos los radares automáticos del país. Se interpretó como un ataque al símbolo de un Gobierno que, según los manifestantes, les "usurpaba" demasiado dinero. Allí había un movimiento detrás y se sospecha que esté pasando lo mismo en Sevilla.
¿Más radares? El Ayuntamiento de Sevilla prevé más radares en vías como la Ronda Urbana Norte y la avenida de la Palmera. Forman parte de su plan contra el ruido, de unos diez millones de euros, que culminará en 2029. Después del vídeo

articles.title: Touch ID ne suffit pas sur l'iPhone Duo : Apple cède et ajoute une reconnaissance faciale au rabais dans iOS 27.3 — Frandroid
articles.text:
C’est un dogme vieux de neuf ans qui vient de fissurer à Cupertino. Depuis l’iPhone X en 2017, aucun smartphone Apple n’avait jamais fait cohabiter l’empreinte digitale et la reconnaissance faciale, la marque répétant à l’envi que Face ID était l’unique voie royale en matière de biométrie.
Sur l’iPhone Duo, vendu tout de même 2 339 euros, Touch ID ne suffit manifestement plus à satisfaire les premiers acheteurs. Le pliant va devenir le tout premier iPhone à cumuler les deux méthodes, mais avec un détail : comme l’explique Numerama, Apple présente explicitement cette nouvelle option faciale comme moins sécurisée que le lecteur d’empreintes. Un aveu rarissime, qui trahit à quel point l’absence de Face ID irrite au quotidien.
Cette nouveauté a été dénichée dans la deuxième bêta d’iOS 27.3, actuellement en test chez les développeurs avant un déploiement attendu en décembre. Baptisée sobrement « Déverrouiller avec le visage », l’option est désactivée par défaut et s’active dans les réglages.
Rappelons que sur ce premier modèle pliant, Apple avait dû faire l’impasse sur Face ID faute de place pour loger le module TrueDepth, ce projecteur de points infrarouges qui modélise le visage en 3D. Il aurait fallu le dédoubler sous les deux écrans dans un châssis de seulement 5,2 mm d’épaisseur une fois déplié, imposant le bouton latéral Touch ID et l’Apple Watch comme solutions de repli, un compromis que nous avions déjà pointé dans notre test de l’iPhone Duo.
    Pour aller plus loin
J’ai testé l’iPhone Duo : un produit qui éblouit pour faire oublier ses compromis
            
Une reconnaissance faciale 2D bridée par Apple elle-même
Privé de capteurs infrarouges, le système se rabat sur l’image plate captée par la simple caméra frontale de l’écran externe : ce qu’on appelle une reconnaissance faciale 2D. Il s’agit du procédé que l’on croise sur de nombreux smartphones Android, nettement plus facile à leurrer qu’une cartographie en relief et totalement inopérant dans l’obscurité.
Apple assure néanmoins aux médias avoir conçu l’algorithme 2D le plus fiable du marché, en précisant que les données biométriques restent confinées dans la Secure Enclave, le coffre-fort matériel de la puce inaccessible aux applications tierces.
La firme à la pomme assume pourtant de castrer volontairement sa propre nouveauté. La fonction ne marche que smartphonz fermé, refuse de valider un achat Apple Pay ou d’ouvrir le trousseau de mots de passe, et expire automatiquement au bout de 45 minutes d’inactivité, ce qui oblige à poser le doigt sur Touch ID pour réarmer le compteur. Pour le moment, Apple a choisi 45 minutes, mais cela pourrait changer selon Numerama.
L’iPhone Duo devient ainsi le deuxième produit maison à adopter ce système allégé, juste après l’écran connecté HomeView lancé en octobre à 299 dollars hors taxes. Apple justifiait alors ce niveau de sécurité réduit par le fait qu’un écran domotique reste à la maison, notait le blogueur John Gruber, un argument beaucoup plus fragile pour un smartphone que l’on oublie volontiers sur la table d’un café.
Pratique sur un bureau, impuissant pour payer
En pratique, ce compromis répond à une frustration bien précise : lorsque l’iPhone Duo est posé fermé sur un bureau, il suffit désormais d’un coup d’œil pour déverrouiller l’écran et lire ses notifications sans avoir à attraper le téléphone pour poser le pouce sur la tranche. Ceux qui portent déjà une Apple Watch au poignet (capable de déverrouiller l’iPhone automatiquement) ou qui l’utilisent principalement ouvert sur sa grande dalle interne n’y gagneront en revanche pas grand-chose.
Si Apple ne précise pas pourquoi elle dégaine cette option deux mois après le lancement, tout laisse penser que la fonction était déjà dans les cartons et avait été écartée en octobre pour ne pas ternir l’image de marque de Face ID. Le vrai correctif matériel attendra la génération suivante : selon Mark Gurman de Bloomberg, Apple veut intégrer Face ID dans l’iPhone Duo 2 en glissant les capteurs directement sous l’écran, même si le calendrier de ce deuxième pliant reste très serré.
    Pour aller plus loin
Apple veut intégrer Face ID dans l’iPhone Duo 2 ainsi qu’un bouton Action, mais le calendrier est très serré
            
Les autres ajustements d’iOS 27.3 pour l’iPhone Duo
Cette mise à jour ne se limite pas au déverrouillage : elle corrige aussi plusieurs petits irritants pointés du doigt depuis la sortie du téléphone fin octobre :
- un nouveau réglage permet enfin de verrouiller et mettre en veille le téléphone lorsqu’on le referme, alors qu’il bascule aujourd’hui automatiquement l’application ouverte vers l’écran externe ;
- le mode « Accès facile », qui décale l’interface vers la droite ou la gauche pour faciliter la navigation à une main sur l’écran fermé, fait son apparition (déjà aperçu dans la première bêta) ;
- Apple revendique désormais 200 000 applications compatibles avec le SDK de l’iPhone Duo, le kit permettant d’adapter l’affichage aux deux dalles, contre 100 000 la semaine précédente. D’ailleurs, téléchargez QUELLE IA qui est compatible iPhone Duo.
Cet ajout de la reconnaissance faciale marque un tournant symbolique. Pour la première fois sur un iPhone, Apple accepte de bricoler une biométrie moins sûre sous la pression des utilisateurs.
À 2 339 euros, on aurait pourtant préféré que les compromis de l’iPhone Duo trouvent une vraie réponse matérielle plutôt qu’un pansement logiciel valable 45 minutes.

articles.title: Papa John's wants your pizza photos for AI quality checks, with free pizza as the reward
articles.text:
Why it matters: Combining Papa John's pizzas with AI sounds like another use of the technology that will make people cringe, but the company claims it's all about making its pizzas better. The fast-food giant is asking customers to help develop its AI quality-control system by sending in a picture of their orders. There's a free pizza on offer in return, which sounds like a good deal, although there are a few conditions.
Papa John's said asking customers to send in a photo of their pizza, along with some feedback, is part of an AI-based quality-control campaign to help make sure each of its pizzas is properly cooked and cut.
CEO Todd Penegor told Reuters the promotion would help improve pizza quality across the chain's franchised restaurants, tackling inconsistencies he described as the brand's "Achilles' heel."
According to the company's announcement, customers must have a Papa Rewards account, opt into text messages, and place an order worth at least $15 through its app or website. They then receive a text inviting them to upload an unedited photo and feedback. Once the photo is confirmed, they unlock a free large one-topping pizza, but redeeming it requires spending at least $5 on their next order.
Penegor said the goal is to replicate what the chain's in-store quality-control cameras already do. Those systems use AI to check for burned cheese, make sure pepperoni slices are cut smoothly, and confirm that the outer crust resembles "a beautiful breadstick."
The problem is that only a few hundred of the chain's roughly 6,000 locations worldwide have those cameras. Photos submitted by customers could give the company a much cheaper way to check pizza quality across more restaurants, though they aren't yet as accurate as the in-store systems.
The company collects the images and customer feedback on what Penegor described as a "huge dashboard." The promotion brought in thousands of photos within days of launching on November 9 and will run until November 20.
According to Penegor, the technology was relatively cheap to build in-house, taking advantage of AI tools the company had already developed with Google Cloud. He said the feedback would help identify which fixes to prioritize and show franchisees where their restaurants are falling short.
This isn't the first non-traditional use of technology in the pizza-delivering business. In 2025, Domino's tested using Boston Dynamics' quadrupedal robot, Spot, to deliver pizzas to customers on a beach and protect the food from seagulls.

articles.title: Le chercheur en guerre contre Microsoft dévoile une 16ᵉ faille Windows, elle peut désactiver votre antivirus
articles.text:
NightmareEclipse a encore frappé. Quelques heures après le Patch Tuesday du 10 novembre, le chercheur Abdelhamid Naceri a mis en ligne une nouvelle faille zero day dans Windows. Baptisée SignDrop, elle permet à un simple utilisateur d’obtenir les droits « SYSTEM », c’est-à-dire les pleins pouvoirs sur l’ordinateur. Comme à son habitude, le chercheur a publié le code d’exploitation sur GitHub, sans prévenir Microsoft en amont, dans le but de mettre la pression sur l’éditeur.
À lire aussi : deux failles de BitLocker permettent de lire les fichiers protégés sur Windows
Une protection de Windows retournée contre lui
Cette fois, le chercheur s’attaque à une protection conçue par Microsoft. La faille se situe dans le CLFS (Common Log File System), un composant clé de Windows qui gère les fichiers journaux du système. Devenu une cible de choix pour les pirates, le composant a eu droit à un mécanisme de protection. L’an dernier, Microsoft a ajouté un système d’authentification, taillé pour signer les fichiers afin de détecter toute modification suspecte.
C’est dans ce système que se trouve la faille SignDrop. Dans les détails, la vulnérabilité pousse Microsoft Defender, l’antivirus par défaut intégré à Windows, à ouvrir un fichier journal (« log ») piégé. Comme Defender dispose des droits les plus élevés du système, Windows crée alors un fichier de signature avec ces mêmes droits, à un emplacement choisi par le pirate. Il n’a plus qu’à y glisser son propre code.
« Si tout est enchaîné correctement, de façon amusante, cette mesure de sécurité légitime peut être utilisée contre elle-même et permettre une élévation de privilèges. Tout est fait correctement par Microsoft ici, mais la logique permet un abus », explique Abdelhamid Naceri.
« Désactiver n’importe quel antivirus »
Le chercheur va plus loin dans son rapport. Selon lui, la technique fonctionne pour « désactiver n’importe quel antivirus
». La demande de création de fichier frauduleuse semble en effet venir du logiciel de sécurité lui-même, ce qui peut berner n’importe quel outil de sécurité. Après avoir testé la faille sur plusieurs versions du système d’exploitation, le chercheur estime que 80 % des installations Windows sont vulnérables. « Si votre installation de Windows a plus de 90 jours », vous êtes vraisemblablement vulnérable, avance Abdelhamid Naceri.
Les chercheurs de Cyderes ont réussi à reproduire l’attaque pour prendre le contrôle d’un ordinateur. Les experts jugent toutefois qu’il est peu probable que 80 % des machines Windows soient vraiment vulnérables. Pour les chercheurs, « la défense est la vulnérabilité ».
Une nouvelle faille signée NightmareEclipse
Le chercheur n’en est pas à son coup d’essai. Également connu sous les pseudonymes de Chaotic Eclipse ou MSNightmare, cet ancien employé de Microsoft enchaîne les révélations depuis le mois d’avril 2026. Parmi ces faits d’arme, on trouve BlueHammer, RedSun, YellowKey, RoguePlanet, ShieldBreak ou encore BigDiskBuster. C’est la seizième faille en un peu plus de sept mois, soit environ une toutes les deux semaines.
Le plus souvent, l’expert attend que Microsoft dévoile son Patch Tuesday avant de dégainer ses découvertes. Pour rappel, le chercheur reproche au géant de Redmond de l’avoir licencié sans bonne raison. En mai dernier, Microsoft avait évoqué la perspective d’une action en justice contre le chercheur, sans mettre ses menaces à exécution jusqu’à maintenant.
À lire aussi : Windows vient de battre un nouveau record monstrueux
Microsoft enquête sur la faille
Microsoft assure avoir pris des mesures à la suite de la découverte d’Abdelhamid Naceri. L’éditeur explique enquêter « activement sur la vulnérabilité signalée » et s’engage à « prendre les mesures nécessaires pour mettre à jour les produits concernés dès que possible ». Microsoft ajoute que Defender « détecte et bloque l’exploitation de cette vulnérabilité », qui n’a pas encore été exploitée par des hackers.

articles.title: Supreme Court keeps injunction against DEI grant defunding in place
articles.text:
On Monday, the Supreme Court announced it would not hear an appeal of a lower court decision that blocked the government from canceling the grants of a handful of researchers whose funding had been revoked during the Trump administration’s purge of DEI-related work. While the decision applies to only seven researchers in California, the lower court had ruled that the government’s actions violated the First Amendment and so may have broad implications.
The Supreme Court provided no discussion of its rejection, and no justices filed a dissent regarding the decision.
The suit was initially filed by a large group of researchers at the University of California, Berkeley and UC San Francisco, contesting grants originally issued by many federal agencies, from the National Institutes of Health to the Department of Transportation. At issue were grants that had been terminated because the agencies decided they violated a Trump executive order blocking the use of DEI. This occurred despite the fact that the government hadn’t bothered to define DEI, and targeted grants were often identified by little more than a keyword search.
In the wake of a Supreme Court decision that held that most grant termination cases had to be heard by a different court, the case was narrowed considerably to just seven UC researchers and a handful of agencies: The Environmental Protection Agency, the National Science Foundation, and the National Endowment for the Humanities.

Moto G77 (256 GB) registra desconto agressivo de 40% na Black November
Moto G77 conta com tela AMOLED de 5.000 nits, câmera principal de 108 MP e bateria prometida para até 37 horas de uso. Oferta com pagamento no Pix pelo Mercado Livre
O Moto G77 (256 GB) está em promoção com 40% de desconto no Mercado Livre. O smartphone sai por apenas R$ 1.499 no Pix em oferta na Black November 2026. Anunciado em março pela Motorola por R$ 2.499, se destaca pela ficha técnica equilibrada, com destaques para a tela brilhante e câmera principal de alta resolução.
O celular utiliza um painel Extreme AMOLED de 6,8″ que reproduz cores intensas, além de entregar resolução Super HD (superior ao Full HD) às imagens. O brilho máximo de 5.000 nits que o Moto G77 promete atingir em circunstâncias de baixa ou nenhuma luminosidade, sendo um dos mais fortes do segmento intermediário. Enquanto a taxa de 120 Hz assegura experiência fluida de modo geral.
O dispositivo traz uma câmera avançada de 108 MP. O sensor principal conta com estabilização óptica (OIS), zoom de 3x para manter a nitidez mesmo a distância, e recursos de IA via Moto AI. Na parte traseira, ainda há uma ultrawide de 8 MP. Enquanto a lente frontal de 32 MP, possui a função Detector de Sorrisos para aprimorar os resultados das selfies.
Equipado com o processador Dimensity 6400 e 8 GB de RAM física, o celular da Motorola com 256 GB de armazenamento entrega desempenho somente para tarefas básicas. Portanto, é mais voltado para usuários com pouco interesse para rodar jogos e executar multitarefas.

A bateria de 5.200 mAh sugere autonomia para mais de um dia de uso intenso, com promessa pela Motorola de até 37 horas de uso, incluindo reprodução de músicas e vídeos. O componente suporta apenas carregamento com fio de até 30 W.

articles.title: Java News Roundup: Lazy Constants, Spring for Apache Pulsar, GlassFish, Hibernate, TomEE, Seed4J
articles.text:
This week's Java roundup for November 9th, 2026, features news highlighting: Lazy Constants proposed to target for JDK 28; TornadoVM jitLLM 3.0; point releases of Seed4J; second release candidates of Spring AI and Spring Boot; first release candidates of Hibernate ORM and Hibernate Reactive; fourth milestone release of GlassFish; and the second milestone release of Apache TomEE.
OpenJDK
JEP 547, Lazy Constants (Fourth Preview), has been elevated from Candidate to Proposed to Target for JDK 28. This JEP proposes a fourth preview, with no changes, after three rounds of preview delivered in the upcoming release of JDK 27 and JDK 26 through JDK 25. Formerly known as Stable Values and Computed Constants, this feature introduces the concept of computed constants, defined as immutable value holders that are initialized at most once. This offers the performance and safety benefits of final fields, while offering greater flexibility as to the timing of initialization. The name change from Stable Values to Lazy Constants with the release of JDK 26, better captures the intent of a high-level use case. The review is expected to conclude on Wednesday, November 18, 2026.
JDK 28
Build 24 of the JDK 28 early-access builds was made available this past week featuring updates from Build 23 that include fixes for various issues. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
For JDK 28, developers are encouraged to report bugs via the Java Bug Database.
Spring Framework
The second release candidate of Spring AI 2.1.0 delivers new features such as: a new DecisionModel API, anchored by the DecisionModel interface, that returns the probability of different outcomes instead of generated text based on yes/no answers, questions about text or a set of fields; and a new similaritySearch(float [], SearchRequest) method, added to the VectorStoreRetriever interface to complement the corresponding overloaded methods, to search with a user's embeddings in more vector stores. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
The second release candidate of Spring Boot 4.2.0 ships with bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: support for reading the value defined in a X-Forwarded-Prefix HTTP header in a WebFlux application on Reactor Netty when the server.forward-headers-strategy property is set to native; and a database assigned to the spring.data.redis.database property is now properly applied to master/replica connections if a value is assigned to the spring.data.redis.masterreplica.nodes property. More details on this release may be found in the release notes and this wiki page.
The Spring for Apache Pulsar team has announced that the project is moving as a subproject within Apache Pulsar at the Apache Software Foundation to "foster even deeper integration and collaboration with the broader Pulsar community." As stated in the blog post:
Bringing this integration directly into the Apache Pulsar project allows the community to streamline development, accelerate feature support, and ensure long-term alignment with the evolution of Apache Pulsar.
Spring for Apache Pulsar 2.0.8, released in October 2026, was the final release under the auspices of the Spring ecosystem.
GlassFish
The fourth milestone release of GlassFish 9.0.0 provides bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: implementation of the Jakarta Persistence 4.0.0-M7 specification with EclipseLink 6.0.0-M1; a move of the Sun Theme module out of the out of the external GlassFish Woodstock Components repository into its own module in GlassFish so that Sun Theme and the Admin Console can be modified together; and an update to versions 1.2.0-M2 and 2.0.0-M1 of Eclipse JNoSQL. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
TornadoVM
Beehive Lab, makers of TornadoVM, has released version 3.0 of jitLLM, a JVM-native LLM inference and serving engine, delivers notable changes such as: 1.43 times faster startup with GraalVM Native Image; an up to 9.3 times faster prefill phase; and a more efficient reading of model weights by eliminating the copy from the mapped GGUF file into a Apple Metal buffer. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Hibernate
The first release candidate of Hibernate ORM 8.0.0 ships with notable changes such as: an implementation of the Jakarta Persistence 4.0.0-M7 and Jakarta Data 1.1.0-M4 specifications (the latter via Hibernate Data Repositories); and support for coordination of graph-based flushing that builds a dependency graph for pending entity and collection mutations. Further details on this release may be found in the what's new page.
The first release candidates of Hibernate Reactive 5.1.0 and 5.0.0 provide notable changes such as: the EXTENDED constant, defined in the Jakarta Persistence PessimisticLockScope enum class, now locks the collection tables as intended to align with the same functionality in Hibernate ORM; and an update to the VertxFactory interface to allow for adding observability without changing the functionality in using the DefaultVertxInstance class. These versions are compatible with Hibernate ORM 8.0.0.CR1. More details on these releases may be found in the release notes for version 5.1.0.CR1 and version 5.0.0.CR1.
Apache TomEE
The second milestone release of Apache TomEE 11.0.0 delivers bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: resolutions to 38 CVEs; completion of their implementation of the Jakarta Authorization 3.0 specification; and TomEE Plume, the enterprise version, now ships the modular EclipseLink JPA artifact instead of the eclipselink Uber-Jar. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
JobRunr
The release of JobRunr 9.0.4 ships with bug fixes and one new feature that improves build caching and security by moving to hardened Docker images. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
JReleaser
The first rolling release of JReleaser 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT provides a new feature in which the -a and -d short option flags, for their respective corresponding --assembly and --download long versions, were removed from the CLI due to the lack of short option flags for the --changelog and --announce flags. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Seed4J
Versions 2.4.0 and 2.3.0 of Seed4J, formerly known as JHipster Lite, deliver bug fixes, dependency upgrades and new features such as: install Playwrite only on applications that execute the relevant Playwright component tests; and improved efficiency by creating one global Maven cache that is shared by the Seed4J build and every generated Maven application that replaces a Maven cache for each generated application. More details on these releases may be found in the release notes for version 2.4.0 and version 2.3.0.
Quarkus
The Quarkus team has introduced the Quarkus Resiliency Testing utility that allows developers to reproduce various failure scenarios and their respective responses while testing an application with the @QuarkusTest annotation. An example application using this new utility may be found here.

articles.title: Jailbroken PS4 runs 9-billion-parameter AI model at up to 43 tokens per second — open-source Garlic LLM bypasses drivers to talk directly to the 2013-era GPU
articles.text:
Jailbroken PS4 runs 9-billion-parameter AI model at up to 43 tokens per second — open-source Garlic LLM bypasses drivers to talk directly to the 2013-era GPU
It needs no PC and no internet, just a console running GoldHEN.
Developer Leonardo Alegría’s open-source project Garlic LLM lets a jailbroken PS4 run the 9-billion-parameter Qwen3.5-9B AI model offline on the console’s 2013-era GPU. The app talks to the GPU directly, and the model is shrunk to about 4.5GiB to fit in the console’s memory, running at 31 to 39 tokens per second.
The project, named after the memory the GPU reads directly — its sibling memory type is “Onion” — relies on a PS4 running GoldHEN, which is a homebrew enabler for exploited consoles. Garlic LLM is a free, single 5.66GB download, available on Hugging Face and installable through the PS4’s Package Installer, with about 6GB free needed, or 12GB if the package is first copied to the console’s internal disk. The developer tested it on a base/Slim PS4 on firmware 11.52.
It’s capable of voice conversation, with spoken replies in seven languages through the Chatterbox speech model and the chat model running at about 22 tokens per second. A held controller button also lets it take dictation with Nvidia’s Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 speech-to-text model, which supports 25 European languages. Parakeet models also power local transcription and dictation apps such as Meetily and Hex. The main model is Alibaba’s small open-weight Qwen3.5-9B, which, at the claimed 31 to 39 tokens per second in text chat — the prompt and test method are not given — is usable on the console.
The closest comparison is the PS5LM fork, which runs llama.cpp as a native app on the PS5 and reaches the console’s AMD GPU through PS5_Vulkan, a port of the RADV driver. The open-source llama.cpp is a widely used program for running language models locally, and RADV is the open-source driver that lets AMD GPUs run Vulkan, the graphics and compute API. On the PS4 there is no such driver layer for homebrew; Garlic LLM uses neither llama.cpp nor a Vulkan port, or so it would appear.
The model’s operations, such as matrix multiplies over 4-bit weights, are compute kernels written in OpenCL C and compiled with LLVM for AMD’s Graphics Core Next (GCN) architecture. The weights are kept in that “Garlic” memory, while the CPU side, in plain C, handles the tokenizer, the interface, text rendering, and audio. The pipeline runs from the prompt to the CPU tokenizer, then, for each token, a PM4 command buffer — the low-level commands a graphics driver would normally generate, which, in this case, the app builds itself — and the GCN kernels, before the token is displayed or spoken. The whole thing is built with the open-source OpenOrbis PS4 toolchain.
One immediate question is how you fit a 9-billion-parameter model in the console’s 8GB of memory, which the CPU and GPU share. At 8 bits per weight, you have one byte per parameter, meaning you’d need at least 9GB, with typically more than that required overall. Part of the answer is 4-bit (“Q4”) weights, which take half as much, although 3-bit (“Q3”) weights, at about 3.5 bits with scales, are used for the two largest matrices in each layer.
Using the combination gets you to about 4.5GiB, versus about 4.9GiB if it were all 4-bit. The attention, or KV, cache is also 4-bit, which lets a 16K-token context fit, in comparison to the model’s native 256K. The Parakeet dictation model adds 0.33GiB and the Chatterbox voice models 0.29GiB and 0.09GiB, for a grand total of 5.23GiB, or 5.62GB, which closely matches the 5.66GB package size.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The next question is performance. Qwen3.5 comes with a multi-token prediction (MTP) head, and Garlic LLM uses it to draft up to two tokens ahead, with the full model verifying. This matches what the model was trained for, and the vLLM instructions on Alibaba’s model card use two speculative tokens. The project credits this for its chat speed on 2013 hardware.
Code also comes out faster with this setup, at up to 43 tokens per second. Also detailed is the default temperature, or model variability, which is 0.7 — Alibaba recommends 0.7 for general tasks with thinking off and 1.0 with it on — although the demo video uses 0, so it is predictable. At 35 tokens per second, the middle of the reported performance range, a 300-token answer takes under nine seconds. As a comparison, the PS5 ran the three-times-larger Qwen3.8-27B at about 20 tokens per second and the smaller Gemma 4 E4B and Llama 3.2 3B at 61 and 124, respectively, which is potentially quicker.
The PS4 Pro is “not tested yet,” but the developer is asking users for reports on GitHub. The PS5 is not supported as the app is written specifically for the PS4’s GPU and system software. The app itself contains no exploit, but GoldHEN is installed at the user’s own risk.
Follow Tom’s Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.
