articles.title: Así cotizan las principales criptomonedas del mundo digital este lunes 16 de noviembre
articles.text:
Las criptomonedas son un activo digital innovador que han experimentado un crecimiento monumental en los últimos tiempos debido a varios elementos que contribuyen a ello, entre ellos que algunos gobiernos hayan decidido darles una oportunidad como moneda de curso legal; no obstante, también han sufrido descalabros que han puesto en duda su viabilidad, como el más reciente episodio conocido como el "criptoinvierno".
Pese a este panorama, cada vez más personas han empezado a adquirir criptomonedas para poder invertir en algo "seguro" y "fiable" tanto a corto como a largo plazo, a pesar de los niveles extremos de inestabilidad que sufre constantemente.
Sin embargo, invertir o comprar en criptodivisas es más fácil de lo que parece. Hay que recordar que se trata de monedas virtuales, por lo que serán controladas en carteras o monederos que comparten esa particularidad, pues a diferencia del dinero corriente, no tienen un soporte físico.
El precio de las criptomonedas hoy
Esta es la cotización de las criptodivisas más destacadas en este momento.
El Bitcoin, cotiza a 64.634,96 dólares, lo que implicó un cambio de -1,026% en las últimas horas.
La segunda criptomoneda más popular del mercado, Ethereum, ha mostrado un movimiento de -1,462% en las últimas 24 horas, por lo que su valor se ubica en 1.808,66 dólares.
En el caso de TetherUs, su precio es de 1 dólares, por lo que en el último día tuvo un movimiento de -0,05%.
Por su parte, BNB, tiene un valor de 590,07 dólares, con un cambio de 1,5%, en cambio el Litecoin cotizó a 44.575 dólares, tras una variación de 0.4271333.
Finalmente, el Dogecoin, una de las monedas virtuales que fue impulsada por Elon Musk, tiene un valor de 0,06 dólares tras presentar un cambio de 2,27% en las últimas 24 horas.
Qué pasa con las criptodivisas
Luego de que en las primeras semanas de mayo del 2022 se viviera el "criptocrash" o "criptoinvierno" que dejaron al descubierto la enorme volatilidad de estas monedas digitales, ha llegado un nuevo periodo de relativa estabilidad.
Bitcoin, ethereum y BNB han mostrado variaciones "controladas", puesto que no se han disparado los precios como en semanas previas. Por ejemplo, a inicios de agosto, las mencionadas anteriormente tuvieron un cambio menor del 2%.
Por otra parte, algo que esta llamando la atención en el mundo de las criptomonedas es que China está ablandando sus restricciones y podría comenzar a permitir su uso. Específicamente sería Hong Kong en donde este cambio se haría presente.
Sumado a ello, la plataforma de transacciones digitales PayPal anunció su propia stablecoin llamada PayPal USD (PYUSD), que cuenta por el respaldo de depósitos en dólares, bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a corto plazo y activos equivalentes.
La compañía ha afirmado en su declaración que permitirá la transferencia de fondos a monederos digitales de terceros y proporcionará detalles sobre cómo integrar su servicio en exchanges centralizados y descentralizados, con el objetivo de ser utilizado en Finanzas Descentralizadas (DeFi, por sus siglas en inglés). Por lo tanto, es muy probable que se utilice ampliamente en la industria Web3.
Criptomonedas en Latinoamérica
Criptomonedas en México: el Banco de México (Banxico) ha determinado que ninguna de las instituciones que participan en el sistema financiero nacional podrá hacer uso o deberá permitir operaciones de ninguna clase a través de este medio de pago.
En territorio mexicano el empresario Ricardo Salinas Pliego, uno de los más ricos del país, ha mostrado interés en las criptomonedas y ha asegurado que varios de sus negocios aceptarán bitcoin en el futuro, incluido su banco; hasta el momento una de sus tiendas más populares ya lo hace.
Criptomonedas en Perú: el Banco Central de Reserva del Perú (BCR) ha dejado en claro que su misión no es ser el primero ni el segundo banco central que regule el uso de las criptomonedas, ello debido a la inestabilidad que las caracteriza. Sin embargo, hace días el presidente del (BCR) aseguró que el BCR trabajaba en un proyecto de moneda digital propia.
Criptomonedas en Colombia: en la nación sudamericana hay más de 500 sitios donde es permitido pagar con criptodivisas. Colombia ocupa el puesto 14 entre 26 países de adopción de criptomonedas, según el informe de Finder.
Criptomonedas en Centroamérica: en el gobierno de El Salvador, el bitcoin, que en septiembre de 2021 se convirtió en moneda de curso legal, ha perdido oficialmente este estatus en este enero del 2025 tras una reforma aprobada por la Asamblea Legislativa del país. Según informó la prensa local, la modificación de la Ley Bitcoin fue impulsada por el gobierno del presidente Nayib Bukele y respaldada por la mayoría oficialista en el órgano legislativo. Este cambio marca el fin de una política que había colocado al país centroamericano en el centro del debate global sobre las criptomonedas.
¿Cómo crear una criptomoneda?
Al momento de crear una criptomoneda es importante primero determinar qué se desea tener: una moneda o un token. La primera usa su propia blockchain, mientras que la segunda se basa en una red preexistente.
De acuerdo con el sitio de Binance, para crear una criptomoneda se necesita de un gran equipo de desarrolladores y expertos; mientras que para el token sí se requieren conocimientos técnicos pero es posible crearlo en minutos a través del uso de otras blockchains como Ethereum o BNB, que son las más populares.
Los costos de creación, el tiempo requerido y el uso de fuerza de trabajo dependerá de si se opta por hacer una moneda virtual o un token. En éste último caso también se puede usar un código establecido para crear tokens o pagar para usar un servicio de creación de monedas.
Es importante saber que antes de crear una criptomoneda se debe considerar su utilidad y estado legal.
En el caso de elegir crear una criptomoneda, entonces se debe elegir una blockchain, posteriormente se debe hacer un plan acorde al funcionamiento y la funcionalidad de la blockchain para diseñar los nodos y la interfaz.

articles.title: Una comunidad permite durante años el uso de una salida de humos y lo prohíbe tras el cambio de propietario la reforma del local: el Supremo anula el acuerdo por ir contra sus propios actos
articles.text:
Que una comunidad de propietarios permita durante años utilizar una instalación y después decida prohibirla puede acabar siendo un problema, especialmente cuando el dueño de un local ya ha invertido dinero en reformarlo. Justo eso es lo que ocurrió en un edificio de Madrid, donde los vecinos exigieron retirar una chimenea de salida de humos que llevaba instalada desde 1990. Sin embargo, el Tribunal Supremo terminó dando la razón a la empresa propietaria del local al considerar que la comunidad había actuado contra sus propios actos.
Como recoge NoticiasTrabajo en su información sobre el conflicto, la instalación había sido autorizada inicialmente a un inquilino con carácter personal y temporal, pero siguió utilizándose cuando este abandonó el local. De hecho, otro arrendatario la empleó al menos desde 2002 sin que la comunidad exigiera retirarla. La situación cambió cuando una empresa compró el establecimiento en 2016 para abrir un restaurante y comunicó su proyecto de reforma a la presidenta y al administrador, que incluso visitaron las obras. ¿Y qué ocurrió? Nadie se opuso al uso de la chimenea y las únicas preocupaciones que trasladaron estaban relacionadas con el ruido.
El Supremo considera que la comunidad actuó contra sus propios actos
Una vez terminada la reforma, llegó el conflicto. En marzo de 2017, la comunidad aprobó un acuerdo para prohibir el uso de la salida de humos y exigir el desmontaje de la chimenea, pese a que había conocido las obras y permitido que finalizaran. La propietaria acudió a los tribunales y perdió en primera instancia, pero la Audiencia Provincial de Madrid anuló el acuerdo al entender que los vecinos habían generado una situación de confianza que después contradijeron. La comunidad recurrió de nuevo y el caso terminó en el Tribunal Supremo.
Aquí entra en juego el artículo 7.1 del Código Civil, que establece que los derechos deben ejercerse conforme a las exigencias de la buena fe. En su sentencia 103/2026, de 29 de enero, el Supremo explica que la comunidad no podía ignorar su comportamiento anterior, especialmente después de permitir durante más de 14 años el uso de la instalación y conocer las reformas del nuevo propietario sin plantear ninguna objeción a la chimenea.
A todo esto debemos sumar que los artículos 7 y 17 de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal regulan las actuaciones sobre elementos comunes y los acuerdos necesarios para modificarlos. Sin embargo, esas facultades también tienen límites, como ha ocurrido en este caso. El Supremo consideró que la comunidad había esperado a que concluyeran las obras y se realizara la inversión para prohibir algo que llevaba años tolerando. Por eso, desestimó su recurso y confirmó la nulidad del acuerdo, al entender que vulneraba la buena fe y la doctrina de los actos propios.

articles.title: Les signalements de contenus pédocriminels liés à l’IA ont bondi de 8 400 % en deux ans
articles.text:
En 2023, les entreprises de la tech ont signalé environ 4 700 contenus pédocriminels liés à l’intelligence artificielle à l’organisme américain chargé de les recenser. En 2025, elles ont transmis plus de 400 000 signalements de ce type.
Childlight, un institut de recherche sur la sécurité des enfants installé à Édimbourg, a relevé ces chiffres dans les signalements reçus par le National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC), et calcule une hausse de plus de 8 400 % en deux ans. Ce total inclut les deepfakes fabriqués avec des applications de « nudification ». Avec ces outils, n’importe qui peut obtenir, à partir d’une photo d’une personne habillée, une image où elle apparaît nue. Ces images sont fausses, mais des maîtres chanteurs peuvent les utiliser pour exiger de l’argent ou d’autres photos aux enfants représentés.
Des photos ordinaires d’enfants transformées en images pédocriminelles
Au Royaume-Uni, les analystes de l’Internet Watch Foundation (IWF), l’ONG qui surveille les contenus pédocriminels dans le monde entier, observent aussi cette progression. Ils ont examiné 6 310 images générées par IA au premier semestre 2026, toutes conformes à la définition légale des abus sexuels sur mineurs. C’est 40 % de plus que sur l’ensemble de l’année 2025.
Pour fabriquer ces images, un criminel n’a plus besoin d’approcher un enfant. Une photo de votre fils ou de votre fille publiée sur un compte Instagram ouvert, sur le site de son école ou sur la page de son club de sport peut servir de point de départ, et les autorités britanniques et l’IWF demandent aux parents de ne plus exposer publiquement les photos de leurs enfants.
Des assistants grand public ont aussi servi à produire ces montages. Début 2026, des internautes ont demandé à Grok, l’IA d’Elon Musk, de dénuder sur X des photos de femmes, parfois mineures, avant que xAI se décide à empêcher son assistant de déshabiller des personnes réelles. Si votre enfant reçoit ce type de chantage, vous pouvez trouver de l’aide au 3018, le numéro national contre le cyberharcèlement.
Childlight demande aux gouvernements de reconnaître une urgence de santé publique
Une meilleure détection et de meilleurs signalements expliquent en partie cette hausse, reconnaît Debi Fry, directrice mondiale des données de Childlight. Mais, comme l’explique la chercheuse, « la rapidité avec laquelle l’intelligence artificielle modifie la menace qui pèse sur les enfants est profondément préoccupante ».
La nouvelle édition de l’indice Into the Light, consacrée à l’Asie de l’Est et au Pacifique, à l’Amérique latine et aux Caraïbes, et à l’Amérique du Nord, mesure aussi les autres formes d’abus. Les précédentes portaient sur l’Europe occidentale. Selon Childlight, plus de 300 millions d’enfants dans le monde subissent chaque année au moins une forme d’exploitation ou d’abus sexuel facilité par la technologie, et un enfant sur quatre sera victime d’au moins une forme d’abus avant ses 18 ans.
L’institut a aussi étudié les violences commises hors ligne. En Amérique du Nord, près d’un tiers des filles et plus d’un garçon sur dix ont subi une agression sexuelle en personne pendant leur enfance. Aux États-Unis, le taux de signalements de contenus pédocriminels a augmenté de 63 % entre 2024 et 2025, contre 18 % au Canada.
« Il est impossible de prévenir efficacement les abus ou de protéger les enfants sans en comprendre l’ampleur et la nature réelles », déplore Paul Stanfield, directeur général de Childlight. L’institut demande aux gouvernements de reconnaître dans l’exploitation sexuelle des enfants une « urgence de santé publique évitable », et d’investir dans des données plus fiables.

articles.title: Intel sued by shareholders who claim it hid PC sales slump before 29% stock crash
articles.text:
What just happened? It's not just Nvidia being sued by its shareholders over claims it withheld important information. Intel is facing a proposed class-action lawsuit over allegations it hid the severity of the decline in PC sales, which the plaintiffs say caused the company's stock to crash almost 29% in one day.
The complaint, filed in federal court in San Jose on November 13, names Intel, CEO Lip-Bu Tan, and CFO David Zinsner as defendants. Michigan's City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System is leading the case, seeking unspecified damages.
Shareholders allege Intel took too long to disclose how weakening PC sales and a buildup of unsold inventory would hurt revenue. They argue those problems outweighed the benefits Team Blue was receiving from data center construction and the AI boom.
The suit specifically accuses Intel of making "materially false and/or misleading" statements that suggested demand was improving. Investors say October's results undermined those assurances, revealing the extent of the PC slowdown after they had bought shares at allegedly inflated prices. The complaint covers purchases between July 23 and October 29.
Despite third-quarter earnings beating expectations and data center revenue jumping almost 80%, Intel's outlook disappointed investors. On October 29, the company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, below Wall Street's roughly $17 billion estimate, and warned of a prolonged PC slowdown. Shares plunged 28.6% the following day, wiping out around $140 billion in market value and making it Intel's worst trading day since 1974.
The lawsuit highlights Intel's PC business revenue falling 9% year-over-year, or about $800 million, to $8.1 billion in the third quarter. Its main accusation is that Intel failed to give shareholders a timely and accurate picture of that deterioration.
Shareholders also say Intel had a reason to hide its problems: it sold $23 billion worth of shares at $95 each in August.
Intel expects PC shipments to drop around 12% this year and another 10% in 2027. AI data centers continue to buy up huge amounts of memory, pushing PC prices higher and putting buyers off. Intel doesn't expect that situation to improve until memory supply and prices normalize, but when that will happen is anyone's guess.
There had already been warnings about consumer pricing getting worse. September brought reports of another planned 10% Intel CPU price increase, with the company reportedly prioritizing more profitable server processors at its factories.
The case follows the shareholder lawsuit against Nvidia and Jensen Huang over his relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative. Both cases allege investors lost money after information they say should have been disclosed earlier became public.

articles.title: Neural Rendering Could Keep Xbox Project Helix Affordable
articles.text:
Monday, November 16th 2026
Neural Rendering Could Keep Xbox Project Helix Affordable
For the 25th anniversary of Xbox, celebrating one of its longest-running projects, Microsoft announced that it sees great potential in new technologies that could lower hardware costs while enhancing visual fidelity. According to Jason Ronald, Xbox VP for next-generation technologies, neural rendering could be one of those technologies that significantly boosts visual fidelity. This would allow the compute requirements to remain within the limits of what a console can support, rather than needing a full workstation, and fit within a home entertainment form factor. Not only would raw compute be lower, but actual memory demand would also be reduced, as neural rendering tends to be more efficient, which is particularly useful when memory is in short supply.
Jason Ronald, Xbox Vice President of Next GenerationThis is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering, because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that.
Neural rendering employs AI to enhance lighting, shadows, and material details using information from the game engine. This technology acts as a final rendering stage, building on the original frame, geometry, textures, and lighting data. This method enables developers to incorporate more realistic lighting and material effects without having to explicitly model and render all the additional details. AMD will power Xbox Project Helix, which suggests we can expect more AI cores embedded in the semi-custom SoCs that power Xbox, featuring next-generation RDNA 5 / UDNA graphics IP.

articles.title: AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
articles.text:
AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
- Date:
- November 14, 2026
- Source:
- University of California - Berkeley
- Summary:
- Scientists have uncovered a hidden warning sign in routine heart scans that could predict sudden cardiac death before it strikes. The AI-powered discovery outperformed conventional screening methods, potentially revealing thousands of people at risk of a fatal heart malfunction that doctors might otherwise miss.
- Share:
More than 300,000 people in the United States die from sudden cardiac arrest each year. This deadly emergency occurs when the heart's electrical system suddenly fails, causing the heart to stop pumping blood. It can strike older adults with known heart conditions as well as seemingly healthy young athletes. Although implanted defibrillators can prevent some of these deaths, doctors have long struggled to determine which patients need them most.
Now, researchers at UC Berkeley have identified a previously overlooked warning signal in routine heart scans that could make it easier to recognize people at risk before a fatal event occurs.
The discovery was made using artificial intelligence trained on more than 440,000 electrocardiograms, or EKGs, collected in Sweden. By comparing the electrical patterns recorded in these scans with information from death certificates, the researchers taught an AI system to recognize subtle differences between healthy individuals, patients with known heart risks, and people who eventually died from sudden cardiac causes.
The team then evaluated the technology using thousands of additional patient records from the United States and Taiwan, testing whether the patterns could reliably identify people at heightened risk in different populations.
AI Detects Hidden Heart Risks That Standard Tests Miss
The results suggest that AI can identify vulnerable patients more effectively than the conventional tests doctors typically rely on. Current screening methods largely focus on how much blood the heart pumps with each contraction, a measurement used to assess whether someone might benefit from an implanted defibrillator.
Using these traditional measurements, doctors can identify a group of patients with an annual sudden cardiac death rate of 4.6%. The AI system, however, identified a group with an annual death rate of 7%, demonstrating a greater ability to distinguish patients facing serious danger.
Importantly, the algorithm also recognized a broader population of people at elevated risk, including thousands who would not normally raise concerns under existing medical guidelines. Most of these individuals would have been classified as relatively low risk using conventional methods.
Another major advantage is that the AI system works with ordinary EKG images, which are already routinely collected in hospitals and medical centers around the world. This means the technology could potentially improve screening without requiring an entirely new type of medical test.
The findings, published in Nature, could eventually help physicians make more informed decisions about who should receive an implanted defibrillator. They also raise an intriguing scientific question about what changes inside the heart produce the electrical patterns that AI has learned to recognize.
"Medical decisions are really hard, and I think that's why AI is so exciting for me," said Ziad Obermeyer, an associate professor at UC Berkeley's School of Public Health and the study's lead author. "We can not only make better decisions, but also start to understand what's actually going on with these patients before their heart stops."
Why Sudden Cardiac Death Is So Difficult to Predict
Sudden cardiac arrest is different from a heart attack. A heart attack happens when blood flow to part of the heart becomes blocked or severely restricted. Cardiac arrest, by contrast, results from a failure of the electrical signals that coordinate the heartbeat.
Immediate CPR and an electrical shock from an automated external defibrillator can sometimes restore the heart's rhythm. However, roughly 90% of people who experience sudden cardiac arrest outside a hospital die within minutes, making early recognition of those at risk especially important.
For Obermeyer, an emergency physician whose research combines artificial intelligence, medicine, and health policy, sudden cardiac death remains one of medicine's most frustrating unsolved problems.
Because victims often die without warning, researchers have limited opportunities to observe what happens inside the heart immediately before it stops. An autopsy may uncover blocked blood vessels, hardened tissue, or other structural abnormalities, but it cannot fully reveal how the heart was functioning in the moments leading up to death.
"One thing that makes the problem very tragic, but also very well suited for AI, is that we have the cure for this problem," Obermeyer said. "If you knew you were one of the people who was going to drop dead, you would go to a cardiologist and you'd get a defibrillator implanted. The problem is that doctors can't figure out who needs one before it's too late."
The Problem With Current Heart Risk Screening
Doctors currently rely heavily on a measurement of how effectively the heart pushes blood out with each beat. Patients whose hearts pump below a specified threshold may be considered candidates for an implantable cardioverter defibrillator, a device that can deliver an electrical shock when a dangerous heart rhythm develops.
But obtaining this measurement generally requires a more extensive medical evaluation. Many people who eventually experience sudden cardiac arrest never receive such testing because they have no obvious reason to suspect they are in danger.
The approach also has limitations for patients who are identified as high risk. About two-thirds of implanted defibrillators in these patients never need to deliver a shock. As a result, many individuals undergo expensive, invasive procedures for potentially fatal emergencies that may never occur.
At the same time, thousands of people who are not recognized as being at risk die unexpectedly each year.
"In some fraction of those people, we could have prevented those deaths if we had just known it in time," Obermeyer said. "There are a lot of lives being lost from people who are dropping dead of sudden cardiac death that are preventable if we just had better AI tools to find these things."
The researchers hope that identifying more accurate warning signs could help doctors direct preventive treatments toward the patients most likely to benefit.
How Researchers Trained AI to Recognize Deadly Heart Patterns
Developing the algorithm required three independent collections of medical data gathered from different parts of the world.
The researchers began with six years of EKG recordings from Sweden's unified healthcare system. By linking these scans to death certificates, they could examine the electrical patterns of patients who later experienced sudden cardiac death and compare them with those of other patients.
The AI learned to identify combinations of spikes, waves, and other characteristics in the recordings that appeared to be associated with increased risk. Once the system had been trained, the team tested it against two additional datasets: two years of anonymized EKG records from a San Diego hospital system and a separate collection of patient data from Taipei.
This international testing helped researchers evaluate whether the algorithm's predictive abilities extended beyond the Swedish population used to develop it.
"Good AI starts with good data," said Obermeyer, who is also part of the joint UCSF-UC Berkeley Computational Precision Health program. "Unfortunately, data like the ones we used for this study are incredibly hard to access. It's a big part of why there's so little clinical AI in use today."
Obtaining and organizing the information was itself a massive undertaking. According to Obermeyer, assembling the datasets took approximately 10 years and involved contributions from two organizations he helped establish, Dandelion Health and Nightingale Open Science. Both organizations work to advance medical research through better access to data and artificial intelligence.
"It's one of the tremendous luxuries of being at Berkeley," Obermeyer said. "You can pursue these projects that just are a slow burn and then have -- hopefully -- a big return when they get over the finish line."
From Hidden Heart Signals to Lifesaving Treatments
The researchers have already begun exploring how the system might be used in actual healthcare settings.
Obermeyer is collaborating with medical systems in Sweden, Taiwan, and the United States to introduce the algorithm into hospital EKG databases. The goal is to examine existing heart scans for signs of elevated risk and identify patients who may benefit from additional monitoring.
Under the proposed approach, physicians would contact patients whose EKGs receive a high-risk assessment and offer them the opportunity to wear a patch that continuously records their heart's electrical activity.
These longer recordings could provide valuable clues about the biological processes responsible for the warning signals detected by the AI. Understanding those processes could help researchers explain why certain hearts are more vulnerable to suddenly developing fatal electrical disturbances.
For some patients, the additional information might ultimately support a recommendation to receive an implanted defibrillator, potentially preventing a sudden and otherwise unexpected death.
Obermeyer has also created a website where people interested in learning about their own risk can provide basic personal information and an email address. The research team can then contact them about EKG analysis when the technology becomes more widely available.
Could AI Reveal New Secrets About the Human Heart?
Beyond its potential to improve the prevention of sudden cardiac death, the discovery highlights how artificial intelligence could help scientists investigate medical mysteries that have resisted conventional approaches.
Rather than simply identifying patients who might need treatment, the algorithm has uncovered patterns in heart activity that researchers do not yet fully understand. Studying those signals could lead to new insights into the electrical disturbances responsible for sudden cardiac death and potentially reveal additional opportunities for prevention.
Obermeyer believes this ability to uncover previously unrecognized biological patterns could become one of AI's most important contributions to medicine, opening new directions for research while helping physicians make better decisions.
"There is also going to be a new way of doing science that comes out of these tools," Obermeyer said, "and it's fun to think about how that starts happening."

articles.title: Barracuda Hacked Amid Surge in Artex-Powered Cyberattacks
articles.text:
The Artex agentic AI penetration testing framework has become a common tool in Chinese threat actors’ arsenal, and Barracuda is one of its victims.
Published on GitHub in July 2026, Artex relies on a planner to formulate an objective and create tasks based on it, and on agents to perform those tasks, while the platform itself records the progress, findings, and assets.
It reportedly used DeepSeek v4.1-flash as the initial model, but can use other LLMs as well, and GLM-5.3 and Grok 4.6 were observed in certain instances. Overall, however, its users mainly rely on Chinese models, which are more permissive compared to US-made ones.
Artex was designed for security testing, but threat actors have been using it as part of in-the-wild intrusions since at least August, and its occurrence in real-world attacks has increased significantly during the past several weeks.
“The framework enables threat actors with minimal technical expertise to conduct complex, multi-target operations simultaneously, fundamentally accelerating attack velocity and expanding operational scale,” the FBI warns in a new alert (PDF).
Mentioning the framework’s use in attacks on South Korean financial firms and ConnectWise, the FBI warns of the risks Artex poses: faster attacks through automation, exploitation of neglected peripheral devices, and the ability to find and exploit supply chain attack vectors.
The framework’s developer removed their GitHub repository in October, but Artex continues to proliferate through other channels. In early November, Censys was seeing roughly 1,500 hosts running exposed Artex consoles.
In October, Artex was used by Chinese espionage group Vapor Panda in a campaign targeting over 200 organizations in 14 countries, including “foreign ministries, a European presidency, and US pharmaceutical, semiconductor, defense, and nuclear organizations,” SentinelOne reports.
Storm-0940 is another Chinese state-sponsored group using Artex, but evidence shows that financially motivated threat actors such as Storm-3358 have also adopted the framework, Cisco’s Talos notes.
Post-exploitation, the threat actors were seen abusing compromised credentials and keys, escalating privileges, deploying persistence, moving laterally, and stealing credentials and data.
“Observed impacts range from access to cloud secrets and mailbox data to the use of compromised applications to reach connected environments,” Talos says.
Amazon describes similar observations, noting that one of the most prominent Artex campaigns was focused on large-scale theft of credentials to access AI models, while another targeted cryptocurrency exchanges.
Barracuda, which fell victim to an Artex-powered intrusion, published similar findings: hackers used an exposed valid cloud access key to map its reach, then reused discovered secrets to access more systems and exfiltrate more credentials and secrets.
“In all, the attacker touched about 10 cloud accounts in roughly 44 hours. The work was methodical and tireless. The probe names, the other indicators we collected, the order in which the attacker worked through our systems, and its built-in routines for hunting credentials and wallets all match Artex,” Barracuda explains.
The attack unfolded between November 1 and November 2, targeted sensitive material across secret stores, configurations, Kubernetes service accounts, and server metadata services, and left a backdoor behind in a Kubernetes cluster.
On some servers, the attackers gained shell access and used it to search for Ethereum keystore files, seed phrase files, extended private keys, and other wallet-related information.
The attack, Barracuda says, was similar to the October intrusion at cloud application hosting platform Railway. Furthermore, it fits the previously reported wave of intrusions at dozens of AI developer platforms.
Barracuda has not attributed the attack, noting that Artex is used by many groups.
Amazon’s analysis of two Artex-powered campaigns revealed that the attackers relied on long-known techniques, but operated at far greater speeds courtesy of AI.
“The agents succeeded where basic security hygiene was missing, including default or hardcoded credentials, keys left in code and public artifacts, unauthenticated interfaces and inference endpoints, and unpatched software. Getting those fundamentals right remains the most effective defense,” Amazon says.
“The reported Artex activity shows that autonomous attackers don’t need a zero-day. They can find exposed services, exploit authorization gaps, and keep adapting while defenders are still triaging alerts and approving a response. When every defensive action has to wait for a person, the attacker controls the pace. Defenders need to move from identifying exposure to verified protection at machine speed,” Miggo Security co-founder and CEO Daniel Shechter said.
Related: Is AI Making Us Worse at Cybersecurity?
Related: OpenAI Unveils Daybreak Red Team, Defense Factory Security Tools

articles.title: Uno Platform 7.0 Adds WebGPU Backend, Apple TV and Reactor Support, and Retires Native Rendering
articles.text:
The Uno Platform team released Uno Platform 7.0, which unifies rendering on SkiaSharp 4 with an experimental WebGPU backend, adds Apple TV as a target platform and supports .NET 11 from day zero. The release also brings third-party .NET MAUI controls and Microsoft.UI.Reactor library to every target, and removes native rendering and Mac Catalyst.
Uno Platform is an open-source framework for building .NET applications with C# and WinUI XAML for Windows, Android, iOS, macOS, Linux and WebAssembly. The team describes 7.0 as its largest release, with 5,219 commits and 704 closed issues since 6.7. According to the team’s benchmarks, 7.0 is about 2x faster at the median and 5x smaller than 6.7, with some operations, such as brush creation, up to 38x faster. These figures come from the vendor and the workloads were not published in detail.
All targets now render through one pluggable pipeline. SkiaSharp 4 is the default, and Uno Platform is a co-maintainer of the library alongside the .NET team at Microsoft. On Android, Windows and Linux, Skia now renders through Vulkan by default. The WebGPU backend, available on all desktop, mobile and WebAssembly targets, is enabled by adding WebGpu to UnoFeatures and registering the backend on the host builder. It uses wgpu-native outside the browser and the browser’s own WebGPU support on WebAssembly. The team measured up to a 50% frame-rate improvement depending on the scene, and says a WebGPU-only app drops about 6 MB of uncompressed native code from WebAssembly builds. A new WebGpuCanvasElement lets applications issue their own WebGPU commands inside the UI.
Through .NET MAUI Embedding, controls from vendors such as Syncfusion, Telerik, Infragistics, DevExpress and Esri previously ran only on iOS, Android, macOS and Windows. They now work on every Uno Platform target, including the web and Linux. In the other direction, existing .NET MAUI apps can reach the browser and Linux through Uno Platform’s .NET MAUI handlers.
Microsoft.UI.Reactor, Microsoft’s declarative C# framework for WinUI with hooks such as UseState and no XAML, now runs on desktop, browser, Android and iOS. It is enabled with the Reactor UnoFeature, is in preview, and can coexist with existing XAML pages in the same visual tree. Apple TV support is added through the net10.0-tvos target framework, targets tvOS 15 and later, renders through Metal and uses the Siri Remote for focus navigation. .NET 11 is supported on every head, for example through dotnet new unoapp -tfm net11.0, while .NET 10 remains the long-term support option.
RichTextBlock and RichEditBox are now available on every platform, closing an issue opened in 2018. WinUI alignment continues with ItemsRepeater and ItemsView ported from current WinUI sources, LinedFlowLayout, the TitleBar control, multiple windows on iPad and Lottie rendering through Composition. Smaller additions include built-in input validation through INotifyDataErrorInfo, TalkBack, VoiceOver and AT-SPI screen-reader support, and the uno-devserver app command for launching and inspecting running apps from scripts and CI.
The breaking changes are:
- Native rendering is retired, although native views such as maps and video players can still be embedded.
- Uno.Sdk single-project apps are the only supported project format, with the UNOB0029 and UNOB0022 diagnostics for older projects.
- Mac Catalyst is removed, and macOS apps use the net10.0-desktop head.
- Apps target net10.0 by default, and the Windows head uses Windows App SDK 2.4. Minimum versions are iOS and tvOS 15.0, Android API 24 and Windows 10 19041.
- Libraries built against 6.x are binary-incompatible and must be rebuilt, and DependencyObject is now a single class without DependencyObjectStore.
Most apps upgrade by changing the Uno.Sdk version in global.json, following the migration guide. The team released Uno Platform Studio 3.3 alongside it.
The release follows Uno Platform 6.7 in September, which added Android TV, Android Auto and Wear OS targets, semantic styles shared by the Material and Simple themes, and damage-region repainting on Skia renderers. It also removed the WPF targets.

articles.title: Amazfit Bip 6: smartwatch oferece tela AMOLED, GPS integrado e mais de 140 modalidades esportivas
articles.text:
Um bom exemplo de smartwatch com bons recursos por preço acessível é o Bip 6, relógio inteligente que combina design moderno, monitoramento de saúde, ferramentas esportivas e uma autonomia de bateria que promete agradar quem não gosta de depender constantemente do carregador.
Com estrutura leve, acabamento em alumínio e tela AMOLED de 1,97 polegada, o modelo apresenta uma proposta interessante tanto para quem pratica atividades físicas quanto para quem deseja acompanhar informações do dia a dia diretamente no pulso.
Tela AMOLED e construção leve
Um dos primeiros destaques do Amazfit Bip 6 é sua tela AMOLED de 1,97″, com resolução de 390 x 450 pixels e brilho máximo de até 2.000 nits.
Na prática, isso significa imagens nítidas, cores vibrantes e boa visibilidade mesmo em ambientes externos e sob luz solar intensa.
O relógio pesa apenas 27,9 gramas sem a pulseira e utiliza uma estrutura com moldura de liga de alumínio e corpo de polímero reforçado com fibra. A combinação proporciona leveza e uma construção adequada para acompanhar diferentes atividades.
Outro ponto positivo é a resistência à água de 5 ATM, que permite utilizar o dispositivo durante atividades aquáticas compatíveis, como natação.
Mais de 140 modalidades esportivas e GPS integrado
Se existe uma área em que o Bip 6 procura se destacar, é no acompanhamento de atividades físicas.
São mais de 140 modalidades esportivas disponíveis, incluindo corrida, caminhada, ciclismo, natação e musculação. Um diferencial interessante é o reconhecimento inteligente de 25 tipos de exercícios de força, com acompanhamento de repetições, séries e períodos de descanso, além do reconhecimento automático de outras sete atividades esportivas.
O dispositivo também conta com GPS integrado e suporte a cinco sistemas de posicionamento por satélite, permitindo registrar trajetos e distâncias sem depender exclusivamente do smartphone.
Para corredores, há recursos específicos como modo de corrida em pista, correção inteligente de trajetos e ritmo virtual, que ajuda a acompanhar o desempenho em relação a uma meta estabelecida.
Outro destaque é a possibilidade de conectar equipamentos esportivos externos, como cintas de frequência cardíaca, medidores de potência para corrida e ciclismo, velocímetros e sensores de cadência para bicicletas.
O sistema PeakBeats também oferece análises do desempenho dos exercícios, enquanto o Zepp Coach utiliza inteligência artificial para ajudar a criar planos de treinamento personalizados.
O relógio ainda permite criar modelos de treinamento pelo aplicativo Zepp e configurar sessões de treino intervalado diretamente no pulso.
Monitoramento de saúde vai além dos batimentos cardíacos
O Amazfit Bip 6 utiliza a tecnologia BioTracker, com sensor biométrico PPG, para acompanhar diferentes indicadores de saúde ao longo do dia.
Entre os recursos disponíveis estão monitoramento contínuo de frequência cardíaca, oxigenação do sangue (SpO₂), nível de estresse e análise da qualidade do sono.
O sistema acompanha diferentes estágios do sono, incluindo a fase REM, cochilos durante o dia, variabilidade da frequência cardíaca durante o sono e qualidade da respiração noturna.
Um recurso particularmente interessante é o Readiness, que apresenta uma avaliação de prontidão física, considerando indicadores relacionados à recuperação e ao estado geral do organismo. A proposta é ajudar o usuário a entender quando está mais preparado para treinar e quando pode ser interessante priorizar o descanso.
Também estão disponíveis exercícios de respiração, acompanhamento do ciclo menstrual, avaliação PAI e alertas para situações como frequência cardíaca anormalmente alta ou baixa, baixa oxigenação e níveis elevados de estresse.
Todas essas informações são organizadas pelo aplicativo Zepp, que apresenta históricos, indicadores e tendências para facilitar o acompanhamento da rotina.
É importante lembrar que os sensores são destinados ao acompanhamento de bem-estar e condicionamento físico, não substituindo exames ou equipamentos médicos.
Bateria para até 14 dias
A autonomia é outro argumento importante do Bip 6. Sua bateria de 340 mAh promete até 14 dias de utilização em condições típicas.
Em situações de uso mais intenso, a fabricante estima até seis dias, enquanto o modo de economia de energia pode ampliar a autonomia para até 26 dias.
Para quem utiliza bastante o GPS, a estimativa de funcionamento contínuo chega a 32 horas.
Como acontece com outros relógios inteligentes, o resultado real depende de fatores como brilho da tela, frequência das medições, notificações e quantidade de atividades registradas.
Conectividade, inteligência artificial e recursos para o cotidiano
Além das funções esportivas, o Bip 6 oferece uma série de recursos inteligentes.
O Zepp Flow permite utilizar comandos de voz e acessar funções de inteligência artificial em países e regiões compatíveis. O relógio também oferece notificações de chamadas, SMS e aplicativos, controle da música reproduzida no smartphone e localização do celular.
Entre os recursos adicionais estão alarmes, relógio mundial, cronômetro, temporizador Pomodoro, previsão do tempo, lembretes de sedentarismo, lista de tarefas, gravação de voz e atualizações matinais.
Outro detalhe interessante é a possibilidade de controlar a câmera do smartphone, recurso disponível para dispositivos iOS compatíveis. O modelo também oferece respostas rápidas a chamadas e mensagens, conforme a compatibilidade do aparelho e do sistema.
A conectividade utiliza Bluetooth 5.2 e o relógio é compatível com smartphones Android 7.0 ou superior e iPhones com iOS 14.0 ou superior.
O aplicativo Zepp é gratuito e permite sincronizar os dados com plataformas de terceiros, como Strava, adidas Running, TrainingPeaks, komoot, Relive, Google Fit e Apple Health.
Onde o Amazfit Bip 6 poderia melhorar?
Apesar do conjunto bastante interessante, o modelo possui algumas limitações que precisam ser consideradas.
A experiência de aplicativos não é tão abrangente quanto a de relógios com sistemas mais completos, como os modelos que utilizam Wear OS. Também é importante observar que recursos como respostas rápidas, assistente de voz e controle de câmera dependem da compatibilidade com o smartphone e da disponibilidade regional.
Outro detalhe é que o GPS, embora integrado e compatível com cinco sistemas de satélite, não utiliza tecnologia de dupla frequência. Isso pode representar uma limitação em trajetos mais complexos, como áreas urbanas com muitos prédios ou percursos cercados por árvores.
Amazfit Bip 6 vale a pena?
O Amazfit Bip 6 apresenta um conjunto bastante equilibrado para quem procura um smartwatch com foco em atividades físicas, acompanhamento de saúde e autonomia de bateria.
Sua tela AMOLED de excelente brilho, o GPS integrado, os mais de 140 modos esportivos, a compatibilidade com sensores externos e os recursos de treinamento inteligente são argumentos importantes, especialmente considerando sua proposta de posicionamento no mercado.
Nosso veredito: o Amazfit Bip 6 é uma opção bastante interessante para quem deseja sair de uma pulseira inteligente básica e avançar para um relógio com recursos esportivos mais completos, sem necessariamente investir em modelos premium.
Não é o smartwatch ideal para quem prioriza uma grande variedade de aplicativos ou uma experiência completa de smartwatch tradicional. Mas, para acompanhar treinos, monitorar indicadores de saúde, organizar a rotina e receber notificações durante o dia, entrega um pacote bastante competitivo.
No final, seu custo-benefício dependerá principalmente do preço encontrado nas lojas e das prioridades de cada consumidor.

articles.title: Los Samsung Galaxy S28 podrían recuperar una función de cámara que el iPhone 18 Pro volvió a poner de moda
articles.text:
Los Samsung Galaxy S27 todavía no se lanzaron, pero los rumores sobre sus sucesores no se están haciendo esperar. De acuerdo con un conocido filtrador, el fabricante coreano planea un importante cambio en la cámara de los Galaxy S28 Pro y Ultra. Esto implicaría la reintroducción de una tecnología con la que la compañía ya ha experimentado, pero que en el último tiempo se ha vuelto a poner de modo. Nos referimos a la apertura variable, por supuesto.
El leaker Yogesh Brar, quien suele publicar información confiable sobre móviles que todavía no se lanzaron, indicó que Samsung estaría analizando la posibilidad de dotar a los Galaxy S28 Pro y S28 Ultra de apertura variable. El susodicho no ha brindado más detalles respecto de este tema, aunque el dato no es descabellado si consideramos que Apple hizo bastante alarde de esta característica con su implementación en los iPhone 18 Pro y Pro Max.
Brar incluso menciona que los Galaxy S28 más premium no serían los únicos que adoptarían la apertura variable. Pese a no hacer menciones puntuales, es lógico pensar que es una referencia a los fabricantes chinos. Después de todo, es bastante normal que los móviles que llegan desde el gigante asiático copien las características de diseño y las funciones que más destacan de los iPhone de última generación.
Samsung reintroduciría la apertura variable en los Galaxy S28 Pro y Ultra
Si te preguntas por qué la apertura variable podría llegar con los Galaxy S28 Pro y Ultra, y no con los Galaxy S27 que se presentarán el próximo año, habría varias explicaciones. En agosto pasado, antes de que se anunciaran los iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max, SamMobile publicó que los buques insignia coreanos de 2027 no traerían esta característica. Esto se debería a que los componentes actuales ocuparían más espacio, serían más caros y no darían una mejora sustancial en la calidad de imagen.
Con un año más para desarrollar esta característica, Samsung podría lograr avances suficientes para reducir los costes y lograr que sea una actualización que merezca la pena y no un simple gimmick. Ya veremos si esto es realmente así, considerando que los Galaxy S28 llegarán recién en la primera parte de 2028. Claro que a la firma coreana ya se le hizo costumbre que sus dispositivos se filtren con bastante antelación, así que no habría que extrañarse si lo mismo sucede con estos. De ocurrir, seguro nos enteraremos de la adopción o no de la apertura variable con anticipación.
Samsung usó apertura variable en sus móviles en los Galaxy S9 y S10 que se lanzaron en 2018 y 2019, respectivamente. La compañía introdujo un sistema que permitía seleccionar entre dos aperturas fijas mediante un sistema mecánico. Y si bien fue una implementación bastante rudimentaria en comparación con la que ha llegado ahora con los iPhone 18 Pro, fue todo un avance para la época.

articles.title: California sues OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents
articles.text:
California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents broke out of their testing environment and hacked other companies, including Hugging Face. In a lawsuit on Monday, Attorney General Rob Bonta accuses OpenAI of violating consumer safety law by knowingly developing a “dangerous product without proper oversight,” as reported earlier by Reuters.
California sues OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents
OpenAI lost control of its AI agents more than 80 times during testing, California’s AG claims.
The lawsuit claims the cyberattack on Hugging Face “was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability.” It alleges that OpenAI recently told the attorney general’s office that it “lost control” of its AI agents more than 80 times during testing.
After revealing the rogue AI attack on Hugging Face in July, news of several other similar incidents emerged, including attacks on an Australian government website, a German wiki site, and the software package manager RubyGems. OpenAI’s agents also tried to “bruteforce” a United Nations website.
“OpenAI’s actions escalated real-world cybersecurity risks, threatening the safety, health, and well-being of society,” Bonta says in the press release. “The company knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it — this disregard for public safety violated California law.”
OpenAI released its new cybersecurity AI model earlier this month, saying that it’s less likely to go rogue and attack other platforms. It’s also giving safety evaluators at Apollo Research access to its AI systems as part of a pilot program that monitors models for misalignment.
“Since the Hugging Face incident, we’ve undertaken an extensive and transparent effort to understand and address misaligned model activity,” OpenAI spokesperson Drew Pusateri says in an emailed statement to The Verge. “This lawsuit appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that’s been identified by every major AI lab. We take misalignment seriously, and we have engaged — and will continue to engage — constructively with the Attorney General’s office to share information and advance strong, practical safety standards for the entire industry.”

articles.title: Galaxy S27 Pro et Ultra : cette image montre-t-elle leur vrai design ?
articles.text:
À quelques mois de leur commercialisation prévue pour le début de l’année 2027, les futurs smartphones haut de gamme de Samsung font l’objet de nouvelles indiscrétions. Après l’apparition de modèles factices en ligne, Ice Universe, un leaker bien connu, affirme détenir le véritable design des appareils et partage un croquis technique détaillant le bloc caméra des futurs téléphones premium de la marque coréenne.
Trois capteurs et pas un de plus
Partagé sur X, ce visuel contredit les récentes maquettes aperçues en ligne la semaine dernière qui affichaient quatre caméras. Ice Universe affirme que ce quatrième capteur n’existe pas. Il n’hésite pas à utiliser les termes « 100 % confirmé » concernant le design et la présence de seulement trois capteurs pour les Galaxy S27 Pro et S27 Ultra.
Comme nous l’avons évoqué la semaine dernière, le Galaxy S27 Pro embarquerait ainsi un capteur principal de 200 mégapixels (un Samsung ISOCELL HP6), épaulé par un ultra grand-angle de 50 mégapixels et un téléobjectif de 10 mégapixels offrant un zoom optique 3x. De son côté, le S27 Ultra conserverait une optique principale de 200 mégapixels et un ultra grand-angle de 50 mégapixels, tout en musclant sa partie zoom avec un capteur de 50 mégapixels doté d’un zoom optique 5x.
Des changements stratégiques pour Samsung
Oui, le Galaxy S26 Ultra a bien quatre capteurs photo, et c’est d’ailleurs une de ses forces, comme nous l’avons souligné dans notre test, alors pourquoi Samsung reculerait sur ce point pour son Galaxy S27 Ultra ? Il semble que la marque miserait gros sur cette nouvelle génération, en prévoyant de concentrer plus de 70 % de la production de ses S27 sur les modèles Pro et Ultra. Ajoutez à cela la hausse du coût des composants, et l’on peut supposer que Samsung devra faire des choix stratégiques pour préserver sa marge sans pour autant faire exploser les prix.
À lire : Le Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra s’inspirerait en partie de l’iPhone 18 Pro
Reste que ces informations proviennent d’une fuite et demandent donc d’être prises avec des pincettes en attendant une officialisation par Samsung. À quelques mois du lancement des Galaxy S27, les rumeurs et fuites en tout genre devraient s’intensifier, apportant un éclairage de plus en plus précis sur les futurs S27.

articles.title: Mais, au fait, pourquoi la saga Grand Theft Auto s’appelle-t-elle GTA ?
articles.text:
Grand Theft Auto VI sort ce jeudi 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S, treize ans après GTA V. Le nom de la série, lui, remonte au milieu des années 1990, dans un petit studio écossais.
Aujourd’hui, trois lettres suffisent à identifier cette franchise, qui compte parmi les plus populaires de l’histoire du jeu vidéo. Mais lorsque DMA Design, un studio écossais installé à Dundee (devenu depuis Rockstar North), commence à travailler sur ce qui deviendra Grand Theft Auto, en 1995, le projet porte un tout autre nom : Race ‘n’ Chase.
À l’époque, l’idée est très différente de ce que deviendra la saga. Les développeurs imaginent un jeu de course-poursuite dans lequel les joueuses et les joueurs incarnent des policiers dans une ville vivante, vue du dessus, avec pour objectif de respecter le code de la route pour arrêter les mauvais conducteurs.
Les quelques testeurs qui ont pu essayer ce prototype à l’époque jugent justement cet aspect profondément ennuyeux. Il faut dire que respecter les feux et la signalisation n’a rien de franchement excitant. Les développeurs décident alors de changer de point de vue : incarner les criminels leur semble bien plus amusant. Mais la conduite, encore largement héritée de cette première version où il fallait respecter les règles, reste épouvantable.
Un bug de programmation dans l’intelligence artificielle rend alors les voitures de police extrêmement agressives. Ces dernières se mettent à percuter les véhicules des joueurs et à les pourchasser avec violence. Un joyeux chaos qui enthousiasme les testeurs et convainc les créateurs de conserver ce comportement, ce qui donnera finalement naissance au premier Grand Theft Auto, sorti sur PC en novembre 1997.
Mais alors, pourquoi Grand Theft Auto ?
Pour comprendre le nom de la franchise, il faut revenir à son sens premier. Aux États-Unis, l’expression « Grand theft auto » désigne une infraction liée au vol d’un véhicule automobile. Dans le droit américain, le terme « grand theft » désigne un vol jugé plus grave qu’un simple larcin, selon la nature ou la valeur du bien dérobé. En Californie, par exemple, un vol devient en général « grand theft » au-delà de 950 dollars (environ 820 euros), mais le Code pénal y range aussi nommément le vol d’automobile.
« Grand theft auto » ne signifie donc pas exactement la même chose que carjacking, ou piraterie routière, en français. Ce dernier terme désigne le vol d’un véhicule directement à son conducteur, généralement par la force ou l’intimidation, et constitue une infraction violente. Le « grand theft auto », lui, désigne plus largement le vol d’un véhicule automobile.
Le titre choisi par DMA Design est donc assez littéral et décrit parfaitement ce que les joueuses et les joueurs passent une bonne partie de leur temps à faire : voler des voitures, les conduire, échapper à la police et recommencer avec d’autres véhicules.
C’est aussi un titre provocateur, qui annonce d’emblée la couleur et ne manque pas de faire réagir. La polémique a bien eu lieu, et elle a été en partie orchestrée. Le 20 mai 1997, six mois avant la sortie, Lord Campbell of Croy interroge le gouvernement britannique à la Chambre des lords sur ce jeu de vols de voitures et de délits de fuite que rien n’empêcherait les enfants d’acheter, d’après le compte rendu de la séance. Selon Mike Dailly, co-créateur du jeu, dans un article de Time Extension du 28 novembre 2022, c’est le publicitaire Max Clifford, chargé de la campagne de lancement, qui a entretenu ce tollé dans la presse. David Jones, l’autre créateur, assure de son côté que l’équipe n’a jamais rien conçu dans le seul but de choquer.
Toujours est-il que, près de 30 ans après ses débuts, cette liberté d’incarner un criminel, de voler des véhicules et de faire ce que l’on veut dans un monde ouvert reste au cœur de l’identité de GTA. La formule s’est considérablement complexifiée au fil des épisodes, mais le plaisir de base demeure : jouer du mauvais côté de la justice. Grand Theft Auto, c’est finalement bien plus qu’une histoire de piraterie routière : c’est une immense simulation de liberté criminelle.

articles.title: Ce forfait 5G de 200 Go coûte moins de 5 centimes le gigaoctet — Frandroid
articles.text:
Lebara est un opérateur virtuel qui utilise le réseau de SFR. Il a fait du petit prix sa spécialité. Parmi ses offres, le forfait 200 Go porte la mention « Le plus vendu » sur le site de l’opérateur. Pour 9,99 euros tous les 30 jours, il comprend 200 Go en 5G, les appels et SMS illimités vers la France (hors MMS), et 15 Go utilisables en 4G depuis l’Union européenne et les DOM. Le gigaoctet revient ainsi à environ 5 centimes.
Ce forfait est actuellement bien positionné sur notre comparateur de forfaits mobile.
Ce forfait Lebara en bref :
- 200 Go d’internet mobile en 5G
- Appels et SMS illimités vers la France
- Dont 15 Go depuis l’Union européenne et les DOM
- Le réseau de SFR
- Sans engagement
En ce moment, le forfait Lebara 200 Go est disponible à 9,99 euros tous les 30 jours, directement sur le site de Lebara.
200 Go
- Appels illimités
- 200 Go en France
- 15 Go en Europe
30 Go
- Appels illimités
- 30 Go en France
- 10 Go en Europe
350 Go
- Appels illimités
- 350 Go en France
- 20 Go en Europe
Assez de data pour ne plus surveiller son compteur
L’Arcep relève une consommation moyenne de 19,3 Go par mois et par carte SIM au deuxième trimestre 2026. Avec 200 Go, on dispose donc de plus de dix fois cette moyenne. Il y a de quoi regarder des séries dans les transports, passer des appels vidéo ou écouter de la musique en streaming toute la journée sans se poser de question. C’est aussi une option intéressante pour ceux qui n’ont pas toujours le Wi-Fi sous la main, en déplacement ou au travail.
Le forfait se renouvelle tous les 30 jours, et non chaque mois calendaire. Sur une année, cela fait donc 13 renouvellements au lieu de 12, soit un peu moins de 130 euros au total. Le tarif reste l’un des plus bas pour ce volume de data. La carte SIM et l’eSIM sont offertes, ce qui évite les frais d’activation que facturent beaucoup d’opérateurs.
Le réseau de SFR, en France comme en Europe
Lebara s’appuie sur le réseau de SFR, et la 5G est incluse, à condition d’avoir un smartphone compatible. Dans le dernier baromètre de couverture de nPerf, publié en septembre 2026, SFR arrive en tête pour la couverture 5G. Son indice de 72,78 % ne le place que 0,44 point devant Bouygues Telecom, puis viennent Free et Orange (1,27 point sépare le premier du dernier). Ce classement porte uniquement sur la couverture.
