articles.title: El nuevo Kindle baja de precio: así es la primera oferta que ha lanzado Amazon antes del Black Friday
articles.text:
Como solemos ver cada año, Amazon ha adelantado algunas de sus ofertas en Kindle antes del Black Friday. Hay bastantes modelos que han bajado de precio, pero esta vez nos centraremos en uno de los más recientes: el Kindle. Se lanzó hace escasas semanas, pero el efecto novedad no ha sido ningún impedimento para dejarlo más barato: ahora mismo Amazon lo tiene con publicidad por 124,99 euros (154,99 euros) y sin publicidad por 139,99 euros (antes 174,99 euros).
Kindle (2026) - Con publicidad
Si prefieres una alternativa, estos son los Kindle que ahora mismo están de oferta:
- Kindle Paperwhite con publicidad (2024) por 144,99 euros (antes 209,99 euros).
- Kindle Paperwhite sin publicidad (2024) por 154,99 euros (antes 224,99 euros).
- Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition (2024) por por 159,99 euros (antes 259,99 euros).
- Kindle Colorsoft (2024) por 164,99 euros (antes 299,99 euros).
- Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition (2024) por 199,99 euros (antes 329,99 euros).
- Kindle Scribe (2026) por 364,99 euros (antes 519,99 euros).
- Kindle Scribe Colorsoft (2026) por 489,99 euros (antes 699,99 euros).
Primera oferta en el Kindle
Si dejamos a un lado los Kindle Scribe y Kindle Scribe Colorsoft, que se lanzaron hace unos meses, el único modelo de la generación actual que Amazon ha bajado de precio es el Kindle. De momento, no hay ofertas en los Kindle Paperwhite (2026), Kindle Paperwhite Signature Edition (2026), Kindle Colorsoft (2026) y Kindle Colorsoft Signature Edition (2026). Una lástima, sobre todo por los modelos Signature Edition que son los únicos compatibles con la funda que incluye botonera, uno de los accesorios más atractivos del catálogo de Kindle.
El Kindle que sí ha bajado de precio es el modelo más básico. Lo podemos encontrar disponible en varios colores y configuraciones de almacenamiento. Es el modelo ideal para dar el salto a este tipo de dispositivos, sobre todo si queremos un modelo pequeño de 6 pulgadas para llevarlo de viaje, o económico si no solemos leer todos los días.
El lector tiene un formato unibody, por lo que no hay "salto" entre los marcos y la pantalla. Es ligeramente más delgado que la anterior generación y, según Amazon, más rápido. Incluye función de brillo ajustable (manual) y la batería ofrece una autonomía teórica de aproximadamente seis semanas.
La batería es reemplazable, por lo que se adapta a la regulación de la Unión Europea. Además, cabe añadir que si tenías un Kindle anterior, las fundas no son compatibles con esta generación actual. Lo que sí es compatible es el accesorio para pasar las páginas; no la funda de los Signature Edition que incluye botones, sino el mando Kindle Click.

articles.title: Lambda Boosts AI Factory Resiliency and Efficiency With NVIDIA Photonics
articles.text:
To train an AI model, thousands of GPUs have to work together, requiring a network that’s fast, efficient and resilient.
Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches. The cloud provider is using the switches to connect NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs, delivering lower power, higher resiliency and longer mean time between interruptions (MTBI) to an AI factory at scale.
“Networking has to keep pace with the demands of increasingly large AI clusters,” said Dave Ward, president of cloud services at Lambda. “Bringing co-packaged optics into a deployment of this scale is an important step toward building the infrastructure needed to support the next generation of AI.”
In the company’s tests using the switches, network latency — the time needed for moving data — dropped by about 4% at rack scale and by up to about 10% at pod scale. Across rack, scalable unit and pod configurations, the network maintains the same throughput as conventional pluggable optics.
Delivering Power Efficiency and Resiliency at Scale
Improving power efficiency and resiliency matters because the network sits at the center of AI factory productivity.
In a large training job, one interrupted link can stall thousands of GPUs. With agentic inference, one network disruption can introduce cascading latency effects on many agents. Every interruption costs time, and every watt spent on networking is a watt not available for compute.
NVIDIA Photonics addresses both power efficiency and resiliency. By replacing pluggable transceivers with co-packaged optical engines on the switch package, it delivers up to 5x better power efficiency and up to 15x higher reliability than conventional pluggable optics. It also uses 4x fewer lasers, which means fewer components that can fail.
Cooler Optics, Replaceable Light Sources Increase Resiliency
Lambda’s deployment uses NVIDIA Photonics switches, each with 144 ports running at 800Gb/s. Liquid cooling carries heat away from the switch chip and optical engines.
The company reports a median optics temperature of 36°C, compared with 51°C for conventional pluggable optics, and its tests find more stable signal integrity.
NVIDIA Photonics also brings the electrical-to-optical conversion closer to the switch chip. Each switch has 18 removable external light sources, which supply light to the optical engines. Optical engines sit alongside the chip on the same package and convert electrical signals into light that carries data over fiber between parts of the cluster.
Technicians can replace the light-source modules in the field, unlike traditional pluggable optics, which require replacing the entire module if a laser fails.
Co-packaging shortens the electrical path from inches to millimeters, which reduces signal loss. It also removes the need for retimer chips, cutting both power draw and the number of parts in the signal path.
Explore NVIDIA Photonics and read Lambda’s deployment announcement.

articles.title: Missão falha e Amazon Leo perde 40 satélites • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Missão falha e Amazon Leo perde 40 satélites
Falha interrompeu sequência de 20 anos sem lançamentos malsucedidos da ULA. Missão terminou cerca de dez minutos após a decolagem.
Um foguete Vulcan, da United Launch Alliance (ULA), falhou neste domingo (15/11) durante uma missão que levaria 40 satélites do Amazon Leo à orbita. O problema ocorreu cerca de dez minutos após a decolagem, em Cabo Canaveral, na Flórida, e resultou na perda de toda a carga.
Segundo a Reuters, esta é a primeira missão malsucedida nos 20 anos de história da ULA, joint venture formada por Boeing e Lockheed Martin. O voo também inauguraria um pacote de 38 lançamentos contratados pela Amazon para ampliar a constelação de internet via satélite.
Além da banda larga, a Amazon também tem ampliado sua constelação de satélites para dar suporte ao Direct-to-Device, que deve concorrer com o famoso plano da Starlink. A falha pesa sobre os planos da Amazon para dar sequência a esse crescimento, que colocou 398 satélites em órbita em 14 lançamentos desde 2025, pouco mais de 10% do objetivo da companhia.
Diferentemente da SpaceX, que utiliza seus próprios foguetes para lançar os satélites da Starlink, a Amazon depende de contratos com diferentes fornecedores para levar sua constelação ao espaço. A Starlink já reúne mais de 11 mil satélites em órbita e atende milhões de clientes ao redor do mundo.
Cerca de dez minutos após a decolagem do foguete na Estação da Força Espacial de Cabo Canaveral, a ULA confirmou que o veículo havia sofrido uma “anomalia” e não conseguiria colocar os satélites em órbita, diz um comunicado publicado pela empresa na rede social X.
De acordo com a Reuters, o problema parece ter ocorrido logo depois da separação entre o primeiro e o segundo estágio do Vulcan. Era no estágio superior que estavam os satélites da Amazon. A causa da falha ainda não foi identificada.
No post, a ULA afirmou que começou a analisar os dados coletados durante o voo. A Amazon também se manifestou após a perda da missão, dizendo que “há risco em qualquer lançamento” especialmente “para missões inaugurais como a LV-01”. A companhia, controlada por Andy Jassy, reafirmou o compromisso de longo prazo com ULA.
A perda da missão quebra uma sequência mantida desde a criação da United Launch Alliance, em 2006, criada com a união dos programas Delta, da Boeing, e Atlas, da Lockheed Martin. A missão com os satélites da Amazon, porém, foi apenas o quinto voo do foguete Vulcan, que estreou em 2024, e o primeiro em nove meses. Ele ficou esse período em solo sob investigações de problemas técnicos pela ULA.
Um deles envolvia os propulsores sólidos laterais, que apresentaram falhas nos dois voos anteriores do foguete. Em outra frente estão os motores BE-4, da Blue Origin, que também teve um foguete que explodiu em maio, poucos dias antes de uma missão que também levaria satélites do Amazon Leo.
Segundo uma fonte ouvida pela agência, a Blue Origin já participa da investigação da falha deste domingo. Até agora, porém, não há indicação de que os motores BE-4 tenham sido responsáveis pelo acidente.
A investigação sobre o Vulcan pode manter o foguete fora de operação por meses, segundo a Reuters, restringindo ainda mais a oferta no mercado após falhas recentes na SpaceX.

articles.title: BDC leads investment in Saskatoon company modernizing railway logistics | BetaKit
articles.text:
Saskatoon’s Standard Rail Corporation has raised $1.85 million to scale its railway logistics platform, the company announced last week.
The news: Standard Rail announced the seed investment on Nov. 12, telling BetaKit that the funding was led by BDC’s Capital Seed Venture Fund, with additional participation from Waterloo’s Infiniq Ventures. Funding will go toward expanding the company’s logistics platform, SIDINGS, as well as growing its engineering and marketing teams.
From the source: “I spent years driving industrial roads looking for track, knocking on doors for storage and transload, and icing it together one site at a time,” said Standard Rail CEO Robert Skarzynski in a press release. “With BDC’s backing, we’re building the system this industry has always needed.”
The context: SIDINGS is designed as a digital platform connecting domestic and international shippers with rail capacity across North America. The platform is intended to replicate the ease-of-access logistics that has become commonplace in both the air and ocean freight industries but has remained largely disconnected in the broader rail transportation industry. The platform is an open network service connecting shippers, facilities, and rail service providers in a single online location. Shippers can search for more than 60,000 rail-served locations in Canada, Mexico, and the United States. The platform also allows users to book, bid, and request pricing online.
Standard Rail said that with BDC’s financing, it will look to onboard more rail service providers to the platform.
Final thought: Prior to launching SIDINGS, Standard Rail was involved in physical railcar maintenance, repair, and fleet services, including logistics planning, which gave the company’s team a frontline view of the rail transportation industry. It was that domain knowledge that Mark Smith, partner and team lead at BDC’s Seed Venture Fund, said clinched the bank’s decision to back Standard Rail, which has several competitors that also service the rail logistics space, including Commtrex and Canadian rival Freightera. Smith called Standard Rail’s hands-on involvement in the industry a strategic advantage as it seeks to scale.
BetaKit’s Prairies reporting is funded in part by YEGAF, a not-for-profit dedicated to amplifying business stories in Alberta.

articles.title: El hacker que filtró GTA 6 se declara culpable y podría pasar más de 10 años en la cárcel
articles.text:
El hacker que filtró GTA 6 hace unos años se ha declarado culpable ante un tribunal de Reino Unido. Arion Kurtaj, un joven de 21 años responsable de la filtración masiva de Grand Theft Auto VI en 2022, confesó que vulneró la seguridad de Rockstar Games y otras empresas tecnológicas cuando formaba parte del grupo Lapsus$. La noticia llega a unos días del lanzamiento del juego y cierra uno de los capítulos más sonados del estudio de videojuegos.
De acuerdo con BBC, Kurtaj se declaró culpable de varios delitos ante el Tribunal de la Corona de Woolwich, en Reino Unido. El joven fue arrestado en 2022 por su participación en los hackeos a NVIDIA y Uber, pero no pudo enfrentar un juicio debido a la severidad de su autismo. Las autoridades lo recluyeron en un hospital psiquiátrico de forma indefinida, aunque una evaluación a finales de 2025 encontró que Kurtak ya es apto para comparecer ante la justicia por sus crímenes.
Antes de que las cosas escalaran, Arion Kurtaj se declaró culpable de todos los delitos durante una audiencia. Aunque el delito de chantaje contra Rockstar Games podría enviarlo 14 años a la cárcel, es probable que el juez determine una pena menor. Kurtaj tenía entre 16 y 17 años cuando cometió los ciberataques, además de que tiene un diagnóstico severo del trastorno del espectro autista. A esto se suma que otro miembro de Lapsus$ al que se le imputaron delitos similares solo cumplió una condena de 18 meses en rehabilitación.
El hackeo a Rockstar Games que filtró GTA 6
La filtración de Grand Theft Auto VI fue uno de los episodios más sonados de la historia reciente de los videojuegos. Antes de que ShinyHunters y Cyberleek acapararan los reflectores por publicar vídeos del juego y afirmar que contaban con una versión de desarrollo, Kurtaj ya se había colado a los servidores de Rockstar Games.
El joven hackeó al estudio mientras se encontraba alojado en un hotel bajo protección policial. Debido a que no contaba con un ordenador, Kurtaj usó un Fire Stick conectado al televisor de su habitación junto con teclado y ratón Bluetooth. Con ayuda de su móvil, el hacker utilizó sus capacidades de ingeniería social para robar los datos de acceso de un empleado y acceder a su espacio de trabajo de Slack. Esto le permitió descargar vídeos y otro material que se publicaba en los canales de desarrollo.
Durante el hackeo, Kurtaj accedió a más de 90 vídeos de pruebas internas y fragmentos del código fuente del juego. Una vez descargados, el joven envió un mensaje masivo a todos los empleados de Rockstar a través de Slack, exigiendo que lo contactaran antes de 24 horas si no querían que publicara el código de GTA 6. El estudio se negó a pagar y los vídeos se publicaron en un foro de internet, volviéndose virales en cuestión de minutos.
Rockstar Games afirmó que el hackeo les costó unos cinco millones de dólares y miles de horas de trabajo adicional a sus empleados. La compañía reforzó sus medidas de seguridad, que durante unos años funcionaron bien hasta que ocurrió el hackeo de 2026.
Grand Theft Auto VI se lanza el 19 de noviembre de 2026 en PS5 y Xbox Series X|S. Cuatro días después se dictará sentencia contra Arion Kurtaj por filtrar los primeros vídeos del juego.

articles.title: The Sound of Smarter Farming - EE Times
articles.text:
It was amid the stillness of the Covid-19 lockdowns that Conrad Young, founder and CEO of Chirrup.ai, realized that birdsong would make an excellent proxy for biodiversity. Birds have always acted as sentinels for changes in the environment, and as he told EE Times, “Birdsong is a pretty powerful and visceral way of understanding what’s going on in the environment but is also scientifically valid and benchmarkable.”
In March 2022, as the pandemic ended, Young launched Chirrup.ai to monitor birdsong and track farmland diversity. The first task was to deploy acoustic sensors and establish a baseline of bird activity that could provide a reference point against future recordings and reveal whether biodiversity was improving, declining, or remaining stable over time. Earlier trials used audiomoths—low-cost, acoustic loggers that record birdsong—but Chirrup.ai has now developed smart acoustic sensors.
The sensor pairs a MEMS analog microphone with a 24-bit digital audio codec, a 240-MHz processor with Bluetooth, and a high-speed 4G LTE modem. A multi-constellation GNSS receiver supporting GPS, GLONASS, and Galileo provides geolocation and timestamping for the acoustic data. The device is powered by a rechargeable lithium-polymer battery.
Chirrup.ai’s technology has already measured biodiversity on more than 300 farms in eight European countries. In the U.K., these include sites on the Greenwich Peninsula in London, broiler farms in Lincolnshire, and pig farms in Norfolk. To record birdsong in the field, multiple devices are placed at least 200 meters apart at the edges of woodland and open land populated by birds but away from roosting sites, footpaths, and roads. Birdsong is recorded for two to three weeks with devices then sent back to Chirrup.ai, where the recordings are converted to spectrograms and analyzed to identify the species and assess biodiversity.
As Young pointed out, farmers do not require instant answers when assessing biodiversity but instead want to understand how nature is changing year on year. “We need a large enough period of sampling, so we’ve got a good representative picture of what’s there, and then we’ll provide an annual snapshot,” he said.
Chirrup.ai technology director Paul Nebel agreed and added that remote analysis of data is preferable to using edge AI right now. “With edge processing, we would need a bigger battery and probably a solar cell, which would make the device way more expensive,” he said.
Sensor aside, identifying bird species from recordings is critical, and Chirrup.ai has developed machine-learning (ML) algorithms to detect subtle nuances in recordings, such as one species mimicking another, and remove background noise. The firm also uses ML platform BirdNET, which is trained on species worldwide.
“Birds are very individual: Some use the same songs day in and day out, but others do not and are very complicated,” Nebel said. “Many have songs to raise an alarm, for waking up, for saying hi to their mates, and for courting. Some birds pretend to be other birds; others even pretend to be mobile phones. We also see birds that have different accents from one country to another, even from county to county.”
These remarkable complexities make human oversight critical, and Chirrup.ai has been working with ornithologists and ecologists who have reviewed thousands of hours of recordings, comparing their judgements against ML predictions, and setting appropriate confidence thresholds. “We need to keep checking that the machine learning doesn’t drift off and remains reflective of what humans hear,” Nebel said.
Chirrup.ai has also developed algorithms that generate a biodiversity index based on its bird species data as well as local environment conditions, such as hedgerow health, land management practices, satellite data on habitats, and species position in the food chain. Work is underway to include other bioindicators, such as weather data, to contextualize changes from season to season, and the firm is also considering extending bioacoustic sensing beyond birdsong. “There are also so many nascent datasets that are becoming available as well as birdsong—we could look at insects, mammals, even the livestock,” Young said.
One firm already working with insects and, very recently, livestock is AgriSound (U.K.). Founded in 2020 by CEO Casey Woodward, the government-funded startup set out to monitor pollinating insects to help growers improve crop pollination and provide insights into biodiversity for farming and land management. Woodward and colleagues developed a solar-powered acoustic sensor, Polly, that monitors honeybee and bumblebee activity in glasshouses, polytunnels, and open fields by detecting wingbeat frequencies.
The sensor combines a MEMS microphone and acoustic sensor array to capture the insect wingbeat sounds, alongside temperature, humidity, and ambient-light sensors to monitor environmental conditions.
An onboard processor runs ML algorithms to analyze the discrete Hertz range of the wingbeat frequency and distinguish bee activity from background noise. The resulting pollinator data packets are transmitted to the cloud via 4G cellular connectivity for visualization and interpretation, typically on an hourly basis, and a Bluetooth module enables firmware updates.
So while Chirrup.ai, with its emphasis on biodiversity insights, currently prioritizes battery life and cost by analyzing recordings remotely, AgriSound processes signals locally to deliver swift results on insect activity. “We are trying to help farmers who want results quickly,” Woodward said. “For example, the almond flowering season may only be 10 days, so growers will want to take recommended interventions pretty quickly.”
Like Chirrup.ai, AgriSound has spent some time developing and training ML algorithms to recognize, in this case, different pollinators. Woodward and colleagues have built an extensive library comprising thousands of hours of insect sounds, recorded under a controlled environment. Here, individual bees have been encouraged to fly toward a flower and collect pollen and nectar while their acoustic signatures are recorded. “Bees are very smart and difficult to incentivize to do what you want,” Woodward laughed.
The sensor has been deployed by U.K. retailer Marks&Spencer to provide insights into pollinator densities and can be found in strawberry, sugar beet, and other farms across the nation. Woodward highlighted how his company’s work in glasshouses has helped to reduce the amount of misshapen fruit. AgriSound’s tech has also reached almond orchards in Spain and Portugal, blueberry crops in the U.S., and avocado farms in South Africa—and is now being extended to livestock. In recent U.K. projects, Woodward and colleagues have worked with veterinary-led sustainable livestock production group Raft Solutions and egg producer Noble Foods to monitor the welfare of laying hens.
“With Raft, we’ve been listening for changes in the gut contractions [of cattle] and how these affect methane emissions from the herds,” Woodward said. “This can take time, as you need a veterinarian to collect the sounds with a stethoscope … but with the hens, we just put our non-invasive sensors into the sheds to record data.”
Pest control
Beyond birds, bees, and bovine, the next acoustic sensing frontier is, arguably, the smaller insect pests that infest crops and devastate yields—think beetles, termites, stem borers, and more. U.K.-based BugBug—launched by Cornell entomologist Emily Bick, director of Indonesian PT Gunung Madu sugarcane plantation Jadey Huray, and University of Wisconsin–Madison researcher and ML engineer Laurence Still—is tackling this problem head on.
Laurence Still, BugBug’s CTO, highlighted how a few years ago, Gunung Madu switched from burning fields before harvesting to the more sustainable method of green cane harvesting—that is, harvesting sugarcane without first burning the crop. “[The plantation] went from 5% crop loss to 50% crop loss due to insects over the course of a year,” Still said. “Burning resets the insect population back to zero, but without this, insect numbers were compounded and compounded.”
To tackle the problem, the colleagues decided to use piezoelectric contact microphones to detect insect vibration frequencies, connecting these to Raspberry Pi processors and clipping them onto plant stems to detect the vibrations caused by the chewing and tapping of feeding insects.
“We record the sound of the damage being done to the plant by the insect,” Still said. “A lot of biological acoustic sensing detects sounds transferred through air, but we’re listening to [vibrations] being transmitted through the plant. These travel very well through hard materials, so we can pick up very, very small signals.”
Trials on tobacco-plant-feeding hornworms, Colorado potato beetles, and European corn borers revealed distinct differences in the feeding patterns, frequency, and amplitude—and low background noise. Following initial success, the BugBug team, led by systems integration engineer Callum Hockey, has since redesigned its device, sticking with the piezo-sensors but switching the Raspberry Pi processor for a custom sound card and embedded electronics. This latest design decreases the form factor, cuts power consumption, and enables field operation with a smaller solar panel.
Recorded data is converted into spectrograms and analyzed using custom ML algorithms. Unlike birdsong and bees, the sounds of insects feeding internally cannot readily be identified and labeled, so BugBug’s ML approach relies heavily on unsupervised learning. Like their peers at Chirrup.ai and AgriSound, Still and colleagues have collected thousands of hours of recordings. These are combined with contextual information, such as insect location on the plant, and plant location, to label populations of sounds rather than individual events. By comparing these datasets, the ML algorithms learn to distinguish insect activity from background noise and identify patterns associated with particular pests. Some processing takes place locally while the Wi-Fi-enabled sensor also transmits data to the cloud for further analysis. However, BugBug is also exploring lightweight ML models that could run on the device in the future.
Still and colleagues have characterized the sounds of more than 25 insect species, amassing data on sugarcane, sweetcorn, oilseed rape, grapevine, coconuts, potatoes, and tomatoes. The sensors can also detect the distinctive feeding sounds of piercing-sucking insects, including aphids and scale insects—the scourge of sugarcane. It’s early days, but the company is investigating if acoustic monitoring can detect the first flight of these insects, just after they emerge from larvae, to give growers an early warning of pest activity.
“Our idea is to put the sensors in the field at the start of the season and build up a picture of insect activity over time,” Still said. “So you see no insects, no insects, no insects, and then you start to see your signal rising—and that’s the time to act. Identifying the optimal time to treat a crop is our goal—timing is absolutely critical.”
Practical proliferation
BugBug is undoubtedly breaking new acoustic sensing ground by using AI to uncover data that was previously inaccessible to humans. “We’re doing something [with AI] that wouldn’t have been possible five years ago, before some of the newer advances in unsupervised learning,” Still said. The company is currently working with leading agrochemical companies to solve practical problems. “You might have a company that has developed a biopesticide but needs to know if it is stopping insects feeding, killing them, and how quickly,” he said. “That’s hard if you can’t see the insect as it’s inside the plant … but with our sensors, you could monitor feeding activity before pesticide and post-pesticide.”
BugBug, AgriSound, and Chirrup.ai are not alone in their development of acoustic sensors and AI to eavesdrop on the environment. In Sri Lanka, Permia Sensing is combining satellite, drone, and bioacoustic data with AI to monitor red palm weevil activity in palm trees. Meanwhile, Biofonic (U.K.) uses below-earth acoustic sensors and ML to gather soil data for sustainable crop management.
Altogether, these companies point to a growing shift toward bioacoustic sensing and AI-driven analysis to check in on nature. Indeed, Young highlighted how the “amalgamation” and AI analysis of so much sound data with myriad databases, combined with years of work with growers, is truly helping agri-industry balance commercial production with ecology.
Woodward concurred. “The beauty of acoustic sensors is that they make the invisible visible,” he said. “To some extent, pest damage can be monitored by looking at bites on a leaf, but you can’t necessarily quantify the number of beneficial insects in a field or poor pollination. I see acoustic sensing as a statistically rich and powerful means of data collection, which in many cases is super-affordable.”

articles.title: Ce robot financé par le Pentagone a assemblé une structure dans l'espace sans aide humaine
articles.text:
Pour installer ou réparer quoi que ce soit à l’extérieur de la Station spatiale internationale (ISS), il n’existe encore qu’une solution : envoyer des astronautes dehors, en scaphandre, pour des sorties extravéhiculaires (EVA) qui durent près de 6 heures chacune.
Mais, le 5 novembre 2026, l’université américaine Caltech a annoncé qu’un de ses robots avait assemblé une structure en orbite, sans le moindre astronaute. « C’est la première fois qu’une structure est construite de manière autonome dans l’espace », affirme Sergio Pellegrino, professeur d’ingénierie aérospatiale à Caltech et chef du projet, cité dans le communiqué. Le robot n’a bâti qu’un petit morceau d’antenne, mais il ouvre une piste pour fabriquer en orbite des objets bien trop grands pour tenir dans une fusée.
Ce robot s’appelle ASTRA. Il est financé par la DARPA, l’agence de recherche du Pentagone, dans le cadre de son programme NOM4D, lancé en 2022 pour apprendre à fabriquer de grandes structures directement en orbite. ASTRA a décollé le 30 mars 2026 de la base de Vandenberg, en Californie, avec la mission Transporter-16 de SpaceX. Ce boîtier d’environ un mètre cube voyageait avec 9 autres charges utiles à bord du Vigoride 7, un remorqueur spatial de l’entreprise Momentus qui lui fournit aussi l’énergie et les communications. Selon Andrew Detor, responsable du programme à la DARPA, il ne s’est écoulé que 15 mois entre l’idée d’une démonstration en orbite et le lancement.
Un jeu de construction piloté depuis la Terre
Mais comment un robot peut-il construire quelque chose seul dans le vide ? La DARPA compare le principe aux jeux de construction de type K’Nex. Un portique robotisé, qui se déplace sur trois axes, attrape des tubes en fibre composite et des jonctions en aluminium rangés dans des distributeurs motorisés, puis les assemble en segments identiques appelés baies. Il y accroche ensuite un film réfléchissant perforé, avant de pousser la baie terminée hors du boîtier pour attaquer la suivante. Il en faut 11 pour boucler l’armature d’une antenne de 1,4 mètre de diamètre, un procédé que l’on peut voir dans une vidéo publiée par Caltech, filmée sur la version terrestre d’ASTRA.
En orbite, les choses se sont révélées nettement plus compliquées. ASTRA est parti avec deux baies déjà montées et n’a réussi à construire que la troisième, faute de temps. Car les ordres de construction partent du sol, et l’équipe ne peut parler au robot que 7 ou 8 fois par jour, pendant une quinzaine de minutes. À chaque imprévu, les ingénieurs reproduisent le problème sur un jumeau d’ASTRA resté au laboratoire, testent une parade, puis envoient la solution en orbite.
Pourquoi se passer des astronautes ?
Actuellement, on ne dispose que de deux façons d’envoyer une grande structure dans l’espace. Soit on la plie pour qu’elle entre sous la coiffe de la fusée, comme le miroir de 6,5 mètres du télescope James Webb. Soit on l’assemble à la main à partir de morceaux envoyés en plusieurs lancements, comme l’ISS, ce qui demande des sorties répétées.
Pour les astronautes, ces sorties dans l’espaces sont un véritable accomplissement. On l’a vu récemment avec l’astronaute canadien Joshua Kutryk, qui a publié une photo de sa sortie dans l’espace, à 400 kilomètres au-dessus de la Terre. Une photo poétique et prodigieuse, mais qui rappelle à quel point ces sorties restent très risquées : en 2013, l’Italien Luca Parmitano a failli se noyer quand son casque s’est rempli d’eau.
Une mission qui s’achève avant la dernière baie
La mission d’ASTRA s’arrête en décembre, et Caltech ne compte plus terminer les 11 baies. L’équipe estime pourtant avoir montré que la méthode fonctionne, même s’il faut simplifier le système. Le programme NOM4D prévoit encore une expérience avant de s’arrêter : l’université de l’Illinois doit envoyer vers l’ISS, d’ici la fin de l’année, un procédé qui durcit des tubes en composite directement en orbite.

articles.title: Accelerate Molecular Dynamics Simulations with Accurate, Flexible Primitives Using NVIDIA cuPotential | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
Molecular dynamics (MD) is an indispensable tool across physics, chemistry, biology, and materials science. Owing to its arithmetic structure, particularly the parallel evaluation of many atom-pair interactions, MD codes were among the first to be ported to run on GPUs. However, as GPUs evolve, optimizing kernels and ensuring compatibility across heterogeneous hardware have become more difficult than ever for many MD engine developers.
Specifically, in simulations run with classical forcefields, the evaluation of long-range interactions under periodic boundary conditions, such as electrostatics and dispersion, remains the major computational and engineering bottleneck.
NVIDIA cuPotential, a focused library designed for molecular dynamics, addresses these challenges. By offering modular primitives with a C API, cuPotential empowers developers and users to select specific components from multiple layers of the stack to accelerate workloads (Figure 1).
cuPotential provides direct space and reciprocal space utilities such as cutoff-based interaction evaluators and charge spreading functions. This release also provides a plugin specifically for OpenMM given its popularity in the developer ecosystem as an example. The goal is seamless drop-in replacements with minimal changes to the user’s code.
This post explains how to integrate the plugin into OpenMM, evaluate accuracy against high-accuracy references, and measure simulation throughput. It also introduces two examples for developers who need control over parameter representation and updates. Finally, it briefly discusses the science and error analysis behind the new splitting and spreading methods. This rigorous attention to accuracy and energy drift in simulation allows developers to integrate and benefit from the acceleration provided by cuPotential kernels without affecting simulation results.
Building the cuPotential runtime and plugin for OpenMM
cuPotential is composed of two parts: a core methods library and a plugin for OpenMM that consumes the primitives that can be built directly in a conda environment on Linux. The following tutorial walks through building the runtime and plugin, installing the Python wheel, and running the supplied molecular dynamics sample.
Prerequisites
- Linux x86-64 with a supported NVIDIA GPU
- An installed NVIDIA driver compatible with CUDA 13.1
- Conda or Micromamba installed and initialized for your shell
- A clone of the cuPotential repository from the NVIDIA/cuPotential GitHub repo
The environment supplies the CUDA toolkit and compilers; a separate system-wide CUDA toolkit installation is not required. The GPU driver must already be installed on the host.
Step 1: Create and activate the environment
Using Conda, create and activate the environment:
conda create -y -n cupotential-build -c conda-forge \
  python=3.12 openmm=8.4.0 \
  cuda-version=13.1 cuda-toolkit=13.1 \
  cmake make gcc_linux-64=13 gxx_linux-64=13 \
  swig pip setuptools wheel numpy
conda activate cupotential-build
Alternatively, you can use Micromamba:
micromamba create -y -n cupotential-build -c conda-forge \
  python=3.12 openmm=8.4.0 \
  cuda-version=13.1 cuda-toolkit=13.1 \
  cmake make gcc_linux-64=13 gxx_linux-64=13 \
  swig pip setuptools wheel numpy
micromamba activate cupotential-build
Next, install the Python build dependencies:
python -m pip install "pybind11>=2.12" nvidia-mathdx
The cuda-toolkit package supplies the CUDA compiler and development tools. Setting cuda-version alone does not install those tools.
Step 2: Point the build helper to the active environment
In plugins/openmm/run_build, replace:
OPENMM=/opt/openmm
with:
OPENMM="${CONDA_PREFIX:?Activate the conda environment first}"
Both Conda and Micromamba set CONDA_PREFIX when an environment is activated.
Step 3: Build and install
Use the cuPotential repository root, with the environment active:
export CUDACXX="$CONDA_PREFIX/bin/nvcc"
export CUDAHOSTCXX="$CXX"
./plugins/openmm/run_build
python -m pip wheel \
  --no-deps --no-build-isolation \
  --wheel-dir plugins/openmm/dist \
  ./plugins/openmm
python -m pip install plugins/openmm/dist/*.whl
The build helper compiles the cuPotential runtime if it’s not already present, then builds the OpenMM plugin. The final installation command also installs the wheel’s declared pip CUDA dependencies.
Step 4: Verify the installation
Run the supplied sample directly:
cd plugins/openmm/samples
./solvated_systems/run
The sample evaluates DHFR (Dihydrofolate reductase), BACE (Beta-secretase 1), and ApoA1 (Apolipoprotein A1), under both NVT and NPT conditions. The DHFR and ApoA1 systems are from the OpenMM benchmark suite, while BACE is from the OpenFE benchmark set. A successful run ends with:
PASS
The samples use AMBER14/TIP3P force field, a 0.9 nm nonbonded interaction cutoff length, a 5 x 10⁻⁴ electrostatic accuracy target, and mixed precision. Its 4 fs timestep is paired with constrained hydrogen bonds, rigid water, and hydrogen mass repartitioning to 1.5 amu.
These runs measure accuracy and performance separately. For electrostatics, it compares both implementations with a double-precision reference, using twice the cutoff length for the short range part and twice the mesh resolution in each dimension for the long range part, with the Ewald splitting parameter held fixed. For truncated Lennard-Jones interactions, it uses a double-precision reference at the same cutoff, preserving the interaction model being tested.
For throughput, each implementation runs 500 warm-up steps followed by 3,000 timed steps. The cuPotential arm uses its own force and integrator, plus its barostat for NPT. The reported speedup therefore describes that integrated configuration.
Using cuPotential with OpenMM
The cuPotential OpenMM plugin provides replacements for the OpenMM nonbonded force, Langevin integrator, and Monte Carlo barostat. In your production MD simulations, the key steps to integrate cuPotential into OpenMM are:
- Replace the system’s OpenMM nonbonded force before creating the simulation context
- Use integrator and optionally barostat from cuPotential
import openmm as mm
import openmm.unit as unit
import nv_openmm_plugin as nv
temperature = 300 * unit.kelvin      # Temperature, 300 K
timestep = 0.004 * unit.picoseconds  # Timestep, 4 fs
friction_coeff = 1.0 / unit.picoseconds   # Friction coefficient in Langevin thermostat
pressure = 1.0 * unit.bar            # Pressure if using barostat for NPT
# Prepare the system using OpenMM. Replace with your system.
pdb = app.PDBFile("solvated.pdb")
forcefield = app.ForceField("amber14-all.xml", "amber14/tip3p.xml")
system = forcefield.createSystem(
    pdb.topology,
    nonbondedMethod=app.PME,
    nonbondedCutoff=0.9 * unit.nanometers,
    ewaldErrorTolerance=5e-4,
    constraints=app.HBonds,
    rigidWater=True,
    hydrogenMass=1.5 * unit.amu,
)
# replace OpenMM NonbondedForce instance with the plugin's NonbondedForce
for index, force in enumerate(system.getForces()):
    if isinstance(force, mm.NonbondedForce):
        system.addForce(nv.NonbondedForce(force))
        system.removeForce(index)
        break
# The cuPotential integrator handles center-of-mass motion removal.
for index, force in enumerate(system.getForces()):
    if isinstance(force, mm.CMMotionRemover):
        system.removeForce(index)
        break
integrator = nv.LangevinMiddleIntegrator(
    temperature,
    friction_coeff,
    timestep,
)
# Optionally, add cuPotential barostat for NPT simulations
system.addForce(nv.MonteCarloBarostat(
    pressure,           # Pressure
    temperature,        # Match the integrator temperature.
    frequency=25,       # Attempt a volume change every 25 steps.
))
# Create the simulation after configuring all forces.
simulation = app.Simulation(
    pdb.topology,
    system,
    integrator,
    mm.Platform.getPlatformByName("CUDA"),
    {"Precision": "mixed"},
)
simulation.context.setPositions(pdb.positions)
simulation.minimizeEnergy() # OpenMM 8.4 only
simulation.context.setVelocitiesToTemperature(temperature)
simulation.step(1000)
This excerpt shows that the integration changes. The complete sample includes system construction, CUDA context creation, accuracy checks, and timing. For NPT simulations, it also uses nv.MonteCarloBarostat.
The current plugin targets solvated, approximately uniform-density systems in rectangular periodic boxes, which is typical in biomolecular simulations. It accepts PME source forces; LJPME, triclinic boxes, and OpenMM particle or exception parameter offsets are not supported. Consult the plugin README before adapting an existing simulation.
Benchmarking cuPotential in OpenMM
When cuPotential is integrated into OpenMM using the built-in plugin, performance is significantly enhanced across a wide range of GPU architectures for system sizes in the range of 24,000 to 400,000 atoms, namely DHFR, TYK2 (Tyrosine Kinase 2 from OpenFE benchmarks), BACE, ApoA1, Water with 100,000 atoms, and cellulose.
Figure 2 shows a collection of speedup measures under the NPT condition for a range of GPUs. Newer generation GPUs, including NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition and NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition, achieve over 3x end-to-end speedups in selected benchmarks. Other tested GPUs (NVIDIA B200, H100, A100, L40S, A10, L4 and T4) also benefit, with gains often around 2x or more. Note that the performance numbers are measured with standard, non-alchemical systems.
Improving accuracy and efficiency through new splitting and spreading methods
Ewald splitting, specifically the Particle Mesh Ewald (PME) variant, has been the de facto method for the past 30 years in the simulation field. Recently, new techniques such as the u-series, midtown splines and prolates have been proposed but not widely adopted by the simulation community given their high technical requirement and sophistication. The NVIDIA team has been collaborating with D. E. Shaw Research and the Flatiron Institute to develop a new set of C2 continuous splitting and spreading functions that are broadly applicable, highly accurate, and performant.
Figure 3 shows detailed error benchmark analyses across various grid resolutions and cutoff distances, highlighting the accuracy profile of the cuPotential approach relative to Ewald and u-series. These analyses are done with the 100K-atom water system under NPT conditions, with statistics computed over 25 frames. Ewald alpha-parameters were tuned to asymptotically reach the desired force tolerance.
Our team’s approach enables reducing the real-space cutoff and/or the reciprocal space grid-size, with no loss in accuracy (compared to the near-exact regime), defined as the L2 Force RMSE at default settings specified by OpenMM. We note up-front that the u-series was not optimized for the force error, but rather the ensemble error, and we simply chose the parameters to attain the desired force error in order to be consistent with OpenMM.
Beyond electrostatics, splitting and spreading kernels for lattice dispersion interactions through cuPotential enables highly nonpolar and membrane systems to be modelled more accurately. Conventional homogeneous analytical corrections can lead to severe simulation artifacts.
cuPotential is able to significantly improve the accuracy in the dispersion energy by several thousand fold compared to conventional methods, while maintaining comparable force errors at significantly reduced computational cost (Figure 4). The u-series is omitted because the original paper from DESRES only covered electrostatics. In practice, reducing cutoff to 6A still poses enormous challenges due to complexities introduced by NBFix as well as combining rules.
Accuracy and energy drift analysis
For long-time scale simulations, measuring energy drift is an important validation step to ensure that leakage is minimized. Although there are many potential sources of error, in addition to splitting, it’s important that the library is not the dominant cause of the drift. Compared to standard OpenMM with a smooth switching function for truncated Lennard-Jones interactions, it’s possible to measure the effect of cutoff truncation attributed to the residual in direct space under kernel splitting.
cuPotential significantly reduces drift by several hundred fold compared to default settings in PME, and far exceeds the typical requirements of the biomolecular simulation community. Figure 5 shows energy drift over the course of 10 ns for a 10,000-molecule rigid water system, with a 9 Å cutoff for cuPotential and standard OpenMM, while a 20 Å cutoff is used for converged PME. We used 2 fs timesteps and 300 K simulation temperature. For drift estimation, energy drift ΔE = E(t) – E(20ps) normalized over 60,000 degrees of freedom.
Get started accelerating MD simulations with cuPotential
NVIDIA cuPotential accelerates molecular dynamics simulations while offering modular flexibility and high numerical accuracy. To get started and learn more, visit the NVIDIA/cuPotential GitHub repo, where you’ll find additional examples, benchmarks, and code to integrate these accelerated primitives in your own MD simulations.
Acknowledgments
We thank our collaborators at D. E. Shaw Research and the Flatiron Institute’s Center for Computational Mathematics for their scientific and mathematical contributions, discussions, and guidance on the error analysis behind the new splitting and spreading methods.

articles.title: NVIDIA subit des pressions pour réintégrer Jensen Huang
articles.text:
Trois jours après avoir quitté NVIDIA, Jensen Huang évoque avec ses proches un retour à la tête du géant des puces, selon le Financial Times. Et ses alliés de la Silicon Valley montent une « cellule de crise » pour convaincre le conseil d’administration de le reprendre.
Encore un rebondissement qu'on n'avait pas vu venir. Jensen Huang a démissionné de la direction de Nvidia, l’entreprise de 4 000 milliards de dollars qu’il avait cofondée en 1993. Son conseil d’administration avait ouvert une enquête après la révélation de sa liaison avec Alice Huang, ancienne dirigeante de Megaspeed, société singapourienne cliente de NVIDIA, que le renseignement américain soupçonne d’espionner pour Pékin. Les administrateurs l’ont poussé vers la sortie après la découverte d’une seconde liaison, avec une subordonnée. D’après le Financial Times, l’ancien patron soutient la campagne lancée pour son retour. Mais contrairement à d’autres fondateurs de la Silicon Valley, Jensen Huang n’a jamais détenu le contrôle du capital de NVIDIA, et il ne pourra revenir que si son conseil d’administration accepte de le réintégrer.
Des milliers de salariés de NVIDIA réclament le retour de Jensen Huang
Sur « Stand with Jensen », un site de soutien à l’ancien P.-D.G, une pétition adressée au conseil de NVIDIA a recueilli 156 850 signatures. Plus de 7 500 salariés de l’entreprise l’ont signée, et plusieurs d’entre eux réclament publiquement son retour depuis sa démission. Elon Musk, prêt à embaucher Jensen Huang quand le conseil délibérait encore sur son sort, et Tim Sweeney, patron d’Epic Games, ont ajouté leur nom à la liste.
Deux gros actionnaires de NVIDIA mènent aussi la charge. Brad Gerstner, fondateur du fonds Altimeter Capital, et Gavin Baker, patron d’Atreides Management, ont écrit au conseil pour lui demander de laisser « toutes les options sur la table, y compris le retour potentiel de Jensen Huang ». Les deux investisseurs invoquent « le succès extraordinaire » de son long mandat, et l’incertitude provoquée par son départ.
Dans les coulisses, des dirigeants de la Silicon Valley se réunissent pour faire pression sur le conseil, comptent demander l’appui de la Maison Blanche. Comme l’explique un proche, « tous les acteurs importants du secteur technologique, en dehors des laboratoires d’IA de pointe, adorent Jensen ».
Le conseil de NVIDIA a approché le patron d’Arm
À Washington, le secrétaire au Trésor, Scott Bessent, a réclamé un « remaniement radical » de la direction de NVIDIA après le départ de Jensen Huang. Et Colette Kress, directrice financière devenue PDG par intérim, cherche avant tout à stabiliser l’entreprise avant la publication de ses résultats trimestriels, le 17 novembre.
Selon le Financial Times, le conseil d’administration a approché Rene Haas, le patron d’Arm, en vue de la succession de Jensen Huang, mais les administrateurs assurent qu’aucune procédure formelle n’a été engagée.
L’enquête indépendante sur ses agissements se poursuit. Depuis la révélation de sa liaison avec Alice Huang, les contrôles de NVIDIA avant la vente de ses puces d’IA à des clients asiatiques liés à la Chine sont examinés de plus près. Et les alliés de Jensen Huang peinent à redorer son image. « Avoir une liaison avec une subordonnée est un motif de licenciement », reconnaît l’une des personnes engagées dans la campagne pour son retour.

articles.title: Microsoft: Windows Server 2016 reaches end of support in 60 days
articles.text:
Microsoft has reminded customers again that Windows Server 2016 will stop receiving security updates after it reaches the end of support in two months.
This follows another warning issued in October, announcing the end of extended support for Windows Server 2016 and encouraging users to upgrade to Windows Server 2025.
Windows Server 2016 reached general availability on October 12, 2016, one month after its official release at Microsoft's annual Ignite conference in September of that year.
It also reached the end of mainstream support nearly 4 years ago, in January 2022, and extended support will end in roughly two months, on January 13, 2027.
On the same date, the company will also stop support for all Windows Server 2016 Essentials features, including Remote Web Access and related Essentials-specific functionality.
"On January 13, 2027, all editions of Windows Server 2016 will reach the end of extended support. The January 2027 Windows security update will be the last update provided during extended support," Microsoft said in a message center update.
"After that date, monthly security updates will continue only for Windows Server 2016 devices enrolled in Extended Security Updates (ESU)."
Windows Server 2025 upgrade
Before Windows Server 2016 stops receiving security updates, Microsoft advised IT administrators to switch to Windows Server 2025, which started rolling out to Windows Insiders in January 2024 and reached general availability in November 2024.
Admins who want to test Windows Server 2025 before deploying it across their organization can get a free 180-day trial via the Microsoft Evaluation Center.
Windows Server 2025 is the latest Long-Term Servicing Channel (LTSC) release for Windows Server, and it will reach the end of mainstream support in November 2029, with an additional five years of extended support until November 14, 2034.
More information about Windows servicing dates is available on the Windows Lifecycle FAQ page or via the Lifecycle Policy search tool.
Last month, Microsoft announced that devices running Windows 11 24H2 Home and Pro editions stopped receiving security and non-security preview updates and advised customers to upgrade to Windows 11 26H2 by installing the Windows 11 2026 Update.
On Friday, it also reminded customers that they can enroll in the Extended Security Updates (ESU) program after Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2021 (a stripped-down Windows 10 edition for mission-critical devices) reaches the end of mainstream support in January, until they can upgrade to Windows 11 Enterprise LTSC 2024.

articles.title: Megaspeed, la empresa ligada al caso Nvidia, dijo que Alice Huang renunció en 2025 y abrió una investigación
articles.text:
Megaspeed International, una empresa de computación en la nube con sede en Singapur, afirmó el 15 de noviembre que la empresaria Alice Huang dejó la compañía el 30 de agosto de 2025 y que contrató abogados externos para una investigación interna sobre su negocio y su cadena de suministro.
La empresa está bajo la lupa por la sospecha de que desvió a China chips avanzados de Nvidia, algo que las normas de exportación de Estados Unidos limitan. La compañía respondió así a las consultas de CNBC y de la agencia AFP.
“La señora Alice Huang dejó oficialmente Megaspeed el 30 de agosto de 2025 y actualmente no tiene ningún cargo en la compañía”, dijo la firma en un comunicado. Agregó que no comenta “asuntos personales y privados” de Huang.
Una defensa sin respuestas a las acusaciones
Megaspeed sostuvo que realiza “un negocio legítimo y legal” y que conoce informes de prensa con afirmaciones sobre su negocio y su cadena de suministro “que no están respaldadas por pruebas verificables”. No respondió a ninguna acusación concreta, según la agencia AP.
La empresa aseguró que sus sistemas de control cumplen las leyes aplicables, incluidas las normas de exportación de Estados Unidos y las reglas de cada país donde opera. También dijo que revisará lo publicado y que informará a sus interesados “según corresponda”.
Megaspeed se presenta como un “socio comercial clave” de la nube de Nvidia en la región: sus clientes alquilan capacidad de cálculo de procesadores gráficos de la fabricante. Tiene oficinas en Singapur e Indonesia, según CNBC.
Singapur investiga a la empresa desde febrero de 2025
El Ministerio del Interior de Singapur informó el 12 de noviembre que la policía y la aduana investigan desde febrero de 2025 a varias empresas, entre ellas Megaspeed, y a sus directivos clave. La sospecha es de declaraciones falsas en la compra de servidores y otros delitos, según Lianhe Zaobao.
Según las autoridades, servidores con chips avanzados se exportaron a Malasia y se sospecha que terminaron en otros destinos, contrario a lo declarado en Singapur. La policía dijo que las investigaciones continúan.
El ministerio identificó a Alice Huang, residente de Hong Kong, como directora ejecutiva y presidenta de Megaspeed, y una de sus controladoras, cuando fue investigada en 2025. La policía comprobó que dio información falsa para minimizar su papel, recibió una advertencia severa el 26 de febrero de 2026 y tiene prohibido volver a entrar al país. Según AFP, no fue investigada por espionaje.
Según informes citados por Zaobao, Megaspeed importó al menos USD 4.600 millones en equipos de Nvidia a través de filiales en Malasia e Indonesia entre 2023 y noviembre de 2025. El secretario del Tesoro de Estados Unidos, Scott Bessent, dijo antes que las autoridades apoyaban desde hacía meses incluir a la empresa en una lista comercial de restricciones.
Jensen Huang renunció el 12 de noviembre como director ejecutivo de Nvidia tras admitir una infidelidad en una carta a los empleados del 8 de noviembre. Según The New York Times, funcionarios de inteligencia de Estados Unidos creen que Alice Huang es un activo de inteligencia de China; Beijing negó las acusaciones de espionaje. Las dos personas no son parientes.
El directorio de Nvidia dijo que investigará el caso. Tres presidentes de comisiones del Congreso de Estados Unidos pidieron a Jensen Huang que asista a una reunión a puertas cerradas el 18 de noviembre, según AFP.

articles.title: Oister Global launches Rs 600 Cr deeptech fund
articles.text:
Oister Global launches Rs 600 Cr deeptech fund
Oister Global aims to invest in about 8-10 deeptech startups with a proven business model & technology and its capital will assist in rapid scaling.
Oister Global, an India-focused multi-strategy private markets asset manager, has announced the launch of a Rs 600 crore deeptech fund to back revenue generating Indian startups.
The Oister Deep Tech Fund aims to raise Rs 400 crore with a Rs 200 crore greenshoe, taking the potential corpus to Rs 600 crore.
A statement from Oister Global said this deeptech fund will build a concentrated portfolio of 8 to 10 mature companies in the frontier tech ecosystem. The fund will focus in sectors such as space technology, defence and aerospace, semiconductors and electronics, quantum technologies, advanced mobility, advanced materials and energy storage.
The fund’s capital will support production expansion, order execution and commercial adoption of these companies.
On the launch of the new fund, Rohit Bhayana, co-CEO & co-founder, Oister Global, highlighted the need for strategic self-reliance in critical technologies with Indian deeptech startups making significant contributions but there were challenges in growth capital.
“Early-stage investors back the idea, and larger institutions tend to wait until a company is well past its hardest years. The growth stage in between, where technology turns into a business, has had very few committed investors. That is the gap we saw, and it is why we launched the Oister Deep Tech Fund,” Bhayana said.
This fund will focus on companies with proven, de-risked technology and proprietary, defensible IP protected by patents in India and internationally. It will look for companies that are revenue-generating, with multiple revenue streams, customers in domestic and international markets, strong policy support and a clear path to liquidity.
Sandeep Sinha, co-founder & co-CEO, Oister Global, said, “Commercialisation is at the centre of how we invest. We look for clear commercial use cases and real paying customers, not just scientific promise, and our role is to help these companies scale and reach new markets. As more family offices and institutions understand the sector, deep tech will become a mainstream allocation rather than a specialist bet.”
Oister said it has already identified an initial shortlist of few companies across sectors, with further investments to be evaluated as the fund is deployed.

articles.title: After a cyberattack, what must Nigerian banks disclose?
articles.text:
When a bank suffers a cyberattack, its customers care more about the intrusion’s technical details than about the bank. Is their money safe? Has their personal information been exposed? And what should they do to protect themselves?
In Nigeria, the answers depend partly on what happened and partly on who needs to be informed. Reporting an incident to the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) is not the same as notifying affected customers. Neither automatically requires a public announcement. But when a breach of personal data is likely to create a high risk to individuals, the law requires banks to tell those affected.
The distinction has become increasingly important as financial institutions face attacks that can expose customer information, disrupt services or compromise funds. It also raises a difficult question for regulators: how can banks be compelled to disclose incidents without turning every announcement into a threat to public confidence?
CBN figures show that Nigerian banks and their customers lost ₦134.48 billion ($100.09 million) to fraud between 2020 and 2025. The figures cover financial losses suffered by victims, not necessarily money that disappeared from the banking system, and do not distinguish cyberattacks on bank infrastructure from other forms of fraud. More recent data from the Nigerian Interbank Settlement System shows that payment fraud losses fell to ₦25.85 billion ($19.24 million) in 2025, from ₦52.26 billion ($38.90 million) the previous year.
The figures do not reveal how many cyber incidents occurred or how often customers were left unaware of compromised information. But they point to the stakes in a financial system where trust is essential to everyday transactions.
Regulators aren’t customers
Under the CBN’s 2024 Risk-Based Cybersecurity Framework, deposit money banks and payment service banks must report security incidents to the Director of Banking Supervision within 24 hours. The requirement allows the regulator to assess threats, monitor institutions, and coordinate responses. It is not a blanket instruction to announce every incident publicly.
“Banks are disclosing attacks currently to regulators, and if any bank fails to, they face sanctions from regulators,” said Festus Amede, chairman of the Committee of Chief Information Security Officers of Nigerian Financial Institutions. He did not say whether any banks have been sanctioned before for not disclosing attacks.
But a regulator and a customer need different information. The CBN may need technical details about the cyberattack, the systems affected, and the bank’s response. Customers need to know whether their accounts or personal information are at risk, and what steps they should take.
A bank can therefore report an incident to the CBN without issuing a public statement. Equally, fulfilling that supervisory obligation does not necessarily satisfy a separate duty to notify customers whose personal data has been exposed.
That second obligation comes under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023. Section 40 requires a data controller to notify the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach likely to pose a risk to individuals’ rights and freedoms. Where the breach is likely to create a high risk, affected individuals must also be notified immediately.
The distinction matters. Not every attempted intrusion exposes personal information, and not every data breach carries the same level of risk. The NDPC’s guidance identifies potential fraud, identity theft, and exposure of sensitive personal data as indicators of high risk. The assessment depends on the information involved and the likely consequences, not simply whether an incident is described as a cyberattack.
Disclosure versus panic
For banks, the challenge is deciding how to communicate while an investigation is still under way. Disclosing too little can leave customers exposed. Saying too much, too soon, can create confusion or undermine confidence before the institution has established what happened.
Gbenga Sesan, executive director of Paradigm Initiative, a pan-African organisation focused on digital inclusion and rights, argues that banks should not use the risk of panic as a reason to withhold information. They should first ensure that an incident is contained or being addressed, then explain what happened and what they are doing about it.
“They need to manage the balance between panic and disclosure,” he told TechCabal.
That balance becomes especially important when personal information is involved. A customer whose account balance remains untouched may still face risks if an attacker has obtained a phone number, email address, or other information that could be used for impersonation or phishing.
“The affected individuals need to be notified, with the bank stating which data was compromised and at the same time confirming what actions have been and will be taken,” Sesan said.
The law requires notifications to explain the likely consequences of a breach, the measures taken or proposed to address it, and how affected individuals can obtain further information. A generic assurance that customers’ funds are safe may therefore be inadequate if their personal information has been exposed.
Iyinoluwa Aboyeji, general partner and co-founder of Future Africa, sees a different danger. In a sector where confidence can determine whether customers leave their money in a bank, he worries that public disclosure could trigger withdrawals and deepen the damage caused by a cyberattack.
“Right now there is no upside except a run on the bank,” he said.
Aboyeji argues that banks should put greater emphasis on prevention and recovery, including cyber insurance that can help institutions manage the financial consequences of a cyberattack. He also warns that a system focused too heavily on punishment could discourage banks from reporting incidents.
“Punishment will make it less likely they disclose a cyberattack, not more likely,” he said.
His argument exposes a tension in the debate. Banks need incentives to report attacks promptly, but customers also need protection from institutions that might prefer to preserve their reputations rather than disclose a breach. The answer cannot be to make transparency optional. Nor should every incident, regardless of its nature or consequences, be treated as evidence of institutional failure.
The distinction regulators must make is between a bank that reports an incident, contains the threat and meets its obligations, and one that neglects basic security measures or withholds information it is legally required to provide.
Customers’ information rights
Recent incidents illustrate why the nature of a cyberattack matters. In August 2026, Zenith Bank told customers that attackers had accessed limited contact information, including email addresses and phone numbers. The bank said its core banking systems and digital channels remained secure.
In November 2026, Lendsqr disclosed attempted cyberattacks, but its chief executive, Adedeji Olowe, said the company’s defences held and no funds, customer data or accounts were compromised. Cryptocurrency platform Patricia disclosed a security breach involving Bitcoin and naira assets in 2023. Subsequent reports dated the incident to January 2022 and estimated the losses at about $2 million.
These cases are not interchangeable. An attempted cyberattack, an exposure of customer information, and a successful theft carry different consequences and may trigger different obligations. A bank can experience a serious security incident without customer data being compromised. Conversely, the absence of stolen funds does not mean customers have no reason to be concerned.
For Sesan, the problem extends beyond whether banks send notifications within the required deadlines. Regulators must establish whether institutions are identifying incidents accurately and acting on what they discover. Banks maintain internal security records, he said, which can help supervisors assess whether incidents were detected and reported.
“The notification is only a part of the measures taken to ensure transparency and ensure that action follows,” he said.
He argued that the effectiveness of the rules ultimately depends on enforcement. “The framework is only as strong as its implementation, and the latter is where we lack.”
That leaves regulators with a responsibility that extends beyond receiving reports. They must verify compliance, require corrective action, and make clear when institutions have failed to meet their obligations. Public reporting on the number and nature of incidents, compliance failures, and enforcement measures could improve accountability without exposing sensitive technical details or compromising investigations.
For customers, the practical test is simpler. They need to know whether their money or personal information is at risk, what the bank has done to contain the incident, and what steps they should take. They also need accessible support and updates if the investigation changes what is known about the breach.
The aim should not be to make every cyberattack a public spectacle. It should be to ensure that banks cannot use the fear of panic to avoid telling customers what they need to know. In a financial system built on trust, silence may protect a bank’s reputation in the short term. It can also leave the people who depend on it carrying risks they were never given the chance to manage.

articles.title: Georgina Rodríguez: “Dejé el currículum en Inditex y empecé en Massimo Dutti, pero paseaba a veces por la Milla de Oro y me encantaba ver los escaparates. Cuando entraba a una boutique de lujo, para mí era como entrar en un museo”
articles.text:
En una entrevista, Georgina Rodríguez explicaba que había dejado el currículum en Inditex y había empezado en Massimo Dutti. Pero también paseaba por la Milla de Oro. Le gustaba mirar cómo eran los escaparates.
Así conseguía ir acercándose a las tiendas que realmente le interesaban. Cuando entraba en alguna boutique de lujo, se sentía como en un museo. Antes de llegar a Gucci, trabajó en un hotel y también estuvo en Inglaterra cuidando niños.
Vivía con su madre y su hermana antes de irse a Madrid. Según contaba, estuvieron muy unidas. Nunca les faltó lo básico. Hubo momentos mejores y peores. En algunos días comían mejor que en otros, e incluso hubo días en los que no había agua caliente.
Cuando tenía 18 años le ofrecieron un trabajo en un hotel de un pueblo cerca de Barbastro (a dos horas y media de Jaca). Entonces, su madre le dejó 100 euros para que pudiera irse del pueblo. Empezó a tener sueldo propio. Pagaba un alquiler y vivía de forma independiente.
De Massimo Dutti a Gucci, con Inglaterra en medio
Según contó, trabajó en el hotel de Graus. Es entonces cuando decide irse a Madrid. Quería estudiar Administración de Empresas. Dejó el currículum en Inditex y después empezó a trabajar en Massimo Dutti.
Tiempo más tarde se trasladó a trabajar a Inglaterra. Era niñera y aprovechaba para aprender inglés. Volvió a España y consiguió entrar en Gucci. Ahí es donde empezó a conocer el mundo de la moda desde dentro.
Su cambio de vida ha acompañado su carrera como modelo y creadora de contenido. También ha tenido proyectos empresariales. Además, es la pareja de Cristiano Ronaldo. Todo esto ha sido en paralelo.
Ese cambio de vida lo recogió el reality de Netflix “Soy Georgina”. Para promocionarlo se utilizó la frase “Antes vendía bolsos, ahora los colecciona”. Según explicaba en la entrevista, es un eslogan que viene de parte de todo lo que significó su vida anterior.
Cuando alguien le comentaba que era maravilloso pasar de vender bolsos de lujo a poder comprarlos, le parecía cierto. En aquella entrevista contaba que de su vida anterior echaba en falta poder salir a la calle sin que la reconocieran. También que no tuviera que preocuparse por quién podía sacarle una foto.

articles.title: Affaire Jensen Huang : une « cellule de crise » pousse pour le retour du patron de Nvidia
articles.text:
L’affaire Jensen Huang n’est toujours pas terminée : après sa démission il y a quelques jours, certains de ses proches et des salariés de Nvidia travailleraient d’arrache-pied pour convaincre le conseil d’administration de l’entreprise de le réintégrer. Une « cellule de crise » se serait même formée autour de l’homme d’affaires, rapporte le Financial Times.
Les soutiens de Jensen Huang veulent son retour à la tête de Nvidia
Une source du média américain a expliqué qu’une cellule de crise serait en train de se créer et elle serait composée de patrons d’entreprises de la tech dans la Silicon Valley. Tous voudraient faire pression sur le conseil d’administration afin de le convaincre de nommer à nouveau Jensen Huang à la tête de l’entreprise. Ces alliés tenteraient même d’obtenir le soutien de la Maison Blanche ; tous disent l’adorer.
Un site Internet s’est même monté en quelques jours, avec une lettre ouverte déjà signée par plus de 158 000 personnes. Parmi les signataires, des dizaines de milliers d’actionnaires de Nvidia, et des gros noms comme celui d’Elon Musk, dirigeant de SpaceX et de Tesla, ou encore celui de Tim Sweeney, dirigeant d’Epic Games. On compte aussi beaucoup d’employés de Nvidia qui réclament le retour de leur ancien reponsable.
Selon plusieurs sources du Financial Times, Huang aurait évoqué un possible retour auprès de ses proches. Il soutiendrait même les efforts de cette cellule de crise. Bien que pour le moment, l’enquête indépendante sur les relations intimes de Huang avec des employées est toujours en cours. Depuis, c’est la directrice financière de Nvidia Colette Kress qui a repris les rênes de la société en intérim, en attendant qu’un nouveau dirigeant soit recruté.
Jensen Huang : un patron très populaire, et qui a rapporté beaucoup d’argent à ses actionnaires
Nvidia a été fondée en avril 1993, notamment par Jensen Huang, qui était auparavant designer de microprocesseurs chez AMD. Depuis le premier jour, il était à la tête de Nvidia et durant ces décennies, il s’est bâti une très solide réputation, tant auprès de ses salariés qu’auprès de ses partenaires. Ce qui explique la mobilisation pour sa réintégration à la tête de Nvidia.
D’un autre côté, ses soutiens ont aussi un intérêt économique. En un mois, l’action de Nvidia en bourse a perdu 25% : un quart de la valeur des actions s’est envolée. Pour beaucoup, sans Jensen Huang, l’action de Nvidia vaut beaucoup moins. Comme l’a rapporté BFM Bourse, c’est ce qu’exprimait par exemple l’analyste Dan Ives : « Nvidia sans Jensen Huang vaut 25% à 30% de moins en bourse. » Les soutiens de Huang sont également convaincus d’autre chose : il est le seul homme capable de faire remonter la pente en bourse de Nvidia.

articles.title: Hace 2.400 años los poblados del norte de la península se vaciaron en un tiempo récord. Los arqueólogos al fin tienen respuestas
articles.text:
No sabemos muy bien cómo, ni por qué, pero hacia mediados del primer milenio antes de Cristo ocurrió algo en el norte de la península ibérica: las poblaciones que ocupaban parte de lo que hoy es Galicia, Asturias o Cantabria abandonaron sus asentamientos en un período de tiempo asombrosamente breve, apenas un siglo. El fenómeno pareció arrancar en el occidente cantábrico entre finales del VI e inicios del V a.C. y hacia el IV ya identificamos indicios de la fundación de nuevos poblados, más fortificados y a mayor altura.
Se trata de un fenómeno que conecta con otras regiones del continente, pero todavía hoy sigue siendo un misterio para los expertos. Ahora un estudio aporta algunas respuestas.
“Un punto de inflexión”. Así es como define Samuel Nión-Álvarez, investigador del Instituto de Ciencias del Patrimonio (INCIPIT-CSIC), lo que ocurrió en Europa hacia el 400 a.C., en plena Edad del Hierro: sin que se sepa muy bien cómo ni por qué varias comunidades sufrieron “un cambio de paradigma en su forma de vida”, una “transformación abrupta” que aún intriga a los arqueólogos de 2026.
Al fin y al cabo, insiste Nión-Álvarez en un artículo que acaba de publicar sobre el tema en Journal of Archaeological Science, se trata de “uno de los puntos de inflexión más significativos, pero menos comprendidos”, de toda la prehistoria europea.
¿Qué ocurrió exactamente? “Una serie de transformaciones sociales, políticas y económicas alteraron significativamente el modo de vida en las sociedades europeas”, explica el investigador en su paper. Hay quien habla incluso de ‘la Crisis de los 400’, una suma de fenómenos que incluyen el abandono de antiguos asentamientos y la aparición de nuevas formas de ocupación, además de cambios a nivel demográfico, social y cultural.
¿Las razones? Se habla de clima, migración y guerras, aunque probablemente lo más lógico es hablar de una combinación de factores.
¿Cómo afectó a la península? Como recuerda Nión-Álvarez, lo más interesante es que los cambios no fueron homogéneos en toda Europa. Si nos fijamos en el sur de Países Bajos y el sureste de la Galia observamos una concentración de asentamientos y una mayor desigualdad social, mientras que en Europa Central se frena la jerarquización. En no pocas regiones se aprecia una contracción demográfica. Entre ese maremágnum de datos y tendencias, el experto del INCIPIT-CSIC ha optado por centrar el foco en el norte de Iberia.
“Pese a su diversidad, toda la península ibérica septentrional experimentó un cambio social significativo alrededor del año 400 a.C. En la Edad del Hierro tardía la región atlántica vio cómo los asentamientos prominentes eran reemplazados por castros más grandes en zonas bajas con mayor potencial agrícola”, señala Nión-Álvarez en su artículo, en el que constata “una interrupción en la ocupación” entre la Edad del Hierro temprana y tardía en varios puntos.
¿A dónde se ha ido la gente? El investigador habla de un cambio relevante en el paisaje del norte peninsular, “un proceso generalizado de abandono y desintegración social” durante la Edad del Hierro temprana, entre los siglos V y IV antes de nuestra era que llevó a que los yacimientos del norte de Iberia fueran abandonados en menos de 100 años. Es más, gracias a su investigación Nión-Álvarez precisa que el cambio empezó en la región cántabra occidental y se fue extendiendo luego hacia el oeste, sur y este peninsular.
Hay pruebas de asentamientos temporales en la región atlántica, pero la tendencia a largo plazo fue otra: se derivó hacia un modelo de poblado más extenso y “arquitectónicamente más complejo”. De los primeros asentamientos, levantados en los siglos previos, se pasó a otros fundados a mayor altura y con más fortificaciones.
266 dataciones y 109 yacimientos. El trabajo de Nión-Álvarez se apoya en 266 dataciones por radiocarbono procedentes de 109 yacimientos de la península, una muestra amplia, aunque conviene tener en cuenta dos factores importantes al manejarla. El primero es que el área analizada en el estudio (región atlántica, cantábrica y meseta oriental) comprende varios miles de yacimientos que abarcan períodos muy amplios. De ahí que la propia investigación llame a la cautela.
En cualquier caso, la muestra es lo suficientemente amplia como para que el autor haya podido arrojar luz sobre cómo fue el proceso de abandono y ocupación de nuevos asentamientos. El otro gran factor es que el período analizado coincide en parte con la denominada “meseta del Hallstatt”, lo que complica analizar con ayuda de los análisis por radiocarbono el período del 760 al 400 a.C.
Revelaciones e incógnitas. El estudio del INCIPIT-CSIC no revela las razones del éxodo, pero sí nos permite comprender mejor cómo se desarrolló con ayuda de marcos temporales: del abandono de los primeros yacimientos en la región occidental del Cantábrico, entre finales del VI y comienzos del V a.C., a la extensión del fenómeno por la región atlántica y parte de la meseta septentrional y la aparición de nuevos asentamientos a comienzos del IV a.C.
No todas las fases avanzaron, eso sí, a la misma velocidad: la fundación de las comunidades avanzó de una forma sensiblemente más lenta.
