articles.title: Beijing now bans owning and storing drones, even if you never fly them
articles.text:
What just happened? Drone users who complain that rules related to UAVs are too tough should be thankful they don't live in Beijing. A law came into effect in the Chinese capital yesterday that makes owning and storing the devices illegal, meaning you can't even keep a drone that you never fly.
While many Chinese cities have no-fly zones in sensitive areas for civilian drones, Beijing is the only one to ban ownership.
The restrictions cover the entire municipality, including its rural areas, spanning around 16,400 square kilometers (6,332 square miles), around half the size of Belgium. Bringing drones or their components into Beijing is also forbidden, so leaving one packed away in your luggage won't get you around the rules.
Authorities announced the extreme measure in September, claiming it was a requirement to keep the city secure. Beijing had already banned drone sales in May, but registered owners were initially allowed to keep their devices if they registered them with authorities, a luxury that has now disappeared.
In June, a small plane crashed into Beijing's tallest skyscraper, killing the pilot and injuring 13 people. It raised concerns about airspace safety and led to the current drone restrictions.
There are a handful of exemptions that allow drones to be owned and used, including activities involving law enforcement, counterterrorism, emergency relief, agriculture, and scientific research.
For ordinary owners, though, complying has meant selling their drones, sending them away, or handing them over for recycling. ABC News reported that some people using buyback sites were receiving less than a quarter of what they originally paid. Keeping a drone could result in confiscation and fines of up to 5,000 yuan ($749).
One Beijing aerial photographer, Matthew Zhang, moved his drone to his parents' home in nearby Tianjin and planned to travel there whenever he wanted to use it. Another owner sent his aircraft to his sister in Australia to keep it in the family.
Even toys appear to be off limits. ABC found that the rules appeared to extend to remote-controlled model aircraft and toy drones, while Taobao had blocked motorized flying products, including powered paper planes, from being sold to Beijing addresses.
It's somewhat ironic that Beijing now has some of the toughest drone restrictions in the world when China is home to DJI and dominates the consumer drone industry. Elsewhere in the country, drones are being used for deliveries, farming, and emergency work, while Beijing residents can't even keep them in their homes.
Some US cities have considered tougher restrictions on drones, but nothing approaching Beijing's. In August, Wheat Ridge, Colorado, was considering banning unauthorized drone flights over streets, parks, and other public spaces. However, the FAA says local authorities can restrict drone takeoffs and landings, rather than flights through the airspace above.

articles.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
articles.text:
AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
Using AI to make bionic vision smarter and more precise, scientists are bringing the possibility of restoring sight to people with blindness one step closer to reality.
- Date:
- November 12, 2026
- Source:
- University of California - Santa Barbara
- Summary:
- Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant. By learning how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation, the technology could bring researchers closer to restoring some degree of sight to people with blindness.
- Share:
Artificial intelligence could help overcome one of the biggest challenges in restoring vision to people who are blind: getting a brain implant to produce reliable visual experiences. Researchers from three institutions, including UC Santa Barbara, have demonstrated that AI can improve how precisely an experimental visual prosthesis stimulates the brain and predicts what a person perceives.
The team used a deep learning system to develop electrical stimulation patterns for electrodes temporarily implanted in the visual cortex, the region at the back of the brain responsible for processing visual information. By analyzing the brain's responses, the technology gave researchers greater control over neural activity and helped them better anticipate the visual sensations produced by the implant.
Published online in the journal Neuron, the proof-of-concept study represents progress toward more advanced visual prostheses, sometimes described as bionic eyes. These devices could eventually become more effective by learning how each person's brain responds to stimulation rather than relying on predetermined settings.
"Building a model in the abstract is one thing," said Michael Beyeler, an associate professor of computer science and psychological and brain sciences at UC Santa Barbara. "Seeing it shape an experiment with a person is something else entirely. That ability to go from theory to something that may one day help people is what drives much of the work in our lab."
How Bionic Vision Could Bypass Damaged Eyes
For decades, scientists have worked to develop technologies capable of restoring some vision to people who are blind, although the results have generally been limited. Some experimental devices stimulate the retina, the layer of tissue at the back of the eye that detects light. Others attempt to activate parts of the visual system farther along the pathway that carries visual information to the brain.
Visual cortical prostheses work differently. Instead of depending on the eyes or optic nerves, they deliver electrical signals directly to the visual cortex. This approach could offer a potential solution for people whose visual pathways have been damaged but whose visual cortex can still respond to stimulation. Possible candidates include individuals who lost their sight because of strokes, neurodegenerative diseases, or traumatic brain injuries.
The ability to regain even limited vision could be especially meaningful for people who remember what it was like to see.
Beyeler highlighted those "who have been able to see for part of their life, but then, because of an inherited eye disease or an accident, have lost their vision," adding, "For those people, the desire may be very strong to get some vision back."
The new findings build on earlier computational research supported by Beyeler's 2022 National Institutes of Health (NIH) Director's New Innovator Award. The five-year, $2 million grant has supported his efforts to make artificial vision systems more accurate, predictable, and effective.
Scientists Test AI With a Brain Implant in a Blind Man
An important opportunity to test the technology came in 2024, when researchers from Beyeler's Bionic Vision Lab traveled to Spain. Their goal was to determine whether their computer models could improve the performance of a brain implant already being used in an experimental study.
At Hospital IMED Elche, the team worked with a 27-year-old man who had become blind following a traumatic brain injury. He had received an implant containing 96 electrodes arranged in an array within his visual cortex. The device was intended to remain in place for six months before being removed.
When researchers activated the electrodes using electrical current, the participant experienced visual sensations known as phosphenes. These can appear as spots, flashes, or shapes of light, sometimes resembling stars or fireworks.
Producing these sensations is possible, but making them consistent and predictable is much more difficult. The same electrical stimulation does not always trigger an identical response, and activating particular electrodes does not guarantee that the person will perceive a specific visual pattern.
To address this problem, the researchers trained a deep neural network, a type of AI designed to recognize complex patterns, to predict how the visual cortex would respond to different electrical stimulation settings. The model also considered the brain's resting activity immediately before stimulation, giving it information about the participant's current neural state.
Using these predictions, the researchers identified combinations of electrical signals that were most likely to produce particular patterns of brain activity.
AI Makes Bionic Vision More Precise
When the scientists tested the stimulation patterns selected by AI, the results were encouraging. The new approach generated the intended patterns of neural activity more accurately than the comparison methods while requiring less electrical current.
Another important discovery emerged when the team examined the relationship between brain activity and the participant's visual experiences. The patterns recorded directly from his brain were better predictors of what he perceived than the stimulation settings themselves.
This distinction matters because activating the brain is not the same as knowing what a person will see. Even when researchers can produce a desired neural response, they still need to understand how the brain transforms that activity into a conscious visual experience.
"Engineers naturally want to treat phosphenes like pixels: stimulate more electrodes, and you should get a more complete image," Beyeler said. "But the brain does not work that way. Electrodes interact, neural responses fluctuate, and what we put into the brain is not necessarily what the person perceives. The challenge is to learn more about that transformation."
The findings suggest that future visual prostheses may need to do more than simply deliver electrical signals. They may also need to monitor how the brain reacts and use that feedback to continually improve stimulation.
Teaching Brain Implants to Adapt to Each Person
A key advantage of the implant used in the experiment was its ability to perform two tasks. It could stimulate the visual cortex with electrical current while simultaneously recording the resulting neural activity.
This allowed researchers to train their AI model using the brain's actual responses rather than relying exclusively on information about which electrodes were activated and how much current they delivered.
The participant also provided feedback about what he experienced. He reported whether he saw a phosphene and, during certain experiments, described its appearance, including its shape, size, brightness, and color.
Comparing these reports with the recorded brain activity revealed that neural responses contained more useful information about the perceived visual sensations than the electrical stimulation parameters alone.
The AI system also used measurements of resting brain activity to account for changes in the participant's neural state before each stimulation. This could be particularly valuable because the brain's response to electrical signals can vary over time, including from one day to the next.
By adapting stimulation to these changing conditions, future prostheses might provide more consistent visual experiences without requiring users to adjust to a rigid set of signals.
"A useful visual prosthesis cannot rely on a fixed recipe," Beyeler said. "It has to learn how an individual brain responds and adapt the stimulation accordingly. Ultimately, the device should adapt to the person, not the other way around."
A Collaborative Step Toward Restoring Sight
The research brought together scientists from UC Santa Barbara, ETH Zurich, and Miguel Hernández University (MHU). Beyeler described the effort as "a true collaboration."
The project was led by co-first authors Pehuén Moure of ETH Zurich, Jacob Granley of UC Santa Barbara, and Fabrizio Grani of MHU. The supervising researchers were Beyeler, Shih-Chii Liu of ETH Zurich, and Eduardo Fernández of MHU. Their work forms part of a larger feasibility trial taking place in Spain.
Although the technology remains experimental and the participant's visual experiences were limited to flashes and shapes of light, the results demonstrate how AI could improve communication between artificial vision devices and the brain.
Rather than treating every brain as if it responds the same way, future bionic vision systems could learn from each individual and adjust their signals accordingly. That personalized approach may prove essential to developing implants that can eventually restore useful vision to people who have lost their sight.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of California - Santa Barbara. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Pehuén Moure, Jacob Granley, Fabrizio Grani, Leili Soo, Antonio Lozano, Rocío López-Peco, Adrián Villamarín-Ortiz, Cristina Soto-Sánchez, Shih-Chii Liu, Michael Beyeler, Eduardo Fernández. Deep learning-based control of electrically evoked activity in human visual cortex. Neuron, 2026; DOI: 10.1016/j.neuron.2026.07.006

articles.title: La estafa de la tienda en línea falsa
articles.text:
La estafa de la tienda en línea falsa
Supuestos comercios ‘online’ lanzan ofertas agresivas para atraer a los compradores, especialmente durante el Black Friday y la Navidad, pero detrás de cada ganga se esconde un engaño
Los ciberdelincuentes crean negocios ficticios en internet desde los que lanzan ofertas para engañar a los consumidores y conseguir su dinero o sus datos personales y bancarios. El éxito de esta estafa reside en que ofertan artículos muy demandados, como dispositivos electrónicos o productos con cualidades casi milagrosas a precios muy bajos. Una vez realizada la compra, el consumidor nunca recibe el producto o le llega uno distinto o de escaso valor. Y sin posibilidad de reclamación alguna, porque los datos de contacto también son falsos.
El Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad (INCIBE) colaboró en el cierre de 4.600 sitios web en España (.es), en 2025, la mayoría relacionados con comercios ficticios. Meta, la empresa matriz de Facebook e Instagram, retiró 159 millones de anuncios fraudulentos, muchos de ellos ofertando productos engañosos, el año pasado.
TÉCNICAS DE MANIPULACIÓN
Urgencia
Los ciberdelincuentes crean la sensación de que, si no se compra ya, se perderá la oportunidad de adquirir un producto con una gran rebaja
Familiaridad
Suplantan a marcas populares, como grandes multinacionales de la moda, la electrónica, además de supermercados
Escasez y oportunidad
Simulan que la página solo dispone de un número limitado de existencias para generar una sensación de pérdida de oportunidad si no se compra
Prueba social
Convencen al comprador de que todo el mundo está comprando con falsos reclamos
Ciberexperto
Nombre Jordi Sánchez
Cargo Experto en fraude de CaixaBank
        “Antes de comprar una ganga, conviene parar un instante y cerciorarse de que la página es legítima. Lo lograremos comprobando la url y buscando información en internet”
0:00
CÓMO RECONOCER UNA TIENDA FRAUDULENTA
- 
                1
                Desconfiar de precios muy bajos. Si un artículo se oferta a un precio muy alejado del habitual posiblemente sea una estafa
- 
                2
                Comprobar las valoraciones y las opiniones. Ayudan a hacerse una idea sobre la fiabilidad del negocio. Desconfiar si todos los comentarios son muy recientes. Hacer una búsqueda si se tienen dudas
- 
                3
                Acceder escribiendo la dirección web en el navegador. Evitar entrar en los comercios en línea a través de enlaces recibidos por correo electrónico, SMS o redes sociales
- 
                4
                Desconfiar de comercios que ofrecen métodos de pago poco habituales o muy limitados. Los comercios legítimos suelen ofreces las opciones de pago más populares
- 
                5
                No dejarse presionar por ofertas por tiempo limitado. Los ciberdelincuentes apremian a la víctima para que se decida a comprar sin reflexionar
No todas las tiendas falsas funcionan igual. Las más comunes son las tiendas que anuncian productos que no existen; también existen tiendas de falsificaciones, que envían un producto de peor calidad que el comprado. Jordi Sánchez, experto en fraude de CaixaBank, señala que este fraude también se extiende a páginas de alquileres vacacionales, donde no solo se intenta robar el dinero de la víctima sino sus datos personales. “Los delincuentes piden la numeración de la tarjeta, pagos mediante Bizum, una copia del DNI...”, explica.
En caso de tener indicios de que se ha comprado en una tienda falsa. Se debe contactar con el banco. Si se han facilitado datos de la tarjeta, habrá que contactar con el banco para que se tomen las medidas pertinentes. Conviene guardar todas las pruebas y acudir a la Policía Nacional o a la Guardia Civil.
Estafas en las plataformas de venta legítimas. No solo las tiendas pueden ser falsas, con frecuencia, los ciberdelincuentes lanzan sus estafas a través de plataformas de compraventa legítimas. Se aprovechan de que el consumidor confía en ellas y buscan maneras de sortear las medidas de seguridad que establecen para proteger a los usuarios. Se pueden dar dos casos: que el vendedor publica un anuncio de un artículo que no posee o de un artículo que se anuncia como original y es una falsificación. El falso vendedor suele pedir al comprador que se cierre la operación fuera de la plataforma, a través de un programa de mensajería instantánea y que se haga el pago mediante canales alternativos a los ofrecidos por la plataforma, de manera que evita los mecanismos de protección que ofrece la plataforma para pagar.
OTROS CASOS DE TIENDAS FRAUDULENTAS
Cada semana aparecen noticias con nuevas maneras de embaucar a ciudadanos con una estafa de este tipo:

articles.title: Get answers from tables with tabular search in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Get answers from tables with tabular search in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base
Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base now supports tabular search, so you can get answers from tables through agentic retrieval. When a question needs data from CSV, XLSX, or XLS files, tabular search looks up values and runs calculations across every relevant row in one or more tables or sheets. It then combines the results with facts from related documents to answer analytical questions that take several steps.
A finance team closing the quarter needs to know “Which departments must write variance commentary?” No single file has the answer. It depends on the variance policy’s threshold, the quarter-close memo’s budget revisions, and math over every department in the profit and loss (P&L) workbook.
Like this finance team, most teams keep their narratives and data in the same place. For example, a Microsoft SharePoint site holds workbooks next to policies, and an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket holds CSV exports next to PDFs. Tabular search answers questions across these files through the same AgenticRetrieveStream request you already use for documents. It runs code over the original file in an isolated sandbox, so the answer uses the whole table instead of only the rows that retrieval returns. For the finance team, one request returns the departments that must write commentary. The answer cites the policy and the memo, and the trace names the workbook the code read.
In this post, you learn how tabular search answers questions that need both table data and facts from documents, and when another tool is a better fit. You also build a knowledge base with sample finance files and use the trace to see which file the code read.
Why tables are hard for retrieval
Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) returns a fixed number of passages that best match a question, which works well for prose. Tables lose information when they’re split into passages, in ways that depend on the table’s shape:
- Long tables – A table with thousands of rows spans many passages, and retrieval returns only the few that best match the question. An answer built from them uses a handful of rows, so a total, a comparison, or a threshold check can be incomplete.
- Wide tables – In a table with hundreds of columns, one row can hold more text than a passage or a search model takes in at once. As a result, values in later columns are harder to match. Long passages from wide tables can also match many unrelated questions and push more relevant passages out of the results.
Retrieval also has to match a question to the right table. Questions use business terms, such as “controllable spend,” but tables hold cost center codes, account names, and numbers. A draft and a final workbook look almost the same to search. The rule that gives the numbers meaning is often in a separate document, such as a policy.
Tabular search therefore splits the work. Retrieval only has to return one passage from the right table file, and code then reads the whole table. Because retrieval still has to find that file first, naming the file in your question helps.
Table 1 shows how plain retrieval and tabular search each handle the finance team’s question, “Which departments must write variance commentary?”
| Compared | Retrieve only | Agentic retrieval with tabular search | 
| What you get back | Passages from the policy, memo, business review, and workbook, but no complete answer | An answer naming Sales, Engineering, and Operations, with each department’s variance against its revised budget | 
| Revised variance percentages | Not available. No file stores them, so no passage can contain them | Calculated from every department row in the final workbook | 
| Sources | Each passage links to its own file, but none of them contains the answer | Citations to the finance policy and the close memo. The trace names the workbook the code read | 
Table 1: The same question with plain retrieval and with tabular search.
How tabular search works in agentic retrieval
In agentic retrieval, an agent uses retrieval to decide which documents matter and then writes the answer. Tabular search is part of that flow, so there’s nothing to turn on.
When a question needs the data in a table, the request moves through these stages:
- Retrieve – Passages come back, including passages from a table file.
- Plan – The agent uses the question and table structure to determine whether to run code over one or more retrieved tables.
- Stage – Tabular search copies the original file into an isolated sandbox with no network access.
- Compute – Model-written code runs over the whole table or sheet.
- Return – The agent gets back only what the code prints, such as totals or matching rows.
- Answer – The agent answers from the results and the passages, with citations.
Tabular search starts when retrieved passages come from a CSV, XLSX, or XLS file and the question needs a calculation across rows or a lookup of specific values.
Knowledge bases, connectors, and APIs
An AgenticRetrieveStream request can search one knowledge base or several. The Retrieve API keeps returning passages and doesn’t run code.
Tabular search works the same way whichever connector brings the files into the knowledge base, including Amazon S3, Microsoft SharePoint, Atlassian Confluence, and others.
Scope and trade-offs
Tabular search is built for questions that need calculations or lookups over the table files it retrieves. Running code adds at least one more agent turn, so answers that use table data take longer than text-only answers. Governed metrics, recurring dashboards, warehouse-scale joins, and reporting controls still belong in your business intelligence (BI) tools. Tabular search works on table files stored next to your documents, and you don’t define a schema.
Solution overview
In this solution, an Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base stores your CSV and Excel files together with related documents, such as PDF and Word files. Your application sends every question through agentic retrieval. When a question needs table data, the answer combines calculations over your tables with facts from your documents. It cites the passages it used, and the trace names the table files the code read.
In Figure 1, an Amazon S3 data source syncs these files into the knowledge base, which keeps embeddings, text, metadata, and the original files. When your application sends a question with AgenticRetrieveStream, agentic retrieval plans the work and retrieves passages from the knowledge base. If the question needs data from a table file, it sends the files to read to an isolated sandbox with no network access. There, model-written code runs over the original file and returns printed results. The answer, with citations and trace events, streams back to your application.
The worked example uses fictitious AnyCompany Retail finance files:
- Final P&L workbook (anycompany-pnl-fy2026.xlsx). It has Notes, Actuals, Budget, and Summary sheets, with one row per month, cost center, and account in the Actuals and Budget sheets.
- Draft workbook. A preliminary copy with different Q3 numbers.
- Finance variance policy (PDF). Defines controllable spend and approved budget, and sets review thresholds.
- Q3 close memo (Word). Lists approved and rejected budget revisions.
- Business review (Markdown). Explains the main variances.
These files are in the tabular-search folder of the sample-managed-knowledge-base-patterns GitHub repository. The folder also has an AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) app that deploys the resources in this post, and Python scripts that ask these questions.
Prerequisites
You need the following:
- Permissions to create AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles, S3 buckets, and Amazon Bedrock knowledge bases.
- For the identity that calls AgenticRetrieveStream, the permissions for agentic retrieval, including bedrock:GetDocumentContent. The agent reads the original table file with the caller’s credentials.
- Amazon Bedrock in an AWS Region where tabular search is available. For Region availability, see Supported AWS Regions.
- Your own CSV, XLSX, or XLS files and related documents.
- To follow the walkthrough: Python 3.10 or later with the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3) version 1.43.123 or later. You can also ask questions from the knowledge base test window in the Amazon Bedrock console or with the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI).
The calling identity needs this policy, from the agentic retrieval documentation:
For costs, see Amazon Bedrock pricing.
Upload your files to Amazon S3
Put the table files and related documents under one prefix.
- Open the Amazon S3 console and choose Create bucket.
- Enter a globally unique bucket name (this post uses amzn-s3-demo-bucket), keep Block all public access selected, and choose Create bucket.
- Choose the bucket, choose Create folder, and enter finance.
- Open the finance folder and choose Upload.
- Choose Add files, select your table files and documents, and choose Upload.
Create the knowledge base and data source
The knowledge base needs an IAM role that Amazon Bedrock can assume. This trust policy allows only the bedrock.amazonaws.com service principal, and only for knowledge bases in your account.
Next, set up the remaining resources:
- Create a role named kb-finance-role with the trust policy.
- Attach an inline policy that allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket and s3:GetObject on its objects.
- Create a knowledge base of type MANAGED with the managed embedding model.
- Create a MANAGED_KNOWLEDGE_BASE_CONNECTOR data source for the bucket, limited to the finance/ prefix.
- Set maxFileSizeInMegaBytes above your largest file.
The inline policy for step 2 allows reads on this bucket only:
This script runs steps 3 to 5 and prints the IDs:
Sync the data source and check file types
Tabular search can start only if the knowledge base assigns the right file type, so check the file type after the first sync.
- Start an ingestion job for the data source.
- Poll the job until its status is COMPLETE.
- Review the job statistics for failed documents.
- Run a Retrieve call with your question.
- Confirm that table passages show _file_type as CSV (for CSV files) or MS_EXCEL (for XLSX and XLS files).
The first script runs steps 1 to 3:
The second script runs steps 4 and 5 so you can check the table file type before asking the question with agentic retrieval. With your own files, ask a question that pairs a rule in one of your documents with a calculation over your tables, and name both.
Ask a question across tables and documents
Send the same question through AgenticRetrieveStream. The script prints the answer, each CodeExecution status, and the files the code read.
For these files, the answer combines two workbook tables with two documents:
- From the documents. The finance policy defines controllable spend as the Contractors, Travel, Software, and Marketing Programs accounts, which leaves out salaries and facilities. The business review explains the main variances.
- From the tables. The code uses every row in the Actuals and Budget sheets, filters both to fiscal Q2 and the four accounts, and then compares cost centers.
- Answer. CC-3010 (Platform) is over by 124,559.90 US dollars, with actual spending of 394,859.90 against a budget of 270,300.00. The business review attributes the variance to contractors brought in for a data platform migration. Counting every operating expense account instead gives 133,434.05.
Read the trace
Trace events arrive in this order:
- Planning. A Planning event with status SUCCEEDED includes a codeExecution action that names the documents the code will read.
- The code step. A CodeExecution event with status IN_PROGRESS (“Running code over 1 document(s)”), then one with status SUCCEEDED. The SUCCEEDED message names each file the code read and its size.
- The answer. A second planning round and the response text precede a final result event that includes the citations. Citations point to the passages the answer used, so a table file the code read isn’t always among them.
In this example, the Planning event names only the final workbook, because the policy and the business review arrive as retrieved passages.
On longer calls, the stream repeats the IN_PROGRESS event every 10 seconds, so a read timeout doesn’t fire. A code step that can’t finish reports FAILED, and the agent usually retries or falls back.
Tabular search runs as part of response generation, which is on by default, so the script leaves generateResponse unset. If you set generateResponse to false, the agent returns retrieval results without running code. For details, see agentic retrieval.
Try more questions
Each of the following questions also pairs a document with the workbook.
Apply memo revisions to quarterly totals
This question needs a budget that exists only after the memo’s revisions:
The answer uses the revisions from the memo and the Q3 actuals and original budget from the workbook. Spending came in 49,572.40 US dollars under the revised budget, so the answer is yes, even though the same spending is over the original budget. Plain Retrieve returns memo and workbook passages, but none of them contains these figures.
Apply a policy threshold after budget revisions
Here is the full version of the finance team’s question from the introduction. It needs the policy’s threshold, the memo’s revisions, and the workbook:
The policy requires commentary when the variance exceeds 5 percent of the approved budget, which includes approved revisions, and the memo approves a Marketing increase and an Engineering cut. The answer is Sales (-6.50 percent), Engineering (+5.79 percent), and Operations (+6.20 percent). Engineering crosses the threshold only because the approved cut lowers its budget.
Continue the conversation
Tabular search also works in multi-turn conversations. Send earlier turns in messages, and it runs in whichever turn needs the table. This first question asks for a calculation from the workbook:
For the follow-up, send the first question, its answer ("role": "assistant"), and the new question in messages:
The variance is 12.40 percent over budget, so it needs written commentary. Because it exceeds 10 percent, the policy also requires review by the CFO, Nikki Wolf. Here, the first turn usually runs code over the workbook, and the second answers the policy question from the history.
For longer sessions, you can keep conversation history in an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore memory resource by setting memoryConfiguration on the request, instead of resending earlier turns. For details, see agentic retrieval.
Best practices for questions over tables
Word your questions with care, because retrieval picks which table the code reads. Focused questions that name their sources help retrieval pick the right table.
- Pair one rule with one table. Name the document that holds the rule, such as “as revised in the Q3 close memo.”
- Name the file when there is more than one version. For example, “use the final FY2026 P&L workbook, anycompany-pnl-fy2026.xlsx.”
- Ask for the calculation when you want one. If a summary sheet holds a figure, the agent can answer from it. Say “Calculate each department’s variance from the Actuals and Budget sheets” to compute from detail rows.
- Ask focused questions. Build larger analyses over several turns.
A few data and application choices help as well:
- Keep tables in CSV, XLSX, or XLS files. Export tables from PDF or Word documents first.
- Set the file size filter above your largest table. Files larger than maxFileSizeInMegaBytes aren’t ingested, so the code can’t read them.
- Keep Excel sheets within 200 MB. As of this writing, tabular search runs code over CSV files up to 500 MB, the ingestion limit, but over Excel sheets only up to 200 MB. You can still ingest larger Excel files, so check sheet sizes before you rely on full-table calculations.
- Use tabular search for analysis. Running code adds an agent turn, so keep plain Retrieve for quick lookups in text.
- Scope files with metadata filters. A filter under retrievalOverrides, for example on _document_title, controls which files the code can read.
- Audit with the trace. The generated code isn’t returned, by design, because it can echo cell values. The trace shows which files the code read.
Clean up
To avoid ongoing charges, delete these resources in order:
- In the Amazon Bedrock console, choose Knowledge Bases, then choose finance-kb.
- Select the finance-s3 data source and choose Delete.
- Delete the finance-kb knowledge base.
- In the Amazon S3 console, select the bucket, choose Empty, and then choose Delete, unless other workloads use it.
- In the IAM console, choose Roles, select kb-finance-role, and choose Delete.
If you deployed with the AWS CDK app from the repository, run npx cdk destroy from its infra folder instead of these steps. It deletes everything the stack created.
Conclusion
The finance team members need to know “Which departments must write variance commentary?” With tabular search in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base, you can answer that question with one agentic retrieval request that uses the workbook, the policy, and the memo together.
In this post, you learned how tabular search answers questions that need both table data and facts from documents, and when another tool is a better fit. You also built a knowledge base with sample finance files and used the trace to see which file the code read.
To get started, see Build a managed knowledge base and agentic retrieval in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide, and AgenticRetrieveStream in the Amazon Bedrock API Reference. To learn more, read Build enterprise search for agents with Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base on the AWS Artificial Intelligence Blog.

articles.title: Recent UnrealIRCd Vulnerability Exploited in Attacks
articles.text:
Threat actors started exploiting a high-severity vulnerability in the open source Internet Relay Chat (IRC) server UnrealIRCd one day after public disclosure.
Tracked as CVE-2026-114713 (CVSS score: 8.6), the flaw is described as an improper neutralization of delimiters and allows attackers to execute commands with server/IRCOp privileges.
The issue exists because the labeled-response module “does not escape the IRCv3 ‘label’ message tag when echoing it into replies, which allows any user on a network with two or more linked servers to inject server-to-server commands that are executed with server authority,” according to a NIST advisory.
Patches for CVE-2026-114713 and eight other bugs were released on November 7 in UnrealIRCd version 6.2.7.1. A hot patch was also rolled out.
According to UnrealIRCd project leader, developer, and maintainer Bram Matthys, this is the most severe security defect discovered in UnrealIRCd.
“Any ordinary user can KILL, GLINE, and do many more bad things. This is the most critical issue found in UnrealIRCd in the past 15 years,” Matthys said.
Matthys has provided instructions on how to update to UnrealIRCd 6.2.7.1 or apply the hot patch and warned that UnrealIRCd 5 and previous releases have reached End of Life (EoL) and won’t receive a fix.
“It is likely that several bugs that are fixed in 6.2.7.1 go all the way back to 3.2.x,” Matthys said.
On November 8, he warned that hackers had already started probing vulnerable UnrealIRCd instances, urging immediate patching.
“We are seeing bad guys exploiting this issue on the internet right now. Hopefully everyone has hot-patched or updated their server, or at the very least has the spamfilter workaround deployed. If not, do so ASAP,” Matthys said.
On November 13, the US cybersecurity agency CISA added CVE-2026-114713 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) list, giving federal agencies only three days to address it, in line with BOD 26-04 requirements.
CISA also added CVE-2026-123039 to KEV. A high-severity flaw affecting multiple Check Point products, it has been exploited in destructive attacks against Israeli organizations, Check Point warned last week.

articles.title: Minister Solomon says Canada’s national AI literacy training will go live next month | BetaKit
articles.text:
Canada’s national AI literacy program will roll out nationwide next month, according to federal AI Minister Evan Solomon.
The news: Solomon broke the news in an as-yet unaired episode of The BetaKit Podcast, telling BetaKit editor-in-chief Douglas Soltys that the much-anticipated literacy program would be available to all Canadians this December. Solomon did not elaborate on what the rollout would look like, or offer specific dates as to when in December to expect the launch, but did say the nationwide programming would take participants about 90 minutes to complete.
From the source: “In December, you’ll see the national literacy program roll out for every single Canadian. This one is for every Canadian—my mom; anybody—and it’s 90 minutes,” Solomon said.
The context: Launching AI literacy training for the general public would be the third and final program delivered as part of Ottawa’s larger National AI Literacy Initiative, which Solomon unveiled in September. Under that framework, the federal government launched a three-hour training course for post-secondary students, as well as an Essentials for Educators course for teachers. It has previously stated that those courses would reach as many as one million students and 50,000 educators.
The $13-million initiative was first outlined in Canada’s National AI Strategy. The government tapped the Alberta Machine Intelligence Institute (Amii) to lead development of the program’s curriculum and its delivery to Canadians.
Final thought: Programming is intended to help learners gain the skills to “more confidently and responsibly” use AI. Solomon’s ministry previously said that training will focus on developing the skills needed to assess AI-generated content, identify misinformation, bias, or privacy concerns, and to provide “practical learning opportunities.” These training initiatives have been central to Ottawa’s efforts to increase AI adoption and trust among Canadians, given that some studies indicate Canada lags behind when it comes to both categories.
BetaKit’s Prairies reporting is funded in part by YEGAF, a not-for-profit dedicated to amplifying business stories in Alberta.
Image courtesy Lilac for BetaKit.

articles.title: NVIDIA Expands Slurm to Bring Quantum Computing Into Supercomputing
articles.text:
Quantum processor deployments at supercomputing centers have grown nearly sevenfold over the past five years, with nearly 30 supercomputing centers around the world now in the process of deploying over 50 quantum processors.
Many of these centers use Slurm to run scientific supercomputing workloads, so expanding its support for quantum processors builds on familiar workflows and tools, enabling computational chemists, nuclear physicists and materials scientists to bring quantum computing into their research domains without friction.
In a new release, Slurm builds on previous work with IBM, Pasqal and the wider quantum computing community to allow QPU builders to create a single interface to their hardware for every supercomputing center, through a simple file. This makes it easier than ever for HPC centers and QPU builders to integrate and serve their hardware.
The expansion is already being adopted by Alice & Bob, IBM, IQM, Pasqal, Quantinuum and MQSC and supports the widely used QRMI and QDMI interfaces.
Beating the Bottleneck
Until now, integrating a QPU into a supercomputing center meant a new software challenge for every new QPU or supercomputing center. By building on existing quantum-HPC interfaces such as QRMI and QDMI, the Slurm expansion allows QPU builders to reuse their integrations across all their deployments. It also means that supercomputing centers can add new quantum processors to their existing scheduling and resource-management workflows without developing bespoke QPU-specific solutions.
For quantum computing to advance science, it needs to be used by scientists. Now scientists can run quantum-classical applications developed with platforms such as NVIDIA CUDA-Q with Slurm coordinating access to all the processing they need.
Slurm 26.11 will be available later this month.
Orchestrating Resources in an Open Quantum-GPU Platform
The Slurm expansion adds a community-developed orchestration layer to NVIDIA’s open platform for quantum-GPU supercomputing, which centers around the CUDA-Q open platform for hybrid quantum-classical computing. At SC26, new releases expand all aspects of the platform:
CUDA-Q QEC allows researchers developing quantum error correction to rapidly prototype and test new ideas, including with a new decoder server. A new TCBP-JOBS decoder is 13,000x faster than the industry standard.
CUDA-Q gets an expanded layer of fault-tolerant primitives that application builders can use to realistically compile their ideas. Fermilab has already used CUDA-Q to perform studies in three weeks that would normally have taken five months.
CUDA-Q Algorithms provides reusable components for builders of quantum applications, including new capabilities in helping design the loading data into quantum circuits and tools specifically for chemistry and materials applications
CUDA-Q Pulse gives quantum hardware builders a layer for shaping the ‘pulses’ needed to control qubits on a QPU, including tools to GPU accelerate their generation.
The quantum ecosystem around the world is continuing to build with this platform. Quantum Motion integrated its QUICHE chemistry framework with CUDA-Q. Altera and Oxford Quantum Circuits designed an FPGA-based controller connecting qubit control and readout to GPUs through NVQLink.
At supercomputing scale, QunaSys used cuQuantum and 1,024 NVIDIA Hopper GPUs on ABCI-Q to simulate more than 300 million quantum operations, reaching chemical accuracy for a four-hydrogen-atom model. NVIDIA researchers used JUPITER to simulate 104 qubits under realistic noise, testing fault-tolerant designs before they’re built.
Learn more about NVIDIA quantum computing technologies.

articles.title: Audible turns to AI to help users discover audiobooks | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Amazon-owned audiobook service Audible is turning to AI to help listeners find their next book. The company on Monday launched a new “audio discovery” feature that provides a brief overview of a book’s themes and a summary of what readers liked about it, as well as commentary from an Audible editor or an author, in addition to playing the narrated sample.
The overview audio itself is generated using AI, and the commentary is pulled from recordings of past Audible interviews, the company says.
The idea is that this type of expanded introduction to a story could help users decide what to listen to next, particularly when they’re on the go and don’t have time to scroll through comments or reviews.
The feature follows last month’s launch of a handful of AI tools that let users engage more with the story, interact with characters, or catch up with the help of recaps. These features have come as Audible faces new competition in the audiobooks market, namely from Spotify, which introduced audiobook listening hours as part of its paid subscriptions. That service expanded last month to over 180 markets.
Audible’s new feature takes a cue from how Amazon is already using AI to help people shop: On the Amazon storefront, AI can summarize buyers’ product reviews so shoppers can get a quick sense of what people had to say, as well as the pros and cons of a particular item. In Audible’s case, it’s pulling information about what people liked about the book from publicly available reviews.
But such a feature could limit users’ exposure to negative reviews if the AI only pulls information from those that offer positive remarks. (Further testing will be needed to see if this is the case, of course.)
Audible says the overviews will also draw on other publicly available materials, like synopses and metadata.
The feature will initially be available for select English-language titles in the U.S., and will arrive alongside new personalized collections based on users’ listening taste that could help them find other books.
The company’s other recent AI features, Recaps and the interactive “Ask a Question” tool, are also now expanding to more U.S. titles, and will become more broadly available in December. These features will only be available to customers who have purchased a title or who have access to the book as part of their Audible membership, the company said.
“Picking your next listen should feel like getting a tip from a friend,” said Andy Tsao, Audible’s chief product and analytics officer, in a statement. “With audio discovery, you’ll get a quick audio take on why the title might be right for you from our editors, fellow listeners, or even the author. Some of the best listening experiences are those rare finds or hidden gems, and we want to make those great discoveries happen more often and more easily,” he added.

articles.title: Elon Musk revela planos para versão do Starship ainda maior
articles.text:
A SpaceX pretende aumentar as dimensões e a capacidade de seu foguete Starship na próxima geração do veículo. Em publicação feita na rede social X no domingo (15), o CEO da empresa, Elon Musk, revelou que a versão V4 terá aproximadamente 70 metros de comprimento, um aumento de cerca de 40% em relação à atual configuração, além de comportar mais de 60% de propelente.
O anúncio foi feito um dia depois de a companhia conseguir recuperar pela primeira vez o estágio superior da Starship usando os braços mecânicos instalados em sua torre de lançamento, no Texas, nos Estados Unidos. A operação ocorreu durante o 15º voo de teste do foguete, realizado em 14 de novembro de 2026, e representou um avanço no objetivo da empresa de reutilizar rapidamente seus veículos.
Starship V4 will be ~70m long, which is roughly a 40% length increase and allows >60% more propellant load. Engine count will be raised to 9, with 3 more Raptor-Vacuum engines added, and these will be higher thrust V4 engines.
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 16, 2026
Starship V4 terá nove motores
Além do aumento de tamanho, a próxima geração da Starship também terá mudanças na propulsão. Segundo Musk, a configuração V4 contará com nove motores, incluindo três unidades adicionais do tipo Raptor-Vacuum.
O executivo também afirmou que os novos motores terão maior empuxo. A configuração representa uma evolução em relação à V3, versão utilizada no 15º voo de teste, que aconteceu em 13 de novembro.
Atualmente, o estágio superior Ship da Starship V3 tem 52 metros de altura e utiliza seis motores Raptor V3. Já o primeiro estágio, chamado Super Heavy, é equipado com 33 motores Raptor.
Quando montada por completo, com os dois estágios acoplados, a Starship V3 chega a 124 metros de altura. O veículo é considerado o maior e mais potente foguete já construído.
Novas dimensões previstas para o foguete
As dimensões mencionadas por Musk também ajudam a entender a escala da mudança planejada. O estágio Ship da V4 deverá ter aproximadamente 70 metros de comprimento, medida semelhante à altura de um foguete Falcon 9 totalmente montado, outro veículo desenvolvido pela SpaceX.
A Starship também terá uma estrutura mais larga. O Ship possui 9 metros de diâmetro, enquanto a coifa de carga útil do Falcon 9 mede 5,2 metros de largura.
A empresa já havia apresentado planos para a V4 anteriormente. Em agosto de 2025, Musk compartilhou uma ilustração que mostrava a evolução do foguete das versões V2 e V3 até a futura V4, cuja estreia estava prevista para 2027.
Na ocasião, o material indicava que a Starship poderia alcançar 142 metros de altura, dos quais 61 metros corresponderiam ao estágio Ship. Entretanto, Musk afirmou que essas medidas estavam desatualizadas e que a altura total da V4 provavelmente ficará mais próxima de 150 metros.
Recuperação do Ship marcou o 15º voo de teste
A apresentação dos planos para a V4 aconteceu após uma operação inédita durante o voo de teste mais recente. A missão originalmente previa recuperar os dois estágios da Starship com os braços mecânicos da torre de lançamento.
O Super Heavy deveria retornar aproximadamente 6 minutos e 30 segundos depois da decolagem. Já o Ship permaneceria em órbita por cerca de 22 horas e 30 minutos, antes de retornar à Terra. Durante esse período, o estágio superior também deveria liberar uma série de satélites de internet Starlink V3, tarefa que foi realizada conforme o planejado.
A tentativa de recuperação dupla, porém, não aconteceu. Um alerta de baixo nível de combustível fez com que o Super Heavy desviasse sua trajetória e realizasse um pouso no Golfo do México na sexta-feira (13).
A recuperação do Ship foi a principal novidade da operação. Por retornar da órbita, o estágio superior enfrenta velocidades e temperaturas mais elevadas durante a reentrada na atmosfera, o que torna a captura mais complexa.
A SpaceX ainda não havia tentado realizar esse procedimento antes do 15º voo de teste. A empresa já tinha conseguido recuperar o Super Heavy em três voos anteriores, mas a captura do estágio superior representou um novo passo para o projeto.
Durante a transmissão da operação no sábado (14), Dan Huot, da SpaceX, comentou o resultado. “Essa era a peça que faltava”, afirmou o representante. Em seguida, acrescentou que a captura de uma Starship muda o cenário para os próximos desenvolvimentos do veículo.
Ana Figueiredo é editora de tecnologia do Olhar Digital. É formada em Jornalismo pela Universidade Federal de Uberlândia (UFU).

articles.title: Kein Code in der Box: Wenn GTA-6-Vorbesteller leer ausgehen
articles.text:
Nach jahrelanger Wartezeit wird Rockstar am 19. November 2026 endlich GTA 6 zum Spielen freischalten. Schon jetzt kann man das Game kaufen und auf die Konsole laden, um am Stichtag gut aufgestellt zu sein. Eine physische Variante auf Disc gibt es zwar nicht. Wer aber trotzdem etwas fürs Regal haben möchte, kann sich die typische Hülle für die PS5 oder die Xbox Series X kaufen. Darin liegt dann keine Blu-ray, aber ein Wendeposter und eben der für den Download benötigte Code. Doch genau diese Zeichenkette aus der Box sorgt bei Fans aktuell für Ärger.
GTA 6 ohne Code in der Box
Laut Polygon haben sich in den sozialen Netzwerken vermehrt Vorbesteller:innen gemeldet, deren Box gar keinen Code enthalten habe. Stattdessen hätten sie nur einen grauen Streifen vorgefunden, der wie Rubbelpapier aussah, aber nicht den Eindruck erweckte, einen Code freirubbeln zu können. Tatsächlich wird der Key schlicht auf diese Fläche gedruckt.
Betroffen sein sollen sowohl die Boxen für die Playstation als auch die für die Xbox. Besonders ärgerlich: Während Amazon Betroffenen das Geld zurücküberwiesen habe, hätten nicht alle Händler:innen mit Kulanz reagiert. So sollen Best-Buy-Filialen in den USA eine Rückerstattung verweigert und Gamestop-Mitarbeiter:innen an Rockstars selbst verwiesen haben. Zwei Nutzer:innen berichten allerdings davor, dass der Entwickler die jeweiligen Support-Tickets geschlossen habe, ohne sich um eine Lösung zu bemühen.
Was steckt hinter den abgelaufenen Codes?
Kotaku verweist dazu auf Fans, die behaupten, die Codes in der jeweiligen Box seien beim Einlösen schon nicht mehr gültig gewesen. Die Vermutung: Mithilfe einer Lichtquelle lasse sich der Code durch die Hülle auslesen und so praktisch aus dem Laden stehlen. Spekulationen zufolge sollen PAL‑Versionen aufgrund einer anderen Packart betroffen sein.
Beweisen lässt sich das nicht. Nachahmen ebenfalls nicht. Denn wir haben den Test mit einer Box selbst vollzogen. Der Eindruck des Redakteurs: „Keine Chance.“ Der Code ließ sich durch die Rückseite definitiv nicht erkennen.
Wie viele Fans von den fehlenden Codes betroffen sind, ist bislang unklar. Rockstar selbst hat zu dem Thema bisher keine Stellungnahme abgegeben.

articles.title: Xbox revela nuevos detalles de Project Helix, que aspira a ser la "máquina de juegos definitiva"
articles.text:
Project Helix es la apuesta de Xbox para su próxima consola, con la que tiene aspiraciones bastante ambiciosas. Desde hace tiempo se sabe que el dispositivo será una suerte de híbrido con PC, pues podrá ejecutar juegos de Windows, y en las últimas horas Microsoft ha revelado nuevos detalles en tal sentido.
En la revista oficial de los 25 años de Xbox, los de Redmond aprovecharon para brindar un poco más de información respecto del futuro de la plataforma. Jason Ronald, quien funge como vicepresidente del área dedicada a Project Helix, dio comentarios muy interesantes respecto de lo que se planea para la sucesora de las Xbox Series X|S.
Ronald hizo especial hincapié en la continuidad de la retrocompatibilidad con los juegos de generaciones previas. Asimismo, explicó que el soporte para juegos de PC no quiere decir que el aparato sea un mero ordenador con el logo de Xbox. Incluso se animó a promocionarlo como "la máquina de juegos definitiva".
"Está diseñada para ser la máquina de juego definitiva, que elimina todas las barreras para jugar que han existido históricamente. Tengo acceso a toda mi biblioteca; puedo llevar conmigo cuatro generaciones de mi catálogo de Xbox, incluyendo mi progreso, y tener todo disponible al instante. Además, hemos quitado las restricciones arbitrarias entre los juegos de consola y los de PC", comentó el susodicho sobre Project Helix.
Project Helix será una Xbox capaz de ejecutar juegos de PC, no al revés
Sobre la compatibilidad con juegos de Windows, Ronald explicó que Project Helix es una Xbox que puede ejecutar títulos de PC, y no al revés. "Tenemos muy claro el objetivo de diseño: Helix está concebida como una consola que, además, es capaz de ejecutar juegos de PC. No se trata de un PC que también permite jugar a títulos de consola. La meta es que el acceso a los juegos sea sencillo, intuitivo e instantáneo. No obstante, si eres un jugador entusiasta o un usuario avanzado que busca un mayor nivel de personalización en cuanto a ajustes y opciones de rendimiento, tienes total libertad para hacerlo".
Los detalles técnicos de Project Helix son todavía un misterio. Es un hecho que el dispositivo va a utilizar un chip de AMD, lo que garantiza que mantenga la retrocompatibilidad con consolas de generaciones previas. De acuerdo con rumores en circulación, el plan de Xbox es lanzar más de una consola en su próxima generación. La compañía apuntaría a estrenar un modelo portátil que podría llegar a finales de 2027, mientras que la versión de sobremesa estaría lista en 2028.
Todos los planes están sujetos a la crisis de la RAM, que ha obligado a Microsoft a replantearse elementos de Project Helix. "Estamos trabajando arduamente para replantearnos todo lo posible sobre Helix, una consola que nos hemos comprometido a lanzar al mercado. Somos muy conscientes de los cambios que debemos implementar como empresa para garantizar que sea asequible y flexible", explicó Matthew Ball, jefe de estrategia de Xbox, en junio pasado.
Ese mismo mes, Asha Sharma, CEO de Xbox, habló de la necesidad de trabajar para reconsiderar la estructura de costos de la consola. Puntualmente, la ejecutiva habló de buscar alternativas que ayuden a mitigar el impacto que la escasez y el encarecimiento de la RAM y el almacenamiento tienen sobre el PVP.

articles.title: Upgrade your phone with these 10 early Black Friday deals — save up to AU$770 off iPhones, Samsung Galaxy, Google Pixel and more
articles.text:
Upgrade your phone with these 10 early Black Friday deals — save up to AU$770 off iPhones, Samsung Galaxy, Google Pixel and more
Premium flagships and budget smartphones from AU$447
It's almost Black Friday and retailers and telcos across Australia, and there's never been a better time to splurge on big purchases, like the best phones and the best cheap phones.
With plenty of launches throughout 2026 across budget, mid-range, flagship and ultra-premium foldables, you can expect a whole heap of deals and discounts — not to mention all the handsets released last year for even more savings, especially if you don't need the latest tech.
While it may be tempting to waiting for further price drops closer to the official Black Friday date of November 27, some phones could end up getting sold out, especially for any standout deals.
Key dates for the 2026 Black Friday sales
- Sale starts: officially November 27
- Early deals: early November
- Black Friday sales end: November 30
- Late deals: early December
Black Friday phone deals: Top retailers
- Amazon: save on the Samsung Galaxy S26 range plus other phone deals
- JB Hi-Fi: save up to AU$1,000 on iPhones, Samsung Galaxy, Google Pixel and more deals
- Kogan: huge savings across a wide variety of phones
- The Good Guys: save up to AU$400 on the Samsung Galaxy S26 range and more
- Vodafone: deals on phones and plans
- Optus: discounts from the teal telco
Best Black Friday phone deals 2026
The iPhone 17 Pro Max may not be the very best iPhone money can buy anymore, but it represents a significant improvement over its predecessors with an updated design, a powerful A19 Pro chipset and still some of the best smartphone cameras.
The Google Pixel 11 Pro was just released in August 2026, but it's already getting more than AU$500 off the sticker price for Black Friday, although this is hardly a surprise given how frequently Google runs discounts on its Pixel handsets in recent years. It saw a price hike over last year's Pixel 10 Pro, but its storage options now start at 256GB, and it has a brighter display, a new glass camera housing and a faster Tensor G6 processor.
The Pixel 11 Pro above is great, but having used the base Pixel 11 myself, I'd argue it's the smarter buy for most people, especially at this sub-AU$1,000 price. It features the same Tensor G6 chipset, 12GB of RAM and 7 years of software support, and it also has three camera lenses like the Pro (although lower-spec ones).
Having just launched in August 2026, Samsung's Galaxy Z Flip 8 is the first of the South Korean brand's 2026 foldables lineup to get a sizeable discount for Black Friday. It features a slimmer chassis, improved hinge, a new Exynos 2600 chipset and better cross-screen app continuity over its predecessor.
As far as mid-range/budget Android smartphones go, you can't go wrong with the Google Pixel 10a, especially with Android 17 set to get a full release next month (or you can access the Android 17 beta now if you're feeling adventurous). While I've criticised the phone for being too similar to its predecessor, the Pixel 9a, it's still a really good budget Android phone, and this discount makes it even more of a bargain.
We named the Nothing Phone (4a) the best cheap phone you can buy in Australia for its spec sheet relative to its price, as well as its unique aesthetics on both the hardware and software side. Only the 256GB storage option is discounted at JB Hi-Fi, but it's an excellent handset for less than AU$600.
A step down to the Galaxy A57, which I found to be one of my favourite mid-range smartphones of the year, the Galaxy A37 is a great no-frills Samsung handset with some respectable specs — a 6.7-inch 120Hz Super AMOLED display, three rear camera lenses, a 5,000mAh battery with 45W fast charging, to name a few. The Exynos 1480 chipset isn't the most beefy and RAM options start at 6GB, but for less than AU$450, it's still a lot of phone for the money.
The Phone (3) is Nothing's first 'true' flagship phone (and still remains the brand's current flagship) after specialising in budget and mid-range handsets since the brand's inception. While its Snapdragon 8s chipset won't match the top flagships, the Phone (3) still has competent cameras, a vibrant 6.7-inch display and 12GB of RAM. Our review only took points off the (admittedly divisive) design and price, but this discount takes care of the latter.
Before Apple debuted the iPhone Air, Samsung squeezed the internals of the Galaxy S25 Plus into a smaller form factor, with the result being a handset that’s a full 1.5mm thinner than the Plus and almost 2.5mm thinner than the S25 Ultra. Some compromises have had to be made, however: a smaller device also means a smaller battery and one fewer camera lens (telephoto).
Once one of our best cheap phones before the (4a) Pro superseded it, Nothing's mid-range Phone (3a) Pro is still a capable and premium-feeling handset that also happens to look unique and quirky at the same time. Our review called it the best phone from Nothing at the time, praising its premium materials, design, software and battery life.
Black Friday phone deals 2026: FAQs
When will the best Black Friday phone deals start in 2026?
While Black Friday is technically on November 27, deals often start much earlier from retailers, telcos and brands across Australia. Most deals are set to wrap up by Cyber Monday, November 30 but some retailers and brands will continue their sales into December and sometimes even straight to Boxing Day.
Where will the best Black Friday phone deals be?
We'll be rounding up all the best Black Friday phone deals right here on this page, so bookmark it and check in regularly for recommendations when the discounts start coming in. As a quick overview, here are the big three retailers and major phone brands that we're expecting to feature the best phone deals until November 30.
- Amazon: hot deals year-round
- eBay Australia: a one-stop shop for a lot of hot offers
- JB Hi-Fi: discounts on big-ticket phones and mid-range marvels
- Samsung: big savings on Samsung Galaxy premium and budget phones
What Black Friday phone deals do we expect to see in 2026?
For Black Friday phone deal hunters, there is good news and bad news. The good news is that there are a few deals already live, and we're expecting more discounts in the next few weeks.
But if you're in the market for a new iPhone, we won’t expect as many deals, as Apple’s handsets don't usually see the same major price drops as Android rivals. In fact, the best deals you'll find will likely come from a telco with a contract agreement, but if you were already shopping for service, you could absolutely score a bargain at least on plan fees.
That said, we’ve seen big discounts on the ultrathin iPhone Air all year, so expect to see similar deals during Black Friday, whether it’s from a telco or when bought outright. On the other hand, if you’re happy with an older iPhone model, they tend to get nice price drops. In fact, the oldest phone that’s slated to get the latest iOS 27 includes the iPhone 11, which originally launched in 2019. While I wouldn’t necessarily recommend a phone that old, it’s a testament to how long Apple supports its iPhones.
For Android phones, Google and Samsung usually offer discounts on both their flagship and budget models relatively frequently. Smaller makers like Motorola, however, are more likely to offer discounts even more often than Google and Samsung, with deals across its full range. Third-party retailers will be a good bet too, including The Good Guys and JB Hi-Fi.
What should I be looking for in a smartphone?
Display
Without question, the best kind of display you can get is AMOLED, as it offers deep blacks and individually-lit pixels, allowing for always-on-displays that consume very little battery due to the majority of the screen turned off. They're also incredibly vibrant, with vivid, organic colours that really bring videos and games to life.
Various types of OLED displays are featured in most top models, including the Samsung Galaxy S26, iPhone 17, Google Pixel 10 ranges and more. Some of the more affordable options, however, still opt for LCD displays, and while they aren't quite as impressive when it comes to vibrancy and contrast, they do tend to offer excellent brightness.
Operating system (OS)
The first big thing you'll need to decide is whether you're after an Android handset, or would prefer to hitch your wagon to Apple's iOS ecosystem.
There are a huge number of Android handsets on offer from several major manufacturers, which all generally have their own strengths (and occasional weaknesses). That means there's a lot more choice for those who want to embrace the customisation and freedom that Google's mobile OS is known for.
On the other hand, Apple's iPhones, while more closed-off in nature, are excellent options for those who prioritise predictability and want to ensure they get the latest OS updates as soon as they're available. They're also ideal for those who already own Mac computers and subscribe to Apple's various services.
Camera
When looking at a phone's camera array, you should consider the types of photos that you want to take. If you want to photograph wildlife or other things you can't easily get close to, then a telephoto lens is essential, with zoom a key factor to consider, while for landscapes a good ultra-wide is your friend.
But of course, still photography isn't the be all, end all. If your needs are more centred around video recording, you will want to track assets like the resolution at which a camera phone shoots video, stabilisation features (for action video) and capture modes.
When you have at least a general idea of what you need from your phone's camera, you can get a better picture of which phone camera setup is for you, with our best camera phones list helping you to easily find which options tick the right boxes for what you might need.
Chipset
Depending on how much you're willing to spend, Android phones offer varying degrees of performance, with top handsets like Samsung's Galaxy S26 Ultra and Apple's iPhone 18 Pro Max offering plenty of grunt under the hood thanks to their top-of-the-line specs.
When purchasing a new handset, it's important to find out if its chipset is powerful enough to handle your daily tasks. At present, the latest Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chipset is what you'll find in most top-of-the-line Android models, even in this year's Samsung models. You’ll find that, among the Snapdragon, Exynos and MediaTek chip families, the more powerful the processor, the higher the model number.
Apple's iPhones, on the other hand, often pack a similar amount of horsepower depending on which generation of device they belong to. Apple's own A20 Pro chip powers its high-end iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone Duo models, while last year's iPhone 17 and 17e handsets are on the A19 processor. Both guarantee terrific performance and will continue to do so for a couple more years yet. After that, you may start to notice some slowdown, depending on how power-hungry Apple makes its next iOS iterations.
Storage
Most manufacturers will offer their handsets with various amounts of onboard storage. Depending on what you want to do with your phone, you'll want to settle on a storage size that's right for you. Smartphone storage can range anywhere from 64GB to 2TB (realistically, you'll be seeing between 128GB and 1TB in most cases), though you can expect the price to rise significantly as that number gets larger. Some Android phones will offer expandable storage via a microSD card slot, meaning you can add more capacity should you ever need it.
What to expect for Black Friday 2026
There are plenty of savings to be had in the final month before the Australian financial year comes to a close, and that makes it a great time to save a packet on the latest phones.
As is always the case, more recent models like those from Apple's iPhone 18 Pro range and the Samsung Galaxy Z foldable lineup won't be seeing the biggest discounts (although we suspect something in the 10-20% range may arrive, and more likely with the latter), but models from the previous generation or more mid-range handsets are quite likely to get hefty savings applied to them.
This means that we may see savings on the more affordable iPhone 17e and models like the iPhone 17 and Samsung Galaxy S26 ranges will be had for a bargain as retailers want to clear their stock.
Since launch, we've seen the Google Pixel 10, 10 Pro, 10 Pro XL and even the 10 Pro Fold receive up to AU$500 off as soon as Black Friday 2025, which was just a few months after launch. We'll likely see the same bargains on the new Google Pixel 11 flagships, either through a telco or outright.
You don't necessarily need to buy the phone of your choice outright either — telcos have started offering discounts on certain models purchased on a plan. For example, Vodafone and Optus discounted the iPhone Air and the Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra by up to AU$800, as long as you got them on either a 12-, 24- or 36-month plan. You can expect more of these this year, although the better discounts and wider variety of handsets will likely be on outright purchases.

articles.title: Le RPG vampirique du créateur de The Witcher 3 baisse fort sur PS5 pour le Black Friday
articles.text:
The Blood of Dawnwalker, le RPG imaginé par le réalisateur de The Witcher 3, est actuellement proposé à 42 € sur PS5 chez Amazon, dans son édition Day One. Il n’était pas descendu sous les 51 € ces 30 derniers jours.
Un mois pour sauver sa famille
Tout commence par un enlèvement. Un puissant seigneur vampire s’est emparé de la famille de Coen, et il compte la sacrifier d’ici un mois. Il vous reste donc trente jours et trente nuits pour la retrouver, ce qui donne à toute l’aventure un vrai sentiment d’urgence. Coen a pourtant un atout de taille, puisqu’il vit entre deux mondes. Le jour, il reste un humain qui se bat à l’épée et à la magie, et la nuit, il devient un vampire capable de grimper aux murs et de se déplacer dans l’ombre. Chaque journée compte, chaque choix a des conséquences, et il faudra parfois accepter de ne pas pouvoir aider tout le monde.
Toute l’originalité du jeu tient dans ce cycle. Le jour, Coen est humain et se bat à l’épée et à la magie. La nuit, il grimpe aux murs, se téléporte d’ombre en ombre et se bat avec ses griffes. Mais s’il ne se nourrit pas, sa soif de sang peut le pousser à s’en prendre aux habitants.
Le temps, lui, n’avance que lorsqu’on fait progresser l’histoire. On peut donc explorer librement ce grand monde ouvert, mais chaque quête importante coûte de précieuses heures, et on ne pourra pas aider tout le monde.
Selon How Long To Beat (site de référence pour se donner une idée de la dutrée de vie d’un jeu vidéo), Il faut compter une quarantaine d’heures en comptant les quêtes secondaires.
Le bon moment pour se lancer ?
Le jeu est sorti début septembre à 69,99 €. À 42 €, il coûte donc 40 % de moins, deux mois et demi à peine après sa sortie.
En comparaison, la même édition Day One est actuellement proposée à 49,99 € sur la Fnac.
Notre test a surtout été séduit par l’écriture du jeu et par son système de temps, qui oblige à faire de vrais choix. Coen s’impose aussi comme un héros attachant, tiraillé entre l’homme et le monstre. Les combats sont un peu moins convaincants sur la durée, et quelques animations manquent encore de finition, mais l’aventure vaut largement le détour, surtout à ce prix.
L’offre est vendue et expédiée par Amazon, et elle est signalée comme étant à durée limitée.
