articles.title: Jensen Huang no tira la toalla: quiere volver a NVIDIA pocos días después de renunciar
articles.text:
Con su renuncia como CEO y presidente de NVIDIA todavía fresca, Jensen Huang no estaría dispuesto a darse por vencido al 100 %. Según un reporte de Financial Times, el ejecutivo ha comenzado a discutir con personas de confianza un posible regreso a la conducción de la empresa.
La idea llegaría de la mano de una movida por parte de colegas de Silicon Valley que pretenden hacer presión para que Jensen Huang pueda regresar a NVIDIA. Sus aliados buscarían generar el mayor ruido posible y para ello intentarían conseguir el apoyo de la Casa Blanca.
Por lo pronto, se desconoce si el regreso de Jensen Huang a NVIDIA es una opción real. El cofundador del gigante verde renunció a su cargo el pasado jueves, envuelto en un par de escándalos notorios. El primero, su relación extramatrimonial con Alice Huang, señalada como una supuesto espía china; el segundo, su amorío con Kimberly Powell, vicepresidenta del área de atención médica de la firma.
El presunto interés de Jensen Huang de volver a ser el CEO de NVIDIA se da en paralelo con una carta pública de empleados, exempleados, accionistas y socios reclamando su vuelta. La misma, titulada Stand with Jensen, cuenta con el aval de Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney (Epic Games) y varios otros ejecutivos tecnológicos de renombre.
Jensen Huang busca regresar como CEO de NVIDIA
Al momento de redacción de este artículo, la carta supera las 178.000 firmas, de las cuales más de 8.800 corresponderían a empleados actuales de NVIDIA. La veracidad de las rúbricas no se ha podido corroborar, pues en varios casos se han detectado nombres mal escritos que son parecidos a los de celebridades o personajes públicos.
Si Jensen Huang realmente regresa como CEO de NVIDIA, no será el primer caso de un movimiento de este tipo en el sector tecnológico. El caso más recordado es el de Sam Altman, destituido como jefe de OpenAI tras un motín gestado por sus principales laderos. Sin embargo, el empresario regresó a la startup de inteligencia artificial unos pocos días más tarde tras el reclamo de los empleados.
La carta abierta de la campaña Stand with Jensen plantea tres medidas a la junta directiva de NVIDIA. Por un lado, el regreso de Jensen Huang como CEO, pero también una investigación independiente y una audiencia justa, así como una explicación pública oportuna.
"Durante treinta y tres años, Jensen volcó todo su ser en la construcción de NVIDIA. Apostó por ideas que la mayor parte del sector descartó, mantuvo el rumbo durante años en los que tales apuestas parecían una insensatez, y permaneció el tiempo suficiente para ver cómo transformaban la forma en que el mundo procesa la información. Muchos de nosotros nos unimos a la empresa gracias a él. Muchos nos quedamos por la forma en que él abordaba el trabajo: como algo que merecía hacerse bien, en equipo, sin importar las horas que hicieran falta. Esta compañía es la obra de su vida. Eso merece algo más que gratitud a posteriori. Merece un trato justo, ahora mismo", dice el texto en favor del exjefe de NVIDIA.
Más allá del apoyo que está viendo Jensen Huang tras su renuncia, no todos están de acuerdo con un posible regreso como CEO de NVIDIA. Una de las fuentes de Financial Times indica que el romance del empresario con Kimberly Powell es causa suficiente de despido para cualquier ejecutivo. Esto, debido a las políticas de la empresa respecto de las relaciones entre directivos y subordinados.
Sea como sea, es evidente que el culebrón de Jensen Huang todavía tiene varios capítulos por escribir. Por lo pronto, Colette Kress continúa fungiendo como CEO interina mientras la empresa evalúa potenciales candidatos. Desde la junta han mencionado que todavía no se contactaron con ningún reemplazante, aunque los principales nombres apuntados serían los de Lisa Su, la CEO de AMD, y Rene Haas, CEO de ARM. Seguiremos atentos a las novedades.

articles.title: Big Nuclear isn’t worried about the Democrats stopping data centers
articles.text:
Constellation Energy – America’s largest operator of nuclear power plants – does not share Wall Street’s concerns that the Democrats will slow down data center development. On the company’s third-quarter earnings call last week, CEO Joe Dominguez was, for lack of a better word, unbothered as he addressed the blue wave.
Big Nuclear isn’t worried about the Democrats stopping data centers
They may have a point.
They may have a point.
“I do think we’ve seen a bit of an overreaction in the market to the election results based upon fear that Democrats won’t let data centers get built,” Dominguez said.
Many of the Democrats who seized control of the House and Senate in this month’s midterm elections ran on anti-data-center campaigns, which triggered a historic $2.5 trillion sell-off in AI-adjacent stocks that reached well beyond tech to the energy, construction, and materials sectors.
Up until a few years ago, many of Constellation’s nuclear power plants were in severe financial distress and in danger of shutting down early. But the data center development boom and its enormous demand for electricity have dramatically reversed the nuclear industry’s fate.
Now, Constellation and other companies like it are signing major deals with Big Tech companies to provide power to data centers. Microsoft, for instance, signed a deal with Constellation to fund the revival of a nuclear plant at Three Mile Island in Pennsylvania. (Three Mile Island is the site of what the Nuclear Regulatory Commission refers to as the “most serious accident in US commercial nuclear power plant operating history.”)
Constellation also signed major contracts in the third quarter to provide power to Amazon and Google data centers, Dominguez said.
Nuclear energy has had bipartisan support for years. The US Department of Energy classifies nuclear as a “clean” energy source because the act of operating a nuclear reactor does not directly produce carbon emissions. This makes nuclear an appealing investment to Big Tech companies that have to balance aggressive data center development with the ambitious climate goals they set long before the AI race took off. Still, nuclear energy has its issues. One of the biggest is nuclear waste, which the US government has not figured out how to dispose of at scale.
Big Nuclear and Big Tech also tout these deals as good for the economy and job creation.
“The market scare that people got last week was not lost on Democrats,” Dominguez said on the call. “They do not want to be the reason that the economy takes a nosedive by halting data center development.”
Of course, Constellation’s future is essentially staked on the data center buildout, and Dominguez’s job is to convince investors they have nothing to worry about.
In this instance, however, Dominguez really does seem genuinely unconcerned by the new Democratic majority in the federal government. It could be that he understands that, yes, while the Democrats won the midterms on promises of data center regulation and the blue wave included many new Democratic governors, data centers aren’t necessarily a strictly partisan issue. Some Democrats have opposed harsh measures like moratoriums — though on the flip slide, Constellation may also have to deal with challenges from the other side of the aisle.
In Virginia, some of the state lawmakers who have been the most vocal about data centers are actually Republican. Virginia Sen. Richard Stuart, a conservative Republican, has aggressively pursued data center regulation. Last month, Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger, a Democrat, denied Stuart’s request for a special session to address a concerning new report from the Virginia Department of Environmental Quality on the state’s groundwater supply, which has become strained amid rampant data center growth.
For years, companies like Constellation have been sitting on a bunch of old reactors teetering on the edge of extinction because they didn’t have enough customers to keep them afloat.
The fight against data centers so far has been highly fragmented and hyperlocal, but that could change soon. The Trump administration loves data centers, and the federal government is working on wresting some control over data center development away from the states. But even then, Democrats and Republicans at the federal level tend to view data centers as an inevitable part of the future that needs some guardrails rather than out-of-control corporate growth infringing on the average American’s quality of life.
Just look at the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, which was co-sponsored by two Democrats. The Senate is expected to vote on a passage of a sweeping bill which is being marketed as a way to speed up the permitting process for new power plants and transmission lines and connect new data centers to the grid faster. New Mexico Sen. Martin Heinrich, one of the Democrats backing the bill, has touted its inclusion of provisions designed to protect utility customers from rising rates due to data centers, ensuring Big Tech pays its fair share of costs. Researchers at Columbia University SIPA’s Center on Global Energy Policy called the bill’s protections “mixed,” noting they do not account for wholesale capacity and energy prices, a “principal way” data center electricity demand can lead to higher household bills.
Senate Democrats are sharply divided on the bill, which critics say will fast-track data center projects at the expense of public input and environmental oversight and lead to a massive overbuild of energy projects that Americans will end up paying for.
On Constellation’s earnings call, Dominguez pointed out that Virginia and Illinois, states with Democratic governors already in place before the election, have seen “a great deal of data center development.”
“The bottom line is that Democrats care deeply about economic growth and they care very deeply about the many labor jobs that go with data center construction,” Dominguez said. “With labor such a key constituent for Democrats, it’s hard to imagine that we are going to halt work …There might be some differences and certainly there are going to be some local areas, I think, that are not going to want data centers.”
Of course, Dominguez is speaking to investors here, and he wants to assuage their concerns. He also has a good point. Grassroots efforts to stop local data center development have been successful and have contributed to broader opposition to data center development across the country. But data center developers can also abandon projects and go elsewhere. Until a few years ago, data centers were largely concentrated in Northern Virginia, but with the AI boom, developers have fanned out across the country in search of available power and land. A total of 38 states have welcomed them with open arms and generous tax breaks, per the National Conference of State Legislatures.
Of course, Dominguez is speaking to investors here, and he wants to assuage their concerns.
Thanks to the convoluted way the US electric grid and energy markets work, Constellation’s power plants don’t even need to be located in the same state as their data center customers — the plant supplying the power just needs to be connected to the same region from which the grid is drawing power. The purchase agreement, in that sense, is symbolic: Because the data center needs more electricity than it can draw from the local grid without causing disruptions for everyone else, the data center pays for independent power providers like Constellation to supply the grid with extra electricity.
That’s why data centers and the enormous amount of electricity Big Tech says it needs to power them have been such a boon for the nuclear industry. For years, companies like Constellation have been sitting on a bunch of old reactors teetering on the edge of extinction because they didn’t have enough customers to keep them afloat.
Nuclear lobbyists will tell you that’s because the NRC’s safety regulations are overly restrictive and lead to untenable upfront capital costs that make projects impossible to finance. (This has been an industry talking point since 1979, after the NRC seriously overhauled its safety standards following the partial meltdown at Three Mile Island. That site is now owned by Constellation, which has signed a 20-year deal with Microsoft.)
Both the Biden and Trump administrations have worked to support the development of nuclear power in the US by passing developer tax credits. The Trump administration has gone even further, pushing for a sweeping reform of the NRC that would make it much easier for new reactors to obtain operating licenses.
And the Department of Energy this month approved a $5 billion loan to Constellation, which the company will use to upgrade its existing nuclear fleet. Another nuclear energy company, Vistra, received a $4.2 billion loan.
It’s not totally unlike the Biden administration’s passage of the Civil Nuclear Credit Program in 2022, which planned to loan $6 billion to struggling nuclear companies in the US.
That’s not lost on Dominguez.
“Interestingly, in many respects the election had the Republicans saying a lot of the same things that the Democrats were saying,” Dominguez told investors on the call. “And I believe that the policy solutions are going to be somewhat similar.”

articles.title: Advanced Metrology for Defect Detection, Tool Health, and Semiconductor Yield Enhancement
articles.text: In advanced semiconductor manufacturing, small defects can have a large effect on yield. Thin film deposition tools must stay stable and qualified. Process drift must be caught early. When a defect does appear, engineers need to know where it came from and how it affects device performance. This webinar shows how in-line inspection and offline characterization combine into one workflow, from tool monitoring to root-cause analysis. In the first half, Dr. Bitan Chakraborty from Intel, explains how surface scan metrology fits into station monitors for thin film tools. The session shows how baseline signatures and real-time monitoring reveal hardware wear, particle generation, and process drift before they reach production wafers. It then moves to in-line scans on patterned wafers. These scans expose layer-level defects and show how they form and spread through multi-layer device stacks. Linking this defect data to electrical test results helps teams find root causes and focus their yield improvement work. In the second half, Dr. Jacob Petersen from Evident Scientific, addresses a common question: what happens after an in-line tool flags a problem? In-line tools are fast, but they cannot always provide the details needed for a firm conclusion. Offline 3D optical profilometry fills that gap by combining three complementary inspection techniques in a single system. It delivers dimensional measurements and helps determine whether a defect lies within the sample or comes from foreign material. The session covers how several optical techniques support inspection from bare silicon to fully packaged chips. It also shows how automation enables fast measurement of features down to the sub-nanometer scale with minimal operator handling. What You Will Learn: How surface scan metrology in station monitors tracks tool health and supports the qualification of thin film deposition processes How baseline signatures and real-time monitoring detect particle generation, hardware degradation, and process drift before production is affected How in-line scans on patterned wafers reveal layer-level defects and show how they propagate through multi-layer device structures When offline 3D optical profilometry should follow in-line inspection, and how it measures dimensions and separates sample defects from foreign material How correlating tool health data, inspection results, and electrical performance links physical defects to yield loss and guides targeted improvement projects Register now for this free webinar!

articles.title: Why does your body store fat in your butt?
articles.text:
Curious Kids is a series for children of all ages. If you have a question you’d like an expert to answer, send it to CuriousKidsUS@theconversation.com.
Why does your body store fat in your butt? - Ellen, age 8, Cambridge, Massachusetts
Have you ever wondered why some parts of your body are firm, like your elbows, while other areas, like your butt, are squishier?
The difference is due to what scientists call fat distribution, and researchers are still trying to understand why bodies store fat in some places but not in others.
All animals have fat in their bodies, even insects. Bears even put on up to 400 pounds (180 kilograms) of additional body fat, the equivalent of 544 large cheese pizzas, to survive hibernation.
Fat is an important and constantly changing part of all bodies, including those of humans and our evolutionary ancestors.
What is fat?
Fat, also called adipose tissue, is one kind of connective tissue that helps hold your body together.
For a long time, scientists thought that adipose tissue was mainly a storage place for the extra energy your body doesn’t use from the food you eat. While fat is a great source of stored energy, it also has many other functions. There are even different kinds of fat.
Visceral fat serves as a sort of protective bubble wrap, surrounding and filling in the spaces between your internal organs. Subcutaneous fat, the layer of fat between your skin and your muscle that you can pinch, is a protective cushion and helps to keep you warm by insulating you like a coat.
Fat also produces and responds to hormones, a type of chemical messenger, to regulate how your body uses energy and to tell you when you are hungry or full.
Different kinds of fat also have different jobs. White fat is the kind of fat most people are familiar with and performs the functions mentioned above.
You may be less familiar with brown fat, which is brown because it contains a lot of mitochondria: the parts of your cells that produce the energy your body needs to perform all its functions.
Not all animals have brown fat, but humans do. Scientists know that brown fat performs a special function to heat your body when you get cold. It doesn’t store energy, like white fat does, to help your body move.
When you were a baby, you had a lot of brown fat along your torso to help keep you warm because your body wasn’t mature enough to maintain your body temperature. As you grow older, you have less brown fat. It is only located just above your collar bone and along your major deep blood vessels, like your aorta.
Why do humans store fat where we do?
Researchers don’t know enough yet about brown fat to know why it is in just a few parts of the body. It is possible that it’s near the neck and around major blood vessels to help insulate the blood and keep overall body temperature in a healthy warm range.
As for white fat, there appear to be three main factors that determine where your fat gets stored: genetics, hormones and age.
Certain genes direct fat to accumulate in the butt, while other genes tell it to collect on the torso.
Hormones like estrogen, which affects almost every system in all bodies but is typically higher in females, direct more subcutaneous fat to gather in the butt, thighs and backs of the arms. Cortisol, the stress hormone, seems to direct visceral fat to accumulate in the belly area.
But why isn’t fat evenly distributed throughout the body? Well, having a lot of fat around your elbows and knees would limit your ability to bend your arms and legs. Storing a lot of fat around your head would possibly put your brain at risk of overheating. Other parts of your body, like hips, butts, breasts and thighs, don’t have these risks – maybe that’s why we store fat there.
Why do people have fat at all?
Don’t be fooled: A lot of animals that look fat, like a hippopotamus, actually aren’t. Hippos only have around 2% body fat, the percentage of how much of your body mass comes from fat; while the average human woman has over 30% body fat.
In the rest of the animal kingdom, biologists typically only see a lot of body fat among hibernating or marine mammals. For the hibernators, the fat serves as energy storage for long, cold winters. For marine mammals like seals and whales, that extra fat is like a giant puffy coat helping to keep them warm in the cold depths of the ocean.
Humans do not hibernate, nor do we live in the ocean, so why do we have a lot more fat than all other primates and most mammals?
Anthropologists like me, who study how the human body has evolved over time, think it has to do with the lifestyle of our evolutionary ancestors who had to gather and hunt to survive. Gathering and hunting were not always reliable food sources. We think our ancestors developed the ability to put on extra fat as a food insurance policy. When food was difficult to find, they could rely on their extra fat stores to carry them through until food became available again.
Researchers are still trying to determine when this extra fat storage evolved. We have one line of evidence from small stone figures known as Gravettian statues.
These ancient statues from 25,000 to 28,000 years ago depict feminine figures who carry a lot of extra body fat. Archaeologists have found them all throughout Europe and Russia.
The way the ancient artists depicted fat on these figures matches how fat looks on bodies today. This accuracy has led researchers to believe that the makers of the Gravettian statues knew how individuals with greater body fat actually looked, meaning at least some people at this time did put on a lot of extra fat.
Europe and Russia back then were much colder than they are today, supporting the idea that our ancestors would have needed the extra fat to get through the extremely cold winters when food was harder to find.
So, the next time you poke at your butt fat, remember that fat is a really important part of our bodies, performs lots of different functions, and is likely evolutionarily ancient for us humans.

articles.title: Neue Wallet-Funktion bei OpenAI: ChatGPT kann künftig euer Geld ausgeben
articles.text:
ChatGPT kann künftig euer Geld ausgeben: Mit der neuen ChatGPT Wallet von OpenAI können die KI-Agenten des Anbieters, die sogenannten Dots, im Namen der User:innen einkaufen. Entwickelt hat OpenAI die Funktion gemeinsam mit American Express, Mastercard und Visa. Karteninhaber:innen behalten dabei ihre bestehenden Kreditkartenprämien und Schutzleistungen, betont OpenAI. Vorerst bleibt der Kreis der Nutzenden allerdings eingeschränkt: Die Wallet steht zunächst nur ChatGPT-Pro-Abonnent:innen in den USA ab 18 Jahren offen. OpenAI will so testen, wie die Funktion im Alltag arbeitet, und sie zusammen mit Unternehmen, Banken und Zahlungsnetzwerken verbessern.
So läuft der Einkauf ab
Die Dots hatte OpenAI Ende September vorgestellt. Das sind interaktive Agenten, die Aufgaben ihrer Nutzer:innen von sich aus erledigen und koordinieren sollen. Mit der Wallet kommt nun das Einkaufen dazu. Wer die Funktion nutzen will, hinterlegt einmalig seine Kartendaten. Danach beauftragt man den Agenten, nach einem Produkt zu suchen. Vor dem Kauf zeigt ChatGPT aber den Artikel, den Betrag und die gewählte Karte zur Kontrolle an. Erst nach einer biometrischen Prüfung – etwa per Gesichtserkennung oder Fingerabdruckscan – geht der Kauf durch.
Die Kartendaten selbst bekommen die Agenten laut OpenAI aber nicht zu sehen. Stattdessen liefern die Zahlungsnetzwerke sogenannte Zahlungstoken: Sie enthalten eine Kartennummer, einen Sicherheitscode und ein Ablaufdatum, die nur für diese eine Transaktion gelten. Weder Händler noch Agent erhalten die echten Kartendaten. Das Prinzip ähnelt dem von Google Pay oder Apple Pay, die als sicherer gelten als herkömmliche Kreditkarten, die im Klau-Fall getauscht werden müssen.
Warum viele Shops noch nicht mitspielen
OpenAI will mit der Wallet einen Markt etablieren, bei dem Agenten den Einkauf im Web übernehmen. Nutzer:innen sollen künftig nur noch Vorgaben machen – also etwa ein Ausgabenlimit oder einen Zeitraum. Den Rest erledigten die Agenten, so das Unternehmen.
Noch sind viele Websites und Zahlungssysteme darauf aber nicht vorbereitet, manche wollen KI-Einkäufe gar nicht. Sie könnten Käufe über die ChatGPT-Wallet schlicht ablehnen. OpenAI will E-Commerce-Unternehmen deshalb beim Einstieg unterstützen und stellt dafür Werkzeuge und Anleitungen in einem „Commerce Partner Playbook“ bereit. Darin erklärt das Unternehmen unter anderem, wie Firmen sicherstellen, dass Käufe von KI-Agenten nicht versehentlich abgelehnt werden. Hilfe holt sich OpenAI dabei von Anti-Betrug-Spezialisten.

articles.title: « Je ressens des vertiges » : le nouveau MacBook Pro pose problème à certains utilisateurs
articles.text:
La sortie de l’iPhone Duo avait été quelque peu entachée par le fait que l’écran de certains appareils se soit brisé après seulement quelques utilisations. Apple avait réagi en expliquant que le problème se situait au niveau de la chaîne d’approvisionnement et qu’il concernait seulement « un petit nombre » d’appareils. Mais l’entreprise à la pomme semble maintenant faire face à un nouveau problème, qui concerne cette fois-ci son nouveau MacBook Pro PROLED. En effet, certains de ses utilisateurs rapportent une expérience d’utilisation peu agréable.
Certains utilisateurs de MacBook Pro PROLED pris de nausées et de vertiges
Il n’est pas ici question d’un écran qui se brise ou de touches du clavier défectueuses, mais d’une réaction de certains possesseurs de MacBook Pro PROLED face à une technologie d’affichage. Pour être précis, l’écran de ce nouvel ordinateur d’Apple utilise une gradation PWM à relativement basse fréquence, comprise entre 240 et 480 Hz selon les conditions. La perception de ce type d’affichage peut différer d’une personne à l’autre. Certains ne perçoivent aucune gêne, tandis que d’autres peuvent être pris de vertiges, de nausées, de maux de tête et d’autres symptômes peu agréables.
Certains utilisateurs de MacBook Pro PROLED ont justement ressenti ces symptômes. À tel point que certains ont été contraints de renvoyer l’appareil en magasin. Sur Reddit, un utilisateur explique : « J’adore le mien, mais il me donne tellement le vertige que je n’ai pas d’autre choix que de le retourner ». Un autre confesse : « Je suis assez naïf pour penser que je ne serais pas affecté, mais je me trompais lourdement ! J’ai le nouveau depuis deux jours et je ressens des vertiges ».
Pourquoi de tels symptômes avec le MacBook Pro PROLED et pas sur d’autres appareils ?
Il faut noter que l’iPhone 18 Pro et les iPad dotés d’un écran OLED utilisent également une gradation PWM à basse fréquence. Pourtant, peu d’utilisateurs font état de vertiges ou de nausées. Pourquoi alors serait-ce le cas sur le MacBook Pro PROLED ? La raison est simple : l’écran de l’ordinateur est plus grand et l’utilisateur y effectue bien souvent des tâches qui demandent une certaine concentration (lecture, travail, etc.). Justement, un utilisateur de Reddit explique : « Je ne pouvais littéralement pas travailler (beaucoup de lecture) sur cet ordinateur portable sans avoir la nausée et me sentir déconnecté de la réalité ».
Malheureusement, Apple n’a pas intégré dans son MacBook Pro PROLED une fonctionnalité permettant d’atténuer les effets indésirables de la gradation PWM à basse fréquence. Dans tous les cas, si vous utilisez un MacBook Pro PROLED et que vous éprouvez des sensations désagréables, ne soyez pas surpris. En revanche, une seule solution serait proposée : un retour en magasin.

articles.title: Google Maps can now build trip itineraries with real-time details about each stop | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google announced on Monday that it’s rolling out new Maps features that are designed to help people plan trips and everyday tasks using AI. The company is launching the ability for Maps to create trip itineraries and find appointments for users.
The new features reflect a broader shift in how tech companies are positioning AI, which is less as a tool that just answers questions and more as an assistant that can complete tasks on users’ behalf. While many companies have released AI agents to complete these tasks, Google is working to bring that approach into a service that millions of people already use every day.
Google says users can use the navigation platform’s “Ask Maps” tool to build step-by-step trip itineraries and get real-time details about their route right when they pull up directions.
For example, you could use Ask Maps to plan a holiday shopping day trip or something more complex, like a three-day road trip featuring coastal hikes and oceanfront dining, Google says. You’ll get a day-by-day itinerary with insider tips and numbered map pins for every stop. Once you’re happy with your itinerary, you can share it with friends and family or export it to Google Docs on desktop.
When you’re ready to head out, you can use Ask Maps to reopen your itinerary or find the “itinerary” badge in your chat history. You’ll have access to real-time information, including traffic conditions, business hours, and a look at what the “vibe” is at your next stop, the company says. You could also adjust your schedule by asking Maps to do something like add a scenic viewpoint or lunch stop along your route. You can then tap any destination in your itinerary to get directions and navigate to your next stop.
Additionally, users can use Ask Maps to find beauty, pet care, auto, and home repair appointments online and call local businesses for you. For example, you could ask: “Find me a 4 p.m. nail appointment near me.” Ask Maps will then display open slots across nearby businesses.
The new agentic calling feature arrives as tech companies continue to introduce AI agents designed to handle time-consuming tasks, such as scheduling DMV appointments and making reservations. For example, Meta’s AI agent Muse recently gained the ability to call businesses on users’ behalf.
Google also announced that you can now use Ask Maps to quickly find places on your lists by asking something like: “Which spots saved in my lists have availability for five people in the next 30 minutes?”
The tech giant says the new updates are starting to roll out on Monday on Android and iOS. As part of the news, Google announced that Ask Maps is expanding to 30 countries across Europe, including Spain, Germany, and the U.K.

articles.title: US data centers now burn more electricity than a midsized country
articles.text:
Fossil fuels are still the biggest source of electricity for hyperscale data centers in the US, a new paper published in the journal Nature Sustainability shows. They likely burn through more electricity collectively than many countries do, resulting in a serious amount of greenhouse gas emissions.
US data centers now burn more electricity than a midsized country
The latest numbers are in on how much energy hyperscale data centers use and the carbon pollution they create.
The study homes in on hyperscale facilities — the massive structures spanning millions of square feet that developers are racing to build in large part to support generative AI. Researchers say the findings show that there’s a lot of work left to do to cut down pollution stemming from AI’s reliance on fossil fuels.
“We tend to discuss AI’s environmental footprint as though it were some fixed property of the technology, when in reality the same computing infrastructure can have dramatically different consequences depending on the electricity system supporting it,” Gianluca Guidi, lead author of the new study and a postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Biostatistics at Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, says in an email to The Verge. “I actually find that encouraging, because it means these impacts aren’t inevitable. We have choices about where we build and how we power this infrastructure.”
“The same computing infrastructure can have dramatically different consequences depending on the electricity system supporting it.”
Guidi and his team used satellite imagery to identify 403 hyperscale data centers in the US, estimating each facility’s power consumption based on its electrical capacity. Using data from the Environmental Protection Agency, they approximated how much carbon pollution each data center would have produced if connected to the local power grid between May 2024 and April 2025.
Altogether, the 403 hyperscale facilities likely consumed around 82 terawatt-hours of electricity that year, about 1.8 percent of all US electricity consumption. That’s even more than the amount of electricity that about 148 nations — a majority of the countries in the world including Austria, Israel, and Venezuela but excluding the largest economies including the US and China — individually burn through each year, according to John Sterman, director of the MIT System Dynamics group and MIT Sloan Sustainability Initiative.
Electricity demand from these data centers produced 25.7 million metric tons of CO2 emissions, comparable to the annual carbon footprint of Denmark, according to the research paper. Sterman says that exceeds the total carbon emissions of about 113 nations. That’s because about 54 percent of the electricity the hyperscale facilities consumed likely came from gas and coal.
Sterman, who was not involved in the research with Guidi, disclosed that he used the help of Claude to compare the paper’s findings to electricity use and emissions of countries. “I think AI can be extraordinarily helpful,” Sterman says. “But we’ve got to figure out a way to limit the harms … Especially because those impacts are irreversible. Once you allow these data centers to emit the CO2, you can never undo that.”
Sterman says policymakers should require data center operators to bring new clean energy online. The study doesn’t account for local air pollution that can result from new gas infrastructure that’s being built to meet data center demand, or gas turbines that some AI companies have installed at their facilities to power themselves without connecting to the grid. And while hyperscale data centers encompass more than just AI-related computing, they also make up just a fraction of the thousands of data centers in the US — with more cropping up each year.
The study showed how big a difference the local electricity mix makes when it comes to the environmental impact of AI and data centers. Generating electricity in heavily coal-reliant Wyoming led to roughly seven times more carbon emissions per kilowatt-hour than in hydropower-rich Oregon. “Two data centers consuming exactly the same amount of electricity can have dramatically different carbon footprints simply because of where they’re located,” Guidi writes.
Fengqi You, a professor in energy systems engineering at Cornell University who was also not involved in the study, says the results highlight the problem of “long-term carbon lock-in.” “Power plants and supporting infrastructure built to meet rapidly growing data center demand may operate for decades. Decisions made today could therefore shape emissions well into the future,” You says in an email to The Verge.
Both You and Guidi also pointed out how problematic it is that researchers have to go through such great lengths to estimate energy consumption because data center operators won’t disclose that information. To that end, Guidi and his colleagues are using their research to build a website to track the environmental impact of individual data centers. A bipartisan bill making its way through Congress could also mandate greater disclosures nationally on data centers’ electricity use.
“Communities and policymakers need reliable, independent data on what these facilities mean for our air, health, and the climate. This study is an important step.” Gina McCarthy, former White House national climate advisor and EPA administrator, said in a statement shared by the research authors.

articles.title: Cómo puede afectar la inteligencia artificial a los empleos
articles.text:
El ifo Institute de Alemania publicó el 9 de noviembre de este año un indicador que detectó una caída del 14% en el empleo a tiempo completo de jóvenes de entre 20 y 24 años en ocupaciones altamente expuestas a la inteligencia artificial. El resultado, registrado desde el tercer trimestre de 2022, apunta a posibles dificultades en el acceso a los primeros puestos laborales, aunque no demuestra que la tecnología haya provocado directamente esa reducción.
El número de trabajadores de ese grupo pasó de aproximadamente 279.000 a 239.000. En contraste, el empleo total en las ocupaciones más expuestas a la IA creció un 1,8% durante el período analizado, mientras que en las menos expuestas disminuyó un 6,4%. Estas diferencias sugieren que los cambios podrían afectar de manera desigual a los trabajadores según su edad y las tareas que desempeñan.
El indicador compara la evolución del empleo y las contrataciones en 140 ocupaciones del mercado laboral alemán. La exposición a la IA mide el potencial de esta tecnología para intervenir en determinadas tareas, pero no equivale a una medición directa de puestos eliminados o reemplazados.
Los empleos de entrada muestran las primeras señales de ajuste
El presidente del ifo Institute, Clemens Fuest, señaló que todavía no se observa una pérdida generalizada de puestos atribuible a la inteligencia artificial, aunque quienes comienzan su trayectoria profesional podrían estar entre los primeros afectados. El organismo considera que las ocupaciones de apoyo administrativo y asistencia informática merecen especial atención por la posibilidad de automatizar algunas de sus funciones.
El economista Yuchen Guo, integrante del instituto, explicó que el resultado depende de si la IA complementa las actividades humanas o las automatiza. En los sectores donde sustituye determinadas tareas, el indicador detecta menores niveles relativos de contratación juvenil.
Sin embargo, los investigadores advierten que también deben examinarse factores como los cambios demográficos, la prolongación de los períodos de formación y las dificultades de incorporación a empleos remotos.
Eurofound no encuentra un desplazamiento generalizado de trabajadores jóvenes
Un análisis de Eurofound, publicado el 16 de septiembre de 2026, ofrece un contrapunto importante. La agencia de la Unión Europea examinó el empleo y las contrataciones en los 27 países del bloque entre 2011 y 2025 y concluyó que la evidencia disponible no confirma un impacto laboral desproporcionado de la IA sobre los jóvenes.
A diferencia del indicador alemán, Eurofound estudió principalmente a personas de entre 15 y 29 años y distinguió las ocupaciones según el uso efectivo de herramientas de inteligencia artificial, no solo por su exposición potencial. Entre los jóvenes recientemente contratados, la proporción que ingresó a ocupaciones de alto uso de IA pasó del 23,1% en 2011 al 27,7% en 2019 y al 30,3% en 2025.
El organismo también registró una desaceleración de las contrataciones después del repunte laboral que siguió a la pandemia. La tasa de incorporación de jóvenes pasó del 17,9% en 2022 al 15,9% en 2025, mientras que entre las personas de 30 a 49 años descendió del 10,2% al 8,9%.
Eurofound señaló que este enfriamiento afectó a ambos grupos y que, en las ocupaciones con mayor uso de IA, la desaceleración posterior a 2022 se produjo en proporciones similares.
Los datos europeos revelan diferencias por edad y sector
La Comisión Europea identificó otra diferencia en su análisis del empleo entre 2022 y 2025. En sectores especialmente expuestos a los avances de la IA, como información y comunicación, finanzas, seguros y servicios profesionales, la ocupación aumentó un 2,4% entre las personas de 20 a 29 años, frente al 6,2% registrado entre los trabajadores de 30 a 54 años.
En Estados Unidos, un estudio de Stanford, actualizado en agosto de 2026, analizó registros de nóminas de millones de trabajadores. La investigación encontró que el empleo de personas de 22 a 25 años en ocupaciones muy expuestas a la IA se ubicaba un 19% por debajo del nivel que habría alcanzado si hubiera seguido la evolución de sus pares en actividades menos expuestas. La cifra representa una diferencia respecto de una trayectoria comparativa, no una caída directa del 19% en la cantidad de puestos.
Los investigadores de Stanford observaron que esa divergencia estaba relacionada principalmente con una menor contratación de jóvenes, más que con un aumento de las desvinculaciones. También identificaron diferencias entre ocupaciones donde la tecnología automatiza tareas y aquellas donde complementa el trabajo humano. No obstante, aclararon que sus resultados son descriptivos y no constituyen una prueba causal definitiva.
La capacitación y las trayectorias laborales entran en el centro del debate
El ifo Institute propone orientar la formación hacia habilidades que permitan complementar las herramientas de inteligencia artificial. Esta recomendación parte de la posibilidad de que determinadas tareas iniciales cambien con la incorporación tecnológica, aunque todavía no se conoce la magnitud de sus efectos sobre las trayectorias profesionales a largo plazo.
La evidencia disponible permite identificar señales tempranas y sectoriales de cambios en las oportunidades laborales de los jóvenes, especialmente en ocupaciones con mayor potencial de automatización. Sin embargo, los resultados de Alemania, Estados Unidos y la Unión Europea no ofrecen pruebas suficientes para afirmar que la inteligencia artificial esté sustituyendo de manera generalizada a los trabajadores de menor edad.

articles.title: Após Microsoft e voos, bancos dos EUA também enfrentam instabilidade
articles.text:
Clientes de cinco grandes bancos dos Estados Unidos relataram problemas para acessar serviços financeiros nesta segunda-feira (16), segundo registros do Downdetector. As reclamações envolveram instituições, como Chase, Wells Fargo, Capital One e JPMorgan, em mais um episódio de instabilidade que atingiu serviços digitais no país.
De acordo com o Futurism, milhares de usuários apontaram dificuldades para acessar suas contas on-line. Os relatos também indicaram problemas em outros serviços populares, incluindo plataformas do Google, da Amazon e a loja de jogos Steam.
A sequência de falhas chama atenção porque acontece após uma interrupção global que afetou serviços da Microsoft e uma paralisação que suspendeu temporariamente o tráfego aéreo nos Estados Unidos.
Chase atribui falhas a problema técnico
- Em meio às reclamações, o Chase afirmou que seus problemas foram provocados por uma falha técnica, e não por um ataque cibernético;
- “Devido a um problema técnico, algumas transações estão demorando mais do que o normal para serem concluídas, mas os clientes continuam tendo acesso às suas contas e aos seus fundos”, declarou um porta-voz do banco à Associated Press (AP), segundo o Futurism;
- A manifestação indica que, ao menos no caso do Chase, a instabilidade não significou que os clientes perderam acesso ao dinheiro ou às contas bancárias;
- Até o momento, não há explicação única confirmada para os relatos envolvendo as diferentes instituições financeiras.
Leia mais:
- Estados Unidos ampliam restrições a chips de IA e incluem o Brasil
- Retorno de Jensen Huang ao comando da Nvidia não é má ideia, diz Trump
- Governo Trump deve incluir Nvidia em grupo de campeãs nacionais de IA
Falhas acontecem após problemas em outros serviços nos EUA
A instabilidade bancária é mais um episódio em sequência de problemas que atingiram serviços importantes nos Estados Unidos.
Na semana passada, uma falha na Microsoft afetou plataformas amplamente utilizadas, incluindo Outlook e Microsoft 365. Nesta segunda-feira, a empresa voltou a registrar reclamações relacionadas a seus serviços, segundo dados do Downdetector.
Outro episódio recente envolveu paralisação do tráfego aéreo estadunidense, que interrompeu temporariamente os voos no país.
O Futurism destaca que a repetição desses problemas alimentou especulações sobre possível relação com o uso de IA por empresas de tecnologia. Entretanto, não há evidências apresentadas de que a IA tenha provocado as falhas bancárias.
A própria Microsoft afirmou que sua IA não esteve envolvida na interrupção global registrada na semana anterior. Por enquanto, os episódios devem ser tratados como ocorrências distintas, sem confirmação de uma causa comum.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: What Is Acoustic Micro Imaging? A Quick Guide To This Inspection Process
articles.text:
Obtaining clear images of gaps and delaminations in advanced packages.
We all know how important inspection is for advanced packaging. Not only are these processes critical for ensuring higher yield, but they’re also integral for maintaining device reliability. As the industry pushes for smaller features and tighter spacing, even the smallest defects can pose major challenges. For instance, delaminations and air gaps can be detrimental in a market that demands increasingly complex devices. Such defects will lead to electrical or mechanical failures down the road.
One technology that’s mitigating these issues is acoustic micro imaging (AMI). AMI is a high-frequency ultrasound technology, and it’s being used by the industry as an inspection method.
At the core of AMI technology is a transducer, or a device that turns energy from one form to another. It starts with a pulse of electrical energy, then converts it to mechanical energy, or a high-frequency ultrasound wave. Because ultrasound doesn’t travel through air, this allows inspectors to obtain clear images of gaps and delaminations in the device that could otherwise be difficult to see.
However, the transducers used for AMI are not all the same. Each transducer handles a specific frequency, and they’re chosen based on the sample that needs to be inspected. By moving the transducer across the sample, the inspector can generate multiple images that can then be analyzed by the AMI software. Through this analysis, the inspector can choose to accept or reject parts based on the number of defects the package is found to have.
So, how do these defects typically present themselves?
The biggest difference between ideal and defective samples is that some defective samples will have very clear air gaps. However, another common defect is thinning of the attach material on solder pads. When this material is too thin, any stress that would be put on the device could lead to delamination. An uneven solder or thermal interface material (TIM) layer may also indicate a larger problem with the build process.
With the ability to gather so much information without damaging the device, why would anyone choose to perform a destructive test to identify a defect, rather than simply use AMI inspection to check for them? One reason is for R&D purposes. Oftentimes, companies want to ensure that a process is fully developed before integrating it into their production cycle, and a destructive test can confirm proof of concept for AMI.
An example of this in action is a standard capacitor inspection. New capacitor companies will often require a destructive test to confirm the presence of voids or delaminations found by the AMI software. Once the destructive proof of concept has been completed, the company can then integrate the software into their inspection process.
There are some key differences between AMI and its transmission technology counterpart, which is more comparable to X-ray. Whereas AMI is an ultrasound technology, transmission scanning uses both a sending and receiving transducer positioned above and below the sample. Both transmission technology and X-ray create composite images, unlike AMI, which inspects layer-by-layer.
Ultrasound and X-ray are complementary technologies. There are some things AMI can do that X-ray can’t, and vice versa. For certain applications, both technologies may be recommended. For example, composite images are preferable for inspecting spherical objects like ball grid arrays.
Although AMI technology has tangible benefits, keeping up with the industry’s rapid pace is a hurdle that AMI must continually overcome. As applications become more complex, AMI software needs to quickly adapt to changing components. For instance, instead of scanning a single flip chip, AMI software could now be required to inspect multi-die stacks.
One way this mounting complexity is being addressed is through machine learning algorithms.
For example, some wafers have via patterns that look similar or identical to delamination, and humans have typically been responsible for distinguishing them. However, through advancements in machine learning, AMI software can now identify via patterns and exclude those from the defect count. As machine learning becomes more robust, it will open new doors for inspecting increasingly complicated devices.
In addition, customer requirements for higher resolution and better throughput are also driving new developments for AMI software. To meet these rising demands, Nordson Test & Inspection developed its automated SpinSAM tool that can inspect four 300mm wafers at a time.
Traditionally, acoustic microscopy systems move the transducer in a raster pattern, which is a small grid made up of individual pixels. This approach allows inspectors to collect data at every XY point, but it also requires decelerating to turn the transducer at the end of each line, thereby reducing throughput. Some acoustic microscopes address the need for better throughput by skipping lines and interpolating data points, or by using multiple transducers and stitching images together – both of which have their own drawbacks.
In contrast, SpinSAM spins the wafer to move the transducer and the wafer continuously, allowing inspectors to scan each pixel faster, allowing for better throughput without image stitching distortion.

articles.title: Helping AI coding agents work smarter, for less
articles.text:
At a glance
- Developers use AI coding agents in the same codebases day after day, yet agents often start each session from scratch: rediscovering familiar facts, loading unused tools, and repeating unsuccessful approaches.
- TokenEconomizer is an open-source plugin that learns from an agent’s past sessions in a repository to reduce waste in future sessions, without modifying the agent or its underlying model.
- Across 277 real bug-fixing tasks, TokenEconomizer reduced costs by 18.4–30.9% across multiple AI coding agents. Costs fell in every repository tested, while task success rates remained broadly stable.
AI coding agents are increasingly helping developers fix bugs and build features largely on their own, but every interaction with their models consumes tokens. In each session, an agent sends instructions, tool descriptions, and session history to its model. Most efforts to reduce this cost focus on individual tasks. Yet developers return to the same repositories, giving agents an opportunity to learn from previous work. Without that learning, an agent may repeatedly rediscover how to run tests, load tools it never uses, or spend dozens of turns revisiting the same error.
In our paper, TokenEconomizer: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents, we ask a simple question: can experience in a repository help an agent solve future tasks more efficiently? TokenEconomizer, an open-source plugin from UC Berkeley, Microsoft Research, and Microsoft Security, turns completed sessions into guidance for subsequent ones. It reduces waste without changing the agent or its underlying model, so developers can use it alongside the coding agents they already rely on.
Where the tokens go
We first profiled Claude Code on 60 tasks from SWE-Bench, a benchmark of real bug fixes in open-source Python projects, running each repository’s tasks in sequence. Three kinds of waste recurred:
- Rediscovering the same facts. After a repository had accumulated at least five completed tasks, 30% of tool calls repeated an action from an earlier task in that repository. Only 7% matched an action in another repository’s history.
- Paying for unused tools. The agent received 23 tool descriptions on every turn, but 16 were never called.
- Getting stuck on failures. The 17% of tasks that failed accounted for 32% of the spending.
We also tested three popular open-source plugins, each built around a fixed cost-saving strategy. Each lowered costs in some repositories but not others. Together, these findings suggest that effective cost control must adapt to the repository, rather than apply the same strategy everywhere.
How TokenEconomizer works
After each session, TokenEconomizer reads the session’s log and updates what it knows about the repository. It then acts through three mechanisms, using only interfaces the agent already provides, as illustrated in Figure 2.
Micro-skills capture repository-specific knowledge in one-line notes. TokenEconomizer identifies recurring patterns across sessions and proposes corresponding notes. They are added to the agent’s starting context only after several sessions have confirmed the pattern, and retires the note if later evidence contradicts it.
Tool pruning removes tools that repository history suggests the agent is unlikely to use, while always retaining core tools for running commands and editing files. Removed tools can be restored if needed.
Failure-loop intervention watches for an agent that keeps hitting the same failure. A judge model decides whether the agent is truly stuck or still making progress. If it is stuck, the agent gets a short note suggesting a different approach. In the open-source plugin, if the agent is still stuck after the note, TokenEconomizer alerts the developer rather than stopping the work itself.
The controller is designed to revise its decisions as new evidence arrives. Reported savings also account for the cost of TokenEconomizer’s own model calls.
Saving costs in every repository
We evaluated TokenEconomizer on 277 SWE-Bench tasks from six repositories, using five different AI coding agent and model combinations. For each repository, TokenEconomizer started with no prior session history.
TokenEconomizer lowered the average cost by 18.4–30.9%, as shown in Figure 3, and saved the most in all 30 repository-combination pairs without performance loss. By contrast, lowering the model’s reasoning effort saved similar or larger amounts but led to substantial performance degradation.
Savings grow as experience accumulates. Early tasks can cost more while TokenEconomizer learns, but cumulative costs fell below the default in every repository by the sixth task, shown inFigure 4. Each mechanism contributes savings on its own, and combining all three delivers the largest reduction.
The savings also carried over to sequential web development, with costs 16.0–21.2% lower on Web-Bench. On security auditing, where every task is in a new repository, costs were 6.4–19.6% lower.
Looking ahead
TokenEconomizer opens a path toward coding agents that learn not only how to solve tasks, but also how to spend computation more effectively. Its lightweight controller shows how experience can improve efficiency without changing the underlying agent or model.
The open-source plugin makes these directions accessible to developers and researchers. It is designed to run alongside existing AI coding agents without modifying their underlying models, requires no API key of its own, and keeps what it learns on the developer’s machine. We invite the community to use it as a starting point for exploring agents that become more resourceful with experience, adapting how they work, as well as what they know.

articles.title: Sortie de GTA 6 en direct : toutes les informations, les astuces et les chiffres
articles.text:
Il n’y aura plus de retard. Après deux reports, GTA 6 sort officiellement ce jeudi 19 novembre 2026. Rockstar Games commercialise enfin son nouveau blockbuster, 13 ans après GTA 5 et 8 ans après Red Dead Redemption 2. GTA 5 s’est écoulé entre-temps à près de 235 millions d’exemplaires, selon Take-Two, la maison mère de Rockstar.
Le lancement de GTA 6 va être décortiqué pendant des semaines. On parle d’un véritable événement culturel, qui est sur absolument toutes les bouches, des sportifs de haut niveau aux hommes politiques. Le monde va s’arrêter pendant quelques jours et s’articuler autour d’un jeu vidéo.
À cette occasion, on vous propose de suivre en direct la sortie de GTA 6, avec tous les détails, les images, les vidéos, les chiffres, les astuces, les rebonds…
Suivez le lancement de GTA 6 en direct
Le trailer des préchargements
Un GTA 6 plus réaliste ?
GTA 6 pourrait être bien plus proche de Red Dead Redemption 2, avec une expérience plus réaliste et plus mature. « Le crime est un élément fondamental de GTA — du moins, ça l’a été jusqu’à présent. Nous essayons de faire en sorte de ne pas punir les gens qui jouent comme ils en ont l’habitude… mais vos actions auront un certain effet sur le déroulement de la partie », a confié Rob Nelson, co-directeur du studio Rockstar North et l’un des trois directeurs créatifs du jeu à Guardian. Il faudra notamment entretenir la relation entre Jason et Lucia.
Un record pour les précommandes
Selon le site Sensor Tower, GTA 6 serait le jeu vidéo le plus précommandé de tous les temps, avec près de 15 millions d’exemplaires (11 millions sur PS5, 3,8 sur Xbox). Cyberpunk 2077 détenait le précédent record (8 millions).
Il existe une édition collector
Rockstar Games a bien évidemment proposé une édition collector de GTA 6, vendu 400 € et sans le jeu à l’intérieur.
On y trouve :
- une figurine de Macca the Gator d’environ 15 cm, avec un compartiment caché ;
- des lunettes de soleil Oakley Frogskins ;
- une casquette New Era ;
- un sac bandoulière Leonida Keys ;
- un miroir magnétique ;
- une cuillère à cocktail ;
- un porte-clés en forme de lame de rasoir ;
- un verre à shot ;
- des pin’s dans une boîte en métal ;
- des autocollants ;
- et un poster recto verso.
Un long aperçu de 27 minutes
La plus longue vidéo officielle de GTA 6 dure 27 minutes. Elle a été diffusée fin août, d’abord sur Netflix. Elle montre plusieurs séquences de gameplay.
Une Xbox One suffit pour jouer
Si GTA 6 sort officiellement sur les nouvelles consoles, une Xbox One, machine d’ancienne génération, suffit, grâce à la technologie Xbox Cloud Gaming (il faut être propriétaire du jeu, bien sûr, et avoir un abonnement Xbox Game Pass et/ou avoir du temps de jeu, facturé 3,49 € pour 10 heures). Les paramètres graphiques seront ceux de la Xbox Series S.
Pas de 60 fps pour GTA 6…
Rockstar Games a confirmé que GTA 6 vise les 30 fps sur toutes les consoles du marché. Même la PS5 Pro à 900 € n’offrira pas un framerate à 60 fps. La console la plus puissante de Sony offrira quand même « des visuels à couper le souffle, avec une clarté améliorée grâce à la technologie PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) et des ombres tracées par rayons, disponibles uniquement sur PlayStation 5 Pro ».
Combien pèse GTA 6 ?
Mieux vaut faire de la place sur sa console avant de lancer le téléchargement. Rockstar Games prévient que le fichier de préchargement pèse jusqu’à 212 Go selon la console. Sur PS5, vous pouvez facilement ajouter un SSD additionnel. Sur Xbox, il faut passer par une carte mémoire propriétaire.
Une femme jouable pour la première fois !
Pour la première fois dans l’histoire de la saga GTA, l’un des personnages principaux jouables est une femme. Il s’agit de Lucia Caminos, qui partage l’affiche avec Jason Duval. Ensemble, ils forment un couple de criminels façon Bonnie et Clyde.
Il existe d’ailleurs une astuce pour y jouer avant…
Vous voulez jouer à GTA 6 dès ce mercredi 18 novembre à midi ? C’est possible, mais uniquement sur Xbox. Il suffit de régler sa console sur la région de la Nouvelle-Zélande pour profiter du décalage, sans aucun risque.
À quelle heure sort GTA 6 ?
Rockstar Games a opté pour un lancement régionalisé. GTA 6 sera disponible dans chaque pays à minuit, heure locale. Certaines régions, comme la Nouvelle-Zélande, y joueront donc avant les autres.
Vous pouvez déjà installer le jeu
Que vous ayez précommandé le jeu en physique ou en numérique, vous pouvez d’ores et déjà installer GTA 6 sur votre PS5 ou votre Xbox. Rockstar Games a lancé le préchargement dès le 10 novembre pour éviter les embouteillages le jour J.
Le deuxième trailer
Que contient vraiment l’édition physique ?
L’édition physique de GTA 6, que ce soit sur PS5 ou Xbox, ne contient aucun disque. À l’intérieur de la boîte, on retrouve quand même un poster au format A3 (mais sans la carte du jeu) et divers feuillets.
C’est quoi cette édition ultime au juste ?
La version Ultime de GTA 6 ajoute ces contenus, qui sont majoritairement d’ordre cosmétique :
- Collection de voitures classiques
- Grotti Cheetah (1995)
- Revolvers Hawk & Little Morgan
- Variantes d’armes personnalisées
- Style de Vice City
- Véhicules pour la planque de Jason
- Modèle rétro pour le Ganado
- Atelier de tuning Rideout Customs
- Sara’s Unisex Salon
- Shitzu Squalo
- Boutique de vêtements Stock 305
- Vapid Dominator Buggy (1967)
- Salon de tatouage Electric Fang Tattoo
- Atelier de tuning One-Eyed Willie
- Les articles du Bonheur
- Repaire des PTT Youngin$
À noter que rien ne vous empêche d’acheter le pack plus tard, facturé 20 €.
Combien ça coûte GTA 6 ?
GTA 6 coûte 79,99 € en édition standard, en version physique (sans disque, avec un code de téléchargement) comme en numérique. Une édition Ultime est également proposée à 99,99 €, exclusivement en numérique, sur le PlayStation Store et le Microsoft Store.
Le tout premier trailer
La première bande-annonce de GTA 6, publiée en décembre 2023, a dépassé les 300 millions de vues sur YouTube.
Les grandes dates de GTA 6
- 4 février 2022 : développement confirmé
- 18 septembre 2022 : grosse fuite, avec plus de 90 vidéos en ligne
- 5 décembre 2023 : première bande-annonce (également victime d’une fuite)
- 2 mai 2025 : premier report officiel, GTA 6 est décalé de l’automne 2025 au 26 mai 2026
- 6 mai 2025 : deuxième bande-annonce
- 6 novembre 2025 : deuxième report, avec la date finale du 19 novembre 2026
- 25 juin 2026 : ouverture des précommandes
- 27 août 2026 : long aperçu de 27 minutes, diffusé sur Netflix avant YouTube
- 10 novembre 2026 : lancement des préchargements
On y est !
Enfin ! C’est la semaine de sortie de GTA 6, le nouveau blockbuster qui sort ce jeudi 19 novembre sur PS5, Xbox Series S et Xbox Series X. La machine médiatique est prête à être mise en route. On risque de manger du GTA 6 pendant des semaines et des semaines, si le jeu est bel et bien à la hauteur de cet événement mondial.
GTA 6, en bref
GTA 6 est le nouveau jeu du studio Rockstar Games, connu pour les sagas GTA et Red Dead Redemption. Après deux reports (il était d’abord prévu à l’automne 2025, puis le 26 mai 2026), il sort ce jeudi 19 novembre 2026 sur PS5, Xbox Series S et Xbox Series X. Rockstar a confirmé son développement en février 2022. En septembre de la même année, plus de 90 vidéos et images du jeu en développement ont fuité en ligne. La toute première bande-annonce date de décembre 2023. Les précommandes ont été lancées le 25 juin 2026, avec deux éditions : une version standard à 79,99 € et une version ultime à 99,99 €, vendue uniquement en numérique.
Le synopsis officiel est le suivant : « Jason et Lucia ont toujours su que la vie ne leur ferait pas de cadeau. Mais lorsque les choses tournent mal, ils découvrent le côté obscur de la région la plus ensoleillée d’Amérique, et se retrouvent au cœur d’un complot criminel qui s’étend dans tout l’État de Leonida. Ils devront plus que jamais compter l’un sur l’autre pour espérer s’en sortir vivants. » GTA 6 se déroule dans l’État fictif de Leonida, inspiré de la Floride, et dans sa grande ville, Vice City, calquée sur Miami.
Si vous avez précommandé la version numérique, le préchargement est ouvert depuis le mardi 10 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series. Prévoyez de la place : selon Rockstar, le jeu peut demander jusqu’à 212 Go d’espace de stockage, selon la console.

articles.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Leads Agentic Inference Performance on MLPerf Endpoints v1.0 | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.text:
Agentic workloads are demanding more from inference systems. AI agents carry growing conversation histories across turns and generate a mix of reasoning, tool calls, and responses. Inference systems must support users at scale while remaining responsive.
MLPerf Endpoints v1.0 evaluates this balance between serving capacity and responsiveness using coding and enterprise workflows through API endpoints. During performance runs, generated tool calls and workflow intent are checked against reference values. Separate SWE-bench Verified evaluations assess end-to-end task-solving capability. These checks evaluate whether faster serving preserves model quality.
In MLPerf Endpoints v1.0, provisional NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 results show over 10x the throughput per kilowatt of provisioned power of NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 at a shared minimum end-to-end interactivity of 50 tokens per second per user.1
This post presents the benchmark results and outlines the hardware and software optimizations used in the submissions.
1MLPerf® Endpoints v1.0, Kimi K3, Standardized division, Available category, published November 9, 2026. NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72, 32 accelerators, result 1.0.1.kimi-k3.agentic_combined.1p, run 9: concurrency = 1,024 queries, TTFT P90 = 4,673.9 ms, system TPS = 41,414.2 tokens/sec, E2E average interactivity = 50.4 tokens/sec per user, operating power = 100.89 kW. NVIDIA GB300 NVL72, 48 accelerators, result 1.0.0.kimi-k3.agentic_combined.1, run 6: concurrency = 48 queries, TTFT P90 = 2,305.1 ms, system TPS = 2,210.4 tokens/sec, E2E average interactivity = 56.2 tokens/sec per user, operating power = 60 kW. Comparison based on throughput per kilowatt at a shared minimum E2E average interactivity of 50 tokens/sec per user. Retrieved from endpoints.mlcommons.org on November 9, 2026. GB300 results verified by MLCommons Association. For the provisional Vera Rubin results: pending MLCommons Association verification, results are subject to change pending peer review. The MLPerf name and logo are registered and unregistered trademarks of MLCommons Association in the United States and other countries. All rights reserved. Unauthorized use is strictly prohibited. See www.mlcommons.org for more information.
The serving demands of multi-turn agentic AI
The MLPerf Endpoints v1.0 dataset captures these workload characteristics: coding trajectories accumulate history over many turns, while enterprise workflows reuse shared instructions, tool definitions, and business rules. Figure 1 shows how context length grows across model responses during extended agentic sessions.
Vera Rubin delivers over 10x the agentic throughput per kilowatt
The submissions span Kimi K3, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash. Table 1 compares provisional Vera Rubin NVL72 results with verified NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 results for throughput per provisioned kilowatt at a shared minimum end-to-end (E2E) interactivity threshold and for E2E interactivity at matched query concurrency.
| Model | Throughput per provisioned kW ratio | E2E interactivity ratio | 
|---|---|---|
| Kimi K3 | 10x | 3x | 
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | 9x | 5x | 
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | 5x | 3x | 
² MLPerf® Endpoints v1.0, Kimi K3, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Standardized division, Available category. GB300 results published November 4, 2026; Vera Rubin results published November 9, 2026, for Kimi K3 and Qwen, and November 10, 2026, for DeepSeek. Retrieved from endpoints.mlcommons.org on November 10, 2026. Comparisons select each platform’s best TPS/kW meeting the stated minimum E2E average interactivity, or best E2E average interactivity at the stated matched concurrency. Records list: result ID; run number; concurrency (queries); TTFT P90 (ms); System TPS (tokens/sec); E2E average interactivity (tokens/sec per user); operating-point power (kW).
Kimi K3: Throughput/kW: see Footnote 1. Interactivity at matched concurrency 1,024 queries: Vera Rubin (1.0.1.kimi-k3.agentic_combined.1p; 9; 1,024; 4,673.9; 41,414.2; 50.4; 100.89); GB300 (1.0.0.kimi-k3.agentic_combined.1; 16; 1,024; 15,223.0; 13,905.8; 16.8; 60).
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: Throughput/kW at minimum E2E average interactivity 280 tokens/sec per user: Vera Rubin (1.0.1.deepseek-v4_1-flash.mlperf_agentic_inference_dataset.1p; 6; 1,408; 427; 272,711.7; 294.49; 75.67), 24 GPUs; GB300 (1.0.0.deepseek-v4_1-flash.mlperf_agentic_inference_dataset.1; 1; 16; 112.8; 3,054.0; 288.65; 7.50), 4 GPUs. Interactivity at matched concurrency 1,024 queries: Vera Rubin (1.0.1.deepseek-v4_1-flash.mlperf_agentic_inference_dataset.1p; 5; 1,024; 505; 204,207.7; 307.36; 63.06), 20 GPUs; GB300 (1.0.0.deepseek-v4_1-flash.mlperf_agentic_inference_dataset.1; 8; 1,024; 4,073.5; 49,701.8; 56.65; 7.50), 4 GPUs.
Qwen3.6-35B-A3B: Throughput/kW at minimum E2E average interactivity 410 tokens/sec per user: Vera Rubin (1.0.1.qwen3_6-35b-a3b.agentic_coding.1p; 8; 320; 75.2; 47,785.5; 411.9; 12.61); GB300 (1.0.0.qwen3_6-35b-a3b.agentic_coding.1; 2; 36; 65.3; 5,960.4; 531.6; 7.50). Interactivity at matched concurrency 256 queries: Vera Rubin (1.0.1.qwen3_6-35b-a3b.agentic_coding.1p; 7; 256; 65.9; 41,142.6; 501.0; 12.61); GB300 (1.0.0.qwen3_6-35b-a3b.agentic_coding.1; 7; 256; 111.7; 23,467.8; 154.5; 7.50).
Ratios are rounded as shown. GB300 results verified by MLCommons Association. Vera Rubin’s results are provisional. Pending MLCommons Association verification, results are subject to change pending peer review. The MLPerf name and logo are registered and unregistered trademarks of MLCommons Association in the United States and other countries. All rights reserved. Unauthorized use is strictly prohibited. See www.mlcommons.org for more information.
Figure 2 shows the tradeoff between throughput per provisioned kilowatt and E2E interactivity across at least seven concurrency levels per curve. The curves show how much throughput each system delivers at a given responsiveness requirement. The step-function plot does not interpolate between measured points to keep comparisons grounded in demonstrated performance rather than estimates.
Higher throughput per kilowatt enables organizations to run more agents simultaneously within the same power budget while meeting the same responsiveness requirement. At low concurrency, faster responses reduce inference wait times for latency-sensitive agentic tasks.
Hardware and software optimizations for agentic inference
NVIDIA Rubin GPUs combine HBM4 memory, NVIDIA Tensor Cores, and sixth-generation NVIDIA NVLink to support the demands of agentic inference. HBM4 enables rapid access to model weights and conversation state, Tensor Cores accelerate matrix operations, and NVLink supports communication across GPUs. Context-aware serving and model-specific kernels build on these capabilities to reuse prior work, independently optimize prefill and decode, and accelerate token generation—translating hardware advances into greater inference capacity and faster interactions.
Context-aware serving and model-specific optimizations improve inference performance
Agentic workloads repeatedly reuse conversation history while adding new instructions and tool results. Efficient serving must preserve reusable state, distribute requests across workers, and accommodate the different execution requirements of prompt processing and token generation. Prefix caching, state reuse, and NVIDIA Dynamo routing help reduce redundant computation and balance serving load, while disaggregated serving supports independent optimization of prefill and decode.
Figure 3 summarizes how context-aware serving and model-specific GPU execution support agentic inference.
Kimi K3, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B also have distinct architectures that benefit from targeted GPU execution improvements. Model-specific kernels, fusion, optimized memory access, and speculative verification reduce data movement and execution overhead. Table 2 summarizes how these serving and execution techniques work together across the three models.
| Optimization | How it improves performance | 
|---|---|
| Context reuse and routing | Reuse previously processed conversation state and distribute requests to reduce recomputation and balance worker load. Example: Qwen’s fine-grained prefix matching reuses previously processed history across turns. | 
| Prefill and decode optimization | Configure prompt processing and token generation independently through disaggregated serving, reducing contention and synchronization waits. Example: Kimi combines disaggregated serving with prefill changes that reduce GPU synchronization waits. | 
| Model-specific GPU execution | Tailor kernels, fusion, and memory access to each architecture, reducing kernel launches and data movement. Example: DeepSeek’s MegaMoE kernel uses Rubin GPU locality and matrix-multiply instructions. | 
| Speculative generation and verification | Propose multiple tokens and verify them together, reducing sequential decoding steps. Example: Qwen’s multi-token prediction pairs token proposals with Tensor Core verification. | 
More productive infrastructure for agentic AI
Agentic inference performance depends on co-design across hardware, system architecture, and serving software. The provisional MLPerf Endpoints v1.0 results show how the Vera Rubin platform brings these capabilities together to address the demands of agentic workloads and create more capacity to serve users and scale applications.
Learn more about NVIDIA training and inference performance in the companion blog post.
